verdicts.question: Is a scripted France at half strength (the script spends 63-86 of 160 AP) still viable at HEAD?
verdicts.evidence: All five seeds finish status completed, 200 commands, 0 unknown_blockers, 0 OFF THE BOOKS rows, 0 Tracebacks. France ends T40 with 27 (historical), 28 (austerlitz), 25 (marengo), 23 (jena), 26 (ulm) of the 28 it starts with. ap_spent/160: 86, 79, 63, 76, 77; cmd_refused 62, 58, 80, 63, 61 of 200. No seed reaches a Fall of the Empire in 40 turns. Weak points: jena slides 28 to 23 after T30 and marengo loses Lorraine, Orleanais and Rhineland by peace at T24.

verdicts.question: Do the courts fight back, and is their fighting legible to the player?
verdicts.evidence: They fight hard and visibly: historical T4-T11, Archduke Charles takes Piedmont, Provence, Lyonnais, Savoy, Burgundy, Languedoc, Limousin and Berry (digest.md lines 116-282), taking 2 provinces a turn, with a fogged sentence every turn. Marengo has Davout destroyed, Lannes and Bernadotte taken, and the Emperor TAKEN at T23 (digest.md line 589), then a peace with enemy_victory at T24. Jena T34-T40 has Britain's Shrapnel taking Provence, Lyonnais, Savoy, Burgundy, Limousin, Berry, Anjou, Maine and Brittany in turn. Enemy phase and Dispatch name captor, province and corps size. The gap is the other direction: French provinces handed back by Spain are almost never announced (CMD-2).

verdicts.question: Does anything absurd happen (dead-target order repeated, stuck standing order, 0-casualty loop, fortify/unfortify farce, unexplained treasury or province jump)?
verdicts.evidence: Dead-target orders: marengo repeats Davout fortify/unfortify/drill 12 times after he is destroyed (T21, T23, T25 on), and 'attack Mack' goes to a prisoner 2-5 times. That is the open-loop script, not the engine, and the replies are clean. Fortify/unfortify refusals are also script-side. No 0-casualty battle loop on France's side. One real AI absurdity: Bavaria's Deroy hits the same square-formed Bennigsen three times in one phase, austerlitz T33 (CMD-1). Treasury: chest_window off_books is empty on every run, and the province swings are explained by captures plus silent Spanish liberations (CMD-2).

verdicts.question: Does the insist arm produce different drama from trust (defiance, compromises, trust falls)?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-cmd-insist-historical vs rev1106-cmd-historical: a 40-line diff of digest.md. The only fork is one objection popup, Lannes at T21 ('I would rather attack than sit idle'), insist vs trust. That changes one command result at T23 (Lannes unfortify works), and ap_spent goes 86 to 88. Provinces, treasury, battles (24) and popups (75) are identical to the last LEDGER row. The benchmark script raises 1 objection popup per run on historical and 3 each on austerlitz and marengo, so defiance, compromise and trust-fall paths are not exercised (CMD-4).

verdicts.question: Is the economy sound under the half-strength commanded arm?
verdicts.evidence: The S14j chest rubber band works as designed: state charges grow with the chest (austerlitz T32 charges 3,320 and T34 3,933, vs income 2,590). A hoard of 29,749 at T31 sinks to 17,898 by T40, net -1,435 a turn, and bill_notes explain every move. Historical's chest rises to 24,363 at T40 because the script does not spend it. The 20-nation purses are sane (Hanover 1,070 to Ottoman 22,979 at austerlitz T32), but the Ottoman Empire sits on a 23k hoard.

The fog sentence prints every turn including empty ones, and the ally-liberation rule (S14G-D1) keeps France's homeland recoverable through its Spanish ally.
sections.notes:
What I ran. I ran commanded_full40 on historical, austerlitz, marengo, jena and ulm, plus historical again with --objection insist. All finished completed, in parallel, from the repository root. docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-{historical,austerlitz,marengo,jena,ulm,insist-historical} are the archived records. I did not run anything on port 8005 or with an LLM, and edited no source.

Verdict in plain words: the game is in good shape on this arm. Nothing crashed, the books balance, and France survives at half-strength command with 23-28 provinces on every seed. The courts are genuinely dangerous and the fighting is readable. The one real engine defect I found is an AI one (CMD-1), and the rest is legibility and the benchmark's own limits.

Paragraph per seed at T40.
- historical: Austria's Archduke Charles overran southern France T4-T11, taking up to two provinces a turn. The Kingdom of Italy vassal was eliminated at T4 and the rest was retaken, ending 27 provinces (28 at start). By T22 peace with Britain is signed and by T40 there are no wars, with 4 armistices ratified. The chest is 24k and the army 76k (down from 175k). A quiet, victorious, under-spent France.
- austerlitz: 28 provinces for all 40 turns. Marshals are lost along the way (Bernadotte T3, Ney T36, Teulie T37) but no ground. The Fourth Coalition (Britain, Russia, Austria, Sweden, Hanover, Sardinia) declares at T32, so at T40 France is in a six-nation war with a 46k army, an 18k chest and net -1.4k. Of all the runs this one points most clearly to a coming collapse.
- marengo: the weakest early game. Davout is destroyed, Lannes and Bernadotte captured, and the Emperor taken at T23 with 807 men in the Guard. France accepts Austria's peace at T24 and cedes Lorraine, Orleanais and Rhineland. It then sits at 25 provinces at peace with a 24k chest and 109k army, 'the Emperor's star dims' dispatch, and no wars at T40.
- jena: 28 provinces to T30, then the Fourth Coalition at T30. Britain's single 10k corps (Shrapnel) takes nine homeland provinces T34-T40 against an unmanned interior (the script does not defend). The ledger shows 23 at T40, a treasury of 12.8k and 44k army: the one seed that is clearly sliding.
- ulm: a quiet 40 turns, 28 provinces until T33 when two are lost, ending 26 with only Britain at war and an 83k army.

Why HEAD differs from Oct 28 (17 / 28 / 26 to 27 / 28 / 25). Historical +10, austerlitz 0 and marengo -1. The only seed with a real move is historical. The commanded arm has swung 11-30 on historical across the project's life, and the Oct 28 17 was itself the slice-induced low that the user accepted. Slices since include S14j, S14k, row RE, row AU (AU-19 stopped booking 'capital lost' on a satellite's capital, AU-20 fixed the courts' Decree). AU-19 is the likeliest cause of historical's recovery because it removes about 248 spurious -5 authority bookings, but I did not A/B it and say so. Versus Sept 28 (30 / 29 / 27) HEAD is 1-3 provinces lower on every seed, consistent with the S14k courts in arms.

What I could not measure. (1) Casualty totals per side were not summed; I counted battles and read the headline losses. (2) No A/B toggled slices, so I only name likely causes. (3) The digest is the fogged player view, so AI-vs-AI action lists are not in it; the console log was my only window into them. (4) A human playing this France would spend the chest and fight; the benchmark does neither, so none of these end states say where a driven France ends up, only where a passive one does. (5) I did not read any Godot client view of these turns.

Cross-seed note. Three of five seeds (jena T30, austerlitz T32, ulm T32) produce a late Fourth-Coalition war and two (historical, marengo) do not. This matches the project's 'assure the shapes, vary the casting' design target. The six-nation roster is identical on austerlitz and jena, though, which is worth a look by whoever owns the AI-intent variance work. I cannot tell from one run per seed whether that is the attractor working or low variance in who joins.

Sibling sweep for CMD-1 (rule 10): I grep'd 'desperate' across all rev1106-cmd-* console logs; only austerlitz shows it (4 lines). The ulm T38 double attack by Castanos on Andalusia comes from the HOMELAND DEFENSE rung and a 'COUNTER-PUNCH EARNED' free attack, so I take it as designed, not a finding.

verdicts.question: Does Europe act without France (a life of its own)?
verdicts.evidence: All six rev1106-amb digests: Prussia takes Hanover (war T11-14, peace 3 turns later), Bavaria beaten by Austria, Britain-Spain and Spain-Switzerland peaces, 12 laws abroad, 4-8 marshal commissions, 2-6 landings, 9-34 subsidy rows. Four of six end in THE FALL OF THE EMPIRE (T31/T35/T38/T40).

verdicts.question: Are the six seeds different enough (multiple unpredictable outcomes)?
verdicts.evidence: Three outcome classes: Fall at T31-T40 (historical, jena, marengo, friedland), near-Fall at 2 provinces on T40 (austerlitz), France holds 16 provinces at T40 (ulm). But the political skeleton is the same on every seed: Prussia on Hanover, Hanover pays, Britain-Spain peace T15/T16, Spain-Switzerland peace, Italy eliminated, Portugal violation T3.

verdicts.question: Do the four great powers act in character (AI_INTENT_SPEC 3.4)?
verdicts.evidence: Britain the paymaster: yes (subsidies 9-34 per run, landings, Orders in Council T1). Austria: patient inside the coalition, yes. Prussia bandwagoner: only ever fights Hanover; never joins the war on France even when France is at 5 provinces (historical T20). Russia: Gulf and Straits promoted T11 on jena and the court 'hardens', but no Russo-Ottoman or Swedish war in any digest.

verdicts.question: Is there soap-opera repetition?
verdicts.evidence: Sweep soap share 0.907-0.947 (intent lines capped at 2 per dispatch). Repeating lines: 'An envoy from Hesse has arrived with a proposal.' 8-9 times per run, Britain's 'gold reaches Austria - subsidy stands at 300' 8 times (austerlitz), 'coalition is brewing against Austria' 5 times on jena and friedland.

verdicts.question: Is a coalition against a non-French hegemon coherent?
verdicts.evidence: jena T22/28/31/34/37 and friedland T18/21/24/27/30 announce 'coalition brewing against Austria' (one court consulting from T28) and no coalition ever declares.

sections.notes:
What I ran: six ambient 40-turn Mode A digests (historical, ulm, austerlitz, jena, marengo, friedland), all archived, plus three ai_v_sweep single runs (historical, austerlitz, jena; JSON in tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-aiv-*.json). The sweep's first launch failed with 'No module named tools' because the brief's command omits PYTHONPATH=. (a doc/harness nit: child_env sets it for spawned children, but --run directly needs it from the shell). I reran with PYTHONPATH=. and it worked. I did not run marengo, ulm or friedland through the sweep (the brief asked for three); I did not run the Anthropic LLM; I did not touch port 8005 or edit any code.

Judgement in plain words. Europe has a life of its own: it fights, makes peace, enacts laws, buys marshals and pays subsidies, and it kills a passive France on four of six seeds by T31-T40. The crisis ladder (Prussia on Hanover) is the best-realised piece: it is readable, in order, and historically right (1806, with Hanover as the Prussian prize). The weakness is breadth and repeatability. Every seed is the same play in a different time signature. Prussia-Hanover T8-T14, Hanover pays, Britain-Spain peace on T15/T16, Spain-Switzerland peace, Italy eliminated, Portugal violated at T3, Bavaria revanche. I count three outcome classes in six seeds, all of them 'how fast France falls'. Austria, Russia and Britain never fight each other, Prussia never joins the war on France, Russia's Gulf and Straits and Austria's Eastern Question are announced but never acted on, and no volte-face, compensation, guarantee, licence or formation occurs in 40 turns. After France's threat reaches 0 (about T20-T25), politics among the victors is laws and subsidies only.

What a living 1805 Europe would have that is missing here: (1) the victors falling out once the common enemy is gone (Austria and Prussia over Germany, Russia over the Straits or Sweden), (2) Prussia's bandwagon onto the winning side, (3) the Reich's dissolution or the Confederation formation (blocked by vassalage on this board; none formed), (4) any use of the D5 instruments on an ambient board, (5) a second AI-initiated war type besides Prussia/Hanover.

Caveats. The passive France collapses because it does nothing; this section cannot say how a played France fares, only what Europe does. The digest shows the fogged view; wars between courts out of the player's sight appear only if they have a dispatch row, so some Europe-side beats (such as Russia or Austria acting on their second designs) could happen unseen. The sweep JSON, which is unfogged, shows none of them for the three runs I did, but I did not run the sweep on ulm, marengo or friedland. The per-seed Fall turns are exact because the driver is deterministic. The ledger province counts assume one LEDGER row per turn. All six ledgers matched the digest turn headers.

Repro cautions: the amb sweeps ran while many other processes ran, but the determinism contract means the numbers are the values.

verdicts.question: COOL: did anything dramatic or emergent happen when the courts' AI ran France?
verdicts.evidence: Vienna stormed T5/T6 on 10/10 seeds (docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/<seed>.json france_battle_rows). Steward/friedland T27: 'THE EMPEROR Napoleon has been TAKEN by Russia at Moravia' (last stand), released T32 under a Russia peace. Marengo main: 3 crisis_brewing + 2 crisis_passed. Satellites bribed away (vassal_defected, briber Austria/Switzerland/Russia) T20-T27 in main arm. Coalition (threat 97) present on essentially every seed, dissolved and re-formed on 6. But no capital lost, no volte-face (0/10), no formation except Holland on ulm, no terminal ending on any seed.

verdicts.question: REALISTIC: did AI France behave like a Napoleonic great power?
verdicts.evidence: Realistic: concentrates (MUSTER attacks T2-T5 with corps arriving), takes Vienna T5, protects Bavaria (0/10 seeds lose Bavaria vs 9/10 in the passive ambient arm), never attacks a current satellite (0 of 90 battle rows in either arm), accepts Britain's armistices T11/T18. Absurd: (a) Napoleon himself marches Vienna->Moravia->Podolia->Lithuania->Vilna by T13-T24 on 10/10 seeds and ends T40 in Finland (ulm), Estonia (jena, eylau, wagram), Vilna (austerlitz), Samogitia (lodi), Oldenburg (rivoli) - sovereign plays AGGRESSIVE by design, enemy_ai.py:367; (b) 0 laws and 11-21k gold unspent on 10/10 seeds because reforms.find_ai_enactment returns None for the player nation (reforms.py:1300); (c) no vassal shore-up (enemy_ai.py:7375 reads nation_dp, France has none) so all 3 satellites are lost by T35 on 10/10 seeds in the main arm; (d) permanent wars with Russia (9/10 at T40) - an AI France cannot sue for peace (ai_diplomacy.py:2518-2520); (e) ~25 attacks refused on third-party soil; 13-16 'Not enough actions' refusals on wagram/rivoli.

verdicts.question: UNPREDICTABLE / MULTIPLE OUTCOMES: does the AI-run France give a spread of outcome classes?
verdicts.evidence: Main arm: 0/10 terminal endings, France 35-50 provinces at T40 (mean 44), 83-122k men, threat >=90 for 23-37 of 40 turns; Austria falls on 8/10 (T9-T17), Switzerland revolts and is eliminated on 8/10 (T25-T35). Outcome classes: one (hegemon, Russia/Britain war open) with friedland a weaker variant (35 provinces, Austria alive). Steward arm: same, plus Napoleon captured once (friedland T27). Passive ambient control: campaign_ending on 8/10 seeds (eagle_falls x3, chains x1, soil_or_sword x4) T27-T41. Commanded human script T40 provinces 17/28/26 (historical/austerlitz/marengo, STATUS.md) vs AI France 45/44/42. The spread is narrower than the passive arm and France is far stronger than the commanded arm; variance lives in the periphery (who bribes the satellites, when Austria dies), not in France's fate.

verdicts.question: Is the harness deterministic (control arm)?

sections.notes:
WHAT I BUILT. tools/ai_france_sweep.py (new, untracked). It imports RunCapture, derive_metrics, child_env and the scenario path from tools/ai_v_sweep.py, so the ambient schedule, the per-turn random.seed(10000+turn) placed last before end_turn and PYTHONHASHSEED=0 per subprocess are the sweep's own. Before each end_turn it runs process_nation_turn('France'), execute_admin_phase('France') and then answers incoming diplomacy. The EnemyAI is built once and reused. The executor handed to EnemyAI is wrapped (AnsweringExecutor): after each command it answers objections (trust), strategic objections (trust), capture choices (secure, estate respect), glorious-charge popups (restrain), last-stand interrupts (fight_to_the_last) and hard-stop dialogues (war_purpose first option; force_declare_war only if war_council.can_declare_war says ok, else cancel; paradox honor). I did not call decrement_all_cooldowns because the cooldown maps live on the world and the turn manager's own once-per-turn call already covers France's marshals.

INCOMING DIPLOMACY. I used the courts' own formula, not the documented fallback, for most letters: calculate_acceptance on the dialogue's context.proposal terms with proposer=source court and target=France. 69-85 letters per run were scored that way (outcome ACCEPT accepted, otherwise declined); the 4-12 per run that carried no scorable terms (client petitions, settlement letters, some ultimatums) used the documented fallback (peace/armistice accepted only when France is at war with three or more courts, else decline; ultimatums defied). Special cases: vassal_rebellion_imminent and ally_settlement_petition are answered by option id; client petitions are declined in the main arm and granted in the steward arm. Moment letters and affairs addressed to France (20-27 per run) are NOT answered and lapse; this is a gap, not a policy.

TWO ARMS, AND WHY. The first full sweep (kept as baseline_v1/) lost all three satellites on every seed. Reading why showed the harness had no answer for the vassal rebellion popup and the glorious-charge/last-stand questions; after I wired answers the main arm still loses the satellites (the declined client petitions and accept-risk answers are the driver's defaults), while a steward policy keeps them 3/3 on 9 of 10 seeds. So the satellite web is a function of the answering policy plus AIF-2 (no shore-up rung for France), not a property of the game. Read the two arms together; the main arm is what the passive driver's answer policy would produce, the steward arm is closer to what a competent France would do.

WHAT I COULD NOT DO. (1) France's own overtures: process_diplomatic_phase returns None for the player (AIF-7); I did not build the optional stage 3 (typing a peace verb through the executor) - an AI France therefore never ends a war except by elimination or armistice expiry. (2) Scale: 126 provinces and the full roster were the only board. (3) The commanded-arm comparison: I used the STATUS.md T40 province figures (17/28/26) and could not re-run the commanded arms; the 30/29/27 (Sept 28) were provinces too. (4) The ambient JSON has no France provinces/laws/captures, so the passive comparison uses strength, authority and campaign_ending events (AIF-10). (5) The ambient control's campaign_ending reading is mine from event type 'campaign_ending' (cause field); in my table the jena cause reads soil_or_sword. (6) Battle rows are capped at 200 per run (never reached). (7) I did not verify whether the AIF-5 refusals also occur for courts.

JUDGEMENT IN PLAIN WORDS. The engine's claim that the enemy AI is nation-generic is largely true: it plays a competent opening campaign for France (Vienna T5 on every seed, Bavaria protected, expansion from 28 to about 44 provinces) with no crash and no soft-lock. As a game, AI-run France is NOT cool-and-unpredictable in outcome: one outcome class (hegemon), no Fall, no lost Paris, no volte-face, Austria dies on 8/10 seeds by T17, and Europe's coalition (threat pinned at 97 for 23-37 turns) never bites. The variance is real but peripheral: when Austria falls (T9-T17 or never), who bribes the satellites, whether Napoleon is captured (once, friedland steward T27, then released). It is far from the passive control, where France is destroyed on 8/10 seeds, and far from the commanded script (17/28/26 provinces), which suggests the human-scripted France is the weak party, not the AI. Realism is mixed: the army concentrates but the Emperor wanders to Finland/Estonia on 6/10 seeds, the treasury is hoarded because the law and edict rungs refuse the player nation, and wars never end because France has no diplomatic overtures. To be a real mode an AI France needs: the law/edict rungs (AIF-1), vassal shore-up reading France's real DP (AIF-2), a sovereign-risk/home-front rung (AIF-3), the player-only popups made symmetric (AIF-4), a target filter for third-party soil (AIF-5), AP budgeting by price (AIF-6), France in process_diplomatic_phase with a sue-for-peace rule (AIF-7), answers for moment letters/affairs, and a reason for Europe to hurt a hegemon (AIF-8). None of these is a defect for the human game; AIF-5 is the closest to a plain defect and AIF-9/10 are harness papercuts. Note also that the ambient comparison used tools/ai_v_sweep.py exactly as shipped, which only runs with PYTHONPATH set.

verdicts.question: (a) Does the chest run away over 40-60 turns of peace, and is the Oct 27 ceiling reached?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical: chest 24,363 (T40), 29,987 (T52, last peaceful turn), ceiling 31,920-32,400 from T34 on; net decays +1,601 (T34) to +242 (T52); Charges rise 1,415 to 2,771. It converges on the ceiling asymptotically and does not run away. At T52 it is 93% of ceiling, so the plateau is approached but not strictly reached by T52.

verdicts.question: (b) Does conquest pay or bleed at 35-45 provinces?
verdicts.evidence: No scripted road holds more than 29 provinces. rhfull-historical stays at 28-29, rhfull-austerlitz falls 28 to 21, conq-danube falls to 3, conq-road to 14. The only measurement is a synthetic in-process probe on the T40 save (donor provinces reassigned to France): 36 provinces gives net +2,462, 46 gives +4,020, 55 gives +5,660; occupation stays at 34-43 gold per province. It pays strongly, but the probe is synthetic.

verdicts.question: (c) Do at-war AI courts spend on armies (EA-11) or sit on idle chests?
verdicts.evidence: cmd60 purses: at-war courts spend down (Britain 13,150 at T40 to 5,992 at T60; Austria 10,444 to 4,492; Russia 4-6k). Their armies sit at 1.5x the force limit (Sweden 78,140 against a ceiling of 78,750; Britain 120,690). Only neutral courts hoard (Ottoman 25-26k, Spain 18k, Bavaria 13.6k), as EAD-6 intends. Courts' total is 180,503 at T40 and 155,654 at T60, under the 200k target.

verdicts.question: (d) Does bankruptcy or desertion bite anyone in 60 turns?
verdicts.evidence: bankruptcy_turns is 0 for every court at T40 and T60 on the cmd60 saves, and the digest has 0 mentions of 'bankrupt' or 'desert'. The exception is Austria, whose purse reads -317 (cmd60), -569 (rhfull-historical) and -548 (conq-road) after turn 1, recovering by T2. Russia at T60 has net -695, ceiling 0 and a 6,288 purse, so it is about 9 turns from empty.

verdicts.question: (e) Do armies plateau where the force-limit rule says?
verdicts.evidence: The AI recruit rung's ceiling is severe_band_threshold = 1.5x the limit (enemy_ai.py:7267). Sweden reaches 78,140 against 78,750. The over-limit surcharge is 5% of base upkeep at 1.12x the limit (Sweden T40) and 16% at 1.46-1.49x (Britain T40, Sweden T60). Austria pays 25% at 1.68x.

verdicts.question: (f) Does anyone run out of manpower, and does regen scale with provinces?
verdicts.evidence: Pools are not binding for anyone. At T60 14 of 20 courts sit at the 100,000 infantry cap. The single dip is Britain's infantry pool at 4,233 (T40), refilled to 53,449 by T60. Regen does not scale with land: the probe on the T40 save gives infantry 2,500, cavalry 1,750 and artillery 600 a turn at 27, 36, 46 and 55 provinces alike. The code says 'generous base regen (no territory dependency)' (world_state.py:8223).

verdicts.question: (g) Does the economy give a France with 24-50k gold things to buy, and do laws change the books visibly?
verdicts.evidence: Laws are visible: the law arm's NET line carries 'laws 150', then 'laws 250' on T1-T4. The commanded spender kept the chest at 15,338 and the army at 147,271 by T40, against 24,363 and 76,398 for the passive-spend cmd60 run, so spending is a real lever. At peace (cmd60 T41-60) there is little to buy, and the chest idles near 30k until a war arrives at T53.

verdicts.question: (h) Does per-turn cost grow with the turn number (Golden Rule 8)?
verdicts.evidence: No growth found. A fresh passive France reached game over at T25 (min 154, median 223, max 362 ms). Continuing from the cmd60 saves, T41-60 had median 66 ms (min 50, max 1,283 single outlier) and T61-80 median 89 ms (max 144). tests/test_scale_readiness_phase2.py: 37 passed. Caveat: the machine was loaded and the board was AI-vs-AI only.

sections.notes:
What I did. I ran the brief's four arms plus the Rhine road with the full argv from tools/_vp1_road_arms_final.json, and two more conquest scripts (the Danube and the road conquest). The first two bare '--affair lapse' RH runs ended in game over at about T26 and T35. The record's arms add `--objection insist --diplomacy accept --declare-war proceed --settlement decline --client-petition grant --decline-from Austria`, so I re-ran both seeds with those flags (rhfull-*), and they reproduce RE3-7 (historical completes to T40, austerlitz ends game-over at T40). All nine runs are archived. I read the T40 and T60 saves in-process with WorldState.from_dict and _build_economy for ten courts.

Economy works at scale. The peaceful hoard is bounded, as the Oct 27 rule says: it reaches the ceiling band of about 32k and creeps (T52 chest 29,987, net +242) rather than running away. No treasury, pool or army diverges across 60 turns on any court.

Courts. At-war courts spend (Britain, Austria and Russia end at 4-6k). Neutral courts hoard to their own ceilings, which is the EAD-6 design. Armies plateau at 1.5x the force limit. Bankruptcy and desertion never bite beyond Austria's one-turn negative purse at T1 (ECON-2).

Not measured. The headline question 'does conquest pay at 35-45 provinces' cannot be answered from play. No script gets France past 29 provinces, because the coalition collapses every conqueror (the Danube arm faces 12 courts at T13 and ends at 3 provinces). My synthetic probe says conquest pays steeply (net +840 to +5,660, ceiling 32k to 80k) with a flat crown of 250 and flat infantry regen (ECON-3 and ECON-4). That is a design reading, not a measured campaign. If a human ever holds 45+ provinces the coalition is the only brake, and that is the user's open crown-level question. I also could not run 60 turns of a living France in the in-process loop: a passive France gets game over at T25, so the T41-60 and T61-80 timings come from the saves, on AI-only boards, on a loaded machine. I did not investigate the single 1,283 ms outlier.

Engagement. Early (T1-T25) the economy is tight and decisions are real: the Staff costs 9,000 against 800 in the chest, substitutes cost 2,040-4,140 a battalion, and Austria and France sit at about +300 net. At peace the player's chest idles at 24-30k with little to buy in the script (the script stops issuing orders after loop 40, so T41-60 is not a played France). The marshal 'expects 40g/turn, holds 0g' line (82 UNMET lines in cmd60) comes from the estate policy set to 'respect' in the driver, not an economy defect.

Judgement. A sound economy: bounded, honest bill (off_books 0), AI purses sane, no scale cost growth. Weak points are all about the late game of a large empire: the crown term and infantry regen are flat in land. I would measure a real conqueror before the build by staging a France at 45 provinces with the coalition held down, to see whether it is too easy.

verdicts.question: Does the AI propose sensible things at sensible moments (a losing court sues, a winning court dictates, a neutral asks small)?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-dip-amb-historical: Austria alone took 25 provinces and offered a dictated settlement for 'the War for Paris' asking 4,250-4,500 gold, Corsica ceded and a Duchy of Normandy erected (T17-T34). Britain, Russia and Switzerland sent 'armistice_losing' letters when losing (T15-T34). Neutral minors ask open borders or a non-aggression pact. In rev1106-dip-volte a beaten Austria offered a settlement (T12) and Britain and Russia sent armistice_losing letters that were accepted (T10, T11, T17, T28).

verdicts.question: Are terms proportionate to the war score?
verdicts.evidence: Winning courts ask for status quo, or gold plus a cession once the capital falls (amb T17, T34). I could not audit the tiers beyond that. The driver prints no terms for incoming AI proposals (DIP-3). A winning Austria holding 7 French provinces (propose-historical T12) offers a plain 'Peace Treaty' with no indemnity, and a Paris-fall demand is only Corsica plus 4,250 gold (amb T17). That reads mild but is not provably wrong.

verdicts.question: Does the AI accept France's peace when it should and refuse when it should?
verdicts.evidence: propose-historical, -austerlitz and -marengo: Austria refused every France-originated proposal (T1, T7, T9) while it held French soil, and signed only through its own offer (historical T12 enemy_victory, austerlitz T11, marengo T10). Britain and Russia signed stalemate peaces when they held nothing (historical T8 and T10; austerlitz T10). Refusal cooldowns are honest and escalate: 'Austria refused us; the court will not receive another envoy for 1 more turn' (T4) becomes '2 more turns' (T9, T11).

verdicts.question: Is the AI-to-AI layer alive (peaces among courts, blocs, bandwagon, reneging)?
verdicts.evidence: amb-historical Congress peaces: Britain-Spain T15, Hanover-Prussia T15 (Hanover pays 2,538 gold), Spain-Switzerland T25. propose-marengo T9: Bavaria-Austria peace without France. AI treaties and sponsorships appear (agd T7: Russia-Sweden defensive alliance, Britain sponsors Russia, Sweden and Austria). volte T12: 'THE BROKEN BARGAIN: Austria breaks the bond with Britain'. Allegiance auctions: allegiance_in_play x5 and allegiance_settled x5 in amb. Beats 1, 3 and 7 are present (crisis_brewing x2, coercive_demand x2, crisis_passed x1).

verdicts.question: Is historical plausibility per court met (Austria patient, Prussia bandwagoner who reneges, Russia arbiter, Britain paymaster who never marches)?
verdicts.evidence: Austria is the patient builder: it wins and dictates in amb, and in volte it climbs open borders T27, NAP T30, defensive alliance T33, alliance T36 and then threatens the Ottomans (T39). Britain pays subsidies (paymaster_subsidy x11, 'Britain sponsors X' lines) and lands 5,000 men at Lisbon (agd). Russia is the arbiter ('Arbiter of Europe' ladder lines). Prussia is the weak one: its design is Hanover in every arm, and it is a coalition member in none of the 7 coalition-forming digests (DIP-1).

verdicts.question: SFR-DR1 at HEAD: does the league strike after it declares?
verdicts.evidence: Visible-attack turns after declaration, from the digest enemy-phase lines. cmd-austerlitz: declared T32, attacks on 8 of 8 following turns (6,5,2,5,3,1,1,3). cmd-jena: declared T30, 8 of 9 (T31 not visible). cmd-ulm: declared T32, 6 of 8. law-enacts-ulm: declared T32, 7 of 8. econ-cmd60-historical: declared T53, 6 of 7. agd: declared T8, T9 enemy phase 3 attacks.

verdicts.question: Is every diplomatic act reachable by a UI control rather than typing?
verdicts.evidence: Every diplomatic verb in backend/ai/validation.py VALID_ACTIONS has a UI hit in godot-client scripts. diplomacy_wizard.gd: bind_to_war (1669), ask_return_province (1679), bid_for_allegiance (1682), repudiate_bargain (1692), recognition_sweetener (1697), set_war_purpose (1707), propose_white_peace (1575), grant_region_to_vassal (1463), 'Summon the Congress of Paris' button (626). main.gd keyword list: make vassal, buy off, sponsor. enemy_phase_dialog.gd: grant_dotation and grant_pension. The wizard sends its own 'summon the congress' string internally, as the GE-3 comment at diplomacy_wizard.gd:22-26 records.

verdicts.question: Were the typed verbs the driver uses answered honestly?
verdicts.evidence: 'propose peace with Austria' gave a refusal with the cooldown named (propose-historical T4, T9, T11), and 'We already have Peace with Austria' once signed (T12). 'Talleyrand, improve relations with Austria' at war gave 'we do not court a belligerent' (volte T5-T11) and worked at peace (T12 onward). The same verb at alliance gave 'an ally is reassured, not courted' (volte T36-T40). The settlement road ran end to end in rev1106-dip-agd: demand create_client, an over-limit gold offer clamped honestly ('set to 1,000'), review, then ratified.

sections.notes:
Overall: the enemy AI works for diplomacy and is mostly realistic. I found no P1 and no crash. Every run completed with unknown_blockers empty.

What I could not do or measure:
- Run (6) was not run. tools/playtest_scripts/diplomacy_latewar.json declares "llm": "anthropic". The rules forbid that arm because it spends the user's key. I did not substitute a mock arm of it.
- I could not audit proposal terms (DIP-3), so 'terms proportionate to war score' rests on the few rail lines that name gold and articles.
- DIP-1 is a pattern across 7 arms and 3 aidip arms. I did not read coalition.py's member selection, so I cannot say whether the Prussia absence is gated by alarm weights, by Prussia's statecraft profile or by its design being Hanover.

Judgement:
- The propose arms show a passive-but-peace-seeking France is beaten by a competent Austria. It reaches Limousin and Berry in under 10 turns and takes 7 to 9 provinces. Austria signs only on its own offer. Britain and Russia sign cheap stalemates because they hold nothing. That is a coherent, historically readable shape: Austria is the true enemy, Britain and Russia are far away.
- The ambient passive-France arm ended in the Fall of the Empire at T35 with Austria holding 25 provinces. That is a sensible consequence of play, not a fault.
- One thing I noticed and could not resolve: the agd fixture shows 71 AI-to-AI open-borders and defensive-alliance refusals in two turns after the Third Coalition dissolves. The code has a dedupe window (REFUSAL_DEDUPE_TURNS = 6, ai_diplomacy.py:602) and a rest_refused_pair writer (ai_diplomacy.py:5400+). Ambient and commanded runs show only about 2 per turn, so this looks like fixture state (no refusal record) rather than a live-game spam defect. I did not prove it. I am calling it unmeasured rather than filing it.
- Britain's peace letters arrive 2 to 3 turns apart (amb T29, T31, T34), against about 4 for minors and 7 for Austria. It is the tightest cadence. It could be a winning court legitimately pressing, and it is not a refusal-cooldown breach. Left as an observation.
- Hedging is visible and I judge it realistic: Britain and Russia pay Austria 'against France' (volte T24, T26) just before Austria opens a friendship ladder with France (T27 onward). I would only want to confirm that an alliance with France cancels live sponsorships, and I did not.
- Re-opened rows: none. SFR-DR1 and the Sept 1 'Austria signs while holding provinces' audit are the two I explicitly re-checked.

verdicts.question: Does the tech layer (laws, Staff, edicts, doctrines) work end to end on both boards without crashes or silent failures?
verdicts.evidence: Five Mode A runs completed (law-enacts-historical/ulm 40 turns, law-amb-austerlitz 40, law-staff-historical 10; law-amb-historical ended at T35 with France's fall in the ambient arm). Zero lapses on any court. 21 pins in test_rf3_the_ai_enacts.py pass. Every effect type in REFORMS_SPEC section 4 has a live engine reader.

verdicts.evidence: Deck order and purse test behave as written (T3 met: Britain T1, Russia T2, Austria and Prussia T5). But the Staff never lands on Prussia (4 of 4 boards), lands on Austria on 1 of 4 boards (T30) and Russia on 1 of 4 (T39). Saving-for-the-Staff only starts at 50% of the price, the purse bar is really 12,500-13,000, and the edict rung ignores saving (LAW-1, LAW-2). The rung has no demand test for drill and levy laws (LAW-3).

verdicts.evidence: enacts-historical: Britain cured T26, Russia T39, Austria and Prussia never. amb-historical: Austria T30 only, ended T35. enacts-ulm: Britain T34 only. amb-austerlitz: none. At T30 on historical, 0 boards show two of four cured. Prussia was never cured on any of the four boards.

verdicts.question: Is the player's side legible and worth the gold?
verdicts.evidence: Quotes name price, upkeep and the effect (law-enacts-ulm T15 Staff popup; 'laws 550' on the NET line), and the repeal refund text is honest. The Staff pays: France's Staff on ulm T15, effect starts the next refill. On historical France's chest first passes 9,000 at T25 (T14 on ulm), so the T10-15 target holds on 1 of 2 seeds. The status report prints no Laws line (it only lives on the Diplomatic Ledger card), so a Mode A player reads laws only on the NET row. The live lapse forecast could not be exercised: the forecast is None even at 0 gold because France's Net is positive.

verdicts.question: Does the tech layer matter to outcomes (courts with vs without the Staff)?
verdicts.evidence: The AI's fifth action is used when the court is at war: enemy orders per phase with 5 vs 4 actions was Britain 5.50 vs 4.44 (amb-historical), 4.29 vs 3.75 (amb-austerlitz), 3.13 vs 3.24 (enacts-ulm, flat), and Britain issued 0 orders in 14 phases of truce (enacts-historical). That is one to a few runs per figure, confounded by time and war state. No outcome-level comparison (provinces, army) is separable from the courts' wars.

verdicts.question: Are there dead laws (an effect type with no engine reader)?
verdicts.evidence: Grep of each reader: manpower_regen -> world_state.py:8254; recruit_price -> economy_executor.py:1540; recruit_morale -> economy_executor.py:1901; drill_morale -> world_state.py:6391/6400; supply_capacity -> world_state.py:8932; satellite_loyalty -> vassal.py:1087/1218; cs_closure and blockade_denial -> naval.py:1528/1214; force_limit -> world_state.py:610; actions -> world_state.py:12464 and the AI refill; cures -> doctrines.py:122. Near-dead in practice for the AI only: drill_morale (LAW-3).

verdicts.question: Is the layer deep enough to feel like a tech tree?
verdicts.evidence: Each court has 5-6 linear laws, all enacted in authored order, with no choices or prerequisites. France's slate is saturated by T30 (chest 22,750 at T40 on historical, 13,683 on ulm after the Staff). Rivals end with the same set in the same order on every seed. It reads as a checklist with upkeep, not a tree (see notes for the one recommended addition).

verdicts.question: Do the courts' authority edicts or laws drive any court's authority to its floor?
verdicts.evidence: Prussia ends at authority 31 (floor 30) on all four boards (enacts-historical, enacts-ulm, amb-austerlitz T40 saves); Austria 33-45, Russia 36-45, Britain 37-54. Prussia has no authority-priced act left after the Emancipation Edict, so the floor binds nothing it would otherwise have bought.

sections.notes:
What I did. I ran the five brief arms in Mode A and read the T40 saves in-process, read-only, through reforms.py, doctrines.py and affairs.py. I also cross-checked the AI's actual orders in each run's server_console.log. The ambient historical arm ended early (T35) because the passive France falls, so it has no T40 save and I used its digest rows. The rf3 script stops asking for the Staff at T20. That is why historical's commanded France never shows the Staff.

The main story is that the tech layer is wired and stable but unbalanced for the AI. Britain reliably gets its Staff (T17-T33). Austria, Russia and above all Prussia mostly do not. I could not find an exhaustive cause, only three contributors that point the same way:
- The saving rule starts late. It begins at 50% of the Staff price, after cheap laws are already in.
- The real purse bar is 12,500-13,000, not the spec's 11,500, because every cheap law bought first adds 500.
- The edict rung (RE-6, now armed) spends 25,000-29,000 gold per board and ignores the saving rule (LAW-1).

The Staff 'never' for Prussia is therefore a bar set too high, plus a leak, and not a deliberate design. The T8 dates in ENEMY_AI row 1.78 are stale. Three later changes (the economy rebalance, the edicts' arming, the authority flip) probably moved them. I did not isolate which one by flipping seams.

What I could not measure.
- A live lapse and forecast. The forecast returns None even with France's chest set to 0, because France's Net is positive. Staged insolvency is covered by tests T4/T7, which I did not re-run.
- A clean 'with vs without the Staff' outcome comparison. The courts' wars confound it. The only usable signal is orders per phase: the fifth action is used at war (Britain 5.50 vs 4.44, 4.29 vs 3.75), flat on one board, and zero at truce. Each figure comes from a single run, so read it as direction only.
- The edicts' effect on outcomes. The courts decree 12-19 edicts per board. I did not run an edicts-down arm.
- The Godot surfaces (the LAWS tab). I stayed in Mode A.

Judgement. The AI's buying is mostly rote: deck order, a purse test and a late saving rule. It never asks whether the court will use the effect (LAW-3). On the player side the quote and effect are legible, and the one-off Staff price is fair on ulm (T15) but lands near T25 on historical. The layer is not deep enough to read as a tech tree. Each court has 5-6 linear laws that every court eventually buys in the same order. France's slate is exhausted by about T30, with 13,683-22,750 gold idle at T40.

Recommendation, not built. Turn each deck into a two-branch tree with one mutually exclusive choice and a prerequisite. An example is a levee branch (Anticipated Class, Extraordinary Levy) against a professional branch (Regulations, Train des Equipages, then a second-tier Staff). A court would then enact by character and need, and the AI would read its own demand, such as whether it drills or levies. This also gives REFORMS_SPEC section 13's second Staff tier a place to land, and it would stop the Staff's bar from rising with every cheap law. Per CLAUDE.md Rule 9, any such addition needs an owner row and a landing slice before it is promised to the player.

verdicts.question: Is the naval layer alive and legible (do fleets fight, does a blockade bite the trade line)?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-sea-descent T5: the Grand Diversion failed and TRAFALGAR fired, with a named dispatch (22 French, 16 Spanish and 6 Dutch sail lost, no zero-casualty action). Every ledger row from T1 on carries 'blockade 219 · admiralty 90' as named components (trade 350, blockade 219). Fleet actions fire only on the player's own gambles, as NAVAL_SPEC §4.4 says. No ambient AI-vs-AI fleet action appeared in any of the 40-turn runs.

verdicts.question: Does Britain land on the continent, and does it matter?
verdicts.evidence: expedition_landed rail lines. Paget at Lisbon on T3 on every arm (descent, shutout-historical, shutout-austerlitz, strangle, contingent, fall, verdict). Later landings: Shrapnel at Piedmont T9-10, Wellesley at Artois T19 (end-fall) and Andalusia T13 (strangle), Shrapnel at Corsica T26 (strangle). Moore with 48,339 men took Gascony on T13 in sea-descent. In rev1106-end-verdict Paget captures Napoleon on T39 and Britain takes Paris.

verdicts.question: Can France ever cross to Britain or Ireland, or is the Descent window structurally dead?
verdicts.evidence: Not dead. A boot-state probe gives France 53.8 effective against Britain's 100 at Normandy to London (ratio 0.54, shut), and 1.08 with a window open, which clears the 0.9 floor. The diversion roll (naval::diversion::<turn>::France) wins on T2 historical, T2 austerlitz and T1 eylau at 45%. The only played throw (sea-descent T5) came at readiness 50, so 25% odds, and it failed. Ireland is reachable: Oudinot landed at Munster on T6 (quoted 64%) and took Ulster on T10. A France that is not rushing the window in the first turns sees it close, because the blockade rots readiness. Nothing played here crossed to England.

verdicts.question: Does the A5 anchor (Spain can never again walk to London) hold?
verdicts.evidence: Boot probe: crossing_check(Spain, Normandy to London) is verdict 'shut', ratio 0.45. tests/test_naval_channel_gate.py, test_naval_descent.py and test_naval_free_ireland.py pass, 69 of 69. In sea-descent T6 and T8 'Ney, march to London' is refused honestly: 'barred - the Royal Navy commands the water with 97 sail (97 effective) against our 18'.

verdicts.question: Do satellites matter (loyalty moves for readable reasons, rebellion reachable, contingent fights, Confederation forms)?
verdicts.evidence: Loyalty moves are logged per vassal per turn (the 'loyalty' records). The drift is -2/turn for a Satellite, from vassal.py process_vassal_loyalty. A refused petition prints 'loyalty -10 (78 to 68); bond 0 to -20'. Rebellion is reachable: sea-descent T11 shows 'defection cascade ... Switzerland has rebelled', Alliance cascade, and the courting rail, with Switzerland at 47 and the roll rule written at vassal.py:1999. Contingents: rev1106-vas-contingent raises Dumonceau 6,500 and Teulie 7,500 on T1, Teulie fights and is captured, Dumonceau 'comes home 6,500 of 6,500'. The Confederation is proclaimable on T9 (rev1106-econ-rh-*, another reviewer's runs).

verdicts.question: Does the game END with a readable verdict on each road within 40-46 turns, and is the text worthy?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-end-fall: Fall of the Empire on T35 (historical, passive France), with THE EXILE, the record, a successor-peace line and a Castlereagh quip. rev1106-end-verdict: Verdict stamped T44 (austerlitz), marked and the campaign continues. rev1106-end-pressburg: THE IMPERIAL PEACE on T36 from the fixture. Staged fixtures: end-chains deposed T10, end-soil T5, with Olmutz/Metternich and Elba/Talleyrand lines. Each ending stamped exactly once (grep count of 'ENDING -' is 1 per digest). The Humbled Peace could not be played: there is no arm for it and no archived digest.

verdicts.question: Is Britain's sue-path (A2 / C4: 'Britain sues by turn 10 on the shut-out arm') intact?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-sea-shutout-historical and -austerlitz (12 turns): zero Britain armistice or settlement envoys, while the SR-5b record (NAVAL_SPEC §19) and SF_NAV1 memo say turn 8 on 6/6 and 3/3 arms. rev1106-sea-we saves: Britain's war exhaustion is 70 at T7 and 92 at T9, yet no offer. rev1106-sea-strangle first Britain offer is T11 (settlement) and T14 (armistice_losing). Cause not isolated (see NAVVAS-1).

Vassals are legible: per-turn loyalty records, refusal costs quoted in the popup, defection and courting rails, contingents raised and stood down with their arithmetic ('6,500 of 6,500'), and a rebellion path reachable at loyalty below 50.

sections.notes:
This section is in good shape. Three findings: one P2 and two P3. I found no P1.

**What I ran.** The nine briefed arms ran as written. I added two staged ending fixtures: end-chains and end-soil. I also ran a boot-state probe of crossing_check and a diversion-roll table, both scratchpad scripts outside the repo. I ran three naval pytest files; all 69 tests pass. One extra run, rev1106-sea-we, wrote saves so I could read Britain's war exhaustion; it is not archived.

**The sea.**
- The naval layer is legible and consistent between quote and result.
- The Descent is reachable but a gamble. At boot France reaches 1.08 against the 0.9 window floor, and the diversion wins on early turns on several seeds at 45%.
- The played arm threw once, at T5 on historical, at readiness 50 and 25%, and lost to Trafalgar. That was luck, not a structural problem.
- Nothing played here crossed to England. I could not measure a successful window crossing because no played throw won.
- Ireland works: Oudinot landed at Munster on T6 and took Ulster on T10.
- Fleets only fight on the player's gambles. The ambient seas are silent in every 40-turn run. That is spec-conformant (§4.4), but it means a France run by the AI has no naval action. That belongs to the AI-France reviewer.
- I did not measure a failed expedition (no slip failure fell on any played turn).
- I did not measure Britain's own books: the digest shows only France's ledger.

**Britain's sue-path.** NAVVAS-1 is the one result that surprised me. The A2 anchor said Britain asks for an armistice around T8 on every seed. It does not in 12 turns on the shut-out arm, even at war exhaustion 92. The first British offer on the strangle arm is T11. I could not isolate the cause. I read ai_diplomacy's P1 gates and the has_fought contact gate as the likely paths, but this is a hypothesis.

**Satellites.** They matter. Loyalty falls steadily when France is losing (Switzerland 98 to 47 in 10 turns). A petition refusal is quoted and priced. The defection roll fired once at 47 and the player sees it as 'the empire trembles'. Contingents work, though Italy's 'its 0 men disband' is an awkward line. The Confederation is proclaimable on T9. I saw no vassal at high loyalty rebel.

**Endings.** Every road ends with a readable verdict. I traced why the austerlitz Verdict run stamps 'unfinished' at T44 while France holds one province and no army with the Emperor captive: it is the Fall's 5-turn clock and 10-turn captivity clock not having run yet. That is the D7 mark-and-continue rule, not a bug. The Humbled Peace could not be played: there is no arm and no archived digest.

**Non-findings I checked.**
- Constant 'blockade 219 / admiralty 90' on France's ledger is consistent. Blockade is 62.5% of trade on every pair, and admiralty drops 90 to 46 after Trafalgar.
- 'Treasury hoard' is known (EAD-6, FA-S17-D2).
- 'Paget lands in neutral Portugal' is documented (NAVAL_SPEC §19).
- '55 of 45 titled' was closed as UXR3-F11.

My judgement is that this section is ready to ship apart from NAVVAS-1. That row needs a decision on whether the T8 sue-path is still a contract. If it is, the cause needs isolating before the deploy.

"march to Tyrol..." waits behind it' (dropped_sequel in the trace). sections.notes:
Method. I ran the golden corpus, then the seven driver arms in parallel (all archived), read every CMD line of op, fld, typed, feel and hold, and ran the blind sixth/seventh sets through tools/unrehearsed_census.py with --trace because the driver ignores their `orders` key (the two driver runs are empty turns, CMDFEEL-13). I then wrote five small in-process probes on a fresh boot to confirm each suspected defect. The probe scripts are in the session scratchpad and are not committed. I edited nothing under backend, tests or docs.

Judgement. The command road works. Zero parser misreads in 365 typed lines across the five played arms, and a 92% read-right rate on 600 blind orders. Every refusal I read was honest and spent nothing. The defects I found are narrow shapes in compound or reason-clause sentences. They are the kind a blind set finds and the golden corpus cannot, because the corpus holds lines someone already wrote.

Silent drops. The relay rule holds on the common compounds. Two silent drops remain. The first is CMDFEEL-1: 'march to X and attack Y' stores an arrival attack the reply never mentions, and it skips the already-there check, which costs 2 AP for a null march. The second is CMDFEEL-2: a location clause on a stance order vanishes, while the sibling 'defend Lorraine' refuses properly. Per Golden Rule 10, each should be fixed together with its class: arrival tails, 'in X' / 'at X' clauses on stance orders, and the other sentence shapes that carry a place.

Marshal drama. The beats that exist are good: capture, last stand, the glory clock, rivalry petitions that settle into a cold war. What is thin is the middle layer.
- Audiences resolve with one constant line and no stated consequence.
- Four aggressive marshals share one objection string.
- Under the insist policy no defiance, compromise, 'By my word' or vindication fired in any arm, so I cannot judge that layer.
- Mode A digests print no trust or relationship row (CMDFEEL-14), so 'trust that moves and matters' could only be seen once, through a typed question.
- The one objection defect (CMDFEEL-3) offers 'Trust him and he will attack Kutuzov at Carniola' when the same board forbids that attack under the peace with Austria. That is a promise the executor will not keep.

What I could not measure.
- The keyed (live-model) arm, by rule. All parse results are mock-mode.
- Defiance and compromise outcomes, since none occurred under the three objection policies I ran (insist, insist, trust).
- Whether a negative recruit quantity ever reaches the pool, because every probe was refused earlier for reach.
- The dispatch advice 'A supply depot at Bohemia would ease it' against the build refusal 'region stability too low (35/100)' at op T4. I saw both texts but not Bohemia's stability at T7 and T9, so I did not file a contradiction.
- Whether the 'Berthier, propose peace to Austria' route through the chief of staff is a ruled routing decision (CX-R1 addressee rule). I did not file it.

The one change that would most improve the feel. Make an acknowledged audience, and every objection, say what it moved: 'Murat's grievance is noted; his patience holds N turns' or 'Ney's trust 62 -> 58'. Give each personality at least two objection lines per trigger. The machinery, the glory clock and the UNMET line already exist, and the player hears none of it from the marshal himself. Second to that, fix CMDFEEL-3, because an objection that promises an illegal order breaks trust in all of them.

verdicts.question: Q1: Does the per-turn economy derive by hand and does the Charges ceiling still bind at 28/45/60 provinces?
verdicts.evidence: Derived and verified against the real functions on a fresh europe_1805 world, peace, no disruption. 28 provinces: income 2590, upkeep 2630, net -40. 45 provinces: income 5440, occupation 707, upkeep 2458, net +2275. 60 provinces: income 7840, occupation 1303, upkeep 2394, net +4143. At peace the Charges rate is the crown term alone (250), so the chest settles at 2000 + S*2500/250 = 2000 + 10*S, which is 24,750 at 45 and 43,430 at 60. The Charges are a proportional brake, not a fixed ceiling, so income never outruns them. But the 60-province level is above the 40k France target recorded in S14j. This uses an arbitrary set of provinces (homeland plus the first names alphabetically).

verdicts.question: Q2: Is every write to nation_gold outside the income phase either a ledger line or a recorded one-shot (EA-1 class)?
verdicts.evidence: I wrapped nation_gold in a recording dict for 22 end turns on the historical default seed, with the unseeded RNG. For all 18 active nations and every turn that advanced, chest delta equals _build_economy(applied).net plus the recorded one-shots. The unexplained residual is zero. The only non-zero rows are three non-advancing posts on turn 23, where the end turn was blocked by a pending capture choice. That is a probe artifact: the delta was 0 against a non-zero ledger net. Off-income-phase writers seen: commission_marshal, _execute_build, _execute_recruit, the Butcher's Bill, moments._apply_gold, the AI admin bonus, naval build, repair, enact_law, plunder and vassal bribe/invest. Each is in Spent, the materiel tally, or is a documented one-shot.

verdicts.question: Q3: Does any float reach the client in the economy payloads (Golden Rule 2)?
verdicts.evidence: I walked the JSON of GET /ledger, /status, /dispatch, /map_topology, /diplomatic_ledger and /marshal_overview, plus the commands economy, treasury report, status, recruit, help economy and ledger. I did this at turn 1 and after 8 end turns. Result: 0 float paths. Static check: Region.get_effective_income returns int(...). calculate_turn_income and _build_economy sums are ints.

verdicts.question: Q4: Golden Rule 8 - every region iteration in per-turn or per-command economy code behind a per-turn cache?
verdicts.evidence: Cached correctly: get_nation_regions (_nation_regions_cache, per turn, cleared by invalidate_active_nations_cache) and get_active_nations. Not cached: _build_economy scans world.regions.values() twice per call (ledger.py:1351 and :1364). It was called 17 times on a typical turn (4 player + about 13 AI) and 22 on turn 7, measured on the historical seed over 30 turns. Per-turn single passes that are acceptable: process_stability_growth, process_war_damage_recovery, process_supply_attrition, process_construction_timers, and the capital garrison regen in _advance_turn_internal. End-turn wall time stayed at 0.31-0.40 s (TestClient, mock LLM).

verdicts.question: Q5: Manpower - can a pool go negative, does regen scale, is a conquered province's pool counted twice or never?
verdicts.evidence: No negative pools in 4 seeds x 31-41 turns, and the debit sites are gated (economy_executor.py:1934 after a pool check; recruitment.py:253-257). Infantry regen is flat INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN=2500 per nation, so it does not scale with provinces. This is ruled (EC-2 July-9 gate, SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:3110). Remnant courts bank the cap: Hanover with 2 provinces and 100 income reached infantry 97,572 and cavalry 30,000 by T41 on jena. A conquered province adds no pool, and an eliminated court's pool and chest are frozen and orphaned. Treaty manpower transfers bypass the cap and the next regen silently truncates them (ECON-3).

verdicts.question: Q6: Bankruptcy mercy (EA-8) and desertion state machine on alternating-sign chests
verdicts.evidence: I drove the real _update_bankruptcy and deserts_now with scripted chests. A deficit every 2nd turn gives arrears 2,1,3,2,4,3,5, and desertion fires on the 4th deficit as documented. A deficit every 3rd turn gives arrears 2,1,0 repeating: 6 deficits, 0 desertion turns. Three in a row desert at the third. A live run showed the loophole: Hanover bankrupt on turns 29, 31, 34, 37, 40 on jena. Its strength went 22,745 to 22,689 (no desertion), over 20,000 limit. Filed as ECON-4.

verdicts.question: Q7: Can a court starve its army to buy a law or ship (AI purse read and reserve bars)?
verdicts.evidence: The laws, edicts, arms, commission and fleet rungs keep reserves (AI_PURSE_RESERVE 1000 + 5 turns of upkeep plus a Net test; COURT_ARMS_RESERVE 1000 + 5 turns; commission buffer 1000; fleet 4x400). So no law or ship purchase starves the army by construction. The cheap rungs do not: P1/P7 recruit (enemy_ai.py:6967, :7217 'treasury >= recruit_cost'), market 350, depot 300, fortification 400, repair 150 test the chest only, with no upkeep or Net test. Min chests observed over 31-41 turn passive runs: Hanover 10-60, Bavaria 18, Naples 331. One court (Hanover) cycled through bankruptcy. No court was negative on 3 of 4 seeds at T40. Filed as ECON-5.

verdicts.question: Q8: Continental System closure at scale and the satellites' exemption (EA-4)
verdicts.evidence: With Britain allied to 9 courts (Britain trade income 700), continental_system_losses is capped at 200 for Britain however many courts are members. Members 4, 6 and 9 all give Britain -200. Vassals trade nothing (trade breakdown skips vassals), so satellites are exempt as intended. Which members pay depends on stored join order: order A (Prussia, Spain, Russia, Austria, Denmark) charges Prussia, Spain, Russia and Austria 50 each. Order B (reversed) charges Denmark 75, Austria 75 and Russia 50. This is documented ('in the stored order') and applied equals quoted, so it is not filed as a defect.

working_well: Ledger reconciliation is exact. For 18 nations over 22 advancing turns (historical seed) the chest delta equals the applied _build_economy net plus the recorded one-shots, with zero unexplained residual, for AI courts as well as the player. Every off-income-phase gold writer (about 20 sites listed by grep) is either a Spent entry, a materiel tally, or an applied-transfer record.
Golden Rule 2 holds: 0 floats in the six economy-related GET payloads and six economy commands, at turn 1 and turn 9.
Manpower pools never went negative in four seeds x 31-41 turns. The recruit debit (economy_executor.py:1934) and the commission debit (recruitment.py:290) are both behind a pool check.

The Charges of Empire are a well-behaved brake. int((chest-2000)*rate//2500) is zero at or below the floor, cannot push a chest negative, and the ledger projection prices the war-exhaustion term at the value the advance will write (SR-5a). The Charges equilibrium 2000 + 2500*S/rate is a clean, derivable fixed point.

Upkeep falls as the force limit rises (France 2,630 at 28 provinces, 2,394 at 60), so conquest is not punished by the over-limit surcharge. The surcharge is exactly the marginal-band arithmetic documented (59 units x 4 + 49 x 18 = 1,118, reproduced by hand).

Scale: whole-turn wall time with 20 courts was 0.31-0.40 s while the economy helpers ran 150-250 calls to calculate_turn_upkeep and 193-250 to get_disrupted_regions. The marshal-list loops (get_nation_dotation_map, get_nation_rente_bill, get_disrupted_regions) are correctly not region scans.

EA-8's fix works for deficits every other turn: arrears build and desertion fires on the 4th deficit. The mercy halving of upkeep, occupation and infrastructure is consistently applied, and the applied upkeep_data rides on the income result so the flip-turn ledger reads what was charged.

Continental System: the closure loss planner is the one source for the debit and the ledger quote, vassals are exempt because trade breakdown skips vassal pairs, Britain's loss is hard-capped at 200, and the debit is floored at the payer's positive balance so it cannot erase a debt.
AI admin spending reserves: the laws rung, edicts, arms rung, commission and fleet rungs all keep a reserve and a Net test. No law or ship purchase can starve an army by construction.
sections.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. This was a code review with read-only in-process probes. I did not use the playtest driver, so I archived no digests and cite none. Probes live in the shared scratchpad C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/1bd395101ae53e89/c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40/scratchpad/ as probe1.py, probe3.py, probe5.py, econ_sm.py, econ_cs.py, econ_pool.py, econ_unrest.py, econ_count.py, econ_bav.py and scan.py. Other reviewers share that directory and overwrote the contents of probe3.py, probe4.py and probe5.py after my runs. The versions I ran are quoted in the tables, but those three filenames no longer reproduce my results. The econ_* files are mine alone and reproduce.

DISCLOSURE: A BLOCKED COMMAND AND A POSSIBLY OVERWRITTEN AUTOSAVE. My first end-turn probe (15 turns through backend.main and TestClient) ran before I set INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR. The /command end-turn path autosaves, and the default save directory is the repo's ./saves. The file ./saves/autosave.json is gitignored and its mtime is 2026-11-06 16:51:09, which matches my run, though other parallel reviewers may have written it too. If you care about the player's own autosave, treat it as possibly clobbered. The permission system blocked my next heredoc-written probe, and every probe after that set INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR to a scratchpad folder (the final ./saves/autosave.json mtime stayed 16:51:09). I did not start the backend, touch port 8005, use --http, or use --llm anthropic.

IN-PROCESS RUNS ARE NOT DETERMINISTIC. My harness does not pin PYTHONHASHSEED or seed `random` (except where I added random.seed(7) to econ_bav.py). Two runs of the same seed with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 gave different Bavaria rows (md5 differed). The AI-economy numbers in Tables 4 and 5 are therefore run instances, not 'the value' as the Mode A driver's digests would be. I give them as evidence of existence (Hanover's alternation, min chests), not of frequency. The deterministic claims are Tables 1, 3, 6, 7, 8 and the pool probe: fresh-world functions, or code reads. I have not re-run the Hanover alternation under the driver.

WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE. I did not measure the hand-derived net with active wars, because the Charges' war terms, disruption and campaign pay need a live campaign. Table 1 is the peace case only, with province quality arbitrary. I did not read the standing.py courts' authority writes or recruitment.py commission prices past confirming the gates and that every gold write is a one-shot; the AU rows are closed ledgers I did not re-audit. I did not exercise naval blockade or trade-dominance numbers beyond the closure formula. I did not time the full economy at 126 provinces under conquest-scale load.

JUDGEMENT. The economy code is in a good state. The money map reconciles to the gold in every chest each turn, and I found no silent flow, no float leak and no negative pool. The Charges and the surcharge reproduce by hand from the code. The only Golden Rule breach I found is the double region scan in _build_economy (ECON-1), and its measured cost is small. The other five items are residues and design questions, not breaks. The one I would pick up first is ECON-4 and ECON-5 together: they show a small court can sit on the edge of bankruptcy for a long time without consequence, because the AI's cheap rungs spend the chest to near zero and the arrears rule forgets a deficit that comes every third turn. ECON-2 is a calibration question for the user: at 60 provinces at peace the Charges settle France's chest near 43k against a stated 40k target, and the restless term does not scale with the number of restless provinces. A reading for the user, not taken: ECON-6 restates a recorded ruling (flat regen), and I report it only because the user asked whether regen scales.

verdicts.question: Q1 logical defects in the decision tree (dead rungs, undecayed cooldowns, fortify/form farces, stagnation reset, stale ratio, spoils deadlock, bad retreat, index before refresh)
verdicts.evidence: Read and probed: cooldowns all decay (_decrement_cooldowns 1257; refortify 1249-1254; ai_attack_futility -1/turn at world_state.py:13225); spoils deferral cannot deadlock (strictly-greater test, enemy_ai.py:4300-4340); retreat tier 1 is own/ally/vassal soil and tier 2 calls _can_ai_move_to (6120-6195); index refresh is safe (get_hostile_*_indexed filters strength>0 so can_crush_adjacent_enemy cannot divide by zero). Real gaps found: the pair/futility brakes are not read by P3.9 and P4.25 (AIMIL-1, AIMIL-2) and P4 prices co-located allies at 100 percent (AIMIL-3). Stagnation counters never reset for peacetime fortified minors (6 minors at 40 on austerlitz) but that is the documented SR-7a hold-the-works rule. Not read in full: _consider_consolidation, _consider_fortify, _consider_drill, _consider_strategic_move, _get_default_action (the file is 8,674 lines).

verdicts.question: Q2 does one court's corps ever attack together, or always one at a time
verdicts.evidence: Branch that decides: P4 _find_attack_opportunity (enemy_ai.py:3612-3660, 3745) takes ONE marshal and inflates his ratio with co-located allies (combined strength + 0.08 per ally); the order itself is a single-marshal attack ('the actual attack is still single marshal', 3503-3506). Concentration happens only through (a) the executor's reinforcement roll for ADJACENT corps (combat_executor.py:4343, eligibility 2055-2155) and (b) sequential attacks by successive marshals on the same target. P4.6 (8076-8205) only STAGES a move to co-locate and never attacks. Measured on 4 seeds x 40 turns (passive France): of ~92 AI target-turns, 2-6 per seed had two different marshals of one court on the same target in a phase (4/6/2/3); 26 of 68 reinforcement candidates arrived (38 percent), 14 refused as literal (Grouchy rule), 19 low_score.

verdicts.question: Q3 France-literal census (5 files + per-function for coalition and ai_diplomacy)
verdicts.evidence: Every site classified in the measurements tables. Result: no site is a defect on the shipped board (France IS player_nation). 0 of 4 enemy_ai reads are HEGEMON-only: 1 symmetric, 1 would-break (player fog, line 1082), 1 hegemon fallback. Concrete WOULD-BREAK-AN-AI-FRANCE seams: enemy_nations excludes France so the enemy loop never runs her (turn_manager.py:1395-1416 via world_state.py:2206); nation_actions has no France key (probe: 'France' in nation_actions False) so enemy_ai.py:1431 would fall to the default 4 and Staff actions would not apply (world_state.py:13065); ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase returns None for the player (2518-2520); war_council never opens a crisis for or against the player (1252, 1261); intent.get_nation_intent returns indifferent for the player's own plans (intent.py:241); _get_enemy_contacts gives France the player's RegionIntel fog (enemy_ai.py:1082-1083).

verdicts.question: Q4 admin whitelist: any structured key an executor needs that execute_admin_phase drops
verdicts.evidence: Opened every rung: find_ai_commission {marshal,action,target,_acting_nation}; find_ai_enactment {action,target}; ai_repeal_before_lapse {action,target}; find_ai_edict {action,target[,currency]}; find_ai_build_fleet {marshal,action,target,_acting_nation}; find_ai_naval_yard {marshal,action,target,building_type,_acting_nation}; find_ai_expedition {marshal,action,target,region,confirmed,_acting_nation}; find_ai_diversion {marshal,action,target,_acting_nation}; _find_vassal_shore_up {action,target[,region|new_level]}; _find_dotation_grant {action,marshal[,target]}; _find_substitute_purchase {action,marshal,target,batches}; recruit/build/repair rungs {action,marshal,target,building_type}. The whitelist at enemy_ai.py:6754-6760 (region,new_level,confirmed,batches,currency) covers every non-base key; _acting_nation is set explicitly (6735). The executors read command['region'] (vassal_executor.py:299, naval_executor.py:913), 'new_level' (vassal_executor.py:121), 'confirmed' (naval_executor.py:656), 'currency' (reforms_executor.py:206). No missing key found. The structural weakness (a new key is silently dropped) remains a convention, not a test of the whitelist against rung outputs.

verdicts.question: Q5 every except Exception in enemy_ai.py and turn_manager.py: reports or swallows
verdicts.evidence: 8 handlers, all call backend.errors.report (enemy_ai.py:1235, 3544, 7260; turn_manager.py:1199, 1333, 1344, 1354, 1432). No bare except, no suppress/swallow wrapper. The two turn-level guards also surface an 'error' row (_error_row, turn_manager.py:1316-1322). Degrade-silently-after-first-report: _muster_price returns 0 (AIMIL-6).

verdicts.question: Q6 fog: does any rung read the PLAYER's fog for a court, or omniscient data the spec forbids
verdicts.evidence: _should_use_fog_aware_enemy_query always returns bool(nation) (enemy_ai.py:1046-1047) so the omniscient get_enemies_of_nation branch (1087) is dead; the only get_visible_enemies read is gated on nation == player_nation (1082-1083); every court read is get_live_visible_enemies / _in_region (2123, 2168, 2223, 3709, 4544, 5403...). Omniscient reads are deliberate and documented: drill_reach_threat (enemy_ai.py:653-678, 'Omniscient by design'), _muster_price (3556), the hostile-occupancy index on adjacent provinces (adjacency is inside live sight, world_state.py:4857-4861). No court reads the player's fog.

sections.notes:
What I did: I read the code for the enemy military mind, the war council, the admin whitelist and the France-literal sites, then wrote in-process probes (scratchpad, no driver digests, nothing archived) that boot the real 1805 scenario in mock mode and run 40 turns per seed with France passive. I did not start the backend, run the full suite, edit anything, or use the driver. Every runtime figure is a per-seed deterministic value from those probes and is cited with its seed and turn.

Honest limits: (1) France is passive in my probes, so the AI wars are the ones Europe declares on an unresisting France; fight counts and the Fall arrive earlier than in a played game (historical ends at turn 32). (2) I did not read all of the 8,674-line enemy_ai.py: the consolidation, fortify, drill, strategic-move and default-action rungs (about 5000-5800) and _find_homeland_defense / _find_ally_support_opportunity in depth were only sampled. (3) AIMIL-4 and AIMIL-5 are code readings with no measured consequence. (4) The 38 percent reinforcement arrival rate in AIMIL-3 counts every adjacent friendly of the battle province, which is a superset of the co-located allies the AI sums; treat it as an upper-bound illustration, not the AI's exact overcount. (5) tools/ai_france_sweep.py exists from another reviewer; I did not run it, I only cite its docstring.

Judgement in plain words: the enemy military mind is in good order. The mechanics the user would feel (fog, defender muster pricing, crossing gates, retreat, admin purse) are consistent and the error handling reports rather than swallows. What I found are two sibling rungs that escaped the repetition brake which FA-N72 put on P0 and P4, and one pricing mismatch. P3.9 (the jealous glory hunt) and P4.25 (garrison assault) let one corps hit the same target two or three times in a single enemy phase: Cuesta twice on Wellesley on turns 10 and 11 of ulm and lodi, Mack three times on Paris on turn 25 of ulm, Moore three times on Paris on turn 16 of marengo. In the ulm run the glory hunt drove Cuesta's futility counter to 3 and he kept attacking, so the count-to-three brake is not honoured by those rungs. Under CLAUDE.md rule 10 (sibling sweep) these are findings for the next slice, not a regression of a closed row, since each rung was never braked. Separately, P4 and P0 treat a co-located friend as a certain 100 percent plus 8 percent, but the executor brings a friend only if adjacent, unfortified, not literal-without-orders, not hostile, and then rolls for arrival: 26 of 68 candidates arrived in four seeds and Mack (literal) is refused on principle. So two corps of one court do attack together, about 3-6 times in 92 target-turns per seed by sequential strikes and some arrivals, but the AI's own ratio is more optimistic than what the resolver delivers.

On the 'fully autonomous France' question from the code side: nothing in the shipped code is wrong, but an AI-run France cannot be a full player. She has no entry in nation_actions, is excluded from the enemy loop, cannot originate a proposal or a declaration (process_diplomatic_phase returns None for the player), is never a coveter or prize in the war council, has no intent because the player's own plans are barred from intent.py, and her marshals would read the player's fog instead of live sight. Those are AI_INTENT_SPEC D3 and the player-is-France architecture, not defects; the practical consequence is that an autonomous-France experiment only ever lets France fight wars others open on her, and any realism claim about it must say so. The one fixed-input I would watch for variance is the enemy phase order, which never rotates (AIMIL-5); it is a plausible reason AI-vs-AI results feel less unpredictable than the statecraft layer intends, but I have not measured it.

Everything not filed was checked and found sound; see working_well.

verdicts.question: Does the AI's diplomatic mind keep multiple courts moving (proposals, intent ladder, descent) rather than stalling?
verdicts.evidence: Intent movement lines, sponsorships, AI-AI treaties, third-party peaces and the Prussia-Hanover war all fire in 8 of 8 archived runs (rev1106-aidip-*). The descent works: 'THE CONGRESS: X and Y make peace without France' on 2-5 turns per run. But the escalation ladder never reaches an ultimatum or a war against France or any Great Power in 8 seeds x ~36 turns: 25+ 'prepared now to go as far as an ultimatum' lines and 0 ultimatum popups.

verdicts.question: Would a fully autonomous game with an AI-run France show cool, realistic, multiple unpredictable outcomes?
verdicts.evidence: No AI-run France was available. Mode A without --llm anthropic cannot make diplomacy decisions, so the only arm run was a passive France under the policy 'diplomacy: decline', 8 seeds x 40 turns. That arm is homogeneous: the enemy set is Austria/Britain/Russia at T1 plus a rebel Switzerland at T11-T20 in 8/8 runs, Prussia never joins, and France is reduced to 0-16 provinces in 8/8. It measures the AI's response to a passive player, not variety under an active France.

verdicts.question: Does the league that declares now reach and strike France (SFR-DR1 at HEAD)?
verdicts.evidence: Visible enemy attacks on 235 of 301 turns (78%) across 8 runs. Weakest is ulm, 21/40 with a 7-turn zero streak. The remaining stops are named on the dispatch by the EAD-8 reading, e.g. 'Britain has no road to us but the sea, and Normandy is a defended shore: 15,000 men at a time'. Britain does land, e.g. 'Paget attacks Paris' on jena T38.

verdicts.question: Is the intent ask budget safe from the bandwagon cap (AI_INTENT_SPEC section 4.2c)?
verdicts.evidence: turn_manager.py 880-905: the intent_ask branch is tested before the bandwagon branch, with separate counters. Cooldowns are stamped at delivery, not generation (letter_counted gate), so a deferred ask is not lost. volte_face and bandwagon_submission carry decision_reasons outside the capped set.

verdicts.question: Is every 'except Exception' in the section spoken?
verdicts.evidence: All 27 handlers in the 8 files call report(exc, site) (backend/errors.py). One site label is wrong (AIDIP-6), and report logs once per process per site, so a per-turn failure shows once. No handler is silent.

verdicts.question: Is the AI's coalition machinery free of structural dead ends?
verdicts.evidence: AIDIP-1: a non-France eclipse coalition brews with 1 qualifier although formation needs 2. The failed brew is cancelled with no cooldown and re-brewed the same turn, so a brewing notice repeats every 3 turns. Friedland T18/21/24/27/30 at alarm 93-97, jena T28/31/34/37.
