sections.notes:
What I did: read the AI diplomacy code against its contracts, ran 8 seeds x 40 turns, and probed three seams with 5-line fixtures. The runs are Mode A with a decline-all-diplomacy France, so they test the AI's response to a passive player. Mode A cannot supply a diplomatic France, and --llm anthropic is forbidden. Questions about an autonomous France or about variance under active diplomacy are UNMEASURED, and AIDIP-7 says so.

What I found: the machinery mostly does what the specs say. The league strikes (SFR-DR1 holds), the budgets (4.2c) are right, and no exception swallows silently. Four real defects came out of the runs and probes:
- AIDIP-1: the eclipse coalition brews on a single qualifier that can never form a league. It cancels with no cooldown and is re-announced every 3 turns, and a hegemon at alarm 97 never draws a league.
- AIDIP-2: the AI's settlement letter quotes an indemnity of 4,200 from a bankrupt court, and ratification then clamps it to the chest. The comment and docstring still promise white peace.
- AIDIP-3: the ordered-pair cooldown that AI-vs-AI refusals write is never read on the trigger path. Refused design asks repeat on a fixed 6-turn cadence.
- AIDIP-4: sell_neutrality can offer 7 gold for a binding neutrality compact.

The rest is P3 doc and label drift (AIDIP-5, -6, -8).

Judgement on realism: against a passive France the AI is competent but monotone. The enemy set is identical on 8 of 8 seeds and France is destroyed on 8 of 8. Prussia, Sweden and the Ottomans never join. Ultimatums are announced as 'prepared to go as far as' about 25 times and never issued. Nothing in these runs shows that an active France would see something different, so I recommend an AI-V-style arm with a scripted active France before claiming 'unpredictable outcomes'.

Verification gaps:
- I did not check whether the 'Hanover pays N gold' rail rows exceed Hanover's chest (AIDIP-2, flagged).
- I did not trace calculate_acceptance's political terms (bilateral_betrayal and grievance) for double counting. I read the sum and found no double use of relation, but I did not prove independence of those two.
- I did not run the league-table riders (EA-19) at a binding truce. settlement_offers.py is the player-side petition and offer table, and the AI letter emitter lives in ai_diplomacy.py (6373+). I checked terms honesty (AIDIP-2) but not truce gating.
- I did not read agendas.py and emergent_designs.py beyond grep. war_council beats (deterrence receipt) were seen only through digest rail rows (crisis_brewing, allegiance_settled).
- Scratchpad note: another process overwrote my first probe file, so I switched to aidip_p2.py. No repo files were edited. The only repo writes are the driver's own tools/playtest_runs and docs/audits/playtest_digests output.

verdicts.question: Q1 Effect wiring: does every law effect type used by the decks have an engine reader (no dead laws)?
verdicts.evidence: All 27 laws (France 6, Austria 5, Prussia 5, Russia 5, Britain 5, Ottoman 1) use only wired types. actions -> reforms.py:186 staff_actions -> world_state.py:12463 (player refill) and :13064 (every court's refill). manpower_regen -> reforms.py:220 apply_manpower_regen -> world_state.py:8253. recruit_price -> reforms.py:230 -> economy_executor.py:1539. recruit_morale -> reforms.py:237 -> economy_executor.py:1900. drill_morale -> reforms.py:252 -> world_state.py:6391. supply_capacity -> reforms.py:261 -> world_state.py:8931. satellite_loyalty -> reforms.py:268 -> vassal.py:1086/1218. cs_closure -> reforms.py:274 -> naval.py:1527/1568. blockade_denial -> reforms.py:289 -> naval.py:1214/1451/3052. force_limit -> reforms.py:165 -> world_state.py:609. cures -> doctrines.py:122/555 (cure_status). Edicts feed the same readers through effect_terms (reforms.py:150). Dead code only: recruit_morale_bonus (reforms.py:243) has 0 backend callers. satellite_loyalty and cs_closure are fed by France's laws only, and France is the player's court, so no AI court ever benefits from those two readers.

verdicts.question: Q2 AI rung: can a court deadlock saving for the Staff, and is the purse arithmetic sound?
verdicts.evidence: Deadlock confirmed. At the boot economy the Staff bar (price + 1000 + 5 x (bill + 300) = 11,500 + 5 x bill) exceeds the chest's fixed point for Prussia (6,140 at k=0 laws) and Austria (5,375), and for Russia once it holds two cheap laws (11,583 against 13,000). Because THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF blocks every cheaper law once the chest passes half the Staff's price, a court can hold chest in [4,500, bar) forever (repro in LAW-2/LAW-3). The upkeep is NOT double-counted: the bar adds the new law's upkeep once (reforms.py:1234) and the Net test subtracts it once. The authority floor 30 strands an authority-priced law once a court sits under 45 (Britain 42 -> 27 refused). The DP floor of 3 equals the base DP at authority 30 to 59, so it adds nothing for a default envoy. The 3-turn latch and the lapse guard cannot starve each other: the latch is derived from in-force laws and the guard stamps nothing.

verdicts.question: Q3 Lapses: order, forecast timing, AI repeal-before-lapse (SFR-B14 class)?
verdicts.evidence: lapse_order reforms.py:630 kills the largest upkeep first, so the Staff (300) always goes before any 100-150 law, and with it the cure (cure_status needs the Staff). The forecast (reforms.py:955) is the projection of THIS turn's end (chest_forecast), shown during the turn before the lapse bites, and the lapse loop (reforms.py:641) uses the same chest rule. ai_repeal_before_lapse (reforms.py:1257) runs at enemy_ai.py:6931 before every other admin rung, and repeal_plan never repeals the Staff because the doomed law is by construction the largest upkeep. Archived lapses are rare and match the rule (rev1106 digests, Austria cannot pay for the Landwehr, Generalissimus, Jager, 5 rows in the whole archive). I did not find an SFR-B14 regression.

verdicts.question: Q4 Edicts: premise readers use the court's own sight; decree currency intact; duration and lapse correct?
verdicts.evidence: The only fog-sensitive premise, _enemy_within_a_march (affairs.py:613-614), reads world.get_visible_enemies for the player and get_live_visible_enemies for a court. The other premises read the lord's own state (corps on pay, cavalry %, Charges terms) or a court's war_intents (diplomacy has no fog). AU-20 sibling sweep: an AST scan of every dict that carries an 'action' key in enemy_ai, naval, recruitment, reforms, affairs, vassal and contingent shows no structured key beyond the whitelist at enemy_ai.py:6764 except annotations (walk_in, _acting_nation, type). The letter path carries currency (moments.py:943 _apply_edict passes row currency; _plan_edict:925 quotes with standing.offer). Edict term: until = turn + term, in force while until > turn (affairs.py:1861-1875), so 8 turns including the decree turn.

verdicts.question: Q5 Standing: every write through standing.move; floors; caps; cooldown keys; court rules vs player's?
verdicts.evidence: No production direct writes: the only 'authority = ' assignment outside standing is a test mock (vindication.py:509); the property setter authority.py:97-101 routes through move(..., 'unattributed'); the tracker's _authority is written only in move (authority.py:111) and load (:380); nation_authority is written only in standing.move (standing.py:206). GRIP_ENEMY_COURT_BASE = 75 (authority.py:460) and is the court's flat grip (authority.py:585). regrow ceilings at CEILING 95 (standing.py:46,289). Court cooldowns are stored as last:<court>|<key> in the player's tracker held (standing.py:309-314) so cannot collide with the player's last:<key> unless a key contains '|'. A court keeps no push-recency (standing.py:818-823 returns [] for a court), so the court Decree price never rises. The laws carry no 60-floor for the player by ruling (AUTHORITY_CURRENCY_SPEC.md line 104).

verdicts.question: Q6 Golden Rule 2: every payload number an int?
verdicts.evidence: In-process walk of laws_payload, standing.payload and doctrines.doctrine_payload for all 6 decks at boot, plus a forced lapse-forecast state, found 0 float values. Source check: laws_payload casts price/upkeep/arrears with int() (reforms.py:846-870); edicts_payload int(until) (:947); lapse_forecast casts shortfall/chest/net (:1035-1042); standing.payload casts every field (standing.py:333-346). edicts_payload with an edict in force was not walked at runtime, only read.

verdicts.question: Q7 Swallowing 'except Exception' in the section?
verdicts.evidence: All 31 handlers across reforms/doctrines/affairs/standing/moments/authority call report(exc, site) (backend/errors.py logs once per site, never silent). The one with consequence is moments._apply (moments.py:1184): an op that raises is logged and the remaining ops of the letter still apply (partial application). Nothing in the section can swallow silently.

verdicts.question: Autonomy of AI laws: do the rival courts actually reform on the shipped tree (6 ambient seeds, 31-40 turns)?
verdicts.evidence: rev1106-amb-* digests: cheap laws land early (Orders T1, Opolchenie T2, Articles of War T6 on all six). Staffs: Britain 5 of 6 (T27-33), Austria 4 of 6 (T27/30/31/40), Prussia 0 of 6, Russia 0 of 6, Ottoman 1 of 6. A cure in force by T30 on historical: Austria only (T30). DOCTRINES_SPEC T8 (two of four by T30 on historical) is therefore missed today.

verdicts.question: Is the law layer a tech tree with real trade-offs?
verdicts.evidence: The Staff plus its cure is a genuine pairing, and Russia's Extraordinary Levy (x0.8 price, -10 morale) and the Ottoman New Order are real trade-offs. The other 22 laws are one-way boosts with an upkeep tax: +25% regen x5 (identical value), drill +5 x3, x0.85 artillery x3, +10 recruit morale x2. No mutual exclusion, no slot cap, no law whose effect scales with authority. See notes.

sections.notes:
I did not run any playtest. I read the six rev1106-amb-* digests that other reviewers had already archived (read-only) and the older archive (97 runs with rival law rows) and ran in-process arithmetic against the real functions on a fresh boot of europe_1805.json (no writes, no server). I did not run pytest.

JUDGEMENT. The wiring is sound: 11 effect types, each with one reader, no dead law, authority behind one writer, courts reading their own sight, no float to Godot, no silent except. The AU-20 sibling sweep came back clean. What is weak is not the plumbing but the AI's pacing of the one law that matters.

THE CORE PROBLEM (LAW-1/2/3). Every rival's doctrine flaw is cured only by 'its cure law AND its Staff' (RV-15). The Staff costs 9,000 + 300 a turn, and the rung's purse bar charges five turns of the whole slate's upkeep on top, so each cheaper law enacted first raises the Staff's bar by 5 x its upkeep. At the boot economy Prussia's and Austria's chest fixed point (6,140 / 5,375) sits far under the 11,500 bar even with no other law, and Russia's drops under it after two laws. The DC-2 'save for the Staff' rule fixed Austria and Britain on the 2026-09-27 economy (cures T19-24) but the S14j rebalance moved them to T27-40, and Prussia and Russia were always 'recorded, not tuned'. The rule itself is also harmful where the target is unreachable: it forbids every cheaper law once the chest passes half the Staff price, so a court in the band buys nothing for the rest of the game (repro in table D). So on the shipped tree two of four rivals never shed their flaw, one sheds it late, and T8 fails. If this is acceptable, a ruling should say so; otherwise it needs an owner row (Rule 9). Fix directions (recommend only): make the bar read the slate's upkeep once, not x5, for the Staff; or let the saving rule engage only when ceiling >= bar; or give Prussia and Russia a cheaper Staff or a different cure carrier.

AUTHORITY (LAW-4). With the courts' battle writes and Decree flipped on, a court's authority only rises by a Bulletin/Te Deum. Every court decrees the Remounts for 3 authority on T1, which is the same pool the 15-authority political laws draw on under a floor of 30. Britain's second authority law (the Militia Transfer cure) needs authority >= 45 and sits at 42 after T1. I could not read courts' authority in a digest, so this is arithmetic plus the arrival pattern, not a traced fact. The AI_DIPLOMACY_FLOOR (3) equals the base DP of a default envoy at authority 30-59, so it does not add a second constraint in practice (a skilled envoy could change that; I did not test one).

LAPSES. Lapse order (largest upkeep first) always sheds the Staff first, which also kills the cure. For a court on the margin that is the worst law to lose, but it is a ruling (R5). The player's forecast is shown mid-turn for the coming end of turn, and the AI repeals the smallest sufficient law first, so I found no SFR-B14 regression. Lapses are rare in the archive (5 rows).

PERF NOTE (not filed). ai_holds_the_purse calls lapse_forecast, which calls the full _build_economy, once per _pick_admin_action and again in find_ai_edict and per candidate law in ai_purse_refusal. With 5 decks and 2 admin AP this is bounded, and it returns early for a court with no laws in force. effect_terms also walks the affairs deck on every call (reforms.py:150-157) from supply and recruit paths; fine at 5 courts, worth caching if the deck grows (Rule 8 concerns regions, not this).

TECH TREE OR SHOPPING LIST. Mostly a shopping list: of 27 laws, five are the same +25% manpower regen, three the same +5 drill morale (which is +50% on a base 10, the best value per gold), three the same x0.85 artillery price. There is no mutual exclusion, no slot cap and no law that scales with authority or war state. Real trade-offs exist only at the Staff-plus-cure pair, Russia's Extraordinary Levy (x0.8 price, -10 morale) and the Ottoman New Order. The recruit-morale laws are also void in any province with a training ground (LAW-8). ONE ADDITION THAT WOULD GIVE IT TEETH (recommend only): a standing-linked cap on laws in force, a cabinet of three non-Staff laws, so that each court must choose its line (Prussia: Krumper regen versus Emancipation price; Russia: levy versus drill), with the upkeep and authority price kept as is. That turns 27 additive rows into decisions, makes the AI's deck order a character statement, and gives the lapse rule something to choose between.

NOT MEASURED. Courts' authority traces; a Prussia whose chest grows by conquest (I held net constant); edicts_payload with an edict in force at runtime; player-side law value (I only read the rival side); any LLM path. Economy at scale and the aliveness of an AI-run France are other reviewers' sections.

verdicts.question: Q2 Serialization: no unserialized field changes play after load
verdicts.evidence: The 24 tests in tests/test_serialization_enforcement.py pass. I booted the 1805 world and played 28 turns (rev1106-turn-serdiff3, not archived). WorldState has 271 live attributes against 212 to_dict keys. to_dict(from_dict(to_dict)) was identical, with 0 diverged keys. Every non-serialized attribute is a cache, a display stash (_last_reply, _income_phase_results, _morning_accounts, _dp_refill, _applied_*), a per-turn latch, or a documented exclusion (positive_threat_delta_this_turn, nation_capitals). Marshal has one unserialized field, _doctrine_terms, which is derived on load by design (marshal.py:864). The strongest evidence is rev1106-turn-reload against rev1106-turn-noreload: 20 turns with 4 reloads, identical battles, casualties and AP, with only 2 flavor lines differing (TURN-3). A from_dict default test (delete each key, reload, compare with a fresh __init__) found only the identity fields Marshal needs, and intel, diplomatic_states and nation_relations, which are only empty for pre-migration saves.

verdicts.question: Q3 Dialogue queue across save/load: nothing lost, duplicated or stuck
verdicts.evidence: Probe tools/scratch qprobe at every end-turn boundary over 30 turns (rev1106-turn-queue3, not archived). I ran save then load and compared GET /mailbox, the manager's current and queued dialogues, both id counters, and the popup keys. 17 of 30 boundaries held a non-empty queue. The only difference was turn 10: the load response adds pending_interrupt for Davout's cannon_fire. That interrupt is intentional (main.py:6595-6601, WO-35, first marshal wins) and the world's interrupts did not change. A hard stop (war_purpose_selection) loaded with the same dialogue_id, and end turn and confirm both refused with the answer words. The modal rides the first /command (diplomatic_dialogue present), as the /load docstring says. No duplicate or lost dialogue was found. clear_stale's queue sweep keeps mailbox, paradox and blocking types. I did not exercise mid-turn saves with settlement hard stops. tools/treaty_fuzzer.py writes under docs/ so I did not run it.

sections.notes:
I did this section as a report-only code review plus three driver runs and eight in-process probes. I edited no repository file. The only repository writes are driver output under tools/playtest_runs/ and the three archived digests.

The turn, the save and the dialogue queue are in very good shape. The serialization surface (about 270 live WorldState attributes) round-trips cleanly. The 20-turn, 4-reload twin differs from the no-reload run only in two lines of Berthier flavor text, which a recorded ruling (IQ-8 item 8) explains. Every save fault reached the player. The queue loses, duplicates or strands nothing across the boundaries I tested. No float reached a response in about 700 samples. Golden Rule 4 holds at every consumable I traced.

The two real findings are both about failure, which is where the section was supposed to be strongest.

TURN-1: V2-19's 'encountered an error' row for a crashed enemy court is built and then discarded by the fog filter, so the player never learns a court skipped its turn. The failure goes only to stderr and the /debug errors tally.

TURN-2: any exception inside advance_turn permanently wedges the campaign. The R20 idempotency stamp is written before the increment, so every retry skips the advance, replays the enemy phase, and answers 'Turn N is already underway!' with success=true. Saves written in that state reload stuck. Both need a bug elsewhere to trigger, which is why they are P2 and not P1, but they are exactly the 'silent failure' class DD-C exists for. With ~550 broad excepts and a 128-module turn, a crash in the advance is plausible, and the current behaviour turns it into a soft-lock.

Smaller items are TURN-3 (the reload contract text), TURN-4 (14 console-only handlers, one in the /command chain at main.py:3991), and TURN-5 (the SYSTEMS_REFERENCE turn order has 8 steps against about 60 in code).

What I could not measure:
- I did not run the treaty fuzzer because it writes under docs/.
- I did not test saves taken mid-turn with settlement hard stops standing.
- I did not trace momentum or last_relationship_change through the clear sites. Rule 4 was checked on the consumables named above.
- The float census covers one 28-turn historical run plus a turn-26 sweep of the GET endpoints. Rare branches (a sitting Congress, the Descent camp, the Moniteur) were not driven.
- The Q2 attribute diff is of one run's end state. Attributes created lazily on rare paths would not appear in it.

Judgement: ready to ship from this section's standpoint. Fix TURN-2 and TURN-1 first. TURN-2 would be a small change: on a failed advance, clear or roll back the stamp, or make end_turn refuse and point at the autosave instead of replaying the enemy phase. TURN-1 would be a notice-rail row that bypasses the fog filter.

working_well: Golden Rule 1 is largely honoured: the muster preview (combat_executor.py:1491, 2343), objection_v2.py:1086, garrison_report.py:321 and the garrison assault all read marshal.py through get_*_modifier(consume=False or True). Reinforcers are scored with consume=False so they do not spend one-time bonuses.

Consumable-state discipline is good: snapshot before consume in battle_report, Iron Resolve and counter-punch consumed inside the modifier (anti-banking), the defender's drill read then cancelled (the Sept 27 GR4 fix), and the coordination stamps registered in COORDINATION_TRANSIENT_FIELDS with several clear paths.
Reinforcement eligibility is thorough (11 rules incl. the naval crossing gate, vassal loyalty, one reinforcement per corps per turn) and a literal marshal's no-march is surfaced with a voice line.

Forced-retreat destination logic is careful: adjacent only, no enemy marshals, at-war soil last, neutral soil forbidden by the movement law, sea crossings demoted rather than soft-locking, and the broken branch avoids staying in place.
Dead and captured targets are handled for SUPPORT and PURSUE, with the fate named in words (quarry_fate, support_friend_fallen, standalone-question retirement).
Every broad except in the section's files reports through backend.errors.report (13 of 13): none swallow silently.

The strategic-objection trust arm is quoted and charged consistently (1 AP) for a preferred strategic pursue at 4, 2 and 1 AP remaining, so the S15H-4 class (an arm paid once, charged twice) did not reproduce there.
Rule 2 held on a real battle result: zero floats anywhere in the result dict, including battle_report and battle_diorama.
sections.notes:
This was the code-review section, so I read code and ran in-process probes on fixture worlds and the Europe boot. I ran no Mode A playtests and wrote no archived digests. I never started the backend, touched port 8005 or ran the full suite. I temporarily put three scratch pytest files in tests/, which imported fixtures from tests/test_strategic_objections.py, and deleted them straight after each run. Nothing under backend/, godot-client/ or docs/ was edited.

Overall judgement: the section is in good shape. The Golden Rules are mostly kept, every broad except speaks, and forced retreat, reinforcement and standing-order handling are careful. I found one real Rule 4 gap and one real defiance-table bug.

- **COMBAT-1 (P1, Rule 4):** a drilled corps never spends its +20% when it assaults a garrison, because the drill clear lives only in combat.py (the comment there already calls it a pragmatic exception to Golden Rule 1). The garrison assault reads get_attack_modifier but clears nothing, so the bonus applies to every later assault. The enemy AI is affected the same way. It is cheap to fix by moving the clear into one helper that both paths call.
- **COMBAT-2 (P2):** the strategic path passes uppercase 'HOLD' into a table that also holds lowercase 'hold', so an aggressive marshal's HOLD defiance sulks instead of attacking. The spec says attack. The existing test pins only the lowercase key, which is why it never failed.
- **Design questions for the user (P3):** COMBAT-3 (PURSUE is in neither personality's defiance table), COMBAT-4 (literal, loyalist and dove popups have no Trust arm, 15 marshals; S15H-3 called it a reading for the user), COMBAT-6 (the Grouchy ambiguity buff never expires) and COMBAT-7 (a Rule 1 residue in combat.py). COMBAT-5 is a small defect: Precision Execution lowers Soult's tactical 9 to 8.

Not measured:
- movement attrition and the crossing-gate seam in movement_executor.py
- tactical_executor fortify, drill and square state transitions beyond the combat read
- overwatch and bombardment-streak clearing
- the first-step-blocking check by a fortified state beyond the preferred-pursue AP probe
- a two-reinforcer battle end to end
- trust at 0 and 100 through the full insist chain
- the forced-retreat destination into a supply-capped region
- the V1 PARTIAL-sight silence rate as a sample (derived analytically only)

No P1 beyond COMBAT-1 turned up in the files I read. A fuller pass on tactical_executor and movement_executor (about 3,300 lines I did not read in full) is the obvious next step.

verdicts.question: Does a 126-province Europe turn stay fast and flat over a long game (scale of end_turn)?
verdicts.evidence: In-process, 60 turns, seed historical: min 23.7 / median 92.6 / max 332 ms. Turns 1-10 mean 98 ms, 11-20 mean 112, 21-30 mean 76. The 190-330 ms window at turns 31-36 and the later turns are on a zombie board (see notes). No growth trend: turns 41-60 sit back at 70-130 ms.

verdicts.question: Is Golden Rule 8 (no per-region scans in hot paths) respected?
verdicts.evidence: About 90 sites iterate world.regions. The hot per-turn ones go through get_nation_regions / get_active_nations / get_neighbouring_nations (25.7k get_nation_regions calls in 24 turns cost 0.043 s). Exceptions: SCALE-1 (ledger._build_economy, 2 full-map scans per AI forecast, 14 calls/turn, 18% of turn time) and SCALE-5 (get_game_state_summary scans all marshals per region on every response).

verdicts.question: Is Golden Rule 2 (int() on every number to Godot) respected at the API boundary?
verdicts.evidence: Zero floats in any JSON body across 804 requests of the 40-turn commanded_full40 run, 388 requests of naval_descent and 598 of sf_nav1_strangulation (a patched TestClient walked every response). Zero floats in 17 GET endpoints at T1 and T40. Static: naval.py:1106,1944,2159,2264,2544 build float round() values, but the executor results that carry them (e.g. movement_executor.py:809 naval_ratio) are dropped before the response; a live blocked Normandy to London order returned no float.

verdicts.question: Do the per-turn caches invalidate correctly (no stale active-nation or region set after an elimination or cession)?
verdicts.evidence: All 19 sites that assign region.controller either call invalidate_active_nations_cache() themselves or sit in a function that does (diplomatic_executor.py:4613->4623, meta_executor.py:1842->1845, vassal.py:2798->2799, settlement_ratify.py:461->511, world_state.py:14210->14272, world_state.py:5481->5482). Only test or debug code (turn_manager.py:1800) is bare. The distance cache is static topology; invalidate_distance_cache has no callers, which is harmless.

verdicts.question: Is state bounded over 100+ turns?
verdicts.evidence: 120-turn in-process run: event_log capped at 500, command_history 50, gazette 20, notifications about 23, moments/affairs/intel/regions flat. One unbounded store: war_instances[*].offer_history grows by one entry per turn (28 KB total at T120 vs 7 KB at T40, n=2 wars) - SCALE-4. Save size is 447 KB at T1 and 736 KB at T40, and to_dict plus json.dumps costs about 8 ms.

verdicts.question: Does command latency grow between turn 1 and turn 40?
verdicts.evidence: Warm /command 'status' T1 median 48 ms, T40 71-83 ms; 'economy' 49-61 -> 47-65 ms; 'Ney, attack Mack' 56-88 -> 65-84 ms (loaded machine, TestClient). The first call after boot is about 200 ms (lazy imports). Every response is 175-190 KB because map_data is re-sent (SCALE-3).

sections.notes:
What I ran. In-process on seed historical (LLM_MODE=mock, PYTHONHASHSEED=0): a 60-turn timing loop, a cProfile of turns 30-35, a second profile of turns 1-24, a 120-turn state-growth run, a TestClient probe of 17 GETs and three commands at turn 1 and on the T40 save, and the driver run commanded_full40 --save-at 1,40 (archived as rev1106-scale-save). I also wrapped TestClient so every response of three scripted campaigns was walked for floats. Scratch scripts live in the scratchpad directory (scale_time.py, prof25.py, growth.py, api_probe.py, t40probe.py, floatwrap.py, census.py). No repository file was edited, and the only git-visible write is the archive directory.

Caveat 1, zombie board. The passive France of the pure end_turn loop loses its capital at turn 25-26 (ending 'eagle_falls', then 'soil_or_sword' each turn). To keep timing the AI I reset game_over, victory and endings before every later turn. Turns 1-25 are therefore a genuine campaign, and turns 26-60 are a world where France is gone and the survivors keep playing. The 190-330 ms window at turns 31-36 and the requested turns 30-35 profile come from that board, so treat them as an AI-heavy upper bound, not a typical player turn. The turn-1 to turn-24 profile is the clean one, and both agree on the hot spots (the AI marshal evaluation, the chest forecast and the effect-term re-reads). I did not run a seeded loop with an active France making moves (that is the playtest driver's job, and the other reviewers have it).

Caveat 2, loaded machine. The command latencies include contention from the other reviewers' runs, so absolute numbers are noisy. The T1 to T40 growth of +20-30 ms is inside that noise, so I do not claim the latency grows.

Caveat 3, scale extrapolation. The map is 126 provinces and 34 marshals, and I did not run the full-1805 map (it does not exist yet), so I did not test the quadratic claims in SCALE-5 and SCALE-6 beyond the profile counts. CLAUDE.md's G4 measurement says a 1805 campaign turn is 6.1x legacy. That fits my 90 ms median and the AI-dominated profile (about two thirds of turn time is _process_enemy_turns).

Judgement. The scale story is healthy for the shipped 126-province game. The caches are disciplined, the state is bounded apart from one slow-growing war ledger, and the API boundary is clean on the integer rule. None of my findings is a P1. The most worth fixing before the full-Europe map are SCALE-1 (the AI asking for a ledger-tab economy rebuild when it needs one number, about 18% of turn time, with the two full-map scans that Rule 8 forbids) and SCALE-3 (a 165 KB whole-map payload on every command, which scales with the map). SCALE-2, 5 and 6 are all the same pattern: a derived value recomputed per call from a static store instead of a per-turn memo. Sibling sweep notes for Rule 10: the class to search for is 'a ledger or display builder reused as an AI read' (grep callers of ledger._build_economy, _levy_block, get_levy_status from backend/ai and game_logic), and the class 'an append to a per-war or per-nation list with no cap' (offer_history is the only one that grew in 120 turns, but an audit of every instance.setdefault(...).append would close it). I did not edit any file or run the full pytest suite."

findings.title: The stagnation breaker's 'surrounded, attack weakest adjacent (desperate)' arm ignores the same-turn already-attacked brake and the futility limit
findings.seam: backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:4941-4955 (the stagnation >= 3 'Surrounded' arm); compare the brake at enemy_ai.py:3381-3399 and the set at enemy_ai.py:1696
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-austerlitz, T33 enemy phase: Bavaria's Deroy attacks Bennigsen three times in one phase. Battles lost: Deroy 1521, 1151 and 1107 vs Bennigsen 433, 432 and 310 (digest.md lines 767-769), with the 2nd and 3rd carrying the 'exhausted from repeated attacks' penalty. server_console.log lines 25139, 25152 and 25165: '[STAGNATION] Deroy: Surrounded, attacking Bennigsen (desperate)' then '[?/3]', '[?/2]', '[?/1] Deroy (priority 70): attack -> Bennigsen'. Directly after the third: '[FUTILITY] Deroy has failed 3x against Bennigsen'. Later desperate attacks on Bennigsen are still made at T37 (digest line 868) and T40 (line 927); the console has 4 'desperate' lines in this run. Code at line 4950 returns {'action':'attack','target': weakest_adjacent.name} after checking only _stagnation_can_strike and engagement_fellows, with no _attacked_targets_this_turn or ai_attack_futility lookup, while P4's brake and the ALLY SUPPORT rung (enemy_ai.py:4597-4601) both read them.
findings.repro: ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name x --fresh --seed austerlitz --script tools/playtest_scripts/commanded_full40.json --diplomacy accept ; then grep -n 'desperate' tools/playtest_runs/x/server_console.log (Bavaria T33: three attacks on one defender)
findings.expected: A marshal attacks a given defender at most once a phase, and not at all once futility is at or above ATTACK_FUTILITY_LIMIT (3) against an unmoved square-formed or fortified target, as FA-N72 intended for P0.
findings.actual: Deroy repeats the same assault three times in a phase and again on later turns, losing about 3.8k men for 1.2k, with the futility counter ignored.
findings.prior_row: FA-N72 (docs/archive/BUG_FIXES_2026_Q3.md:1572: P0 reads neither the futility counter nor the already-attacked set) - same class, a sibling arm that was not swept

mechanism.evidence:
The code path is as filed. backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:4941-4955 (the `if stagnation >= 3:` surrounded arm) builds weakest_adjacent from `_stagnation_can_strike` and `engagement_fellows` only. It then returns `{"action":"attack","target": weakest_adjacent.name}`. It never reads `_attacked_targets_this_turn` or `world.ai_attack_futility`. The brake that does read both is `_engageable_enemies` (enemy_ai.py:3381-3399), which skips a pair already attacked this turn and any pair with futility >= ATTACK_FUTILITY_LIMIT. The pair is stamped at enemy_ai.py:1696 after each executed attack, so the arm could have read it.

The log matches. tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-austerlitz/server_console.log lines 25137, 25150 and 25163 show "[STAGNATION] Deroy: Surrounded, attacking Bennigsen (desperate)" three times inside one "Bavaria TURN: 3 actions, 1 marshals ['Deroy']" phase. They are followed by "[?/3]", "[?/2]" and "[?/1] Deroy (priority 70): attack -> Bennigsen". Deroy's strength falls 20418, 19267, 18160 across the three. Line 26064 shows a later desperate attack on ArchdukeJohn. The "P0 ENGAGEMENT ... enemies = []" line before each repeat shows the stamped-pair brake never reached this arm.

I did not re-run the playtest. The mechanism and the log are enough.

Severity is P3, not P2. Four points limit it:
- The arm fires only for a boxed-in corps with stagnation >= 3, here a lone Bavarian vassal corps idle 26 turns.
- When Bavaria has one marshal, the alternatives are to pass or to do nothing, so the repeat is wasteful rather than catastrophic.
- It sits in the FA-N72 class: P0 once lacked these brakes and a sibling arm was not swept (CLAUDE.md rule 10).
- I did not find a closed BUG_FIXES row covering this arm, so it is a live sibling defect.
mechanism.note: Fix shape: route the surrounded arm's candidate list through `_engageable_enemies`, or apply the same two checks inline. Those checks are the pair brake `(marshal.name, enemy.name) in _attacked_targets_this_turn` and `ai_attack_futility[f"{marshal.name}:{enemy.name}"] >= ATTACK_FUTILITY_LIMIT`. Pin it with a surrounded single-marshal board that gets 3 actions and must attack at most once per phase. This is a game defect, not a harness defect.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the playtest. I re-read the existing run log and the code. (1) backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:4941-4955 (the stagnation >= 3 "Surrounded" arm) picks weakest_adjacent after only `_stagnation_can_strike` and `engagement_fellows`. It then returns {"action":"attack","target":weakest_adjacent.name}. It never reads `_attacked_targets_this_turn` or `world.ai_attack_futility`. The brake at enemy_ai.py:3381-3399 does read both, but it filters only the P0/P4 enemy list. (2) tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-austerlitz/server_console.log lines 25137-25175 show one Bavaria turn ("3 actions, 1 marshals ['Deroy']"). In that single phase, "[STAGNATION] Deroy: Surrounded, attacking Bennigsen (desperate)" appears three times, each followed by "[?/3]", "[?/2]" and "[?/1] Deroy (priority 70): attack -> Bennigsen". Three "Event type: battle" lines follow. Deroy's strength falls 20418 -> 19267 -> 18160. Only after the third attack does "[FUTILITY] Deroy has failed 3x against Bennigsen" print. The arm never consults that counter. Line 26064 shows a later desperate attack on ArchdukeJohn. (3) Searching docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "desperate" found no closed row or ruling covering this arm.
reproduction.note: The defect is real. It is a sibling of FA-N72, a class Rule 10 says to sweep. I rate it P3 rather than P2. It fires only for a stagnated (26+ idle turns) marshal that is fully surrounded and has no move available. It was seen on one minor-nation marshal, Deroy of Bavaria, and costs that one army men without affecting mechanics or crashing anything. Fix: apply the same `_attacked_targets_this_turn` and `ai_attack_futility` filter inside the arm's candidate loop.

findings.title: French provinces liberated by an ally (Spain) and handed back are silent: the player sees 'X has fallen' and later just a changed count
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:1128 liberation_line / backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:2546 (the surfaces that carry the 'handed back' sentence) vs the AI-vs-AI liberation path
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-jena T34-T40: the fogged enemy phase and Dispatch report 11 French provinces captured, while the ledger falls only 28 to 23 (net -5). T36 reports 2 captures (Savoy, Franche-Comte) but the ledger moves 26 to 25; T40 reports 2 (Brittany, Provence) and the ledger reads 23 (+0). The saves back this up: saves/rev1106-cmd-jena_t40.json has France holding Provence, Berry, Limousin and Lyonnais, all reported fallen earlier. server_console.log lines 25937 and 26833 show Cuesta (Spain) targeting Provence. The digest carries one 'handed back' sentence in the whole run (Lyonnais, retaken by Spain at T38). digest.jsonl has no province_changed_hands row for the other returns.
findings.repro: Read tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-jena/digest.md T34-T40 against saves/rev1106-cmd-jena_t40.json (23 France-controlled regions)
findings.expected: A French province returning by an allied liberation is announced as the S14G-1 sentence says: 'X, France's province, retaken by Spain - handed back to France', at least on the Dispatch or campaign log.
findings.actual: The province count moves with no line saying why. 'Fallen' is announced loudly and the return is not, which makes the ledger look inconsistent with the dispatch.
findings.prior_row: S14G-1 / S14G-D1 (liberation hand-back is ruled behaviour; this is its legibility only)

mechanism.evidence: The dispatch gap is real. backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:2539 reads `elif captor == player_nation and region and e.get("liberated_to"):`, which is the only branch that emits `region_liberated`. When an ally such as Spain retakes France's province, `captor` is Spain. `_ours_to_lose` is false because the previous holder is an enemy. The `captor == player_nation` branches don't match either, so no dispatch line is produced. This was traced by hand from the code; I did not run the dispatch. The event itself exists. `complete_liberation` (world_state.py ~1155) says it is "Shared by the instant capture and the occupation completing, for either side" and logs a `region_captured` row with `liberated_to`. campaign_log.py:2174 formats that row with `liberation_line(... by=captor)`, and the fog filter at campaign_log.py:1178 shows it when the province is PARTIAL+ visible, which French home soil should be. So the campaign log very likely carries the "retaken by Spain - handed back to France" sentence; I did not open the log to confirm. The dispatch and the per-turn enemy-phase digest line, which shows only "Cuesta attacks Lyonnais", do not. The jena save confirms the outcome: at t40, saves/rev1106-cmd-jena_t40.json has Provence, Berry, Limousin and Lyonnais controlled by France, and Burgundy by Britain. digest.jsonl contains the full sentence once, in the Spain action message: "Lyonnais, France's province, retaken - handed back to France." The digest.md line for the same event reads "Region captured: Lyonnais (was Britain)" with no "handed back" text. tools/playtest_driver.py:1272 builds that line from `conquest` events and ignores `liberated_to`, so part of the "silent" symptom is a harness formatting gap. I found no BUG_FIXES row for the ally-captor dispatch case. S14G-1 shipped the dispatch headline for the player's own liberations only.
mechanism.note: I narrowed the finding. The player's Dispatch is silent for allied liberations of French ground; that part is real and is a legibility gap, not a mechanics defect, because S14G-D1 behaviour is correct. I did not verify the campaign log's visibility of these rows, so the "silent everywhere" and "ledger looks inconsistent" framing is not established. The "no province_changed_hands row" evidence should be dropped: that event type does not appear in the code I traced. The digest's lack of the sentence is partly a driver formatting issue (playtest_driver.py:1272). A sibling to check under Rule 10 is the opposite direction, an ally losing ground, which the `_on_our_side` logic does handle.

reproduction.evidence:
I confirmed the silence two ways.

1. Digest and save read. rev1106-cmd-jena/digest.md:
   - Line 913 (T37) reads "Spain: Cuesta attacks Lyonnais — Region captured: Lyonnais (was Britain)". It has no "handed back" wording, and the T37 DIPLO line has no province_changed_hands.
   - grep for "handed back|retaken" over digest.md returns nothing, so the finding's "one sentence in the run" is slightly off. The count is zero.
   - saves/rev1106-cmd-jena_t40.json has France controlling Lyonnais, Provence, Berry, Limousin and Brittany. T34-T38 report each as "fallen to Britain".
   - The T40 save is taken before T40's enemy phase, so Provence, Berry and Limousin had returned to France without a line.
   - Brittany is France's at that save and falls only in T40's enemy phase, so it is not an example.

2. In-process probe. I loaded the T40 save with WorldState.from_dict, set Lyonnais.controller to Britain, then called world.capture_region('Lyonnais','Spain'). France and Spain are in a DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE.
   - The call returned True and the controller became France, so the hand-back works.
   - world.event_log gained no row.
   - world.pending_dispatch_events stayed empty.

Why it is silent:
- backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:2539 gates the "region_liberated" headline on `captor == player_nation`. Spain as captor never reaches it.
- announce_third_party_capture (world_state.py:1708-1716) returns early when `player in (old_controller, capturing_nation)`. For a liberation, capturing_nation is passed as the holder, which is France, so it returns silently.
- liberation_line (world_state.py:1128) is therefore never invoked for an allied AI liberator.

The S14G-1 and S14G-X2 rows in docs/BUG_FIXES.md cover only the player as liberator. X2 says "announced to the court that holds it", which is a third-party court, not the player.
reproduction.note: This is a legibility gap, not a mechanics bug. The hand-back itself works and the ledger count is correct. The fix is to announce an allied liberation of the player's own province on the Dispatch and in the campaign log. The finding's phrase "one handed back sentence" is inaccurate (zero in the digest), but that does not change the verdict. The digest line 913 text "Region captured: Lyonnais (was Britain)" also misdescribes a liberation. One uncertainty is whether the in-game campaign log (fog-filtered) shows any row for Spain's captures. I could not check that. The event_log and pending_dispatch_events were both empty in the probe.

findings.repro: diff tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-historical/digest.md tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-insist-historical/digest.md

findings.title: Eclipse coalition against Austria re-announces 'brewing' every 3 turns with one qualifying court and never forms
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/coalition.py:3913-3966 (7b eclipse pass) vs :2445 form_coalition and :3819-3822 cancel arm
findings.evidence: rev1106-amb-jena T22,T28,T31,T34,T37 and rev1106-amb-friedland T18,T21,T24,T27,T30: 'LOG coalition_brewing_started: Coalition brewing against Austria - Switzerland consulting (their alarm: 62)'. No coalition_declared row in any of them. The 7b pass starts a brew when `if _eclipse_qualifying:` is non-empty. form_coalition then returns `if not qualifying_nations or len(all_members) < 2: return {"success": False, "message": "Insufficient nations for coalition."}`, and the countdown-expiry arm cancels with no cooldown. The next 7b pass starts a new brew.
findings.repro: Run: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name x-jena --fresh --seed jena ; then grep 'brewing against Austria' tools/playtest_runs/x-jena/digest.md (also --seed friedland).
findings.expected: An eclipse brew starts only when the qualifying set can actually form (two or more members), or a failed formation sets coalition_cooldown. The player should not read a fresh 'coalition is brewing' every 3 turns that never resolves.
findings.actual: 5 announcements per run, each a one-court brew that cannot form (T28 onward), and a repeat of the same dispatch line. jena T22 (Prussia and Saxony consulting) also ended with no formation; I could not tell from the digest why.

mechanism.evidence:
The code path matches the finding.

1. coalition.py:3916-3920 (7b eclipse pass) starts a brew whenever `_eclipse_qualifying` is non-empty. It does not require two members, and it does not check `form_coalition`'s own gate.
2. coalition.py:2445-2446, `form_coalition`: `if not qualifying_nations or len(all_members) < 2: return {"success": False, "message": "Insufficient nations for coalition."}`.
3. coalition.py:3794-3800, countdown expiry in the section 6 brew handling (`elif brewing["turns_remaining"] <= 0:`): when `form_coalition` fails, the code runs `world.coalition_brewing = None` and `dismiss_by_type`. It does not set `coalition_cooldown`, and it logs no `coalition_brewing_cancelled` row.
4. The 7b guard at ~3908 is `not world.coalition_brewing and world.coalition_cooldown <= 0`, so the next pass restarts a new brew.
5. `BREWING_COUNTDOWN = 3` (coalition.py:134), which gives the 3-turn cadence.
6. Digest rev1106-amb-friedland shows "coalition_brewing_started ... against Austria" at T18 (Prussia and Bavaria), then T21, T24, T27 and T30 (Bavaria alone). Those are the five announcements in the finding.
7. A grep of that digest for `coalition_declared` and `coalition_brewing_cancelled` found no matches, so nothing formed and nothing was logged as cancelled.
8. rev1106-amb-jena shows the same pattern, with "Prussia and Saxony consulting" at line 551 and "Switzerland consulting" at lines 687, 761, 839 and 899 (alarm 62-76), and no `coalition_declared`.
9. BUG_FIXES.md has no closed row for this. OCT27-4 and OCT27-5 are different eclipse-coalition defects (the successor scoring and the stale card).

I did not run the driver. I did not determine why the T18/T22 two-court brews (friedland T18, jena T22) also failed to form. That is not needed for the core claim.

The impact is cosmetic and repeats a dispatch line. Mechanics are unaffected: a failed brew forms no coalition, and a one-court brew cannot declare anything.
mechanism.note: The defect is real: the 7b eclipse pass starts a brew without checking the formation gate, and the expiry-failure arm sets no cooldown. A suggested fix is to require at least 2 members (qualifying plus already at war with the target) before starting the brew, or to set `coalition_cooldown` when the expiry formation fails. I rate it P3 rather than P2 because the effect is repeated dispatch and log noise every 3 turns, with no mechanical or state corruption. It also touches the AI-aliveness pillar a little, since an anti-Austria league never actually forms in these seeds.

reproduction.evidence:
I reran `tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name rev1106-verify-amb1 --fresh --seed jena`. The digest has five brewing lines: line 551 (Prussia and Saxony consulting, alarm 74), then lines 687, 761, 839 and 899 (each "Switzerland consulting", alarms 62, 62, 67, 76). The verify run matches the original rev1106-amb-jena digest line for line, and none of the ten digests (both runs) has a coalition_declared row or a "Coalition against Austria" declaration.

Code reading, backend/game_logic/coalition.py:
- The 7b pass (about line 3913) starts a brew on `if _eclipse_qualifying:` alone. It does not check that the set can form.
- `form_coalition` (line 2445) returns "Insufficient nations for coalition." when `len(all_members) < 2`. all_members is the qualifying nations plus the non-vassal nations at war with the target, minus France. A lone Switzerland with nobody else at war with Austria gives 1 member.
- The countdown-expiry arm (about line 3811) cancels with only `world.coalition_brewing = None` and `dismiss_by_type`. It sets no `coalition_cooldown`, so the 7b guard `coalition_cooldown <= 0` passes on the next pass and a new brew starts.
- I found no closed row covering this. BUG_FIXES OCT27-5 covers only the stale brew card, and DESIGN_REFINEMENT OCT27-D2 sets no cooldown after an eclipse league dissolves, which is a different path.

Not established: why the T22 brew with Prussia and Saxony did not form. That is 2 qualifying members, so it should pass the length check, and it may have failed in the declaration step (line 2490). I did not trace it.
reproduction.note: The defect is real and reproduces, but P3 fits better than P2. The effect is a repeated "Coalition brewing" log line and dispatch line, plus a rail notice at NORMAL priority. It changes no mechanics: no war is declared and nothing else is gated. Suggested fix: have the 7b pass require `len(set(qualifying) | set(at_war_with_target)) >= 2` before it brews, or set a cooldown when the countdown-expiry arm cancels an eclipse brew.

findings.title: Third-party war declarations are unannounced on 4 of 6 ambient seeds because the dispatch fog rule is partial_on_nation
findings.evidence: rev1106-amb-historical, austerlitz, jena, friedland: dispatch_type_counts diplomatic_war_declared = 0, yet the sweep derives Prussia's war on Hanover (rev1106-aiv-historical.json: opened_turn 11, entry_path war_declaration) and the digest shows 'Prussia: Brunswick attacks Hanover - Region captured'. ulm T14 and marengo T19 do print 'Prussia has declared war on Hanover' because those boards had PARTIAL sight. Spec basis: docs/archive/SESSION_8_PLAN.md:317 'PARTIAL+ on declarer'. Memory rule: diplomacy has no fog.
findings.repro: playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --seed historical; grep -c 'declared war' digest.md (0) against --seed ulm (1).
findings.expected: A formal war between two courts is a public act. The player sees the declaration, or the intent doc states explicitly that war timing is fogged.
findings.actual: The player sees the crisis, the refused final demand, then captures, with no declaration row on 4 of 6 seeds. Whether it appears depends on sight of Hanover or Prussia.

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism confirmed by hand trace. diplomacy.py:11838 queues "diplomatic_war_declared" with fog "partial_on_nation" and template_vars nation=aggressor, target=target. dispatch.py:8838-8855 shows that rule checks only PARTIAL+ on the nations in template_vars. It always shows an event that names the player nation. Otherwise it needs _get_nation_visibility (diplomatic_ledger.py:300-325) to be FULL or PARTIAL. That function takes the best sight over the nation's living marshals' locations, so it is army-sight based and not a diplomatic-relations check. For a Prussia-on-Hanover war with neither court in sight, the event is dropped. A war_declared WAR_DECLARED notification is added unconditionally (diplomacy.py:11826-11833). However, rev1106-amb-historical/digest.md shows no war_declared rail row near turn 11 even though Hanover appears 20 times in it. The only war_declared rail row across the rev1106-amb-* digests is the ulm one ("RAIL diplomatic_war_declared: Prussia has declared war on Hanover..."). So in practice the player gets no declaration line on the fogged seeds. The 4-of-6 seed count was not re-run. I relied on the mechanism plus the historical digest and the single ulm hit in the amb digests. I found no closed BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row for this symptom. The only grep hits are S14E-9 and S14G-10, which are about the declaration beat's cost wording and not its visibility. The fog rule looks like a deliberate Session 8D choice and was not re-checked against its spec text. It conflicts with the user's recorded rule that diplomacy has no fog, so this is a design inconsistency and not a code bug.
mechanism.note: The real defect is a design inconsistency. A formal third-party war declaration is gated on army sight of either belligerent, while the project rule says diplomacy has no fog. The fix is one line: change the fog rule to "always" for this event, as the AI-intent spec's "no fog on dispositions" would suggest. Alternatively, document that declaration timing is fogged. P3 at most because the crisis, refused demand and captures still surface. Not re-run: the 4-of-6 seed count. Not verified: where the unconditional WAR_DECLARED notification surfaces, since the digest rail does not show it.

reproduction.evidence:
I did not re-run the playtests. I read the committed digests under docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-*/ and the code.

Digests, counting "diplomatic_war_declared" in each meta.json:
