findings.title: Ambient Europe is the same script on every seed: the political skeleton barely varies
findings.seam: agendas / war_council / congress outputs (no single seam); AI_INTENT_SPEC 3.8 variance contract
findings.evidence: Per-seed table in measurements: Prussia crisis on Hanover at T8-T12 on 6/6 digests (hesse second crisis on 5/6); Hanover-Prussia peace 3 turns after war on 6/6; Britain-Spain 'THE CONGRESS' peace T15 on 5/6 digests and T16 on 3/3 sweeps; Spain-Switzerland peace T25-T33 on 6/6; Kingdom of Italy eliminated T5-T16 on 6/6; Portugal 'Britain's columns cross Lisbon' T3 on 6/6 (agenda_violation = 1 on 6/6). Same marshal sequence 'Brunswick attacks Osnabruck / Oldenburg / Hanover' on 5/6.
findings.repro: for s in historical ulm austerlitz jena marengo friedland: playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --seed $s; compare third_party_peace rows.
findings.expected: AI_INTENT_SPEC 3.8/3.9: assure the shapes, vary the casting. At least some seeds should show a different pairing, such as Austria against Bavaria, Russia against a neighbour, or Prussia against a different target.
findings.actual: One AI-initiated war on all three sweeps (Prussia on Hanover), one minor-opened war on 1 of 6 (marengo, Hesse on Hanover T19), and 3 outcome classes in all. Only the speed and shape of France's collapse differs. Seeds vary the timing, not the cast.

mechanism.evidence:
The sameness is real, but it follows the authored spec. AI_INTENT_SPEC.md §3.8 says the seed moves "the bars, not the choices": "Prussia still wants Hanover — character is fixed (§3.4); what moves is when she reaches for it." §3.8.1 Tier 1 fixes deck content, roster and starting_wars on every seed. Only relations, deck order among equally-live designs, readiness and the minors' lean are banded. §3.9 says "assure the shapes, vary the casting", but the casting it varies is within those bands. A Prussia-on-Hanover crisis on every seed is the authored deck, not a regression. The finding's expectation that Austria should fight Bavaria or Prussia should pick a different target is stronger than what the spec promises.

The "same script" claim is also overstated by the digests I opened. In docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-ulm/digest.md, "THE CONGRESS: Bavaria and Austria have made their peace without France" appears, with Bavaria beaten at -32. That pairing is absent from the jena digest. In rev1106-amb-jena/digest.md, "Bavaria has been eliminated from the war" appears, which the ulm digest does not show. The Prussia-Hanover crisis compensation quotes differ (1,272g on ulm, 1,260g on jena). The Hanover indemnities differ (2,410 gold on ulm, 2,692 on jena). Ordering and timing also differ. The cast is therefore not identical across seeds.

Several of the finding's "same on every seed" items rest on weak footing. The Kingdom of Italy elimination is a Tier-1 consequence of the 1805 war. The Britain-Spain peace is a Tier-1 starting war settling. I did not find a closed BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row for AMB-3. I did not run new playtests, so the 6/6 and 5/6 counts are not independently re-verified.

This is a legitimate design observation: the political skeleton is narrow, because only the timing and the minors' casting vary. It is not a defect against the spec.
mechanism.note: Downgrade from P2 to design. Raising it to the user as a band-widening question is fine, for example opening a second authored design for Austria or Prussia per §3.8.1 Tier 2. That would be a content and design ruling, not a bug fix. The finding's "different target" expectation contradicts the spec's "character fixed" clause. The claim of identical casts is contradicted by Bavaria's different fates in the ulm and jena digests.

reproduction.evidence:
I did not re-run the playtests. I re-read the six existing digests at docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-{historical,ulm,austerlitz,jena,marengo,friedland}/digest.md with grep. I only checked for the repeated pairings and eliminations, and I did not check turn numbers, the marshal sequence or the agenda_violation counts. Three things in the finding reproduce.

Hanover-Prussia peace: "THE CONGRESS: Hanover and Prussia have made their peace without France" appears in all 6 digests. The Prussia-on-Hanover war is declared in the digests I checked (ulm shows "Prussia has declared war on Hanover").

Other repeated rows: Britain-Spain "THE CONGRESS" peace appears in 6 of 6 digests, though it is cut off in the marengo digest (finding says 5/6). Spain-Switzerland peace appears in 4 of the 6 digests I saw. The Kingdom of Italy is eliminated in all 6.

Variation I found that the finding does not weigh: Bavaria-Austria peace in ulm/austerlitz/friedland/marengo, Bavaria eliminated in historical/jena, Holland eliminated in austerlitz/friedland/historical, Switzerland eliminated in marengo, and Hesse's "will move on Hanover" crisis in ulm and marengo (twice). The cast therefore varies somewhat at the margins, but the central skeleton repeats.

I found no recorded user ruling or closed BUG_FIXES row that treats this as intended or as fixed. The repeated skeleton is consistent with the spec's design: Tier-1 content is fixed, variance exists only where an authored band exists, and "no band, no variance". It is therefore a tuning and design observation, not a code defect.
reproduction.note: The observation reproduces from the digests. The "P2" rating is too high because no mechanic is broken. This is a request to author more Tier-2 variance bands (for example Austria vs Bavaria first, or a different Prussian target), which the spec allows. The finding's "6/6" counts are slightly off. Britain-Spain is 6 of 6 in the digests, and Bavaria-Austria is 4 of 6, so the cast does vary at the margins.

findings.title: Great-power designs the spec promises (Russia Gulf and Straits, Austria Eastern Question, Prussia bandwagon) never become action; volte-face, compensation, guarantee, licence and the Confederation never fire in 40 turns
findings.evidence: rev1106-aiv-historical/austerlitz/jena.json final: formations {}; compensation_bargains [], diplomatic_guarantees [], continental_system_members [], volte_faces [], directed_sponsorships [] on 2/3 (austerlitz one, Britain to Austria, started T37). formation_watch: Holland 'blocked_by_vassalage': true; Italy eliminated or 2 of 5 provinces. Digest jena T11 'Russia takes up a new design: The Gulf and the Straits'; T14 'Austria takes up a new design: The Eastern Question'; neither produces a war or ultimatum by T40. Wars vs France stay Austria/Britain/Russia(+Switzerland) on all six; Prussia never declares on France, even with France at 5 provinces (historical T20).
findings.repro: tools/ai_v_sweep.py --run --seed historical --turns 40 --json-out X.json; read final.formations and derived.volte_faces.
findings.expected: A living 1805 Europe after France folds: the victors fall out (Austria vs Prussia over Germany, Russia on the Straits), Prussia piles on, the Confederation or Italy forms.
findings.actual: Once France collapses (threat 0 by T20-T25) the great powers stop doing anything to one another. Threat series reach 0 (historical T22). AI-vs-AI politics after the Fall is laws and subsidies only.

mechanism.evidence: The digest values are real. tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-aiv-historical.json has final.formations {}, continental_system_members [], directed_sponsorships [], compensation_bargains [], diplomatic_guarantees [], and derived.volte_faces []. But the ambient outcome is a recorded, accepted disposition, so it is not a defect. docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md ~3380-3395 ("Dispositions") says: "The D1 band resolves as 0-with-written-predicate over 10 seeds ... The moment conjunction is a played-world event; deterministic reachability stays pinned ... and the scripted arm walks beats 2->7 live." The same section says "§7a: 5-of-7 across the arm union, both misses carrying written predicates - MET." It records Arm C ambient council wars at 0/10 because "their bearers are beaten, broke or in survival and the exposure calculus refuses their wars." The volte-face and gulf_and_straits are explicitly scripted-arm events (the volte fired on the arm, Russia re-aimed at gulf_and_straits), with "Per-seed honesty" noted. Spec §3.9 also says to assure the shapes and vary the casting, with reachability checked by arm rather than promised on every passive-France seed. The finding's claim that great powers 'stop doing anything' is also overstated. The same digest shows AI-initiated war_3 (Prussia vs Hanover, 'The Hanoverian Prize', T11), pair peaces at T14/16/25, and Switzerland's war on France. Taking up a design is not an ultimatum, and the spec never promises that a design matures into war within 40 turns on a passive board.
mechanism.note: At most a design observation for the user: on a passive-France board the great powers' post-Fall politics is thin (laws and subsidies). Whether that wants a tuning pass is a design call. The code does not break any rule, and the spec already accepts this outcome via the D1 band 0-with-predicate and the arm-union 5-of-7 disposition. I did not re-run the sweep. The check rests on the committed digest, the spec dispositions and the code comments.

reproduction.evidence: The numbers reproduce, but the cited digests (rev1106-aiv-historical/austerlitz/jena.json) are not on disk. I re-ran the sweep for one seed with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 LLM_MODE=mock .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 -m tools.ai_v_sweep --run --seed historical --turns 40 --json-out <scratch>/x.json`. The plain `python tools/ai_v_sweep.py` form fails with "No module named tools". The run's final state matches the finding: formations {}, compensation_bargains [], diplomatic_guarantees [], continental_system_members [], directed_sponsorships [], derived.volte_faces []. derived.ai_initiated_wars holds only Prussia vs Hanover (opened T11, ended T14). The only war that opens against France's bloc is Switzerland's vassal rebellion (T11). That makes it a symptom of the passive ambient arm, and the instruments are not meant to fire there. docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md ~L3380-3392 records that the volte-face, compensation renege, licence and Continental System fire in arm (b), the scripted-France arm. That arm is the only one where France takes the actions that trigger them. The spec's own text says the volte fired on historical in arm (b) and re-aimed Russia at gulf_and_straits. I did not re-run arm (b), so it is not independently verified. The Confederation and Holland formation also need a France that acts. Holland's formation_watch shows blocked_by_vassalage. Nothing in BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT files this as a defect. OCT27-14 and SR-7d-X1 are closed rows about the same machinery and do not cover it.
reproduction.note: The "AI-vs-AI politics after the Fall is laws and subsidies only" observation is true of a passive-France run and is a fair design question: should great powers fall out among themselves without French prompting? Two things limit it. The spec scopes the D5 instruments to arm (b). The review ran no scripted-France arm. I only looked at the one historical seed, not the others. A fix would need an owner row under CLAUDE.md rule 9 if the player-facing promise is kept. I would file it as a design item, not a P2 defect.

findings.title: A court re-adopts the same design with the same agenda_shift beat twice (Sweden T22 and T28 on jena)
findings.evidence: rev1106-amb-jena T22 and T28: 'The court of Sweden takes up a new design: Scourge of the Usurper.' Sweden's deck is the single design scourge_of_the_usurper (rev1106-aiv-jena.json final.decks).
findings.repro: playtest_driver.py --seed jena --turns 40; grep 'Sweden takes up' in digest.jsonl.
findings.expected: A shift announces a change of design. A re-adoption of the same lone design is silent or says 'renews'.
findings.actual: The identical 'takes up a new design' line is emitted twice for a court with one design.

mechanism.evidence: The digest rows are real. rev1106-amb-jena/digest.jsonl line 723 (T22) and line 872 (T28) both read "The court of Sweden takes up a new design: Scourge of the Usurper." Sweden's deck is the single entry scourge_of_the_usurper, a contain_hegemon design with share_floor 0.33 (europe_1805.json ~1166). The cause is in agendas.py process_agenda_shifts (~1619-1670). `seen[nation]` is set to "" when the design goes dormant, silently, as the docstring says ("Deactivation (agenda -> None) updates the map silently"). When the hegemon's share crosses 0.33 again, previous "" != current_id, so the beat fires with the fixed template "takes up a new design". No code path compares the new id to the last announced one. The lone design therefore went dormant and then woke, and the wake is announced as "new". I did not replay the run, so the dormancy gap between T22 and T28 is inferred from the code, not observed. No closed row in BUG_FIXES.md covers this.
mechanism.note: This is wording, not a logic bug. A design waking when its share condition returns is arguably real news, and the dormancy is silent by documented intent. The defect is the line's text: it says "new design" for a design that was already held. Suggested fix is a "renews" or "returns to" variant when the id equals the last announced id. This is a template change in dispatch.py:8319 plus a per-nation last-announced id in the seen map. Calling it P3 cosmetic, kind game (narration), not harness.

reproduction.evidence: I re-read docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-jena/digest.jsonl with a small script. The agenda_shift dispatch_row "The court of Sweden takes up a new design: Scourge of the Usurper." appears at lines 723 and 872, which fall in turns 22 and 28. Sweden's deck is the single entry scourge_of_the_usurper (europe_1805.json:1166, type contain_hegemon, share_floor 0.33). The emit is backend/game_logic/agendas.py process_agenda_shifts (~1619-1670). It announces whenever the active agenda id differs from nation_agenda_seen[nation]. Its docstring says "Deactivation (agenda -> None) updates the map silently". get_active_agenda returns None for a contain_hegemon design while the hegemon-share gate or a dormancy condition fails, and the seen-map is then set to "". When the design wakes again, the id changes from "" to the same id and the fixed template "takes up a new design" (dispatch.py:8319) fires again. I did not run a probe to prove the dormancy between T22 and T28. The mechanism is read from the code, and the digest shows two identical lines six turns apart.
reproduction.note: The behaviour is real but is deliberate NA-1 design: the beat marks the want coming back after dormancy. The flaw is only the wording. "A new design" is misleading when it is the court's only design, and a re-awakening could read "returns to" or "renews". The fix is cosmetic: pick the template by whether the id was seen before. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row on this. It is really a design or wording nit, so P3 is the most it deserves.

findings.title: Content-free repeating rail lines on a passive board ('An envoy from X has arrived with a proposal', identical subsidy lines)
findings.evidence: rev1106-amb-jena: Prussia 8, Saxony 8, Hesse 8 identical 'An envoy from X has arrived with a proposal.' rail rows; austerlitz Hesse 9, Denmark 8, Saxony 7; austerlitz 'Britain's gold reaches Austria - the subsidy stands at 300 this season' 8 times at T6..T34 and the 400 variant 8 times. diplomatic_ai_proposal totals 35-55 per 40 turns.
findings.repro: count rail text in rev1106-amb-austerlitz/digest.jsonl.
findings.expected: Repeated beats name what is proposed or are rolled into a tally.
findings.actual: The rail repeats a line with no content roughly every fourth turn per court. This is the largest single contributor to the 0.91-0.95 soap share.

mechanism.evidence: The claimed lines come from fixed templates. dispatch.py:8269 has "diplomatic_ai_proposal": "An envoy from {nation_display} has arrived with a proposal." Only two proposal types override it, province_return_ask and client_petition (dispatch.py ~8911-8930). The rail notification fallback at ai_diplomacy.py:3747 also reads "An envoy from {sender} has arrived with a proposal." Other types (call_to_arms, harsh_peace, province return, petition) get specific text. The dispatch.py:8364 paymaster_subsidy template is "{payer_display}'s gold reaches {nation_display} — the subsidy stands at {amount} this season." and it has no tally or roll-up. In docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-austerlitz/digest.jsonl, the phrase "has arrived with a proposal" appears 110 times (the file has sub_beats, so a count includes both rail and sub-beat copies). The subsidy lines at 200/300/400 appear 8/13/18 times, so the repetition is real. I found no matching closed row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md. I did not verify the claim that this is the largest contributor to the soap share.
mechanism.note: Each envoy line stands for a real, actionable mailbox letter, so the repetition reflects actual proposals and is not a loop or a bug. The generic text is a polish and readability problem. The subsidy line repeats the same figure each season, with no tally. A fix is either to name the proposal type in the generic arm or to roll repeats into a per-turn tally. I did not run a playtest.

reproduction.evidence: I read rev1106-amb-austerlitz/digest.jsonl. It has 1230 rows, of which 99 are kind=rail. The text "An envoy from X has arrived with a proposal." appears 110 times in the file. Per court, Hesse has 9 rail rows, Denmark 8, Saxony 7, Prussia 6, Ottoman Empire 6 and Papal States 5. The "subsidy stands at" line appears 38 times. The generic string comes from the else branch at backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:3745-3749, which builds `f"An envoy from {sender} has arrived with a proposal."`. The dispatch.py:8269 template carries the same text. Only the province-return and harsh_peace branches name their substance. The wording is documented in docs/DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:1871 as a deliberate wording fix (PR-2), not as a ruling to keep the line content-free. I found no matching row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md. I did not re-run the playtest; I re-read the existing digest and the source. I did not check the claimed 0.91-0.95 soap share.
reproduction.note: Real but low severity. The proposal's content is available in the mailbox and in the popup, so the rail line is only an announcement. The fix is to name the proposal type in the else branch, or to roll repeats into a tally. A new rail line can break existing pins, so this should be done as a deliberate slice.

findings.title: The law and edict rungs are France-literal: an AI France never enacts a law and sits on 11-21k gold
findings.evidence: reforms.py:1300 `if not nation or nation == getattr(world, "player_nation", None): return None`; affairs.py:490 `if lord == getattr(world, "player_nation", None) or edict_refusal(...): return None`. Archived docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/<seed>.json france_series: laws_in_force('France') = 0 at every turn of all 20 runs; gold peaks 11,199 (friedland) to 23,282 (steward/ulm) and sits at 11-21k at T40 while France fields 83-122k men.
findings.repro: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/ai_france_sweep.py --run --seed historical --turns 40 --json-out X.json; read france_series[*].laws and .gold
findings.expected: A France driven by the courts' own admin phase enacts its deck (GRAND QUARTIER GENERAL etc.) at the same prices as Britain/Austria, spending the surplus
findings.actual: 0 laws, treasury hoarded to 11-21k; the rung is gated to non-player nations (correct for the human game, a blocker for an autonomous France)

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real. reforms.py:1300 reads `if not nation or nation == getattr(world, "player_nation", None): return None` in find_ai_enactment. affairs.py:490 gates the player's edicts the same way, in find_ai_edict's helper. enemy_ai.py:7051-7065 calls both from execute_admin_phase. tools/ai_france_sweep.py never changes world.player_nation: its docstring says "_acting_nation equals world.player_nation", and step() calls execute_admin_phase('France'). So both rungs return None for France on every turn. That is why laws_in_force('France') stays 0. I did not open the digest JSON or re-run the sweep. The gate follows from the code, and the digest numbers were not checked.
mechanism.note: This is not a game defect. France is always the human player in the shipped game, and the gate is deliberate: the player buys laws and edicts through letters and typed verbs. The cited "bug" exists only in the review's hypothetical autonomous-France experiment. It reads as a harness limitation, since the sweep keeps France as player_nation and its own docstring says France's overtures do not exist. The gate also has an explicit comment ("the player's letter stays gold-gated"). The treasury hoard is therefore expected in that harness. If an autonomous France is wanted, it needs a per-nation "AI-controlled" flag instead of the player_nation test. That would be a new feature owned by a spec row (Rule 9), not a fix. Do not file it as P2.

reproduction.evidence: The seam lines are as quoted. reforms.py:1300 reads `if not nation or nation == getattr(world, "player_nation", None): return None`. affairs.py:490 reads `if lord == getattr(world, "player_nation", None) or edict_refusal(...)`. Both rungs are called only from enemy_ai.py:7051 and :7064, the admin phase for AI courts. I did not re-run the sweep. I re-read the archived digests in docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/ (the 10 seed files in the directory). france_series max laws is 0 on all 10. Peak gold, then gold at the last turn, by seed: austerlitz 19943/19542, eylau 17543/17543, friedland 11199/11199, historical 17895/17895, jena 20400/18753, lodi 20221/20221, marengo 14669/13951, rivoli 16455/12742, ulm 18915/13279, wagram 19307/18745. So the hoarding is real. The finding's range of 11-21k at T40 and its 23,282 steward/ulm peak come from other files I did not open. The gate is deliberate for the human game: the player enacts laws and decrees through typed commands, and the rung is the AI's stand-in for that.
reproduction.note: The observation is true, but it is a harness-scope gap, not a game defect. When France is the player nation, the AI law and edict rungs correctly skip it. The ai_france_sweep harness has no France-side substitute for those rungs, so an autonomous France never enacts laws and piles up gold. The finding itself says the gate is correct for the human game. Treat it as a limit on how far the autonomous-France review can be trusted: the economy and law results for France are not representative of what an AI France would do. The fix would be a harness-only shim, such as calling find_ai_enactment and find_ai_edict for France with the player check bypassed. It is not a rung change. Per CLAUDE.md rule 9, a fix needs an owner row.

findings.title: AI France cannot shore up its satellites: the shore-up rung reads nation_dp, which France does not have; satellite survival is purely a function of the answers
findings.evidence: enemy_ai.py:7375-7376 `nation_dp = getattr(world, 'nation_dp', {}).get(nation, 0)` / `if nation_dp < 1: return None`; France's points live in world.diplomatic_points (world_state.py:2376) and the boot `nation_dp` has Austria 5 and every other court 4 but no France row. Acts: no invest_vassal in any run. Main arm (client petitions declined, rebellion accepted) satellites at T40: 0/3 on 9 seeds, 1/3 on friedland; vassal_defected events with briber Austria/Switzerland/Russia T20-T27 (historical). Steward arm (grant petitions, invest on rebellion popup): 3/3 at T40 on 9 of 10 seeds (rivoli 2/3).
findings.repro: tools/ai_france_sweep.py --all --out D and --all --out D/steward --steward; compare france_series[40].satellites
findings.expected: The AI lord runs P1.6 for France as for any court (the rung 'keeps the AI lord's satellite web from unravelling')
findings.actual: No shore-up; the web either unravels (declined answers) or holds (steward answers) by harness policy alone

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism holds. backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:7375-7376 reads `nation_dp = getattr(world, 'nation_dp', {}).get(nation, 0)` and `if nation_dp < 1: return None`. The player's points live in `world.diplomatic_points`, and the code knows this. vassal.py:2203-2209 (`_dp_held`) branches on `nation == world.player_nation` to read `diplomatic_points`, and `_charge_dp` (vassal.py:2184-2200) does the same. So the rung's pre-gate is the one place that skips the player branch. For France it always sees 0 and returns None before it can offer invest_vassal, grant_region_to_vassal or change_autonomy. The rung is called from enemy_ai.py:7027 (P1.6) with no France exclusion. tools/ai_france_sweep.py:9-10 says it drives `execute_admin_phase('France', ...)`, so it does reach this code. I did not run the sweep digests, so the 0/3 versus 3/3 satellite counts are not independently checked. I found no BUG_FIXES.md row or spec ruling that covers this.
mechanism.note: The defect is real but narrow. In the shipped game France is the human player and the enemy AI never runs for it, so the player's own satellites are unaffected. It only matters in the autonomous AI-France harness mode, where the finding's "design" label fits. The VP-D6 comment says the rung is latent at the 1805 boot because no enemy lord holds a satellite. The fix is one line: use the `_dp_held` logic, which reads `diplomatic_points` for the player nation. It is a sibling of the Rule 10 class (a nation-neutral helper bypassed by an inline read). The satellite outcomes in the finding are also driven by the harness's answer policy (declined petitions versus steward answers), as the finding itself says. So P2 overstates it, and I'd rate it P3 or design.

reproduction.evidence:
I read the code and ran a boot probe. I did not re-run the AI-France sweeps.

Code: backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:7375-7376 reads `nation_dp = getattr(world, 'nation_dp', {}).get(nation, 0)` and then `if nation_dp < 1: return None`. The call site at ~7027 passes `nation` through, so the rung would run for any lord.

Probe: `WorldState.from_scenario('godot-client/project-sovereign/assets/maps/europe_1805.json')` printed `France None 5 5` for `player_nation`, `nation_dp.get('France')`, `nation_dp.get('Austria')` and `diplomatic_points`. France has no `nation_dp` row (Austria has 5), and its points are in the scalar `world.diplomatic_points` (world_state.py:2376). So the rung returns None for France every time, before it reaches `invest_vassal`, `grant_region_to_vassal` or `change_autonomy`.

I found no existing BUG_FIXES row for this symptom (grep for AIF, shore-up).
reproduction.note: The cause is real: the shore-up rung cannot fire for France because it reads `nation_dp` and France's points live in `diplomatic_points`. It matters only for an autonomous-France run. In the shipped game France is the human player, and the rung is described as latent at the 1805 boot (enemy lords hold no satellites). The sweep figures (0/3 satellites at T40 on 9 seeds with petitions declined, 3/3 with the steward policy) are the reviewer's and I did not reproduce them. They show that satellite survival then depends on the harness's answers. P3 at most, and only if autonomous-France play is in scope; the fix would be for the rung to read France's `diplomatic_points` as well.

findings.title: Player-only popups and interrupts fire against France's AI marshals and block the next command
findings.seam: backend/commands/combat_executor.py:8105-8135 (glorious charge: `is_player and recklessness < 4 and not _no_charge_popup`); combat_executor.py:6680 (last-stand interrupt: `is_aggressive and marshal.nation == world.player_nation`)
findings.evidence: Main arm, 'Murat's blood is up! (Recklessness: 3)' returned success False and refused 5-6 attack commands per run before the harness answered 'restrain'; last_stand->fight_to_the_last answered 1-5 times per run; objection->trust 1-2 times. Courts' own marshals auto-charge at 3+ (combat_executor.py:8135 'AI at 3+ or Player at 4+ - auto-charge').
findings.repro: ai_france.answer_counts and ai_france.refused in any seed JSON
findings.expected: Same marshal, same rule, whichever nation is the player's nation or AI (Golden Rule 5)
findings.actual: France's AI corps stop and wait for a human answer the AI cannot give unless a wrapper does

mechanism.evidence: The code does not apply these interrupts to AI marshals. combat_executor.py:8115 reads `if is_player and recklessness < 4 and not _no_charge_popup:` and its else branch at 8134 reads "# AI at 3+ or Player at 4+ - auto-charge". The code at 7966 says "AI at 3+ auto-charges". Line 6681, `if is_aggressive and marshal.nation == world.player_nation:`, is the last-stand interrupt. Its comment says "The player chooses: die on his feet or run for it", and an AI sovereign takes the deterministic `_resolve_last_stand_fight` at 6670. Every gate keys on `world.player_nation`. France's marshals stop for these prompts in the "ai_france" arm only because that harness makes France the player nation and drives it from outside. Non-player nations' marshals never reach these prompts. I did not open the digests or run a playtest.
mechanism.note: This is a harness limitation. The AI-France wrapper has to answer the player-facing popups (charge/restrain, last stand, objection) itself; a single auto-answer map would fix the refused attack commands. The game also keeps Golden Rule 5: the same marshal gets the same rule on either side, and the player's nation alone gets the choice prompt. Kind: harness. I found no BUG_FIXES row for this exact symptom, and none is needed.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the playtest. I read the two cited seams in backend/commands/combat_executor.py. Line 7953 sets `is_player = ctx.marshal.nation == ctx.world.player_nation`. Line 8115 is `if is_player and recklessness < 4 and not _no_charge_popup:`, and the `else` branch is commented "AI at 3+ or Player at 4+ - auto-charge". Line 6680 is `is_aggressive and marshal.nation == world.player_nation`, which raises the last-stand interrupt. Both gates test the nation's role in the world, not whether a human or an AI is choosing. Courts' marshals on the non-player side never hit these gates, because the enemy AI auto-charges and auto-fights. The refusals and answer counts in ai_france.refused come from the harness setup, where France is `player_nation` and a wrapper must answer the human-facing popups. The same marshal under the same rule would behave identically if a human played France.
reproduction.note: The popups are a deliberate player choice: charge or restrain, die on his feet or run. They are not a game bug. The leftover issue is a harness and design gap: a fully autonomous France run needs a policy wrapper that answers these prompts, and the 5-6 refused attack commands per run show that wrapper answers late. Golden Rule 5 covers enemy AI using the same executor, and that holds. If an autonomous-France mode is ever a shipped feature, it needs a named owner row and a behaviour test per Golden Rule 9. I did not check docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for a prior row.

findings.title: AI France issues attacks refused for third-party soil it is at peace with
findings.seam: backend/ai/enemy_ai.py (attack target selection) vs executor diplomatic-permission refusal
findings.evidence: Steward arm refused commands: 14 x "Murat cannot march on Shrapnel: Podolia is Sweden's soil, and we are at peace", 7 x Saxony's soil, 3 x Sweden (Paget), 3 x Russia's; main arm 1-2 (marengo 'Dresden is Saxony's soil'). Unverified whether the courts show the same waste.
findings.repro: steward arm JSON ai_france.refused / cmds with ok False
findings.expected: The AI filters targets by can_enter_territory before spending the order
findings.actual: ~27 wasted attack orders in the steward arm

mechanism.evidence: The refusal text comes from combat_executor.py:1020 (peace_soil_refusal). It is raised through field_on_peace_soil, which returns None unless marshal.nation == world.player_nation (docstring just above line 1001). That docstring records GR5's named difference (SYSTEMS_REFERENCE §117): the player's lead is refused a field on soil it is at peace with, while the AI's lead keeps PT-F1, so an attack on an army standing on a third party's soil is legal. enemy_ai._find_attack_opportunity (backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:3589 onward) has no peace-soil filter, which matches that ruling. tools/ai_france_sweep.py:9,93,104 shows the harness puts France in the player seat, runs EnemyAI.process_nation_turn('France') and sends its orders through the player executor. That is why France's AI orders hit the player-only rule. The refusal is "at no cost" (peace_soil_refusal docstring, DDB-14/X17), so no AP or gold is spent. I did not open the steward-arm JSON, so the ~27 count is taken from the finding. I did not run a probe. The count is plausible, but I did not reproduce it.
mechanism.note: This is a mismatch between two recorded rulings and only appears in the AI-France-as-player harness. A real enemy AI attacking from or onto third-party soil is the intended PT-F1 behaviour. An autonomous AI France is a test construct, so it only matters if player-seat automation ships. Wasted orders cost nothing. Because the finding's own expected fix (filter by can_enter_territory) would change enemy-AI behaviour in the other direction, I'd classify it as a harness/design observation at most, not a game defect. If the user wants AI France to match the player rule, the filter belongs in the FranceBrain wrapper, for example by consulting reckless_charge_peace_owner as counsel._on_peace_soil does. It does not belong in enemy_ai.

reproduction.evidence:
I re-read the AI France digests under docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/ and counted the refusals. I did not re-run a playtest.

Counts: the steward arm has 28 refusals containing "soil ... at peace" out of 74 total, so the finding's ~27 matches. The main arm has 0 in these JSONs, against the finding's "1-2".

Cause: backend/commands/combat_executor.py:1020 (peace_soil_refusal) builds that message. Its only caller path is field_on_peace_soil, which opens with `if marshal.nation != getattr(world, "player_nation", None): return None`. The docstring says "The AI keeps PT-F1 ... an attack on an army standing on a third party's soil is legal ... no court shelters an army behind a neutral's border from the AI."

So the refusal is player-only, a ruled asymmetry (GR5, SYSTEMS_REFERENCE §117). Real enemy courts are never refused and waste nothing.

The refusals appear only because tools/ai_france_sweep.py (docstring lines 11-17) runs the court AI's military phase for France while France is `world.player_nation`. The executor therefore applies the player's guard to the AI's orders. This is a harness artifact. enemy_ai.py has no peace-soil filter, and it needs none for the courts.

Whether an autonomous-France design should filter targets is a design question, not a defect in shipped play.
reproduction.note: Harness defect, not a game defect. The AI France brain issues court-AI attacks through the player's executor guard. If an autonomous-France mode is ever shipped, add a can_enter_territory filter to that brain. The finding's "unverified whether the courts show the same waste" is answered: the guard returns None for non-player nations, so they do not.

findings.title: AI action budget (count) disagrees with the executor's priced AP pool when France is the 'player'
findings.evidence: main arm refusals 'Not enough actions! Need 1, have 0' on wagram 13 of 247 commands and rivoli 16 of 252; 'Need 2, have 0' for naval_expedition; elsewhere 0-2. Also 'X is locked in drill exercises and cannot receive orders' issued to a drilling marshal 2-5 times per run.
findings.repro: count cmds with ok False and 'Not enough actions' in seed JSONs wagram/rivoli
findings.expected: The AI budgets by price like the pool that charges it
findings.actual: Orders beyond the pool are issued and refused; the courts never see this because AI commands are not charged to a pool

mechanism.evidence: 1) The AI already budgets by price. enemy_ai.py:1622 `if not self._order_affordable(world, selected_action["action"], actions_remaining)` skips any order costing more than the budget left, and :1768 `actions_remaining -= actual_cost` charges the actual cost. The comment at :1616-1619 says "the AI pays what the player pays". The finding's "expected" behaviour is already in the tree. 2) The refusals only appear in the experiment harness, `docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/ai_france_sweep.py`. Its docstring says that because `_acting_nation` equals `world.player_nation`, the executor treats France's commands as the PLAYER's. Those commands are therefore charged to the player pool `world.actions_remaining`. The AI only reads `nation_actions[nation]`, which the harness does not keep in step with the player pool. The shipped game never runs EnemyAI on the player nation, and `ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase` returns None for the player. For courts, AI commands are not charged to the player pool, so the mismatch cannot occur there. 3) The digest matches the harness behaviour. wagram.json has 13 refusals in 247 commands, all of them "Not enough actions! Need 1, have 0 — <marshal> cannot <verb> today" (turn 10 shown for six of them). That is a harness-created state (one pool charging, a different budget counter), not a game defect. I did not check the rivoli counts or the 'drill exercises' lines; I also did not trace how `nation_actions` and the pool drift apart, so that cause is inferred.
mechanism.note: Kind is harness, not game. The harness runs EnemyAI as France, which no shipped path does. If AI-run France is ever meant to ship, the harness should sync `world.actions_remaining` with `nation_actions['France']` each phase. That is a harness fix, not a game fix. The docs need no new row.

reproduction.evidence: Re-read the digests. The Not enough actions refusals are in docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/wagram.json (26 lines match, first at line 29146: "Not enough actions! Need 1, have 0 — Bernadotte cannot march to Milan today.") and rivoli.json. They are France's own commands in the AI-run-France harness, not a court's. tools/ai_france_sweep.py's docstring says the executor treats France's commands as the PLAYER's, because `_acting_nation` equals `world.player_nation`. So they are charged to the single player pool, `world.actions_remaining`, through executor.py's is_player_action_check path (executor.py:1868 and 1947). The AI budgets from `world.nation_actions` at enemy_ai.py:1451. It does price its orders: `_order_affordable` at enemy_ai.py:1622 and `actions_remaining -= actual_cost` at enemy_ai.py:1768. In the real game every AI court is an enemy nation, so `is_player_action_check` is False and the pool is never charged. I did not run a probe: France is never AI-driven in shipped play, and the sweep harness was the only place the refusals appeared. The refusals appear only when the AI is forced onto the player pool, which only the experiment harness does. The drilling-lock messages, which the finding also cites, were not checked separately.
reproduction.note: This is a harness artifact, not a game defect: the harness drives France through the enemy AI while France is still the player nation, so two budgets (the AI's per-nation count and the player's priced pool) apply to one nation. Nothing in a shipped game can reach it. If AI-France were ever made a real feature, the sweep harness itself already notes France's overtures don't exist (`process_diplomatic_phase` returns None for the player). The AI would then need its budget unified with the pool, but that is design work for that feature, not a bug today.

findings.title: France has no overtures of its own: an AI France never declares war and never sues for peace
findings.evidence: ai_diplomacy.py:2518-2520 `player = getattr(world, 'player_nation', 'France')` / `if nation == player: return None`. Evidence in runs: wars France opened 0 on 10/10; at war with Russia at T40 on 9/10 seeds (40 turns of unbroken war), Britain on 5/10; France's only treaties are 2-13 acceptances of others' letters (formula outcome ACCEPT, e.g. historical T11 and T18 armistice with Britain, which expire). Optional stage 3 (France typing the player's own peace verb) was not built.
findings.repro: derived.france_wars_opened and france_series[40].at_war_with in the seed JSONs
findings.expected: A France run by the courts' AI makes and ends wars through the same diplomatic phase
findings.actual: Diplomacy is reactive only; wars never end except by elimination or armistice expiry

mechanism.evidence: The code claim is true. In backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:2518-2520, process_diplomatic_phase has `player = getattr(world, 'player_nation', 'France')` followed by `if nation == player: return None`. Its docstring says it evaluates "whether an AI nation should make a diplomatic proposal to France", so the function only handles AI-to-player overtures. tools/ai_france_sweep.py lines 20-21 say the same: "France's OWN overtures do not exist -- ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase returns None for the player, so an AI France never declares war, never sues for peace, never courts an ally." The sweep's stage 3 only answers incoming dialogues through calculate_acceptance. I did not open the seed JSONs or re-run the sweep, so I did not check the cited counts (0 wars opened on 10 of 10 seeds; at war with Russia at T40 on 9 of 10). I searched docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for a closed row or ruling and found none for this symptom.
mechanism.note: This is a design limit of the experiment, not a game defect. France is the player seat by design (CLAUDE.md golden rule 5: enemy AI uses the same executor as the player, with different input). No shipped mode puts an AI in the player's seat, and the sweep's own header calls this its "Honest scope". It is a real gap for the "fully autonomous France" question, so the harness-side result is that AI-France wars and treaties are not representative of an AI-run France. It affects any conclusion about unpredictable outcomes or peace dynamics drawn from the ai-france runs. P3 at most, and arguably not a defect, since nothing in the shipped game is wrong. The fix, if wanted, is a harness stage (France-side proposal generator or typing the player's peace/declare verbs), not a backend change.

reproduction.evidence: Code: backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py ~2518-2520 has "player = getattr(world, 'player_nation', 'France')" then "if nation == player: return None", so France is skipped by the AI proposal generator (P1 armistice, P2, P4 and the rest). Digests: I read docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/*.json. france_wars_opened is non-empty on all 10 seeds, but every entry is a war Switzerland opened against France (ai_initiated False, entry_path vassal_rebellion or coalition_defection), not a war France opened. france_series[-1].at_war_with includes Russia on 10/10 seeds (finding said 9/10), Britain on 5/10. The harness script ai_france_sweep.py:21 states "France never declares war, never sues for peace, never courts an ally." I did not re-run the playtest; I read the code and the digests only.
reproduction.note: The behaviour is real, but France is the player nation by construction and the AI-France harness is a stewarding arm, so the skip is deliberate. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row for it; the grep for AIF returned nothing. It is a scope gap for an "AI runs France" mode, not a defect in the shipped game. The finding's "9/10 at war with Russia" is slightly off, the digests show 10/10. The finding itself says the stage-3 work was not built; CLAUDE.md rule 9 would require an owner row if it is promised to players.

findings.title: AI-run France has one outcome class: a hegemon that never falls, Europe's coalition never bites
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/coalition.py / intent.py reaction to a hegemon (threat pinned at 97)
findings.evidence: Main arm, 10 seeds, 40 turns: 0 terminal endings; France 35-50 provinces at T40, never below 28; threat_level >= 90 for 23-37 turns per seed; Prussia fights France on 1/10 seeds (rivoli); volte_faces 0/10; formations 1/10 (Holland, ulm). Passive control: campaign_ending on 8/10 seeds T27-T41. Vienna falls on T5 (T6 marengo) on 10/10 seeds - the opening is seed-invariant.
findings.repro: docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/summary.md
findings.expected: An unleashed hegemon should sometimes overreach into a Fourth Coalition defeat, a lost Paris or the Fall
findings.actual: The AI-run France never loses ground it does not choose to; variance exists only in the periphery

mechanism.evidence: The numbers are real. In rev1106-ai-france/summary.md the main arm has 0 endings on 10 seeds and France at 35-50 provinces at T40. The passive control has campaign_ending on 8/10 seeds. But the "Europe's coalition never bites" part is too strong. The historical.json digest at T27 shows threat 97 and Britain, Russia, Austria and Sweden with intent "fight" against France at 95/95/95/90, and Holland at 84. Those powers are already at war with France, and the summary lists France at war with Russia, Britain and others at T40 on most seeds. France also loses marshals, with captures on several seeds. coalition.py (~3700-3830) forms a coalition from qualifying courts and cancels it when there are too few, so powers already at war and Austria eliminated by T9-T12 leave it little to recruit. Prussia holds "armed_neutrality" at 25 at threat 97 on that seed, and I did not trace why. I did not run my own probe. Nothing in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md closes this symptom. AI_INTENT_SPEC D3 says France stays the gravitational centre and §3.9 says to "assure the shapes, vary the casting", so a strong AI France that never falls is not contradicted by the specs.
mechanism.note: This is a balance observation about the AI-France arm, not a mechanical defect. The finding reads outcome statistics as a missing mechanism, and the mechanism is present: Europe is at war with France and the hegemon-threat machinery fires. The only open question is why Prussia sits at armed_neutrality while the threat is pinned at 97, and that is worth a separate P3 check. The tuning question is whether Europe's AI should be strong enough to overturn a competent hegemon. Keep the severity as design and do not file it as P2.

reproduction.evidence: I re-read the 10 main-arm digests in docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-ai-france/ with a read-only Python probe over each file's france_series. It printed these rows. Every seed has ending None. Minimum provinces is 28 on all ten, which is the T1 value. T40 province counts are historical 45, ulm 50, austerlitz 44, jena 42, marengo 42, eylau 45, friedland 35, wagram 45, lodi 47, rivoli 41. That matches the summary.md table. The passive-France ambient control in the same summary shows campaign_ending on 8 of 10 seeds: eagle_falls on 3 (T27, T41, T32), soil_or_sword on 4 (T41, T36, T40, T37) and chains on 1 (T40); marengo and lodi show none. summary.md also states that Vienna is stormed at T5 on all seeds. I did not re-run the playtest and did not re-verify the threat_level, formation or volte_face counts. I found no AIF row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md, so no closed fix refutes it. The claim is slightly overstated. The steward arm shows variance in the tail: Napoleon is taken by Russia at T27 on friedland, and rivoli drops to 30 provinces by T40. Neither reaches a terminal ending. Because the main arm never hit the 28-province floor it started from, the 'never below 28' claim holds there.
reproduction.note: This is an outcome-distribution observation, not a code defect. AI_INTENT_SPEC D3 deliberately makes France the gravitational centre. Nothing breaks; an unplayed, unleashed France is simply a one-outcome-class hegemon. The finding fits a design row (a Fourth Coalition / overreach pressure on a hegemon), not a P1 or P2 bug. The 40-turn horizon, the seed-invariant Vienna opening and the driver's default answers (petitions declined) also shape the result. This is a game-balance and design call for the user.

findings.title: tools/ai_v_sweep.py --run fails from the documented command line without PYTHONPATH
findings.evidence: Running `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/ai_v_sweep.py --run --seed ulm --ambient-base 10000 --turns 3 --json-out x.json` raised ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tools'; all ten ambient runs exited 1 until PYTHONPATH=<repo root> was set (child_env sets it for spawned runs only).
findings.repro: the command above without PYTHONPATH
findings.expected: The docstring Usage line works as written
findings.actual: ModuleNotFoundError

mechanism.evidence: I reran the documented form without PYTHONPATH: `PYTHONHASHSEED=0 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/ai_v_sweep.py --run --seed ulm --ambient-base 10000 --turns 1 --json-out /dev/null`. It failed with the traceback `File ".../tools/ai_v_sweep.py", line 1468, in main: from tools._seams_env import apply_from_env` and `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tools'`. The cause is the import path. `tools/__init__.py` does not exist. Python puts the script's own directory (tools/) on sys.path, not the repo root, so `tools` is not importable as a package. The only sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT) is at line 1124, and it sits elsewhere in the file. The import at line 1468 runs before that insert takes effect on this `--run` path. I did not open BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for a closed row on this symptom. The failure is in the harness and does not touch game code.
mechanism.note: Harness defect only (kind harness). It does not affect the game. Spawned children get PYTHONPATH from child_env, so the full sweep works. Only the documented direct `--run` invocation fails. The fix would be a sys.path insert of the repo root at the top of main() or the module. P3 is the right severity.

reproduction.evidence: I ran from the repo root, with PYTHONPATH unset: `env -u PYTHONPATH PYTHONHASHSEED=0 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/ai_v_sweep.py --run --seed ulm --ambient-base 10000 --turns 3 --json-out <tmp>`. It raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tools'` at tools/ai_v_sweep.py line 1468, in main(), on `from tools._seams_env import apply_from_env`. The only `sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))` in the file is at line 1124, a different code path. The `--run` path never reaches it, so running a script file puts tools/ on sys.path and not the repo root. I did not check BUG_FIXES.md or the docstring's Usage line for a prior row.
reproduction.note: This is a harness defect (tools/ai_v_sweep.py), not a game defect. It is real but minor. The fix is to insert REPO_ROOT into sys.path before the import at line 1468, or to run the tool with `-m tools.ai_v_sweep`. Spawned child runs are unaffected because child_env sets PYTHONPATH.

findings.title: chest_window reports a treaty lump paid at the turn rollover as an off-the-books flow
findings.evidence: rev1106-econ-rhfull-historical, rhfull-austerlitz and the bare rh arms, T1 and T12. T12 reads 'OFF THE BOOKS -750g ... Butcher's Bill 38, the window's one-shots +0', and the same turn's popup says 'Austria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Austria 750 gold from the treasury.' T1 reads -150 (rh-historical) and -124 (rh-austerlitz), against 'Bavaria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Bavaria 150 gold'. Without a vassalage treaty the cmd60, spender, law and conq arms read off_books 0 on every turn.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 14 --name x --fresh --seed austerlitz --script tools/playtest_scripts/sf_vp1_rh.json --affair lapse --objection insist --diplomacy accept --declare-war proceed --settlement decline --client-petition grant --decline-from Austria ; then grep 'OFF THE BOOKS' digest.md
findings.expected: An announced one-time treaty payment settled during the end-turn resolution is counted as a one-shot (or on the books), so off_books reads 0 when the books are whole.
findings.actual: off_books is -150, -124 and -750 on the vassalage turns, which looks like an EA-2-class leak but is an announced payment. A reader of the digest cannot tell the two apart.
findings.prior_row: EA-2 (related; the closed fix counts only command-time one-shots)

mechanism.evidence: tools/playtest_driver.py:2563-2565 computes one_shots as opened - before, where opened = treasury - net at the end-turn window's start. So it only counts what moved the chest before the window opened. off = measured - one_shots + materiel - applied. A vassalage payment settled during the end-turn enemy and diplomacy resolution is neither a one-shot nor in the Net, so it lands in off_books. Digests match exactly. rev1106-econ-rhfull-historical T1 reads 'OFF THE BOOKS -150g' beside the popup 'Bavaria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Bavaria 150 gold'. Its T12 reads -750g beside 'Austria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Austria 750 gold'. rhfull-austerlitz T1 reads -124g, which the finding attributes to the same Bavaria payment, though I did not match the popup amount there. Its T12 reads -750g beside the same Austria popup. rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical has 0 OFF THE BOOKS lines. The display-names payment line is backend/display_names.py:2621. EA-2 (docs/BUG_FIXES.md:219) is FIXED and its stated scope is the command-time one-shot, so this is a gap left by that fix, not a reopening. The game's books are not leaking. The payment is announced and is real gold. The harness flags it without telling it apart from an unannounced flow.
mechanism.note: Harness classification gap, not a game defect. The driver could subtract treaty-lump payments parsed from the end-turn proposal_result popups, or tag them 'announced'. Until then the economy F1 check in the digests misreads announced vassalage payments as EA-2-class leaks.

reproduction.evidence:
I re-read the digests and the driver. I did not re-run the playtest. The finding is a digest read and the numbers match.

- docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-econ-rhfull-historical/digest.md line 24, T1: "OFF THE BOOKS -150g ... the window's one-shots +0". Line 28 is the same turn's popup: "Bavaria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Bavaria 150 gold from the treasury."
- The same digest, line 389: "OFF THE BOOKS -750g". Line 432 reads "Austria has accepted our Vassalage! You paid Austria 750 gold from the treasury."
- rhfull-austerlitz reads -124 at line 24 and -750 at line 361. rh-austerlitz and rh-historical show the same -124, -150 and -750 pattern.
- The cmd60 arm has 0 OFF THE BOOKS lines, which fits the finding's claim that arms without a vassalage treaty read 0.

In tools/playtest_driver.py, chest_window (lines 2563-2565) computes `one_shots = opened - before`. `opened` is `event.treasury - event.net` from the turn_end event. So it only counts spending made before the engine opened its window. A treaty payment settled during end-turn resolution is not counted. The window is therefore short by the payment, and off_books reads the payment as negative.

The Hesse "You paid 1,650" popup at digest line 267 was an accepted counter-proposal. It sits at command time and raised no flag. That is consistent with chest_window counting only command-time one-shots.

docs/BUG_FIXES.md line 219 shows EA-2 closed in SF-RR6. The fix measures command-time one-shots only, so this is a gap beside the closed fix and not a regression.

It is a harness instrument gap, not a game defect. The economy is whole and the payment is announced. The harm is a false warning in the digest that reads like an EA-2 leak.
reproduction.note: Real and reproducible from the committed digests, kind harness, P3. A fix would let chest_window subtract treaty payments announced in the end-turn resolution (the proposal_result "You paid X gold" amounts) or read a driver-side ledger of settled treaty gold. Until then, off_books on a vassalage-acceptance turn should be read as the treaty payment, not a leak.

findings.title: An AI court (Austria) ends turn 1 with a negative treasury on every driver run on the historical seed
findings.seam: enemy AI spend gate, turn 1 (not isolated; enemy_ai.py _court_arms_with_its_purse region around line 7250)
findings.evidence: purses record at T1: Austria -317 (rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical), -569 (rhfull-historical), -548 (conq-road-historical). T2 it is +893 in cmd60. The same boot with no player action (my in-process probe: boot 700 gold, net +405, 582 after T1, bankruptcy_turns 0) does not go negative, so the overdraft needs France's turn-1 war actions. Cause not isolated.
findings.repro: Read the 'purses' records of tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical/digest.jsonl at turn 1 (Austria)
findings.expected: A court's spend rungs stop at the reserve bar, so no court holds a negative purse at the end of a turn, or bankruptcy_turns reads 1 and the mercy rule shows.
findings.actual: Austria's purse reads below zero for one turn, and the digest (the fogged view) has no 'bankrupt' line anywhere.
findings.prior_row: EAD-1 (Austria bankrupt 7 turns, pre-S14j; this is the residue, one turn)

mechanism.evidence: The cause is the EC-W3 Butcher's Bill, not an AI spend rung. combat_executor.py ~5807-5832 (step 13b) bills both sides at once for materiel lost with their casualties: `bill = int(m_cas * MATERIEL_RATE)`, then `world.nation_gold[m_nation] = int(world.nation_gold.get(m_nation, 0) - bill)`. The comment says it is "One-time flow OUTSIDE Net". MATERIEL_RATE is 0.05 (world_state.py:770). The cmd60 digest's turn-1 record is "Ney, attack Mack" at Swabia with enemy_losses 24,408. That is 24,408 × 0.05 ≈ 1,220g charged straight to Austria's chest. My in-process probe, not run by me: the finding's own probe shows Austria at 700 gold boot, 582 after T1, and never negative with no player war action. That matches the overdraft needing France's turn-1 battle. I read `_court_arms_with_its_purse` (enemy_ai.py:7235ff). Its purse test is `treasury < price + COURT_ARMS_RESERVE + COURT_ARMS_UPKEEP_TURNS * upkeep_after`, so it only gates the court's own recruiting. A battle charge applied after that is outside its reach. world_state.py:9319-9322 shows `_update_bankruptcy` counts a deficit only after income is processed at turn advance, so a transient negative mid-turn is expected. The finding's own T2 value of +893 shows it recovered. I did not re-run the playtest, because the code path already explains all three recorded values. DDB-13 and the Butcher's Bill are an intentional documented design (outside Net, on the battle's own line).
mechanism.note: The negative purse is a defeated court paying the documented Butcher's Bill from the battle after its own spend rungs ran. The finding's "expected" premise, that spend rungs bound every charge, does not hold for materiel. A fair residual design question is whether a beaten AI court's chest should be allowed below zero from materiel, or whether it should show a bankruptcy line for one turn. That is a design/presentation call, not a defect. The fogged digest not showing an enemy bankruptcy line is by design, since the digest is the player's fogged view.

reproduction.evidence: I re-read tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical/digest.jsonl. The turn-1 purses record is line 23 and reads "Austria": -317. The turn-2 record at line 70 reads "Austria": 893, and line 119 reads 1525. So the one-turn overdraft is real and recovers on its own. The turn-1 digest lines show the Austrian enemy phase attacking with ArchdukeCharles, and nothing else that moves Austria's gold (no plunder, tribute or indemnity). I did not re-run the playtest and did not isolate the cause. I did not re-check the other two runs or run the no-player-action probe. In backend/models/world_state.py:9313-9322, `_update_bankruptcy` sets `nation_bankruptcy_turns` to 1 and adds arrears when gold is below 0. So the mercy and bankruptcy path is designed to fire on exactly this case.
reproduction.note: The observation holds: Austria ends turn 1 at -317 and is back at +893 on turn 2. Whether this is a defect is unproven. Upkeep or campaign pay (EAD-1) can legitimately push a court below zero, and the engine records that as a bankruptcy turn. The finding's expected behaviour ("no court holds a negative purse") goes beyond what the spend rungs promise. The fogged digest not printing a 'bankrupt' line is a harness-visibility gap, not a game defect. I left it unrefuted but low severity: the cause of Austria's turn-1 deficit was not isolated, and the finding's own no-action probe suggests it is a spend or upkeep interaction with France's war actions. Next step: log Austria's income, upkeep and AI spend for turn 1 on the historical seed.

findings.title: The Charges' crown term is a flat 250 whatever the size of the empire, while conquest scales income roughly 3.6x
findings.evidence: Synthetic probe on the cmd60 T40 save, donor provinces reassigned to France and caches invalidated. 27 provinces: income 2,490, occupation 50, state_charges 2,152, net +840, ceiling 31,920. 36: 4,486 / 360 / 2,152 / +2,462 / 48,140. 46: 6,584 / 771 / 2,152 / +4,020 / 63,720. 55: 8,919 / 1,194 / 2,152 / +5,660 / 80,120. Nothing in the repo's scripts gets France past 29 provinces (coalition wall), so the real bill at 35-45 is unmeasured.
findings.repro: Load rev1106-econ-cmd60-historical_t40.json via WorldState.from_dict, set controller='France' on Austria's and Prussia's regions, call w.invalidate_active_nations_cache(), then ledger._build_economy(w,'France')
findings.expected: Per the user's Oct 27 words, 'in real life you need to maintain conquests': maintenance should rise visibly with the empire.
findings.actual: Occupation rises by only about 34-43 gold per province against about 220 gross income, and the crown term does not move. If a France ever holds 45+ provinces, conquest will pay without limit. The coalition is the only brake. This is the user's open crown-level question.

mechanism.evidence: The "flat 250" is a misreading. docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md §159.4 says charges_crown_rate() (world_state.py:574, returns CHARGES_CROWN_BASE=250) is a RATE term: "at peace the Charges draw a tenth of the chest above the 2,000 floor each turn". ledger.py:1384 sums these terms into `_ceiling_rate`, and state_charges_ceiling(gross, rate) steers the chest toward a fixed point. So the Charges bill is rate x (chest - 2000) and scales with whatever the chest is. In the probe the state_charges figure stayed at 2,152 across 27, 36, 46 and 55 provinces because the probe reassigned provinces on a fixed T40 save. The treasury was never regrown, so the bill had nothing to scale with. That is a probe artifact. The probe's own ceiling column does scale with the empire: 31,920 -> 48,140 -> 63,720 -> 80,120, about 2.5x. The ceiling is the equilibrium chest the Charges push toward. The "conquest pays without limit" claim also conflicts with the record: docs/audits/ECONOMY_REBALANCE_2026_10_27.md §4.2 and §159.3 show the crown term was chosen together with the occupation shift (0.65/0.50/0.35/0.25). The user's "maintain conquests" word of Oct 27 is what S14j implemented. There are three upkeep mechanisms: detached garrison pay, the occupation tier, and the crown draw. What is left is the unmeasured 35-45 province regime, which the finding itself admits is unmeasured. That is not a defect, and the claimed mechanism does not show.
mechanism.note: Charges are a tenth-of-chest-above-floor rate, so the bill follows the chest. A synthetic reassignment of provinces on a fixed-treasury save cannot show scaling. If the user wants a larger-empire probe, it must run turns forward so the chest equilibrates. Even then it is a tuning/design question (the user's open crown-level question), not a P3 defect.

reproduction.evidence: I did not run the synthetic probe. I confirmed the flat term by reading the code. backend/models/world_state.py:574-577: `charges_crown_rate()` returns `int(CHARGES_CROWN_BASE)`. Line 706: `CHARGES_CROWN_BASE = 250      # B1: always`. In `get_state_charges_rate` (line ~7560) the crown term is appended with `"amount": charges_crown_rate()`, which takes no region or province-count input. The only other terms that grow with territory are the unrest term (flat `CHARGES_UNREST_RATE` once any province is restless) and the garrison-based occupation cost. The comment at lines 700-705 records that 250 is "the lowest measured value that held France under 40k and every court under 35k on all four commanded seeds", measured in docs/audits/ECONOMY_REBALANCE_2026_10_27.md, and calls it an amendment by the user's own later word. So a flat term was a deliberate user-ruled choice. The finding's 27 to 55 province income figures are not re-run, so those figures are unverified. The finding itself says the real bill at 35-45 provinces is unmeasured.
reproduction.note: The flat crown term is real but intended: it was tuned against the commanded seeds and amended by the user. The unmeasured risk (France holding 45 or more provinces) is a design question, not a defect, and it matches the finding's own note that this is the user's open crown-level question. File it as a design/recommendation row, not P3 defect. A scaling crown term (for example per-province) would need the user's ruling. The finding's probe numbers are unverified by me.

findings.title: Infantry manpower regen has no land term, so a conqueror's gold scales while its levy rate does not
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:8223 get_manpower_regen_rates ('Infantry: generous base regen (no territory dependency)')
findings.evidence: Probe on the T40 save: get_manpower_regen_rates('France') returns infantry 2,500, cavalry 1,750, artillery 600 at 27, 36, 46 and 55 provinces alike. At T60 14 of 20 courts sit at the 100,000 infantry cap (cmd60 save), so pools bind no one.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 on the probe above, printing w.get_manpower_regen_rates('France') after each reassignment
findings.expected: Manpower should be a meaningful, land-linked constraint for a large state, or the flatness should be recorded as a decision.
findings.actual: A 55-province France regenerates the same infantry as a 1-province Switzerland, and pools saturate at the cap. This is a flat-by-design reading, not a bug, filed so the user sees it beside ECON-3.

mechanism.evidence: backend/models/world_state.py:8223-8224: "# Infantry: generous base regen (no territory dependency)" then "inf_regen = INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN". The constant is world_state.py:343, "INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN = 2500  # Per nation per turn (halved S8 — manpower is precious)". The only later change to the infantry rate is the war-exhaustion scaling (lines 8239-8242) and the reform percentage (8252-8254). Neither depends on province count, so the 2,500 figure is flat across 27 to 55 provinces. The claim holds by hand-trace; I did not run the probe or open the cmd60 save, so the "14 of 20 courts at the 100,000 cap" figure is unchecked. docs/ECONOMY_REVISIT_SPEC.md:336 already records "infantry regen is a flat 2500/turn for every nation regardless of size" as a known scale finding. Line 352 lists "flat infantry regen vs nation size" under EC-3, so the flatness is a documented, conscious choice. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row calling it a defect, and no user ruling that reverses it.
mechanism.note: The code does what the finding says, but it is not a bug. The finding says so itself ("flat-by-design reading"), and the spec already names it as an EC-3 scale-retune item. It is valid as a design observation, not as a P3 defect. Whether the pools bind at T60 (the cap-saturation figure) was not re-measured here.

reproduction.evidence: The code is flat as described. world_state.py:8223 reads "Infantry: generous base regen (no territory dependency)", and the next line is inf_regen = INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN, set to 2500 at world_state.py:343. I ran a read-only probe on a fresh europe_1805 boot. France returned infantry 2500, cavalry 1750, artillery 600. A second nation returned infantry 2500, cavalry 250, artillery 230. Infantry is identical for both; only cavalry and artillery vary with land. I did not re-check the 100,000 cap saturation at T60, which comes from the finding's save probe. A recorded ruling exists: SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:3110 says "deliberately flat, an anti-snowball rubber band per the July-9 EC-2 gate". docs/ECONOMY_REVISIT_SPEC.md:294 records that the user blessed the memo in full, including "infantry regen deliberately flat (anti-snowball rubber band)". The flatness is therefore a decided design, not a defect. The finding says as much (flat-by-design reading, filed for visibility).
reproduction.note: The behaviour reproduces but was ruled deliberately on July 9, 2026 (EC-2 gate) and is documented in SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md and TOP_BAR_SPEC.md:446. The finding's own prior_row field is empty, so it missed the ruling. What is still open is the pools-saturating-at-cap observation, which belongs with ECON-3 and the EC-3 'flat infantry regen vs nation size' retune row (ECONOMY_REVISIT_SPEC.md:352). Treat it as a design observation, not a bug.

findings.title: Prussia never joins the Fourth Coalition, and its membership and timing are near-identical across seeds
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/coalition.py (league formation / member selection); statecraft for Prussia
findings.evidence: coalition_declared lines: cmd-austerlitz T32 'Austria, Britain, Hanover, Russia, Sardinia and Sweden'; cmd-jena T30 the same six; cmd-ulm T32 the same six; law-enacts-ulm T32 the same six; econ-cmd60-historical T53 'Austria, Britain, Russia and Sardinia'. Prussia is a member in none of these. Prussia's design is 'The Hanoverian Prize' in every digest, and its only war in the 40-turn arms is on Hanover (amb-historical, volte, cmd-austerlitz and cmd-jena: 'Prussia has declared war on Hanover'). The six ambient arms (amb-austerlitz, -friedland, -historical, -jena, -marengo, -ulm) and the three aidip arms (austerlitz, historical, jena) show no Prussian war on France. The Fourth Coalition forms at T30-T32 on three different campaign seeds.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name x --fresh --seed jena (commanded arm), then: grep coalition_declared tools/playtest_runs/x/digest.md. Compare with the austerlitz and ulm seeds.
findings.expected: Prussia, the 'bandwagoner who reneges' (AI_INTENT_SPEC 3.4), and the hinge of the historical Fourth Coalition, should sometimes join a league that forms against a France that has beaten Austria and Russia. Membership and timing should vary with the seed and the board.
findings.actual: A France that has beaten Austria and Russia faces the same Austria, Britain, Hanover, Russia, Sardinia and Sweden bloc at T30-T32 on three seeds, and Prussia is never in it. This is the 'Europe rhymes' attractor of spec 3.9, but with no Prussian casting. This reads as the board's cumulative alarm crossing the threshold on schedule. Whether it is the intended rhyme or a homogeneity gap is the user's call; I did not trace the member-selection code.

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism: coalition.py:1838-1879 `qualifies_for_coalition` admits a court only when relation to the target is below -10, or it is a Congress refuser, and it is not a vassal, at war, or under a truce cooldown. No Prussia-specific exclusion or authored casting was found. Prussia's statecraft (the 'bandwagoner who reneges', AI_INTENT_SPEC 3.4) has no hook in member selection. In the cited commanded digest (rev1106-cmd-jena) the player accepts Prussia's open-borders proposal, and Prussia's only stated war is on Hanover (design 'The Hanoverian Prize'), so a Prussia on good terms with France fails the relation gate. That is inference, since I did not read Prussia's relation values. Two details of the finding are wrong. The member lists are not identical across digests: the rev1106 coalition_declared lines show at least five different lists (e.g. 'Austria, Britain, Russia and Sardinia'; 'Britain, Denmark, Hanover, Hesse, Naples, the Ottoman Empire, ...'; 'Austria, Britain, Denmark, Naples, the Ottoman Empire, Portugal, Russia, Sar...'). Only the same-seed commanded arms repeat the six-court list. The finding also says it did not trace member selection, and no closed row or ruling covers this case. BUG_FIXES PC-F66 notes Prussia 'is also excluded from the coalition (coalition.py:1587)', but that cited line is threat-decay code, so the note is stale or mis-cited and is not an authored exclusion. I did not run a playtest.
mechanism.note: Survives only as a design and casting question: Prussia's casting in the Fourth Coalition depends on relation drift, not on a Prussian statecraft hook, and the commanded arm accepts Prussia's treaty. It is not a defect. The 'near-identical across seeds' claim is overstated, because the lists vary across the ambient and aidip arms. Whether a relation-gated Prussia that stays out matches the 1805 attractor (spec 3.9) is the user's call, and I would not file it as P2.

reproduction.evidence: The symptom reproduces, and I traced its cause. Digests: coalition_declared at T32 lists Austria, Britain, Hanover, Russia, Sardinia and Sweden, with no Prussia, on cmd-austerlitz, cmd-jena and cmd-ulm. I re-ran the cmd-austerlitz arm: `playtest_driver.py --turns 30 --seed austerlitz --name rev1106-verify-dip1 --fresh --script tools/playtest_scripts/commanded_full40.json --objection trust --diplomacy accept --save-at 14,22,28`. Its digest.md line 687 reads "coalition_brewing_started: Britain, Russia, Austria, Sweden, Hanover and Sardinia alarmed (threat: 60)", again with no Prussia. findings.title: White-peace summary says 'takes nothing and gives nothing' while the same dispatch lists French provinces left with the enemy
findings.evidence: rev1106-dip-volte T12 RAIL settlement_summary: 'the white peace of the War for Berry - the table with Austria takes nothing and gives nothing.' The next RAIL line, status_quo_conceded, reads 'Berry and Provence - left with Austria by the peace, titled to them by treaty.' The ratification popup also says 'Status quo: Berry and Provence stay Austrian by the treaty.' Source line 1680: "Sire, the white peace of {war_label} takes nothing and gives " / "nothing. {price_line}".
findings.repro: Run tools/playtest_scripts/volte_court_austria.json --turns 12 and read the T12 block of digest.md. Or any peace where status_quo_retentions is non-empty and there are no clauses.
findings.expected: After SR-1a made status quo a cession in both directions (BUG_FIXES SF7-X7, whose fix added the status-quo lines to the forecast and the morning), the summary should not say the peace 'takes nothing'. Austria keeps two French provinces by title.
findings.actual: The Talleyrand template says nothing is taken, one line above the dispatch that says two provinces are conceded. The voice template predates the titled-status-quo rule (S14E-10 wording). Cosmetic and consistent in effect.

mechanism.evidence:
The template is real. backend/game_logic/diplomatic_templates.py:1680-1681 reads "Sire, the white peace of {war_label} takes nothing and gives " / "nothing. {price_line}". compose_summary_oneliner (settlement_presentation.py ~736) fills it for any white peace, and price_line (_white_peace_price_line) only lists shut-out allies or says "No ally is left out by it". Neither reads status_quo_retentions, so the sentence is unconditional.

The digest shows the contradiction. rev1106-dip-volte/digest.jsonl line 475 is the RAIL settlement_summary: "the white peace of the War for Berry — the table with Austria takes nothing and gives nothing. Bavaria is left out...". Line 476 is status_quo_conceded: "Berry and Provence — left with Austria by the peace, titled to them by treaty." Lines 482-483 repeat both as dispatch rows. digest.md lines 388-389 show them side by side.

I found no closed row or ruling that covers this. BUG_FIXES S14E-10 rewrote the advisory to name the allies' price. SF7-X7 added the status-quo lines to the forecast and the morning. Neither touched the "takes nothing" wording. The only other "takes nothing" strings are diplomacy.py separate_peace_words (about allies) and unrelated comments.

Mitigation: "takes nothing" can be read as "no clause takes anything", since status quo is a titling rather than a clause. The next line states the concession, so no player is misled about the outcome. The effect is wording only.
mechanism.note: Confirmed as a P3 wording inconsistency. The voice template ignores status_quo_retentions, so a white peace that titles enemy-held French provinces still says "takes nothing and gives nothing". A fix would branch the template or append the status-quo clause, and would not change any mechanic.

reproduction.evidence: I read the digest and the source and did not re-run the playtest. The template is at backend/game_logic/diplomatic_templates.py:1680-1681: "Sire, the white peace of {war_label} takes nothing and gives " / "nothing. {price_line}". The line is unconditional. settlement_presentation.py:738 passes only price_line, built from allies left out, so the template never learns about status-quo retentions. docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-dip-volte/digest.md line 388 reads "RAIL settlement_summary: Sire, the white peace of the War for Berry — the table with Austria takes nothing and gives nothing." Line 389 reads "RAIL status_quo_conceded: Berry and Provence — left with Austria by the peace, titled to them by treaty." Both lines come from the same dispatch, so the contradiction is real. SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:12088 records the "takes nothing and gives nothing" wording as the intended S14E-10 white-peace advisory. That entry predates the titled-status-quo rule, and no closed row or ruling covers this wording.
reproduction.note: This is cosmetic. Austria keeps Berry and Provence by title, which matches the mechanics, and only the Talleyrand voice line is inaccurate. A fix would make the template conditional on non-empty status_quo_retentions. It is a game text defect, not a harness defect.
