findings.title: The AI edict rung ignores 'save for the Staff' and spends the chest the Staff needs
findings.evidence: reforms.py:1310 'if THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF:' gates only the laws rung. find_ai_edict calls edict_refusal(... with_reserve=True) and never reads the saving flag; grep of SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF in backend shows only reforms.py and counsel.py. Census of the T40 saves, Staff bar versus chest: enacts-historical Austria gap 2,375 (edict gold spent 4,000), Prussia gap 2,870 (4,000 spent); amb-austerlitz Austria gap 1,037 and its T33 Magazines cost 2,500 (campaign_log 'Austria decrees the Magazines for 8 turns (2,500 gold)'). Gold spent on edicts per 40-turn board across the five courts is 25,000-29,000 (enacts-historical 27,500; enacts-ulm 25,000; amb-austerlitz 29,000), three times the Staff's price. The counterfactual (edicts skipped) was not re-run.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <census> over docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-law-amb-austerlitz/saves/*_t40.json: for Austria compare reforms.ai_purse_refusal(w,'Austria',staff_row,gold,net_before_charges=True) with the T33 Magazines decree in digest.jsonl (campaign_log, log_turn 33).
findings.expected: A court that is saving for its Staff (chest at or above 50% of the price) also holds back gold edicts, as it holds back cheaper laws; REFORMS_SPEC section 7 says the rung saves for the Staff and enacts nothing cheaper.
findings.actual: Edicts keep draining 2,000-2,500 gold a decree while the court is within one decree of the Staff's bar, so the cure and the fifth action slip.

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism confirmed by reading the code. reforms.py:1310 `if THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF:` sets `saving` (chest >= 0.5 x Staff price, Staff not in force), and the loop then does `if saving and not is_staff(row): continue`, so only the laws rung is gated. affairs.py find_ai_edict (2010-2045) checks only: `ai_decrees()`, `armed`, `nation in REFORM_DECKS`, `ai_holds_the_purse` (lapse guard), cadence, then `edict_refusal(..., with_reserve=True)`. The bar in edict_refusal (affairs.py ~1925-1928) is price + AI_PURSE_RESERVE + upkeep turns x law_upkeep_bill, with no Staff term. A grep for SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF in backend matches only reforms.py and counsel.py:493 (the player-side advice). So a court with chest >= 50% of the Staff price keeps decreeing gold edicts. Two parts are not verified. I did not open the digests or re-run the counterfactual, so the gap figures and the effect on Staff timing are unmeasured. I did not check whether the Staff was already enacted in those runs.
mechanism.note: The asymmetry is real, but the "defect" label is weak. RECURRING_EVENTS_SPEC.md:29 rules the Edicts in as "the honest recurring sink" for gold, and REFORMS_SPEC §7 / DOCTRINES_SPEC:421 describe saving for the Staff as applying to the laws rung, which RE-6 never extended to edicts. I found no spec sentence requiring edicts to yield to the Staff, so this reads as a design gap or sibling (Rule 10) more than a bug. It matters only if the DC-2 T8 cure-timing target is missed. Impact is unproven until someone re-runs with edicts held down (arm AFE) and compares the Staff enactment turn. A cheap fix would be to read the same `saving` predicate in find_ai_edict for gold-priced edicts. That fix would change BASELINE_SERIES and the records.

reproduction.evidence:
The code gap is real; the harm is not shown. I read the code and the digest and ran no census or playtest.
- reforms.py:1310-1318: find_ai_enactment holds back every non-Staff law ("if saving and not is_staff(row): continue") once the chest is at or above 50% of the Staff's price.
- affairs.py:2034 (find_ai_edict): the only purse test is "edict_refusal(world, nation, e, treasury=int(treasury), with_reserve=True)". That test adds the price, AI_PURSE_RESERVE and five turns of upkeep (affairs.py:1926-1929). It never reads THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF or the Staff's price.
- A grep of SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF in backend/ matches only reforms.py and counsel.py, so the edict rung is not gated by the saving flag.
- Digest rev1106-law-amb-austerlitz, digest.jsonl line 1027: "Austria decrees the Magazines for 8 turns (2,500 gold)", log_turn 33. In the same digest Austria's only law lines are the Landwehr (220) and the New Infantry Regulations (354). No Staff enactment line appears for Austria.
- Not reproduced: the Staff gap figures and the 25,000-29,000 gold per board. The counterfactual (edicts skipped) was not run, so I cannot show the Staff would have come in.
- Docs: RECURRING_EVENTS_SPEC.md:29 rules the Edicts in as "the honest recurring sink" for gold. REFORMS_SPEC §7 and DOCTRINES_SPEC DC-2 define the saving rule for the laws rung only ("enacts nothing cheaper" means laws). No doc rules that edicts must also save for the Staff, and no doc rules that they may not.
- A prior note records that Prussia and Russia never afford the Staff in forty turns, held by the chest half. That was measured before the courts' Edicts were armed. RE-6 and AU-4 later put the courts' edicts into the board.
reproduction.note: I rate it P3 design/balance, not P2. The asymmetry is real and unrecorded, but the spec calls edicts the recurring gold sink on purpose, and the defect has no counterfactual. Before it is promoted, someone should re-run one board with an arm that holds edicts down while a court is saving, to see whether the Staff or its cure comes in earlier (DOCTRINES T8: Austria cured turns 20-22, Britain 19-24). The fix would be small: give find_ai_edict the same saving check as find_ai_enactment, behind a seam.

findings.title: Staff and doctrine-cure arrival has drifted far from the T8 record; Prussia never reaches it and its cure is cosmetic
findings.evidence: Row 1.78 records Austria Staff T20-22, Britain T19-24, Prussia and Russia never. Measured now: Britain Staff T26 (enacts-historical), T17 (enacts-ulm), T27 (amb-historical), T33 (amb-austerlitz); Austria T30 on amb-historical only, never on the other three boards; Russia T39 on enacts-historical only; Prussia never on any board. Real purse bar read from the saves is 12,500-13,000 (Prussia 13,000; Austria 12,750), not the 11,500 the spec quotes, because bar = price + 1,000 + 5 x (slate upkeep + 300) and each cheap law bought first adds 500. Prussia's chest at T40 was 10,130 / 9,130 / 8,080, which is above the Staff's 9,000 price but under its bar. Cures by T30 on historical: Britain only on enacts-historical, Austria only on amb-historical. The 'two of four by T30' target holds on 0 of 4 boards. Prussia's Articles of War reads 'cures Brittle while its Staff stands' and is enacted T5-6, but the Staff never stands.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <bar script> docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-law-enacts-historical (prints gold, bar, gap, refusal per court); grep law_enacted_abroad in digest.jsonl for the dates.
findings.expected: DOCTRINES_SPEC T8: at least two of the four rivals cured by T30 on historical; the 'never' for Prussia and Russia was a recorded finding that the rung was told to fix ('A miss is this rung's to fix').
findings.actual: Zero of four boards meet it; the dates moved later after the economy rebalance, the edicts' arming and the authority flip (those three are the likely causes, not isolated).
findings.prior_row: DC-2 / DOCTRINES_SPEC section 6 T8; REFORMS_SPEC section 7 'A miss is this rung's to fix'

mechanism.evidence:
I traced the mechanism in code and read the docs. I did not rerun the bar script, so the measured dates and chest figures rest on the digests and the reviewer's numbers.

Code: `reforms.py:1236-1240` computes `bar = need + AI_PURSE_RESERVE + AI_PURSE_UPKEEP_TURNS * (law_upkeep_bill(world, nation) + upkeep)`. `AI_PURSE_RESERVE` is 1000 (line 1163). The bar therefore grows with every law already on the slate, which matches the reviewer's account of cheap laws raising it. The save-for-the-Staff rule (`THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF = True`, line 1161, used at line 1310) only applies once the chest passes half the Staff's price.

Digests: `rev1106-law-enacts-historical` and `rev1106-law-amb-historical` show `law_enacted_abroad` rows where Prussia enacts the Articles of War ("cures Brittle ... while its Staff stands"), the Military Reorganisation Commission and the Emancipation Edict, and Austria enacts the Landwehr, New Infantry Regulations and Generalissimus. These cheap laws are bought while the Staff is not yet in force. The Articles of War cure text therefore reads as a promise that never takes effect for Prussia.

Docs: `docs/ENEMY_AI_REFERENCE.md` row 1.78 and `DOCTRINES_SPEC.md` (DC-2 landing record, T8 at line 439) record Austria cured at T20-22 and Britain at T19-24, and "two of four by 30 on historical" as the pass criterion. They also record that Prussia and Russia never afford the Staff in forty turns, "recorded, not tuned". The cheap-laws-first bar growth is acknowledged in the spec at line 421. The "never" for Prussia is a known, recorded outcome. The T8 target of two cures by T30 is not met on the current tree.

The cause is likely the later economy, edict and authority-flip changes, as the reviewer says.
mechanism.note: The drift is real, and the Prussia and Russia "never" is a recorded, unfixed outcome rather than a regression. It is balance and tuning, not a crash or an integrity break, so I lowered it from P2 to P3 (kind design). The rung's own contract ("A miss is this rung's to fix") makes a re-measure of T8 on the final tree the natural follow-up. The reviewer's quoted bar of 11,500 is the spec's figure. The code formula confirms the real bar is higher once cheap laws are on the slate.

reproduction.evidence: I did not run the finding's bar script. I re-read the digest.jsonl of the four law boards (rev1106-law-enacts-historical, enacts-ulm, amb-historical, amb-austerlitz) with an in-process script that lists law_enacted_abroad rows with their turns. My turn tracker was rough, so I used it only to cross-check. The Staff laws it reads match the finding: Britain's Horse Guards Reforms T26 on enacts-historical, Austria's Corps d'Armée T30 on amb-historical, Russia's Divisional System T39 on enacts-historical. No Prussian Staff enactment appears on any board. Prussia's Articles of War (the cure law) is enacted T5-6 on every board, but the cure only takes effect while the Staff stands. Cures by T30 on historical are therefore Britain alone on enacts-historical and Austria alone on amb-historical, so DOCTRINES_SPEC T8 (docs/DOCTRINES_SPEC.md:439, two of four cured by T30 on the historical seed) holds on no board. The shipped record, docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md §84.4, says 'Austria cured turns 20–22, Britain 19–24 ... Prussia and Russia never afford the Staff in forty turns (the chest half).' So the 'never' for Prussia and Russia was already recorded at DC-2. The new part is the slip in Austria's and Britain's dates, from T19-24 to T26-34 or never. I found no later row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md that accepts this drift; my search covered 'T8', 'never reaches', 'Staff never' and 'cure ... turn N'. The purse bar of 12,500-13,000 against 11,500 and the exact causes were not re-verified.
reproduction.note: The drift reproduces. It is a balance and pacing miss against a spec pass criterion, not a crash or rule break, and AI economy tuning is a user call, so I rate it design (P3 at most). The 'never' for Prussia and Russia is old, already recorded in §84.4. The new news is that Austria's and Britain's Staff dates slipped, so the 'two of four by T30' target no longer holds. The finding's attribution to the economy rebalance, edicts and authority flip is unverified. The cure laws arrive early (T5-12) and are inert without the Staff.

findings.title: The law rung has no demand test: courts buy drill and levy laws they never use
findings.evidence: Console logs: AI 'drill' orders in 40 turns (enacts-ulm / amb-austerlitz): Prussia 0 / 0, Austria 0 / 3, Russia 3 / 3, Britain 1 / 1. Prussia still enacts the Military Reorganisation Commission (+5 drill morale, 100 gold a turn) at T9-11 in every run, about 3,100 gold of upkeep by T40 for zero drills. On amb-austerlitz Russia buys the Extraordinary Levy (T7, 100 a turn) and has zero 'recruit' admin orders in 40 turns (admin tallies: Russia {decree_edict 4, build 9, enact_law 2, recruit_marshal 1}). The rung takes the first law in deck order that clears the purse, with no read of whether the court drills or levies.
findings.repro: grep '\[AI ADMIN\] Attempting: recruit' and 'drill' orders per nation in docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-law-amb-austerlitz/server_console.log against the digest's law_enacted_abroad rows.
findings.expected: A law's upkeep buys something the court will use, or the deck order puts the Staff and the doctrine cure first.
findings.actual: Cheap-first buying burns upkeep on dead-for-the-AI effects, and also raises the Staff's purse bar (LAW-2).

mechanism.evidence: backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1315-1328 does take the first law in deck order that passes law_refusal and ai_purse_refusal, with no read of whether the court drills or levies. That matches the docstring ("the first law in deck order"). docs/REFORMS_SPEC.md:324 says "The deck order is authored... The rung takes the first law that law_refusal passes and whose purse test passes". Spec lines ~335-338 already name the side effect: "This rung takes the first law a court can afford, so cheaper laws may be enacted first, and their upkeep raises that bar." The mitigation exists: reforms.py:1161 THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF = True, with AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF_FROM = 0.5, so once the chest passes half the Staff's price the rung enacts nothing cheaper. The spec also says "Moving a cure to a cheaper law is structural and goes to the user." I did not open the digests or the console logs, so I could not check the per-nation drill and recruit tallies. The mechanism claim stands: the code has no demand test.
mechanism.note: This is spec-recorded behaviour, not a defect. Upkeep burned on laws the court never uses is a real gap in the AI's economy, but a demand-aware rung or a reordered deck would be a design change for the user, per the spec's own rule on cures. The finding is correctly labelled kind design; P3 is generous. No closed row or recorded ruling covers "no demand test", so it is not refuted.

reproduction.evidence: The mechanism is real, but I could not reproduce the zero-drill and zero-recruit tallies. (1) backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1316-1330 find_ai_enactment loops the deck in order and returns the first row that passes law_refusal and ai_purse_refusal. It has no read of whether the court drills or levies; the only reordering is the Staff-saving switch. (2) docs/REFORMS_SPEC.md:324 and :590 record "deck order... authored", "the first law that law_refusal passes". It is the ruled GR5 design, so this is not a defect. (3) The rev1106-law-amb-austerlitz digest.jsonl does show law_enacted_abroad rows for "Prussia enacts the Military Reorganisation Commission — +5 morale from every drill", "Austria enacts the New Infantry Regulations — +5 morale from every drill" and "Russia enacts the Extraordinary Levy — infantry levies cost 20% less". (4) The cited server_console.log does not exist in the digest folder (only digest.jsonl, digest.md and meta.json), and no "AI ADMIN" lines are archived anywhere. The per-nation drill and recruit counts (Prussia 0 drills, Russia 0 recruits) and the ~3,100 gold upkeep figure are therefore unverified. I did not re-run the playtest.
reproduction.note: Kind is design, not a defect: the seam matches the spec and the finding's own expected outcome is a design change (reorder decks or add a demand read). It is not tied to an existing BUG_FIXES row. The "cheap-first" wording is loose, since it is deck order and not price order. The empirical dead-upkeep claim is unconfirmed because the console log is missing from the archive.
