findings.title: rf3_commanded_enacts stops asking for the Staff at T20, so historical's Staff is never measured and the commanded France ends with a 22,750-gold chest and nothing to buy
findings.evidence: enacts-historical digest: 20 attempts, last refusal 'costs 9,000 gold; the treasury holds 4,712' at about T20; France's chest first passes 9,000 at T25 (ledger records) and ends at 22,750 (T40 save: France laws anticipated_class and code_abroad only, staff 0). On ulm the Staff lands T15 (the chest passed 9,000 at T14). So the script's T1 acceptance (Staff by T10-15) reads 1 of 2 seeds, and the other is a script cut-off, not a game answer.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name x --fresh --seed historical --script tools/playtest_scripts/rf3_commanded_enacts.json --diplomacy accept; count 'enact the Staff' commands.
findings.expected: The script keeps trying until the Staff is in force.
findings.actual: Attempts stop at T20 on a board whose chest crosses the price at T25.

mechanism.evidence: I parsed tools/playtest_scripts/rf3_commanded_enacts.json. "enact the Staff" appears on turns 1-20 and on none of turns 21-40, although the script runs 40 turns. The digest docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-law-enacts-historical/digest.md has exactly 20 "enact the Staff" commands. The ones I read were all refusals of the form "costs 9,000 gold; the treasury holds N", with N between 601 and 1,816. So the script stops asking at T20, before the 9,000 price is reached on this seed. I did not check the T25 crossing or the 22,750 end chest.
mechanism.note: This is a harness script cutoff, not a game defect. The Staff refusal is the game working as designed: a 9,000-gold price against a chest that has not reached it. The fix is to repeat "enact the Staff" through T40 or until the law is in force. Until then, acceptance readings of the Staff on historical are unmeasured.

reproduction.evidence: I counted `grep -c "enact the Staff" tools/playtest_scripts/rf3_commanded_enacts.json` and got 20 occurrences. They sit in turns 1-20. The script's turn 20 block (lines ~158-164) is the last to contain "enact the Staff", and turn 21 onward has none. In docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-law-enacts-historical/digest.md there are 20 CMD `enact the Staff` lines, all refused: "costs 9,000 gold; the treasury holds N". N rises from 800 at T1 to 4,712 (line 572, T18), 5,236 (T19) and 6,041 (line 621, T20). The chest is still climbing toward the 9,000 price when the script stops asking. I did not re-run the 40-turn playtest. I did not verify the T25 crossing or the 22,750 end chest from ledger records; the claim is consistent with the 6,041 at T20 and the rising trend. The `_note_rf3` in the script says the Staff is enacted "at its first affordable turn", but with a fixed 20-turn ask window that is not true on a seed whose chest crosses the price after T20.
reproduction.note: This is a harness defect in the script, not a game defect. Add "enact the Staff" to later turns (T21-T30 or to T40), or make the script retry until the Staff is in force. As filed, the T1 acceptance (Staff by T10-15) is measured on ulm only, and historical's Staff is never measured. I did not check whether a closed BUG_FIXES row covers this.

findings.title: Britain's turn-8 sue-path no longer fires on the shut-out arm (C4 red; VP-1's 'Britain sues turn 8 on every seed' stale)
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:~2640-2720 (P1 armistice_losing gate, coalition_blocked / league gates) and :2699 (P2 has_fought gate, P2_NO_CONTACT_ESCAPE_TURNS=15)
findings.evidence: rev1106-sea-shutout-historical and rev1106-sea-shutout-austerlitz (accept, 12 turns): no 'Britain armistice' or 'Britain settlement offer' ENVOYS line in any of 12 turns. Same script gave 'Britain armistice losing' on T8 in archived sr5b-accept-historical (digest line 209). rev1106-sea-we saves: Britain war_exhaustion 26 (T3), 48 (T5), 70 (T7), 92 (T9). rev1106-sea-strangle: first Britain offer T11, armistice T14. In shutout-austerlitz Paget is 'a prisoner of Spain at Madrid' by T7 and Soult never reaches Lisbon, so Britain and France may have no recorded contact. This is a hypothesis; the gate was not isolated.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --llm mock --fresh --turns 12 --name x --script tools/playtest_scripts/sr5b_shut_out.json --diplomacy accept --seed historical ; grep -ci 'Britain armistice' tools/playtest_runs/x/digest.md  (0). Compare docs/audits/playtest_digests/sr5b-accept-historical/digest.md.
findings.expected: Britain asks for an armistice around T8 at war exhaustion 70-80 (NAVAL_SPEC §19 'turn 8 on six arms of six'; SF_NAV1 memo item 5; score_run naval C4 <= T10 on 3 of 3 seeds).
findings.actual: No offer by T12 on two seeds at war exhaustion above 90, and T11 on the strangle arm. The A2 'Britain sues without a soldier crossing' win path is silent on the shut-out arm. Cause not isolated; candidates are the post-AU-4 courts-in-arms board, the contact gate, or the coalition league gate.

mechanism.evidence:
Two parts hold up and one does not. (1) The reviewer's repro omitted `--declare-war proceed`. The script header in tools/playtest_scripts/sr5b_shut_out.json says "Pair with --declare-war proceed (the declarations are this arm's point)". rev1106-sea-shutout-historical/meta.json has `"declare_war": "cancel"`, so the Portugal and Papal declarations were cancelled, which makes it a harness misuse. (2) I re-ran it correctly (`--diplomacy accept --declare-war proceed --seed historical`, name rev1106-verify-navvas1, 12 turns). It still shows no "Britain armistice" or "Britain settlement" ENVOYS line. The observation therefore stands, but the cause is not a gate bug. The autosave at T13 shows war_scores['Britain|France'] = -1, ai_stalemate_counters['Britain|France'] = 12, and war_exhaustion Britain = 134. By hand through ai_diplomacy.py:
- P1 (:2633) needs war_score < effective_peace_threshold. That is -40 + we//20, which comes to about -34 plus the ticking-pressure and agenda terms. -1 is far above it. High war exhaustion only releases the coalition gate in coalition_break_ranks_reason; it never lowers the score the P1 gate reads.
- P2 (:2699-2703) calls pair_has_fought. Britain and France never fought in this run, and Portugal's war score is 0, so the threshold is max(stalemate, P2_NO_CONTACT_ESCAPE_TURNS=15). The counter is 12 at T13, so the offer would come at about T16.
This is the AUD-b rule (:75-84, "a never-fought war may sue only after 15 turns"). In the archived sr5b-accept-historical, the T8 "Britain armistice losing" (digest line 209) came from a board where British corps had actually fought and lost. In the current run Soult makes no contact with Britain. The code can produce the observed silence, and it does so by design.
mechanism.note: No code defect found. The documented "turn 8 on six arms of six" (NAVAL_SPEC §19, line 2095) was measured on the Sept 28 board, where a British corps fought and lost. On today's tree that contact does not happen on the shut-out script, so the sue-path waits for the 15-turn no-contact escape. At most this is a stale-claim and benchmark-instrument item for the NAVAL_SPEC §19 / score_run C4 expectation. A balance question remains for the user: Britain at war exhaustion 134 with no contact never sues before about T16. That is a design choice, not a bug. The cause was not isolated further: I did not trace why Soult and Britain make no contact on this tree (a mismatch with the fight-dependent T8 baseline), and I did not run the sea-strangle arm.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the finding's repro: playtest_driver.py --llm mock --fresh --turns 12 --name rev1106-verify-navvas1 --script tools/playtest_scripts/sr5b_shut_out.json --diplomacy accept --seed historical. It completed, and `grep -ci 'Britain armistice'` on tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-verify-navvas1/digest.md gave 0. A grep for Britain armistice, settlement or offer lines in the same digest found nothing. The archived docs/audits/playtest_digests/sr5b-accept-historical/digest.md gives 2 matches, including line 209 "ENVOYS WAITING 2 · Britain armistice losing · Austria peace", with the Britain Armistice mailbox item at line 221. The rev1106-sea-shutout-historical digest also gives 0. So the symptom is real: no Britain suit within 12 turns on the same script and seed that produced one at T8 in the archive. I did not isolate the cause, which the finding itself does not claim to have done either. The finding's own hypotheses are the post-AU-4 board, the contact gate, or Paget's capture on the shut-out line. I found no closed BUG_FIXES row or spec ruling that accepts this change.
reproduction.note: The symptom reproduces, but the cause is unproven, so this is PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED. It may be the script's contact path breaking on the new board rather than a game defect: the script is a shut-out arm in which Paget is captured and Soult never reaches Lisbon. If a bisect shows Britain still sues on an ordinary war path, downgrade to P3 and treat it as a stale script or stale VP-1/C4 claim. To isolate it, hold the courts-in-arms seam (arm AUC) down and re-run.

findings.title: Ending's successor-peace line prints 'the 1792 frontiers's terms'
findings.evidence: f"{DICTATED_TIER_LABELS[tier]}'s terms" and f"({full['label']}'s terms were the Emperor's to refuse)"; tier 3 label is 'the 1792 frontiers'. rev1106-end-chains T10 ending: '(the 1792 frontiers's terms were the Emperor's to refuse)'. The same string appears in end-fall T35.
findings.repro: grep -n "frontiers's" docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-end-chains/digest.md docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-end-fall/digest.md
findings.expected: 'the 1792 frontiers' terms' (plural possessive), as for 'Châtillon's terms'.
findings.actual: Apostrophe-s on a plural noun in the last paragraph of the Fall screen, the text the player reads last.

mechanism.evidence: backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:1218 has DICTATED_TIER_LABELS = {..., 3: "the 1792 frontiers"}. Lines 1628-1630 build f"{DICTATED_TIER_LABELS[tier]}'s terms" and f"({full['label']}'s terms were the Emperor's to refuse)". When full['label'] is tier 3, this prints "the 1792 frontiers's terms". The digests show it verbatim: rev1106-end-chains/digest.md:272 and rev1106-end-fall/digest.md:876 both contain "(the 1792 frontiers's terms were the Emperor's to refuse)". Grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md for "frontiers's" found no closed row. The path is also reachable at the lower tier, because the line uses tier-1 for the signed terms and the full tier for the refused label.
mechanism.note: Real but cosmetic grammar slip. The fix is a possessive helper that gives "frontiers' terms" for the plural label. The sibling labels (Reichenbach, Frankfurt, Châtillon) are singular, so only tier 3 is affected. The refused-tier branch is the one that reaches it.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the grep from the finding. It hit rev1106-end-chains/digest.md:272 and rev1106-end-fall/digest.md:876. Both contain "(the 1792 frontiers's terms were the Emperor's to refuse)". The source is backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:1218, `DICTATED_TIER_LABELS = {0: "Reichenbach", 1: "Frankfurt", 2: "Châtillon", 3: "the 1792 frontiers"}`. The line at 1628-1630 formats `f"{DICTATED_TIER_LABELS[tier]}'s terms"` and `f"({full['label']}'s terms were the Emperor's to refuse)"`. `full['label']` is a tier label, so the plural noun gets "'s". A grep of BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "frontiers's" found no closed row or ruling.
reproduction.note: This is a real but cosmetic grammar defect. It only shows on tier 3 (the 1792 frontiers). A fix would use a possessive helper that adds "'" alone when the label ends in "s", or the label could be stored as "the 1792 frontiers'". The same class may exist at the Châtillon label sites, but those are singular and fine.

findings.title: Grant-autonomy reply prints the nominal loyalty change, not the applied one, and has no 'buys nothing' guard at the cap
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/vassal.py:2557 (loyalty_msg = f"+{plan['gain']} loyalty (increased autonomy)") with plan gain set at :2465-2470
findings.evidence: rev1106-vas-probe T1: 'invest in Switzerland' refuses with 'loyalty is already full (100/100) - nothing is charged'. The next command, 'grant Switzerland autonomy', succeeds with '+10 loyalty (increased autonomy). Tribute rate: 75% to 50% (a permanent income cut)'. Loyalty was already 100 and after = min(100, 100+10) = 100, so the applied change is 0 and the permanent tribute cut is bought for nothing. The wizard line (_autonomy_consequence) correctly says 'loyalty stays 100'. The downgrade branch prints a literal '-15 loyalty' even when clamped at 0.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --llm mock --fresh --turns 3 --name x --script tools/playtest_scripts/vassal_probe.json ; read the T1 command lines
findings.expected: The reply prints the applied delta ('loyalty stays 100'), and the verb refuses or warns when the gain is 0 (the invest verb's pattern).
findings.actual: Reply claims +10; a permanent 25-point tribute cut is paid at the cap with no warning. Quote and applied value disagree (ACH-1 class).
findings.prior_row: ACH-1 (class: quote and applied value disagree); IQ7-RV5 related

mechanism.evidence: backend/game_logic/vassal.py:2447-2449: `gain = int(10 * mult)`, `after = int(min(LOYALTY_MAX, before + gain))`, so at loyalty 100 gain is 10 and after is 100. :2465-2466 stores `gain=int(gain)` (the nominal value) beside `loyalty_after`. change_vassal_autonomy sets `state["loyalty"]=plan["loyalty_after"]` (the correct applied value) but then prints `loyalty_msg = f"+{plan['gain']} loyalty (increased autonomy)..."` (about :2557), so the reply says +10 when the applied change is 0. The downgrade branch prints the literal "-15 loyalty (decreased autonomy)" even when clamped at 0. No cap guard exists in autonomy_change_plan (:2395-2441): the only refusals are not-a-vassal, invalid level, not the lord, same level and no DP. The invest verb does have one ("loyalty is already full", vassal.py:2278). The wizard line `_autonomy_consequence` already prints "loyalty stays N" when after == before, so the reply and the wizard disagree. I did not run the digest; the code trace alone is enough to confirm it.
mechanism.note: The misprint is real (a quote and applied value mismatch, ACH-1 class). The "buys nothing" framing is overstated. Granting autonomy also changes the autonomy level and its drift, and it is a deliberate policy act. Only the loyalty message is wrong, and a refusal at the cap is a design choice. The minimal fix is to print `plan['loyalty_after'] - plan['loyalty_before']`, or reuse the wizard's "loyalty stays N" wording, for both branches.

reproduction.evidence: Read-only code verification; I did not run the playtest. vassal.py:2462-2465 sets gain=int(10*mult) and after=min(LOYALTY_MAX, before+gain). It stores plan['gain'] as the nominal gain, not after-before. vassal.py:2557 prints f"+{plan['gain']} loyalty (increased autonomy)" and :2559 prints a literal "-15 loyalty (decreased autonomy)". At before=100 the applied change is 0 but the reply says +10, and the 75% to 50% tribute cut is still applied with no guard. The only gate before the apply is a DP check (:2431-2439). I found no "already full" or "loyalty stays" text in this verb. Grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md found no closed row or ruling covering it.
reproduction.note: Real but minor: the reply misstates the applied loyalty, and the verb has no warning or refusal at the cap. The player pays 1 DP and takes a permanent income cut for nothing. The downgrade reply likewise prints -15 when the loyalty clamps at 0. Fix: print after-before, and refuse or warn when the gain is 0, as invest does.

findings.title: 'march to X and attack Y' bypasses the already-there check, spends 2 AP on a null march, and never tells the player about the stored arrival attack
findings.seam: backend/commands/strategic_executor.py (MOVE_TO with attack_on_arrival / arrival_target) via parser 'target_overrides_tactical'
findings.evidence: Probe on a fresh 1805 boot (Lannes starts at Franche-Comte): 'Lannes, march to Franche-Comte' -> 'Lannes already stands at Franche-Comte - nothing spent.' AP 4->4. 'Lannes, march to Franche-Comte and attack Mack' -> 'Lannes begins march to Franche-Comte. He will drop this order for any battle within two provinces...' AP 4->2; the stored order has path [], attack_on_arrival True, arrival_target 'Mack', and no dropped_sequel/warning in the reply. 'Lannes, march to Paris, then attack Mack' (Mack ~6 provinces away) likewise stores arrival_target Mack and the reply only says 'begins march to Paris'. Same shape in rev1106-cmd-feel T8 ('Lannes, move to Swabia and attack Mack').
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 (TestClient over backend.main, mock parser, fresh _reset_world_state): post 'Lannes, march to Franche-Comte and attack Mack' and compare world.actions_remaining before/after and L.strategic_order.to_dict()['arrival_target']
findings.expected: Already-there refusal with nothing spent, or at least the reply naming the second leg ('then attacks Mack on arrival') so the tail is not silent (CR-7).
findings.actual: 2 AP spent on a zero-length march; arrival attack stored and never disclosed.

mechanism.evidence: I reproduced both probes on a fresh boot with the mock parser. 'Lannes, march to Franche-Comte and attack Mack' took AP 4 -> 2. The reply was only 'Lannes begins march to Franche-Comte. He will drop this order for any battle within two provinces...'. The stored order had path [] and arrival_target 'Mack'. 'Lannes, march to Paris, then attack Mack' took AP 2 -> 0. The reply gave the route and said nothing about Mack, but the stored order has arrival_target 'Mack'. The null march is deliberate. strategic_executor.py ~1665-1680 skips the already-there refusal when parsed_command has attack_on_arrival or arrival_verb. Its comment says: 'A march that carries a verb for its arrival ("then fortify", "then attack Mack") keeps the verb's business and is left alone.' Spending the AP is therefore not a defect, because the arrival attack is real work. The real defect is the missing disclosure. For MOVE_TO, no reply text names the second leg (grep for 'then attacks' or 'on arrival' finds nothing outside PURSUE, around line 2600). CC-X6 in BUG_FIXES.md closed the silent-drop class for HOLD and SUPPORT, where the flag is never read. This is the sibling case: the flag is read and acted on, but the reply never says so. The CR-7 'no silent tail' principle applies.
mechanism.note: Partly refuted. The '2 AP on a null march' half is intended behaviour, so the finding should not ask for an already-there refusal. The valid half is that the MOVE_TO reply does not name the stored arrival attack, and a reply like 'then attacks Mack on arrival' would fix it. P3 because the order works as stored and only the message is silent. File it as a sibling of CC-X6.

reproduction.evidence: I ran a TestClient probe against backend.main on a fresh boot, calling M._reset_world_state() before each command. 'Lannes, march to Franche-Comte and attack Mack' went from AP 4 to 2. The reply was only "Lannes begins march to Franche-Comte. He will drop this order for any battle within two provinces...". The stored order had path [] and arrival_target Mack. The reply carried no dropped_sequel or warning. 'Lannes, march to Paris, then attack Mack' replied only "begins march to Paris. Route: Nivernais → Burgundy → Limousin → Paris...". The stored order had arrival_target Mack and the reply never mentioned Mack. I did not capture the output of the plain 'march to Franche-Comte' control, so the finding's "nothing spent" claim for it is unverified. I found no BUG_FIXES row for this symptom. The closest, CC-X6, covers HOLD/SUPPORT tails and not MOVE_TO.
reproduction.note: The core claim holds. A march to the marshal's own province spends 2 AP and stores an arrival attack, and the reply never names that second leg. The impact is modest: a wasted 2 AP and an undisclosed tail. Neither corrupts game state, so P3 fits better than P2.

findings.title: Location clause silently dropped: 'take up a defensive position in Lorraine' shifts stance where the marshal stands, while 'defend Lorraine' refuses with the reason
findings.seam: backend/commands/tactical_executor.py defend/stance path + parser target extraction for 'defensive position in X'
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-hold T2: 'Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine' -> 'Napoleon shifts from NEUTRAL to DEFENSIVE stance. Effect: -10% attack, +15% defense.' Napoleon had been drawn to Swabia by the corps system (probe: napoleon at Swabia). The same state answers 'Ney, defend Lorraine' -> 'Ney stands at Rhineland, not Lorraine, Sire - a defence is stood where the corps stands... Nothing has been relayed.' and 'Have Davout head over to Lorraine and dig in there' refuses likewise.
findings.repro: Fresh boot: 'Ney, attack Mack' then 'Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine'; compare with 'Ney, defend Lorraine'
findings.expected: Same refusal naming where he stands (or the stance shift disclosing 'at Swabia, not Lorraine').
findings.actual: Stance spent and changed at an unnamed place; the named province vanishes in silence.

mechanism.evidence:
The digest line is real: docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-hold/digest.md, T2: "Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine -> Napoleon shifts from NEUTRAL to DEFENSIVE stance." The same turn's "Have Davout head over to Lorraine and dig in there" is refused with "Davout stands at Swabia, not Lorraine, Sire".

Mechanism: backend/commands/exit_predicate.py:~48 defines `STATIONARY_ARMS = frozenset({"drill","fortify","defend","wait","form_square","unfortify"})`. `place_pre_check` returns None at once for any action outside that set, and executor.py:2206 is its only caller. `stance_change` is not in the set, so no place check runs for it.

`tactical_executor._execute_stance_change` (~line 940) reads `command.get("target_stance") or command.get("target")` as the stance and ignores any province. A named province is therefore dropped silently and the stance changes where the marshal stands.

The sibling arm `defend` was fixed by SFR-D7 (BUG_FIXES.md:272, DD-0 S4), which lists the stationary arms. I found no spec text or ruling that deliberately leaves stance_change out. This is the unswept sibling that CLAUDE.md Rule 10 requires to be filed.

Limits: I did not run a live repro. I traced it by hand and checked it against the digest. I did not confirm exactly what the parser puts in `command["target"]` for this phrasing. That does not change the result, because `place_pre_check` never looks at the command for stance_change.
mechanism.note: The defect is real, but P2 is too high. The marshal still adopts the stance he was asked for, at his own location, and the AP cost is that of the order he actually gave. The only fault is that the named province is silently ignored, where the sibling `defend` order refuses. The fix is small: add stance_change to STATIONARY_ARMS, with `_ARM_WORD`/`_ARM_VERB` entries, and make sure `command["target"]` holding a province does not collide with a stance string.

reproduction.evidence: I reproduced it in two playtest runs (mock LLM, historical seed). The first, rev1106-verify-cmdfeel2, had Ney attack Mack on T1. On T1, "Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine" shifted him to DEFENSIVE, but I never checked where he stood then, so that run does not show the drop. On T2 it had "Ney, defend Lorraine", refused: "Ney stands at Swabia, not Lorraine, Sire — a defence is stood where the corps stands... Nothing…". "Napoleon, defend Lorraine" was refused the same way. The second run, rev1106-verify-cmdfeel3, is the clean repro. Ney attacks Mack on T1. On T2 "Napoleon, take up a defensive position in Lorraine" returns "✓ Napoleon shifts from NEUTRAL to DEFENSIVE stance. Effect: -10% attack, +15% defense." The next command, "where is Napoleon", returns "stands at Swabia with 9,075 men". So the stance was applied at Swabia and the named province Lorraine was silently dropped, while the defend verb refuses the same place with the reason. The refusal text comes from backend/ai/state_desk.py:3563 and backend/commands/exit_predicate.py:51. The original digest, rev1106-cmd-hold lines 66 and 69, shows the same split. I found no row for it in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md.
reproduction.note: The behaviour is real, but the cost is small. A stance is a state on the marshal, not tied to a place, so the player loses at most one action's worth of clarity and nothing is mis-executed. Both stance_change and defend are "done where the corps stands" verbs, so the sibling (defend) already refuses and the stance path should follow it. P3 rather than P2 because no wrong mechanic fires. I did not identify the exact line in tactical_executor.py where the stance path ignores the location.

findings.title: A marshal's objection offers 'Trust him and he will attack X' where the same board refuses that attack (peace); retreat objection fires for a marshal whose colleague is told 'not in danger'
findings.seam: backend/commands/disobedience.py / objection_v2.py alternative-action builder (preferred action not pre-validated against war/peace)
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-op T10: 'Ney, retreat' -> "Ney firmly objects: 'Retreat? We can still fight!' (Trust him and he will attack Kutuzov at Carniola instead.)" while France is at PEACE with Austria since T6 and the next command in the same turn 'Soult, attack Kutuzov' -> 'Soult cannot march on Kutuzov: Carniola is Austria's soil, and we are at peace with Austria - no corps of ours may take the field there.' Same turn 'Lannes, retreat' -> 'Lannes is not in danger. No retreat necessary.' (digest.jsonl confirms the three records in order).
findings.repro: Replay: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 10 --name x --fresh --script tools/playtest_scripts/sr_exit_aar_typed.json --objection insist --diplomacy accept ; read turn 10 CMD lines
findings.expected: The advertised Trust alternative is an order the executor would carry out; objection evaluated after the action's own validation (CLAUDE.md Don't Do: objection before validation).
findings.actual: The player is offered a counter-action that is illegal on the same board; the retreat objection appears for a marshal in the state where a sibling is refused as not in danger.

mechanism.evidence: The seam is confirmed by reading the code. In backend/commands/disobedience.py, `get_enemies_in_range` (line 62) filters only on war status (`is_at_war`), visibility and distance. It does not ask whether the enemy stands on peace soil. `_can_execute_suggestion` (line 294), the function that vets alternatives, checks only `enemy.strength > 0` and `fortified` for an attack (lines 311-323). A grep of disobedience.py, objection_v2.py and executor.py found no reference to `peace_sanctuary` or `peace_soil_refusal`. The real executor does check it: `combat_executor.peace_soil_refusal` (~line 1013) prints "...Carniola is Austria's soil, and we are at peace with Austria - no corps of ours may take the field there." The digest matches. docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op/digest.jsonl turn 10, seq 9: "Ney, retreat" -> "(Trust him and he will attack Kutuzov at Carniola instead.)". Wars at turn 10 are Russia only. digest.md line 330 has Soult's attack on Kutuzov refused as peace soil. Kutuzov is at war with France, so the war filter passes him, while the soil belongs to peaceful Austria. The aggressive chain at disobedience.py:1140 therefore offers `_attack(Kutuzov)`. The row is not closed: the S14E-4 and DDB-14 rows only covered the peace preview, the what-if and the muster, and none of them touched `_can_execute_suggestion`. The finding's second half does not hold. Ney and Lannes are different marshals, and 'not in danger' is a per-marshal state, so the digest shows no contradiction there. Declining to flag the retreat objection as a defect.
mechanism.note: The real defect is narrow. `_can_execute_suggestion` never checks the peace-soil rule, so the Trust alternative can name an attack the executor will refuse at no cost. This is a legibility dead end: the player clicks Trust and gets a refusal, nothing is spent and nothing is corrupted. That makes it P3, not P2. It is a sibling of DDB-14, S14E-4 and the Master Rule #1 class, and under CLAUDE.md Rule 10 it should be filed. A fix would call the `_pursuit_capture_guard` / `field_on_peace_soil` predicate inside `_can_execute_suggestion`'s attack branch, and the same predicate for the move alternative. The retreat-objection half of the title should be dropped.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the playtest. I read the digest at turn 10 and the code. docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op/digest.jsonl turn 10 has "Ney, retreat" with "(Trust him and he will attack Kutuzov at Carniola instead.)". Two lines later "Soult, attack Kutuzov" fails with "Soult cannot march on Kutuzov: Carniola is Austria's soil, and we are at peace with Austria". The wars record at turn 10 lists only Russia as an enemy. In backend/commands/disobedience.py the aggressive alternative builder `_get_aggressive_preferred` (line ~2639) filters candidates with `world.is_at_war(marshal.nation, m.nation)` and the RS-5 seen/believed-position and `_crossing_open` checks. It never asks the executor's peace-soil gate that produces "cannot march on" (combat_executor.py:1019). A Russian marshal standing on Austrian soil while France is at peace with Austria therefore passes the war check but is refused at execution. I found no closed row in BUG_FIXES.md for this.
reproduction.note: Only the first half of the finding stands. The offered Trust alternative can be an attack the executor refuses on peace-soil, and the objection builder never asks that gate. The retreat half is not a defect. "Ney, retreat" and "Lannes, retreat" are different marshals, and `world.is_in_danger(marshal)` (executor.py ~2578) is evaluated per marshal. Ney in danger and Lannes not is consistent. I could not confirm that the Trust button is refused when pressed, only that the same attack is refused for Soult. The impact is cosmetic or cheap, so I rate it P3, not P2. A fix would add the executor's peace-soil refusal predicate to the candidate filter.

findings.title: A commander named in the purpose clause hijacks the target: 'ride for Swabia and find Mack's flank' -> 'Mack is a commander, not a province. Name the province'
findings.seam: backend/commands/parser.py scout/move target extraction (reason-clause commander overrides the first named province)
findings.evidence: Probe, fresh boot: 'Murat, ride for Swabia and find Mack's flank.' -> "Mack is a commander, Sire, not a province. Name the province to scout, or 'Murat, pursue Mack'."; 'Massena, send patrols into Tyrol and report John's strength.' -> 'Archduke John is a commander...'. Blind-set rows with the same reply: 'Order Marshal Massena to Tyrol in order to threaten Archduke John', 'Bernadotte goes to Swabia and falls on Mack's rear', 'Transfer Bernadotte to Tyrol to threaten John', 'Soult will push patrols toward Swabia to fix Mack's position' (unrehearsed_2026_10_11 sixth+seventh, census class 'asked').
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/unrehearsed_census.py --blind tools/playtest_scripts/unrehearsed_2026_10_11_seventh.json --out OUT.json --trace  (rows 'Transfer Bernadotte to Tyrol to threaten John', 'Soult will push patrols toward Swabia...')
findings.expected: The province the player named is used; the commander in the reason clause is context.
findings.actual: Refused (nothing spent) telling the player to name a province they already named; 6 blind lines of 600.

mechanism.evidence: I reproduced it on a fresh in-process boot with LLM_MODE=mock through the FastAPI TestClient on /command. "Murat, scout Swabia and find Mack's flank" returned "Mack is a commander, Sire, not a province. Name the province to scout, or 'Murat, pursue Mack'." "Massena, send patrols into Tyrol and report John's strength." returned "Archduke John is a commander, Sire, not a province. ..." The reply text comes from `_marshal_not_a_province` at backend/commands/movement_executor.py:284-286. It fires when the scout/move target resolves to a foreign marshal's name. The target slot therefore holds the commander from the purpose clause, not the province the player named. The refusal returns `variable_action_cost` 0, so nothing is spent. No closed row covers it: grep of BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "is a commander" finds nothing, and DD0-19 (the sixth blind set) does not touch this class. I did not trace which parser stage swaps the target.
mechanism.note: The defect is real in the game's parser, not the harness. Nothing is spent and the refusal is explicit, but its text tells the player to name a province they already named. Frequency is low, about 6 of 600 blind lines. P3 fits better than P2 because the player can retry with "Murat, scout Swabia" and loses nothing. The probe also shows that "ride for Swabia" with no commander in the clause parsed as a different action (it printed the combat-range filter lines). I did not check it.

reproduction.evidence:
I booted a fresh mock-mode 1805 world, using the same path as tools/unrehearsed_census.py (M._reset_world_state, a fresh CommandParser, then TestClient POST /command), and sent each line on its own.

Refused, success False:
- "Murat, ride for Swabia and find Mack's flank." -> "Mack is a commander, Sire, not a province. Name the province to scout, or 'Murat, pursue Mack'."
- "Massena, send patrols into Tyrol and report John's strength." -> "Archduke John is a commander, Sire, not a province..."
- "Transfer Bernadotte to Tyrol to threaten John" -> same refusal naming Archduke John.
- "Soult will push patrols toward Swabia to fix Mack's position" -> same refusal naming Mack.
- "Bernadotte goes to Swabia and falls on Mack's rear" -> same refusal naming Mack.

Controls: "Murat, scout Swabia" succeeds, so the province is readable on its own. "Murat, ride for Swabia" is refused only for the honest board reason (enemy at Swabia, use ATTACK). The commander in the purpose clause is what changes the answer.

The refusal text comes from backend/commands/movement_executor.py:284-285, in _marshal_not_a_province, which is reached when the parsed target is a marshal's name. A search of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md found no closed row or ruling for this symptom. The nearest sibling, SF7-X10, fixed condition clauses (until/while/before) and the CRT-1 blanking covers reason clauses, but purposive "to threaten/find/fix/fall on/report X" tails are not covered.
reproduction.note: The defect is real and cheap to hit, but it is P3 rather than P2. It happens before any cost, so nothing is spent. The player is told to name a province they already named, and the line works when retyped without the purpose clause. The finding's blind-set count of 6 lines in 600 (1%) is plausible but I did not re-run the full census. A fix would extend the parser's reason-clause blanking (sibling of SF7-X10 / A_BLANKED_CLAUSE_NAMES_NO_TARGET) to purposive tails ("to threaten X", "and find X's flank", "to fix X's position", "and falls on X's rear", "report X's strength"). Under Rule 10, sibling verbs (scout, move, transfer, send patrols, go) need sweeping at the same time.

findings.title: Roles swapped or mis-scoped: 'March Bernadotte to Dresden and let the Elector...' asks 'Which marshal shall march to Bernadotte?'; 'Move everybody at Rhineland to Swabia' asks 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland?'; 'fortify everyone' asks which marshal while 'everyone fortify' fans out
findings.evidence: Probe: 'March Bernadotte to Dresden and let the Elector see French bayonets.' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Bernadotte, Sire?'; seventh set 'Move everybody at Rhineland to Swabia.' and sixth 'Everybody who is at Rhineland goes to Swabia' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland, Sire?'; 'hold ney' -> 'Which marshal shall hold Ney, Sire?'. rev1106-cmd-feel T8: 'fortify everyone' -> popup marshal_choice 'Which marshal shall carry out this order' answered with first option Ney, while T2 'everyone fortify' -> 'The order goes to the army, corps by corps - 10 corps, 10 actions for the 2 in hand'.
findings.repro: Probe lines above via POST /command on a fresh boot (mock parser)
findings.expected: Marshal and destination read correctly; 'everyone' recognised as a group address in both positions.
findings.actual: Nothing spent (honest) but the question asked is the wrong one, and the first offered option (Ney) is not a sane reading of 'everyone'.

mechanism.evidence:
I reproduced it in-process: TestClient POST /command, LLM_MODE=mock, CommandParser(use_real_llm=False), fresh 1805 boot per line (scratchpad p.py). Output:
- 'March Bernadotte to Dresden and let the Elector see French bayonets.' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Bernadotte, Sire?'
- 'Move everybody at Rhineland to Swabia.' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland, Sire?'
- 'Everybody who is at Rhineland goes to Swabia' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland, Sire?'
- 'hold ney' -> 'Which marshal shall hold Ney, Sire?'
- 'fortify everyone' -> 'Which marshal shall carry out this order, Sire?'
- 'everyone fortify' -> 'The order goes to the army, corps by corps — 8 corps, 8 actions for the 4 in hand'.
- Extra sibling: 'march everyone to Swabia' -> "Region 'Everyone' not found."
The plain form 'Bernadotte, march to Dresden' reaches the executor and gets the Saxony border refusal. So the lead-verb form "March Bernadotte to Dresden and ..." mis-binds the marshal as the destination.
The digest rev1106-cmd-feel T8 shows 'fortify everyone' raising a marshal_choice popup that the 'first' policy answered with Ney.
Mechanism: clarification.py:210 builds f"Which marshal shall {verb}, Sire?" from the extracted target, so the target slot is wrong. In llm_client.py the group-address handling (everyone/everybody at ~100, 374; the collective forms at 3790 and 3947) only recognises 'everyone' in some positions. Neither BUG_FIXES.md nor DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md has a row or ruling for these sentences.
mechanism.note: The defect is real. It is mock/fast-parser behaviour, and nothing is spent or mutated because the executor only asks a question. The popup for 'fortify everyone' is a choice the player can answer or cancel, and the first option is only the driver's 'first' policy. Impact is wrong-question friction, not a state or mechanics error, so I rate it P3 rather than P2. It is worth a fix under the sibling-sweep rule: 'fortify everyone' should fan out like 'everyone fortify', 'Move everybody at X to Y' needs a group-address arm, and the 'March <marshal> to <place>' extraction needs repair. Related finding: 'march everyone to Swabia' gives "Region 'Everyone' not found."

reproduction.evidence:
I ran an in-process probe. It used the test harness from tests/test_cx_r1_the_unbound_name_spends_nothing.py (the `board` fixture, which gives a fresh shipped 1805 board with the mock parser, and `_drive`, which posts to /command). On master ad73ba09 the probe printed:
- 'March Bernadotte to Dresden and let the Elector see French bayonets.' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Bernadotte, Sire?'
- 'Move everybody at Rhineland to Swabia.' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland, Sire?'
- 'Everybody who is at Rhineland goes to Swabia' -> 'Which marshal shall march to Rhineland, Sire?'
- 'hold ney' -> 'Which marshal shall hold Ney, Sire?'
- 'fortify everyone' -> 'Which marshal shall carry out this order, Sire?'
- 'everyone fortify' -> 'The order goes to the army, corps by corps — 8 corps, 8 actions for the 4 in hand'.
In each clarification case the only state change was `dialogue`, so nothing was spent. I found no matching row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md. I did not re-run the rev1106-cmd-feel playtest, so the T8 popup choice of Ney is not independently checked.
reproduction.note: The parser mis-scopes the sentences (CONFIRMED, via /command with the mock parser), but no state changes and no gold or AP is spent. The mis-asked question is a clarity and UX defect rather than a mechanics one. I rate it P3 instead of P2: the cost is one extra clarification, and the same order already works in the 'everyone fortify' phrasing. The 'hold ney' clarification, with the marshal name as the object, is the clearest parser bug.

findings.title: 'the Emperor' as a subject is not the sovereign: 'The Emperor's corps will move to Orleanais' -> no Marshal 'Emperor's'
findings.evidence: Blind sixth set: 'The Emperor's corps will move to Orleanais.' and 'The Emperor orders a general attack on Swabia.' -> "There is no Marshal 'Emperor's'/'Emperor' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?" while 'Napoleon, attack Mack' works. The closed row covers only the referent position ('Ney, support the Emperor').
findings.repro: Probe: post 'The Emperor's corps will move to Orleanais.'
findings.expected: The sovereign addressed by his title in subject position resolves to Napoleon.
findings.actual: Refused with 'Whom did you intend?'

mechanism.evidence: I ran normalize_sovereign_address(text, 'Napoleon') from the repo venv. "The Emperor's corps will move to Orleanais." and "The Emperor orders a general attack on Swabia." both come back unchanged, so they fall through to name resolution and fail as the finding says. By contrast, "The Emperor will march to Swabia" is rewritten to "Napoleon, march to Swabia". backend/commands/parser.py:717-720 shows why. _SOVEREIGN_EMPEROR_LEAD_RE requires "the emperor" followed by a modal (will/shall and the like) and then an order verb. The possessive "Emperor's corps" and the verb "orders" match neither. Lines 700-716 give a deliberate reason for this narrowness: an earlier version without the verb gate rewrote sentences about a different sovereign into orders (the NP-V follow-up). I did not find a ruling in the docs that treats these two forms as intended refusals.
mechanism.note: The behaviour is real, but it is a narrow phrasing gap in an intentionally gated rule, not a regression. The refusal ("Whom did you intend?") is safe and recoverable, and the player can type "Napoleon, ..." or "The Emperor will ..." instead. The "Emperor's corps" form is a possessive, and "The Emperor orders a general attack" is a third-person narration. Rewriting either risks the cross-sovereign misreads the gate was added to prevent. I counted it as P3 with design leanings. A fix would add a possessive form and "The Emperor orders ..." to the lead rule, with a corpus row for each. I did not check whether the refusal text comes from the unbound-name path, and I did not run a /command probe.

reproduction.evidence: I ran normalize_sovereign_address(text, "Napoleon") in-process (PYTHONPATH=. with .venv python). Results: "The Emperor's corps will move to Orleanais." came back unchanged. "The Emperor orders a general attack on Swabia." came back unchanged. "The Emperor will march to Swabia" became "Napoleon, march to Swabia". "Ney, support the Emperor" came back unchanged, which is correct because that is the referent position. The cause is in backend/commands/parser.py near lines 696-720. _SOVEREIGN_EMPEROR_LEAD_RE only matches "the emperor" followed by an optional modal (will/shall/must/am going to) and then a bare order verb. It does not match a possessive ("Emperor's corps") or a third-person finite verb such as "orders a general attack". I did not run the full /command path, so the "Whom did you intend?" refusal text is not reproduced here. The unchanged text does fall through to marshal-name resolution, which is consistent with the reported message. I found no NPC-18 row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md (it appears only in SCORE_FINISH_SPEC.md as a parser rider), so no closed row or ruling refutes this.
reproduction.note: Real but a narrow, contrived phrasing gap: third-person narration about the Emperor. It fails safe, refusing and asking whom the player meant, and spends no action points. The common forms "the Emperor will march ..." and "Emperor, attack ..." work. P3; it could also be filed as design if the possessive and "orders" forms are judged out of scope.

findings.title: Compound whose head is valid is refused by its tail noise with absurd suggestions: 'bring the Army of Italy to Piedmont and hold the passes' -> Region 'Passes' not found. Did you mean 'Posen' or 'Paris'?
findings.evidence: Probe and seventh set: 'Massena, bring the Army of Italy to Piedmont and hold the passes.' -> "Region 'Passes' not found. Did you mean 'Posen' or 'Paris'?" (nothing relayed for the Piedmont leg).
findings.repro: Probe: post that line on a fresh boot
findings.expected: Piedmont leg relayed with the tail reported as waiting (as 'hold Milan and march to Tyrol' does), or at least no nonsense suggestions.
findings.actual: Whole order refused; suggestions share no meaning with 'passes'.

mechanism.evidence: I booted the app in-process with TestClient and posted both lines to /command on master ad73ba09. 'Massena, bring the Army of Italy to Piedmont and hold the passes.' returned success False and "Region 'Passes' not found. Did you mean 'Posen' or 'Paris'?". The sibling 'Massena, hold Milan and march to Tyrol' returned success True, relayed the hold, and Berthier reported the tail as waiting. The same refusal is in the audit record docs/audits/unrehearsed/2026_10_11_seventh_keyed.json around line 5232. That record's mock_chain parse reads the line as action=hold, target=Piedmont. The parse is wrong: the intended action was a move to Piedmont, then hold. I did not trace the full path through the clause split into strategic_executor._suggest_region_for_phrase, but the probe is enough to show the symptom is real. A search of docs for 'hold the passes' found only the audit JSONs, with no BUG_FIXES row for it.
mechanism.note: A real but minor parser and UX defect, and the game is not harmed. The whole order is refused with no state change. The fuzzy region suggestions ('Posen', 'Paris') are nonsense. Closest sibling: 'hold X and march to Y' works. The failing shape is 'move X and hold Y' where the hold target is a noun phrase that is not a region.

reproduction.evidence: Ran an in-process TestClient probe (scratchpad p.py, PYTHONPATH=. with .venv python) posting "Massena, bring the Army of Italy to Piedmont and hold the passes." to /command on a default boot (europe 126 regions, seed historical). The log showed "[OK] Parsed: hold", then "[STRATEGIC] Creating HOLD order for Massena -> Passes", and the final message "Region 'Passes' not found. Did you mean 'Posen' or 'Paris'?". Nothing was relayed for the Piedmont leg, and "Passes" is not a region. The suggestions are fuzzy-match noise. The suggester is _suggest_region_for_phrase at backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:621. I did not trace the clause-split code in parser.py. No row mentions CMDFEEL in docs/BUG_FIXES.md (grep empty), so no closed row or ruling covers it.
reproduction.note: Reproduces as filed. The parse picked "hold" for the whole line and treated "the passes" as a region, so the move to Piedmont was dropped. Refusing the order with an honest error costs nothing and no state changes, so P3 stands. I did not run the "hold Milan and march to Tyrol" comparison.

findings.title: A typo in a marshal's name gets no suggestion while a typo in a region does ('Nay attack Mack' vs 'Swabland')
findings.seam: backend/commands/executor.py unbound-name path (CX-R1: an unbound name spends nothing)
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-typed T4: 'Nay attack Mack' -> "There is no 'Nay' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?" while 'Davoust, fortify' resolved and T5 'Ney, march to Swabland' -> "Region 'Swabland' not found. Did you mean 'Swabia'?"
findings.repro: Probe: post 'Nay attack Mack'
findings.expected: "Did you mean Ney?" like the region path.
findings.actual: Bare refusal listing no candidates (safe, but a dead end for a one-letter slip).

mechanism.note: The symptom is real and reproducible, but it is a deliberate noise guard, not a defect. A three-letter word binds only on an exact match. The refusal itself is pinned by tests/test_cx1_a_question_never_orders.py as "a one-letter slip -> refused free, names the miss". The finding would stand only as a UX nicety: offering "Did you mean Ney?" for very short names. That would need a decision about short-word noise, because "Nay" is also an English word. The refusal costs 0 AP and executes nothing, so there is no mechanical harm. This is a design question, not a P3 bug.
mechanism.evidence: Probe: scratchpad/probe_nay.py, in-process TestClient in mock mode on master. "Nay attack Mack" and "Nay, attack Mack" both returned "There is no 'Nay' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?" with no clarification options. "Ney, march to Swabland" returned "Region 'Swabland' not found. Did you mean 'Swabia'?". "Davoust, fortify" resolved to Davout. This matches digest rev1106-cmd-typed T4/T5. The suggestion path does exist (parser.py ~2240 and 2364 return kind "marshal_suggest"; clarification.py:475 builds "Did you mean X?"). It is not reached for "Nay" because of the guard at backend/commands/parser.py:1668-1670: "# Words shorter than this can only bind as an EXACT name — a three-letter fuzzy hit is noise, not a typo. _MIN_FUZZY_TARGET_LEN = 4". The refusal comes from backend/commands/executor.py:2076, `_unbound_addressee`, in the CX-R1/FA-22 path. The pin is tests/test_cx1_a_question_never_orders.py:439, UNBINDABLE ("Nay attack Mack", "a one-letter slip"), with the class docstring at 429-430. The pin was written because "Nay attack Mack" previously sent Soult into a real battle.

reproduction.evidence:
I ran an in-process probe with a TestClient on backend.main.app, once on the legacy world (SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO=none) and once on the default Europe 1805 boot. The probe script is in the scratchpad as p.py.

Europe 1805 boot (the finding's board):
- "Nay attack Mack", "Nay, attack Mack", "Nay, fortify" and "Nay fortify" all returned "There is no 'Nay' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?" with no clarification_kind and no options.
- "Ney, march to Swabland" returned "Region 'Swabland' not found. Did you mean 'Swabia'?"
- "Davoust, fortify" resolved and fortified Davout.

Legacy world (SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO=none): the same "Nay" commands returned "I do not find 'Nay' in the order of battle, Sire. Did you mean Ney?" with clarification_kind=unknown_name and the option ['Ney'].

The digest line also matches: docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-typed/digest.md:103 shows "Nay attack Mack" refused with "Whom did you intend?".

The cause is a split between two code paths. The parser's unknown-name suggestion (parser.py ~2487, clarification.py:475 "Did you mean {label}?") fires on the legacy board but not on Europe. On Europe the typo falls through to the executor's CX-R1 unbound-addressee refusal at executor.py:2076-2077, which hardcodes "Whom did you intend?" and lists no candidates. I did not establish why the parser path is skipped on Europe, but that is likely the sibling-sweep seam. I found no BUG_FIXES.md row or recorded ruling that makes the bare refusal intended.

The refusal is safe: it spends nothing and no wrong marshal acts. It is a dead end for a one-letter slip, and it is inconsistent with the region path.
reproduction.note: The finding is real but minor. A fix would offer the nearest roster name from the executor's unbound-name refusal when it fuzzy-matches (the parser's marshal_suggest clarification already does this on the legacy board). The 'design' label undersells it a little: the suggestion exists in the codebase and simply is not reached on the Europe board, so it is closer to a P3 defect than a design choice.

findings.title: A war-purpose card is offered (and answered) for an attack whose declaration is barred by the fresh-peace floor
findings.seam: backend/commands/combat_executor.py _stage_war_purpose_selection (call sites ~7879/9795/11195) vs diplomacy.offensive_call_bar / pair cooldown
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-op T7: 'Ney, attack Hungary', 'Lannes, attack Tyrol' (x2) and T8 'Massena, attack Archduke Charles' each -> "Choose your war purpose against Austria. Issue the attack again after the declaration is settled." then popups war_purpose_selection #18/#19 -> 1 and "refused: Our peace with Austria is fresh: no war may be declared on her for 4 more turns." (3 more turns at T8). Same state, different order shape: 'Soult, attack Vienna' (T6) is refused up front as 'at peace with Austria'.
findings.repro: Replay cmd-op (see CMDFEEL-3 repro) and read turns 6-8
findings.expected: The bar is read before the purpose card opens, one refusal naming the turns left.
findings.actual: Two modal cards then a refusal, and the first reply says checkmark.

mechanism.evidence: Seam, combat_executor.py `_attack_war_and_bombard_target` (~8760-8766): for the player, after friendly_fire_refusal it goes straight to `return ctx._stage_war_purpose_for_attack(...)`. The same happens at ~8850. The stager (`_stage_war_purpose_for_attack`, 7877-7890) returns success True and the message "Choose your war purpose against Austria. Issue the attack again after the declaration is settled." `_stage_war_purpose_selection` (13002) calls `open_flow` with no bar check. It does not read `declaration_cooldown_left`, `peace_with_target_is_fresh` or `offensive_call_bar` (diplomacy.py:11092, which bars callees only). The fresh-peace floor is only read on the declaration path, whose sentence is built at diplomacy.py:4271 ("Our peace with ... is fresh: no war may be declared on her for N more turns"). Digest docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op/digest.md, Turn 7, lines 229-232 and 233-236: 'Ney, attack Hungary' and 'Lannes, attack Tyrol' each get "✓ Choose your war purpose against Austria...", then two war_purpose_selection popups (#18, #19), then "refused: Our peace with Austria is fresh: ... for 4 more turns". Turn 8 repeats it with 'Massena, attack Archduke Charles'. The finding's claims hold. 'Soult, attack Vienna' is refused up front because it takes a different, non-staging path. PC-F73 (BUG_FIXES.md:2040) only fixed the wording of the refusal; it did not add a pre-check on the purpose-card path, so the fix does not cover this.
mechanism.note: Real but cosmetic. No state is corrupted: the declaration is still refused and no AP or DP is lost. The player sees a misleading success reply, then answers a modal card that cannot succeed. The fix is to read the pair-cooldown / fresh-peace bar in `_stage_war_purpose_for_attack` and refuse with the pair_cooldown_words text before opening the flow. The same check belongs at the other call sites (9795, 11195, 12704). Sibling sweep (Rule 10) applies.

reproduction.evidence: The repro is a digest read, so I re-read docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op/digest.md and did not re-run the playtest. Lines 229-236 and 240-243 show 'Ney, attack Hungary' and 'Lannes, attack Tyrol' (twice), each returning "✓ Choose your war purpose against Austria. Issue the attack again after the declaration is settled." Each is followed by two war_purpose_selection popups answered "1", then "refused: Our peace with Austria is fresh: no war may be declared on her for 4 more turns." Line 272-275 shows 'Massena, attack Archduke Charles' at T8 with the same sequence and "3 more turns". Line 3 shows the policy war_purpose "1". The turn-6 peace is shown at digest lines 215-222. The code agrees. backend/commands/combat_executor.py:7877 defines `_stage_war_purpose_for_attack`, which calls `_stage_war_purpose_selection` (line 13002) and returns success=True with the "Issue the attack again" message. Its only inputs are `get_available_war_objectives` and `_war_purpose_prompt`. It never calls `offensive_call_bar` or the pair-cooldown check, which sit at diplomacy.py:11092 and :4271. No fresh-peace check precedes the stage at call sites 8766 and 8850. The bar is therefore only discovered after the card is answered. I found no closed row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for this. PC-F73 and PC-X8 only fixed the wording of the refusal.
reproduction.note: Real but minor. The player ends up refused with the right words, but only after a modal card whose first reply reads as a success. The finding gives the 'at peace with Austria' refusal for 'Soult, attack Vienna' at T6 as the contrast, and I did not re-check that line. The fix is to read the bar before staging the purpose card. The finding's cited call sites 9795/11195 were not individually verified. It is a game defect, not a harness defect.

findings.title: 'recruit for Marmont' (uncommissioned) ignores the named marshal in its reply
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-op T5, T8, T9 x2, T10, T11: 'recruit for Marmont' -> "'No marshal is available to receive reinforcements, Sire.' Recruits join a marshal who can reach the depot: Ney (out of range..." while 'Marmont, move to Normandy' -> "There is no 'Marmont' in the order of battle". Six repeats of an unanswered line.
findings.repro: Replay cmd-op; or probe 'recruit for Marmont' on a fresh boot
findings.expected: 'Marmont is not in your order of battle - commission him first' (the CX-R1 voice).
findings.actual: Reply talks about other marshals' range and never mentions the name typed.

mechanism.evidence: The digest lines match. docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op/digest.md lines 276, 298, 299, 340 and 380 show `recruit for Marmont` answered "'No marshal is available to receive reinforcements, Sire.' Recruits join a marshal who can reach the depot: Ney (out of range…". Line 333 shows `Marmont, move to Normandy` answered "There is no 'Marmont' in the order of battle". I probed the parser with `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8`, which runs the mock parser. `recruit for Marmont` returns marshal=None, action=recruit, confidence 0.8. `recruit for Ney` returns marshal='Ney'. So an uncommissioned name after 'for' is dropped at parse time. The recruit then runs as a marshal-less levy, and the failure text comes from `_recruit_block_reason` (backend/commands/economy_executor.py:322) and `_recruit_block_reason_from` (~:341). That text lists the other marshals' range and never mentions the typed name. CX-R1 (backend/commands/executor.py:1239, `_unbound_addressee`) only covers an ADDRESSED name ('Zorglub, recruit…') and does not cover a 'for <name>' tail. BUG_FIXES.md has no closed row for this class. SFR-H7 and DDB-R5 cover a named marshal who IS bound. I did not probe whether `recruit for <unknown name>` spends gold when some marshal is in reach. That would be a worse sibling and is worth a Rule-10 sweep.
mechanism.note: The defect is real but small. In the cited case nothing is spent, and the refusal is accurate about the range problem, so only the voice is wrong. The fix is to bind or refuse a 'for <Name>' tail that names a pool marshal who is not commissioned, and to point at `commission <Name>` as the CX-R1 voice does. Sibling to sweep: a 'for <unknown name>' recruit where a marshal is in range, which could levy for someone other than the man named.

reproduction.evidence: I ran an in-process probe: fresh 1805 boot, mock parser, FastAPI TestClient posting to /command. 'recruit for Marmont' returned success False with "No marshal is available to receive reinforcements, Sire.' Recruits join a marshal who can reach the depot: Ney (out of range...)...". 'recruit for Zorblax' (an invented name) returned the same text. 'Marmont, move to Normandy' returned "There is no 'Marmont' in the order of battle, Sire. Whom did you intend?". 'recruit for Ney' reached the named-marshal path and returned a gold refusal. So the unknown-name recruit never reaches the named-marshal branch. The no-marshal text comes from backend/commands/economy_executor.py:413, with the nearest-marshal fallback at about line 1702. Grepping docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md found no closed row for this symptom.
reproduction.note: It reproduces as filed. The reply is a refusal, so nothing wrong is executed. The player is only misled about why: the unknown name is silently dropped and the reply blames range. Likely cause: the parser or fuzzy match fails to resolve the name and the command falls through to the nearest-marshal path. I did not trace that step. The fix is to run the same unknown-name check that the move verbs use before the recipient search.

findings.title: Marshal drama text is thin: one objection string for four aggressive marshals; audience resolution is a constant line with no stated consequence; audiences fire up to 5 times in 10 turns
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-fld: marshal_audience on T1 (Murat), T4 (Bernadotte), T5 (Davout), T6 (Murat), T10 (Bernadotte), each answered acknowledge with the identical "X's grievance runs its course" (also 5/5 in cmd-feel). Fortify objections: Ney, Murat, Lannes and Massena all say "I would rather attack than sit idle." (cmd-feel T2, cmd-hold T2, blind sets); only Massena also varies to 'Sire, we have the advantage. Let me strike!'.
findings.repro: grep -c 'grievance runs its course' tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-fld/digest.md
findings.expected: Acknowledging an audience says what changed (trust, expectation, relationship); aggressive marshals have distinct voices.
findings.actual: Constant sentence, no delta shown; repetition is the main thing the player hears from marshals.

mechanism.evidence: The facts are real, but they describe thin copy and not a malfunction. (1) backend/game_logic/jealousy.py:4239 is the final else arm of the confrontation choice handler and returns f"{marshal.name}'s grievance runs its course." This is the acknowledge/default arm. Every other arm (rebuke, honour) states a trust delta. `grep -c` on docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-fld/digest.md returns 5, and cmd-feel also returns 5. (2) backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:800 returns "'I would rather attack than sit idle.'" for the aggressive personality on fortify/hold/wait/defend at low concern. Lines 796-798 add only the EXTREME and STRONG variants, so the copy is keyed on personality and concern level, with no per-marshal voice. cmd-feel digest lines 44 and 50 show Lannes and Ney getting the identical line. Only the tone prefix differs. The marshal_audience popups fire at turns 1, 4, 5, 6 and 10 in cmd-fld (digest lines 30, 127 and 159 are three of them). The finding's claim that Massena varies is explained by concern level, not by marshal.
mechanism.note: Copy and feel polish, with no mechanics defect. The audience frequency is jealousy-engine behaviour by design, and acknowledge is deliberately the do-nothing option, so an unchanged message is arguably honest. The valid content is that the acknowledge line shows no delta, and that the aggressive marshals share one objection string per concern level. I did not check docs/BUG_FIXES.md or the specs for a ruling that covers this.

reproduction.evidence: Repro: `grep -c 'grievance runs its course'` gives 5 in rev1106-cmd-fld/digest.md, 5 in cmd-feel and 2 in cmd-hold. The only source is backend/game_logic/jealousy.py:4239, in the acknowledge else-branch: `message = f"{marshal.name}'s grievance runs its course."`. That line is constant per marshal and states no trust or relationship delta. The honour branch above it does state its delta. backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:798-800 returns the one line "I would rather attack than sit idle." for any aggressive personality on a fortify, hold, defend or wait order at the default concern level. The digests show this line on many different marshals' fortify objections. The same function has a distinct STRONG line, 'Sire, we have the advantage. Let me strike!', and an EXTREME line. A grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for the string and for CMDFEEL-11 found no match, so no closed row or ruling covers it. I did not check how often audiences fire (up to 5 in 10 turns). The finding's own cmd-fld evidence lists 5 audiences, and the 5-in-cmd-fld count matches it.
reproduction.note: The facts are real, but this is a text-variety and feedback gap, not a mechanical defect. Mechanics are unaffected: acknowledge runs deterministically and the objection options are correct. Audience frequency is not verified. The suggested fix is to add a delta line to the acknowledge arm and per-personality or per-marshal variants of the aggressive fortify objection. Both are cheap copy changes.

findings.title: Morning dispatch headline repeats: crowding template on 5 of 18 mornings; an identical sentence two mornings running
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-op headlines T2, T7, T9, T12, T13 all 'X stand N men at P, which feeds 60,000. N too many. M men lost in K turns...'; rev1106-cmd-feel T8 and T9 both read 'Sire - Prussia moves toward war with Hanover. The design is open; the timing is not.'
findings.repro: read DISPATCH lines of docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-op and rev1106-cmd-feel
findings.expected: A headline that has not changed is demoted when something newer exists.
findings.actual: Same sentence leads consecutive mornings.

mechanism.evidence:
The symptom is real in the digests, but both halves are the ruled behaviour of `_select_headline`, not a defect.

1. Identical sentence two mornings running. `rev1106-cmd-feel/digest.md` lines 264 and 289 (T8, T9) both read "Sire — Prussia moves toward war with Hanover. The design is open; the timing is not." The exact-repeat demotion exists at `backend/game_logic/dispatch.py:3643-3649`. It only fires when there is another distinct candidate: `if _prev_text and len(candidates) > 1 and candidates[0]["text"] == _prev_text`. In both mornings the other items under the DISPATCH line are RAIL entries (settlement offer, landing, proposals), not headline candidates. So Prussia/Hanover was probably the sole candidate. I did not re-derive the candidate list.
2. Why a sole candidate repeats. The comment block at `dispatch.py:340-380` says a standing crisis is "demoted to a sub-beat (never suppressed)". The pin `test_headline_keeps_its_lead_when_it_is_the_only_news` keeps it leading when it is the only news. The authors judged repetition better than a page that says nothing.
3. Crowding template on 5 of 18 mornings. In `rev1106-cmd-op/digest.md` the lines at 69, 262, 309, 433 and 465 (T2, T7, T9, T12, T13) are the supply_strain headline. `supply_strain` is in `STANDING_HEADLINE_CLASSES` (`dispatch.py:380-382`). That class has a lead cooldown and an escalation ladder (`_STANDING_ESCALATION`, loop around `dispatch.py:3715-3750`). The sentences are not identical: the men, the excess and the losses change each morning. T12 reads 97,700 men and 10,066 lost in 3 turns; T13 reads 67,231 men and 9,220 lost. The player's armies were over supply for 13 turns, so the headline was true each time. The class is also a recorded earlier fix (the "measured over 42 played turns" comment).
4. Not a closed row. I found no `BUG_FIXES.md` or `DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md` row that rules this exact repeat out. The recorded intent is "yield to other news, else escalate".

Residual gap. The Prussia/Hanover brewing-crisis class is not in `STANDING_HEADLINE_CLASSES`, so it has no escalation text. When it is the sole candidate it repeats verbatim, which is a small polish gap against the stated principle. The finding's "expected" line, that a repeated headline is demoted when something newer exists, matches the existing rule and is already implemented. It is only unmet when nothing newer exists.
mechanism.note: Design, not P1/P2/P3. Both behaviours follow from the pinned rule "demote when other news exists, otherwise keep (supply_strain escalates)". Optional polish: give the brewing-crisis headline an escalation variant or add it to the standing set. That would need an owner row under Golden Rule 9, and I did not open one.

reproduction.evidence:
I read the digests and the headline code. I did not run a playtest or an in-process probe, so I never saw the candidate list for T8/T9.

cmd-op: the crowding headline leads T2, T7, T9, T12 and T13, but the sentences differ because the figures change (69,295, 60,853, 60,126, 97,700, 67,231 men). Only T12 and T13 are consecutive. T7 and T9 have the Prussia-Hanover dispatch at T8 between them.

cmd-feel: T8 (digest.md:264) and T9 (:289) do carry the identical sentence 'Prussia moves toward war with Hanover. The design is open; the timing is not.' (template `europe_crisis`, dispatch.py:660). The T8 rail shows crisis_brewing, which suggests it was the only live candidate.

The rule the finding asks for already exists. `_select_headline` (dispatch.py ~3626-3636) demotes an exact repeat of yesterday's headline whenever another distinct candidate exists, in the 'Creative audit July 19 2026' block: `if _prev_text and len(candidates) > 1 and candidates[0]["text"] == _prev_text: ... candidates.insert(0, ...)`. So the repeat only survives when nothing else is on the page, which is the finding's own 'unless something newer exists' condition.

Standing classes also have a lead cap (STANDING_LEAD_MAX=2) and escalation variants. The crowding template is a standing class (`supply_strain`), so it is already throttled and varied.

I found no BUG_FIXES row for either symptom. This is a repeat of a standing crisis on a quiet board, not a rule violation.
reproduction.note: At most this is a design preference: a non-standing `europe_crisis` headline could escalate or vary wording on day two when it is the sole candidate. Nothing is broken. The existing exact-repeat demotion works as specified, and the crowding lines are not verbatim repeats.

findings.title: Blind unrehearsed_* scripts use an 'orders' key the playtest driver ignores: run as written they play ten empty turns
findings.seam: tools/playtest_driver.py script loader vs tools/unrehearsed_census.py (the real consumer)
findings.evidence: rev1106-cmd-unrehearsed-6 and -7: meta commands 10, ap_spent 0, cmd_refused 0; digest shows only 'end turn' each turn. The script keys are name/_note/orders (300 lines); census ran them instead (sixth 277/300, seventh 276/300 read right).
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 10 --name x --fresh --script tools/playtest_scripts/unrehearsed_2026_10_11_seventh.json
findings.expected: A script with no 'turns' (or an unknown top-level key) errors or says it played nothing.
findings.actual: Silent no-op run that looks like a completed 10-turn arm.

mechanism.evidence: tools/playtest_driver.py:4639 reads only `script.get("turns")`: `turn_scripts = {str(k): v for k, v in (script.get("turns") or {}).items()}`. Nothing in the driver warns on unknown top-level keys. The unrehearsed_* scripts (7 files in tools/playtest_scripts) use `name`/`_note`/`orders` (the seventh file starts `{"name": ..., "_note": ..., "orders": [ {"line":..., "intended":...}`). Their real consumer is tools/unrehearsed_census.py:232 (`blind.get("orders", [])`). So a driver run plays only `end turn`, as the reviewer's digests show (ap_spent 0).
mechanism.note: This is a harness defect, not a game defect. The scripts are census inputs, not driver scripts, so the behaviour is only a footgun: the driver gives no warning when a script has no `turns` key. A guard in the driver, or a rename or README note on the files, would close it. I did not run the driver, since the code path is clear from reading it. I did not find a closed BUG_FIXES row for it.

reproduction.evidence:
The mechanism is confirmed by reading the code. I did not run the playtest.
- tools/playtest_driver.py:4639 reads only `script.get("turns")`: `turn_scripts = {str(k): v for k, v in (script.get("turns") or {}).items()}`. A grep for `"orders"` in the driver found no loader for that key.
- tools/playtest_scripts/unrehearsed_2026_10_11_seventh.json has top-level keys `name`, `_note` and `orders`. Its lines look like {"line": "Soult, march to Swabia.", "intended": {...}}. It has no `turns` key.
- The real consumer is tools/unrehearsed_census.py. Its header describes the blind file as "150 orders with their intended reading" and runs it one line per fresh boot through POST /command. The driver is not its consumer.
- The reviewer's digest figures (meta commands 10, ap_spent 0, only "end turn") are what the driver would produce for a script with no `turns` entry. That matches 10 empty turns.
- The driver does `json.loads` and then silently ignores unknown top-level keys. It does not warn or error.
reproduction.note: This is a harness defect, not a game defect. The scripts are census inputs, and running them through playtest_driver.py is a misuse. The real gap is that the driver accepts a script with no `turns` key and unknown top-level keys without saying so. A one-line warning or error would close it. I found no existing BUG_FIXES row for it; the grep for the finding id returned nothing.

findings.title: Mode A digest prints no marshal trust, relationship or vindication row, so 'trust that moves and matters' cannot be measured from it
findings.seam: tools/playtest_driver.py digest rows (only redemption popup carries trust)
findings.evidence: No digest row among kinds {turn,command,battle,popup,enemy_phase,ledger,dispatch_row,...} carries a marshal's trust; the only trust number seen came from a typed question (cmd-hold T1: 'Bernadotte's trust stands at 40 of 100 - Strained'). No defiance/compromise/vindication line appeared in any arm.
findings.repro: grep -ci vindicat tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-*/digest.jsonl
findings.expected: A per-turn MARSHALS row (trust, glory, grievance) like LEDGER's vassals row (IQ-7 precedent).
findings.actual: Marshal drama is only visible through popups.

mechanism.evidence: The cmd-hold digest (docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-cmd-hold/digest.jsonl) has these row kinds: applied_bill, autonomous_attack, battle, campaign_log, chest_window, command, dispatch, dispatch_row, economy, enemy_phase, envoy_digest_answer, envoys, forecast, ledger, loyalty, note, order_progress, popup, purses, rail, turn, turn_events, turn_spend, wars. None is a marshal trust, glory or grievance row. The only "loyalty" rows are vassals (Switzerland, Holland). The string "trust" appears in just 2 lines of that digest, one command row and one popup row. In tools/playtest_driver.py, "trust" is only the objection policy (lines 94, 689, 3273), a trust_note on a battle (2058), and the redemption popup summary (3526). The vassal precedent is real: `ledger_line` (line 2644) builds a "vassals" record (line 2704) from the ledger's vassals section (line 1858). No equivalent exists for marshals.
mechanism.note: This is a harness observability gap, not a game defect. Marshal trust, glory and grievance exist in the game and in the marshal_overview and ledger builders, but the Mode A digest does not emit them. P3 is fair. A MARSHALS row built on the vassals-row pattern would fix it.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the repro. `grep -ci vindicat tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-cmd-*/digest.jsonl` returns 0 for all 13 cmd arms. I then counted the digest row kinds in cmd-hold and cmd-feel. The kinds are note, turn, command, wars, chest_window, applied_bill, loyalty, battle, enemy_phase, envoys, ledger, purses, economy, dispatch, rail, turn_events, dispatch_row, campaign_log, envoy_digest_answer, popup, forecast, turn_spend, order_progress and autonomous_attack. None is a per-marshal trust, glory or grievance row. The `loyalty` kind is the vassal row, not marshals. Only 4 rows in cmd-hold and 9 in cmd-feel contain the word "trust" at all. I did not open them, so I cannot say what they are. In `tools/playtest_driver.py`, `self.d.popup("redemption", _summ(payload, "marshal", "trust"), ...)` (line 3526) is the only place trust goes into a digest. `ledger_line` (line 2644) takes a vassals bit and no marshals bit. No closed row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md covers a MARSHALS digest row. SFR-D2 added the typed question "how loyal are my marshals?", so the game itself answers it. This is a gap in the playtest driver, not a game defect.
reproduction.note: Harness defect (kind=harness). The game is fine. The Mode A digest has no marshal trust/glory/grievance row, so marshal drama can only be measured from popups or typed questions. Adding a per-turn MARSHALS row, following the IQ-7 vassals-row precedent, would fix it.

findings.title: _build_economy scans every region twice per call and is called 17-22 times a turn (Golden Rule 8)
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/ledger.py:1351 and :1364 (_build_economy); callers backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:7322, backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1239 (ai_purse_refusal), ledger.py:836 and :1100
findings.evidence: ledger.py:1351 and :1364 read `for region in world.regions.values():` (construction_queue and income_breakdown). CLAUDE.md Golden Rule 8 forbids this in functions called more than once per turn. Measured on the historical seed over 30 turns (in-process, mock LLM): _build_economy 15-22 calls per end turn (4 player + 11-18 AI), max 22 on turn 7. That is about 2 x 126 x 17 = 4,300 region visits a turn. The AI calls build construction_queue and income_breakdown, which no AI caller reads. get_nation_regions(player) is the cached equivalent. Total end-turn wall time was 0.31-0.40 s, so the cost is small today. The rubric would call this P1 because it breaks a Golden Rule; I filed it P2 because I measured no player-visible harm. The cost grows with every AI purse test added.
findings.repro: INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR=<tmp> ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 <scratchpad>/econ_count.py 30. It wraps ledger._build_economy and counts per end turn. Alternatively run AST scan <scratchpad>/scan.py backend/game_logic/ledger.py and read the _build_economy hits.

The reviewer's own measurement shows no player-visible harm: 0.31-0.40 s per end turn in total. I found no closed row or user ruling that covers this seam.
