findings.title: The Charges' restless-interior term is binary: 1 and 32 restless provinces cost the same rate, and the peace-time chest level at 60 provinces overshoots the 40k target
findings.evidence: Probe: France with 60 provinces (32 conquered), peace, chest 20,000. Restless provinces 1, 5, 20 and 32 all give rate 325 (crown 250 + restless_interior 75) and charges 2,340. Occupation rises 1,363 to 3,403 across the same range, so the per-province price is carried by Occupation alone. The term is `if restless_regions:` with a fixed CHARGES_UNREST_RATE. At peace the chest settles at 2000 + S*2500/rate. Derived S is +4,143 at 60 provinces (+2,275 at 45), giving 43,430 at rate 250 and 33,000 at rate 325. The 'France under 40k' calibration (S14j) was measured at war on four commanded seeds, not on a 60-province peace.
findings.repro: Run <scratchpad>/econ_unrest.py (fresh world, 60 provinces to France, vary stability of the conquered set). Then <scratchpad>/probe1.py for the 28/45/60 net table.
findings.expected: A named term that prices how restless the empire is, or a stated ruling that the term is binary. At scale (126 provinces) a binary any-province trigger is nearly always on and stops discriminating.
findings.actual: Rate is the same for 1 and 32 restless provinces. No spec ruling found for the 'binary' choice. The code comment calls it 'any held province disrupted ... or at/below the unrest line'.
findings.prior_row: FA-D1 (slice 17, restless-interior terms carry the provinces); EB-1

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is as filed. backend/models/world_state.py:7598-7613 collects restless_regions across the nation's provinces, then appends a single term `if restless_regions:` with `"amount": CHARGES_UNREST_RATE`. That constant is a fixed 75 (line 709), so 1 restless province and 32 restless provinces add the same 75. The `regions` list is display-only. The B1-B5 terms (war 50, ill 75, grip 50, unrest 75) are all flat condition terms, so unrest is consistent with its siblings. The per-province price is carried separately by Occupation, which is what the finding says. I found no spec ruling for the binary choice. A grep of docs/audits/ECONOMY_REBALANCE_2026_10_27.md for unrest, restless, binary and "any province" returned nothing, and BUG_FIXES.md has no matching row. The 40k calibration comment at lines 700-707 names "four commanded seeds" and does not mention a 60-province peace. I did not re-run the reviewer's probe or independently check the 43,430 / 33,000 chest figures.
mechanism.note: This is a P3 design observation, not a defect. The code does what its comment says ("any held province disrupted ... or at/below the unrest line"), and Occupation already scales with province count. The finding's claim that the term "stops discriminating" at 126 provinces is plausible but unmeasured here. Resolving it needs a user ruling, either that the term is binary by design or that it should scale. The chest-overshoot claim rests on the reviewer's probe numbers and was not reproduced.

reproduction.evidence:
I did not re-run the probe scripts. I only read the code and docs.
- Binary term confirmed. backend/models/world_state.py:7605-7613 has `if restless_regions:` and appends one term whose amount is the fixed `CHARGES_UNREST_RATE` (line 709, value 75). The term is the same for 1 or 32 restless provinces. The count only changes the label ("+N more") and the `regions` list.
- No ruling found. Greps of docs/audits/ECONOMY_REBALANCE_2026_10_27.md, docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "restless", "binary" and "UNREST_RATE" found nothing that rules the term binary. FA-D1 (slice 17) only made the term name its provinces.
- The term is small in practice. docs/audits/ECONOMY_GATE_2026_10_05.md:83 puts "restless interior" at 1-3% of charges. The Occupation term carries the per-province price, as the finding says.
- Not verified: the 43,430 and 33,000 chest figures at 60 provinces.
reproduction.note: This is a real design observation, not a defect. The code does what its comment says, and the term is a flat B4 line in the spec table. At the 126-province scale a flat any-province trigger will almost always be on, so it stops discriminating. The 40k-at-peace overshoot is an unmeasured extrapolation. The finding should go down as a design note with no fix required unless the user wants a scaled term.

findings.title: A treaty manpower transfer bypasses the pool cap and the next regen silently deletes the surplus
findings.evidence: The receiver is credited with `to_pool.get("infantry", 0) + transfer` (world_state.py:15386-15387) and `... + transfer` (diplomatic_executor.py:4637-4638) with no MAX_INFANTRY_POOL clamp. The source is debited unconditionally while the credit is guarded by `if to_nation in self.manpower_pools`, so men vanish if the receiver has no row. _process_manpower_regen then runs `pool["infantry"] = min(pool["infantry"] + inf_regen, MAX_INFANTRY_POOL)` (:8187). Probe: Austria infantry pool set to 140,000 (as a transfer would leave it), one _process_manpower_regen call, pool = 100,000. The surplus 40,000 is deleted with no notice. A lord receiving tribute men past the cap is told nothing.
findings.repro: <scratchpad>/econ_pool.py prints: cap 100000 pool before regen 140000 after regen 100000.
findings.expected: Transfers are clamped at the cap (and the sender debited only for what lands), or the regen never lowers an over-cap pool.
findings.actual: Over-cap pool created by a transfer, silently cut by regen.

mechanism.evidence: I read the code and traced the logic by hand. I did not run the reviewer's probe. world_state.py:15383-15387 credits the receiver with `to_pool.get("infantry", 0) + transfer` and no cap. The source is debited at :15381 whenever it has a pool row. The credit is guarded by `if to_nation in self.manpower_pools`, so the men vanish when the receiver has no row. diplomatic_executor.py:4634-4637 does the same for ultimatum demands: it debits the target and credits `to_pool.get(unit_type, 0) + transfer`, with no MAX_* clamp. world_state.py:8187 runs `pool["infantry"] = min(pool["infantry"] + inf_regen, MAX_INFANTRY_POOL)`, with MAX_INFANTRY_POOL = 100000 at :390. An over-cap pool therefore drops to 100,000 on the next regen, and the surplus is gone without a notice. Both paths are reachable. diplomatic_templates.py:3653-3655 can demand up to 5,000 `manpower_infantry`, and `manpower_per_turn` is a live stream clause (diplomacy.py:236 and :375). No row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md covers the symptom, and I found no recorded ruling. Impact is small: a transfer only wastes men when the receiver is already near the cap, and the per-transfer sizes are modest.
mechanism.note: The defect is real but minor, so P3 stands. The sender is debited in full while the receiver loses the surplus above the cap. A clamp should cap the credit at the receiver's headroom and debit the sender only for what lands. The sibling sweep should cover the cavalry and artillery branches in diplomatic_executor.py:4634-4637, which have the same flaw, and the no-receiver-row path.

reproduction.evidence:
I read the code and confirmed the mechanism. I did not get the probe to run.

- world_state.py:15383-15387: `manpower_per_turn` debits the source with `max(0, from - transfer)`. It credits the receiver with `to_pool.get("infantry",0) + transfer`, with no MAX_INFANTRY_POOL clamp. The credit sits behind `if to_nation in self.manpower_pools`, while the debit is unconditional on the source side.
- diplomatic_executor.py:4634-4638: the peace-deal manpower demand has the same unclamped credit.
- world_state.py:8187: `pool["infantry"] = min(pool["infantry"] + inf_regen, MAX_INFANTRY_POOL)`. MAX_INFANTRY_POOL is 100000 at line 390. An over-cap pool is therefore cut back to the cap on the next regen.
- grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "ECON-3" and "manpower transfer" found no closed row or ruling covering this.
- My own probe failed. The scratchpad script p.py called `WorldFactory.create`, which returned None, so I never got a pool to regen. The reviewer's reported figures (140000 before regen, 100000 after) are consistent with line 8187, but I did not reproduce them.

The impact is small. `manpower_per_turn` amounts are tiny per turn (rates of 2 per 2000 infantry), and a receiver only loses men if its pool is already near the 100k cap. Regen already clamps to the cap on its own. The peace-deal demand path can move larger amounts in one go.
reproduction.note: The cap-bypass and the unconditional debit are real in code (lines above), so the finding stands as P3. It is a minor accounting defect, not a P2. It is only reachable when the receiver is near the 100k cap, and the loss is silent.

findings.title: EA-8 residue: a deficit every third turn (or sparser) is never remembered, never deserts, and takes the halved-upkeep mercy indefinitely
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:9310-9327 (_update_bankruptcy), :9329-9341 (deserts_now), constants :517-519 (ARREARS_PER_DEFICIT=2, ARREARS_DESERT_AT=5, one mark wiped per solvent turn)
findings.evidence: Deterministic state-machine run on a fresh world, driving the real _update_bankruptcy and deserts_now with scripted chests. Pattern D S (every 2nd turn): arrears 2,1,3,2,4,3,5,... and desertion fires 5 times in 16 turns (the EA-8 fix). Pattern D S S: arrears 2,1,0,2,1,0 over 6 deficits, 0 desertion turns. Pattern D S S S: 0 desertion turns. Live instance (in-process, unseeded RNG, SOVEREIGN_SEED=jena, passive France): Hanover bankrupt on turns 29, 31, 34, 37, 40, strength 22,745 to 22,689 over 20,000 limit, with no desertion. The halved-upkeep turn after each deficit builds the buffer that funds the next full turn. The EA-8 comment says 'a single deficit is forgotten after two solvent turns', so this is the rule as written. But the class the row fixed (a standing discount on the army with no consequence) survives at period 3.
findings.repro: <scratchpad>/econ_sm.py (prints arrears traces and desertion counts per pattern). The live instance needs a run, SOVEREIGN_SEED=jena INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR=<tmp> <scratchpad>/probe5.py 40, and is not byte-reproducible because in-process runs do not seed random.
findings.expected: A chest that ends below zero on 1 turn in 3 for 12 turns should accrue consequence (arrears floor, desertion, or a demobilisation rung).
findings.actual: No consequence beyond the mercy discount; the chest hovers around 0 indefinitely.

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real. world_state.py:9317-9327 (_update_bankruptcy) adds ARREARS_PER_DEFICIT (2) on a deficit turn and subtracts 1 on a solvent turn (`arrears = max(0, arrears - 1)`). deserts_now (:9341) needs arrears >= ARREARS_DESERT_AT (5), and bt>=3 can never occur if the chest recovers. The consecutive count resets to 0 on every solvent turn (:9322). Hand trace, pattern D S S: arrears go 2, 1, 0, so the peak is 2 and desertion never fires. Pattern D S: 2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 5, so desertion fires at the 4th deficit, matching the EA-8 fix. The constants comment (:513-518) says "a deficit every other turn deserts at the fourth instead of never; a single deficit is forgotten after two solvent turns", so a deficit every 3rd turn or sparser is forgotten by design. BUG_FIXES.md:225 closes EA-8 for the "alternating" exploit only (FIXED Oct 5, 2026, SYSTEMS_REFERENCE §97.6). No recorded ruling covers period 3. I did not run the scripted probes or the live Hanover instance. The finding is a rule-as-written boundary of the EA-8 fix, not a code bug.
mechanism.note: Severity is overstated as P3. The mercy discount applies only on the turn after a deficit, so at period 3 it covers about one turn in three. The row's target was the greedy alternating exploit (a 224,000-man army), and that case is fixed. Treat this as a design reading for the user: either accept the sparse-deficit tolerance, or make arrears decay slower than 1 per solvent turn. This is not a defect and needs no fix row.

reproduction.evidence:
I ran a read-only probe with PYTHONPATH=. and the venv python. It drives the real WorldState._update_bankruptcy and deserts_now on a stub with scripted chests (-5 on a deficit turn D, +5 on a solvent turn S), 24 turns per pattern. Constants and code are as the finding quotes: world_state.py:517-519 (ARREARS_ARE_REMEMBERED=True, PER_DEFICIT=2, DESERT_AT=5), :9315-9327 (+2 per deficit, -1 per solvent turn, floor 0), :9341 (desert only at arrears >= 5).
Arrears traces (first 12 turns) and desertion turns out of 24:
- D: 2,4,6,... gives 22 desertion turns.
- DS: 2,1,3,2,4,3,5,4,6,5,7,6 gives 9. Desertion fires from turn 7, which is the EA-8 fix working.
- DSS: 2,1,0,2,1,0,... gives 0.
- DSSS: 2,1,0,0,2,1,0,0,... gives 0.
So the period-3 and sparser results match the finding. Arrears reset to 0 every cycle and the army never deserts.
The code comment at world_state.py:505-520 documents this rule: "a single deficit is forgotten after two solvent turns". It targets only alternating deficits. EA-8 is listed as FIXED in docs/BUG_FIXES.md:214. I found no ruling or row covering period-3 deficits. I did not re-run the live Hanover instance, so that part is unverified.
reproduction.note: The state-machine claim reproduces exactly, and period-3 deficits have no consequence. The behaviour matches EA-8's documented rule, so it is a residue of design intent, not a regression. If kept, it should be recorded in a spec as an accepted limit (CLAUDE.md rule 9). A cheap tuning would be a slower decay, such as -1 only every other solvent turn, or a longer window. I'm rating it design/P3. It is not a bug in the fix, and it needs a user ruling on how strict the mercy should be.

findings.title: The AI's cheap admin rungs (urgent/rebuild recruit, market, depot, fortification, repair) spend to near-zero with no reserve and no upkeep or Net test
findings.evidence: The laws rung (reforms.ai_purse_refusal: reserve 1000 + 5 turns of upkeep + forecast Net >= 0), the arms rung (COURT_ARMS_RESERVE) and the fleet and commission rungs all keep reserves. These rungs test the chest against the price alone. Minimum chests observed in 31-41 turn passive runs on 4 seeds: Hanover 10, 44 and 60; Bavaria 18; Naples 331. Hanover's alternating-deficit pattern appeared on 1 of 4 seeds (jena). A recruit adds 8g per 1,000 men of upkeep per turn and a built structure adds 20-40g of infrastructure upkeep (EC-U2), so a court with Net near 0 that buys these deepens its own structural deficit. This is the cause of the bankruptcy cycle in ECON-4.
findings.repro: INK_IRON_SAVE_DIR=<tmp> SOVEREIGN_SEED=<seed> <scratchpad>/probe5.py 40 (min chest by nation), seeds jena, marengo, friedland, historical.
findings.expected: Every purchase rung either keeps a reserve or is skipped when the court's forecast Net after the new upkeep is negative, as the laws and arms rungs already do.
findings.actual: These rungs leave the chest at a few gold and bypass the Net test.
findings.prior_row: EA-11 (court arms with its purse), EA-18

mechanism.evidence:
I traced the cited seams in backend/ai/enemy_ai.py at ad73ba09 and the code matches the finding.

Price-only gates, verbatim:
- :6967 `if treasury >= recruit_cost and region and getattr(region, 'stability', 100) > 50:`
- :7217, the same line on the rebuild rung.
- :7119 `treasury >= 350` (market), :7129 `>= 300` (depot), :7141 `>= 400` (fortification), :7160 and :7170 `>= 150` (repair).

None of these rungs applies a reserve, an upkeep forecast or a Net test. The 'treasury' variable is just `world.nation_gold.get(nation, 0)` (:6925).

For contrast, the court-arms rung does keep a reserve. It is gated at :7313: `if treasury < price + COURT_ARMS_RESERVE + COURT_ARMS_UPKEEP_TURNS * upkeep_after:`, with `COURT_ARMS_RESERVE = 1000` at :184. The laws rung does the same through `reforms.ai_purse_refusal`.

The asymmetry is therefore real. A court with a small chest can spend it to near zero on these rungs.

Two things I did not verify:
- I did not re-run the passive runs, so the minimum chests (Hanover 10, 44 and 60; Bavaria 18; Naples 331) are unconfirmed.
- The causal link to the ECON-4 bankruptcy cycle is unconfirmed. ECON-4 does not appear as a row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md.

No closed row or user ruling covers this. EA-11 only made the AI able to arm. EAD-9 kept the plain purse read on the laws rung and says nothing about these cheap rungs.

Two points argue against any severity above P3:
- The urgent recruit and rebuild rungs spending down is plausibly intended, since survival outranks hoarding.
- The bankruptcy mercy system exists as a backstop.
mechanism.note: The seam is real: price-only gates on the cheap admin rungs, with reserve gates on the laws and arms rungs. It reads as an unreserved-spend design inconsistency, not a defect. The urgent and rebuild recruit rungs arguably should spend to the bone. The market, depot, fortification and repair rungs are the real candidates for a reserve or Net test. The claim that these rungs cause the ECON-4 bankruptcy cycle is plausible but unproven. Confirming it needs a probe that holds these rungs down and checks whether the Hanover deficit pattern disappears.

reproduction.evidence: Code: backend/ai/enemy_ai.py has bare price-only tests: line 6967 `if treasury >= recruit_cost and region and ...stability > 50`, line 7119 `treasury >= 350` (market), 7129 `>= 300` (depot), 7141 `>= 400` (fortification), 7160 and 7170 `>= 150` (repairs), 7217 recruit again. Beside them, line 7313 `if treasury < price + COURT_ARMS_RESERVE + COURT_ARMS_UPKEEP_TURNS * upkeep_after` is the arms rung's reserve, and the laws rung uses reserve 1000 (line 184 and 129). So the asymmetry is real. Repro: I wrote my own 40-turn passive probe (scratchpad sv_probe.py, 'end turn' x40 through TestClient, min of world.nation_gold per nation), because probe5.py in the scratchpad had been overwritten by an unrelated script. Seed jena, 41 turns: min chests Hanover 60, Naples 331, Bavaria 507 (France -464 is the player). Seed marengo, 30 turns: Naples 331, Hanover 616. The Hanover 60 and Naples 331 minima match the finding; the other numbers (10, 44, 18) were not reproduced on my two seeds. I did not check friedland or historical. I did not verify the causal claim that these rungs cause the ECON-4 bankruptcy cycle, nor the per-recruit upkeep figures. I also did not find a closed BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row ruling this.
reproduction.note: The asymmetry is real and confirmed in code: the cheap rungs have no reserve or Net test, while the laws and arms rungs do. It reproduces as a mild design inconsistency. Hanover dips to 60 on jena and Naples to 331 on both seeds. Hanover recovers and nobody is shown going bankrupt in my runs, so P3/design is the right level. The claim that this causes ECON-4 is unverified. Minima of 10, 44 and 18 were not seen on my seeds.

findings.title: Manpower regen is flat per nation: a 60-province France regenerates what a 28-province France does, while its force limit and income more than double
findings.evidence: Ruled in the EC-2 July-9 gate and recorded at SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:3110 ('deliberately flat, an anti-snowball rubber band'), so this is a decision, not a defect. Measured consequence at scale: force limit 130,000 at 28 provinces, 210,000 at 60 (FORCE_LIMIT_PER_REGION=2500); gross income 2,590 to 7,840; infantry regen stays 2,500 a turn, so a 210k establishment is refilled only by gold through the substitute market. Remnant courts bank the cap for nothing: Hanover, 2 provinces and 100 income, infantry 97,572 and cavalry 30,000 at T41 (jena). A conquered province adds no pool and an eliminated court's pool and chest are frozen (Bavaria gold -45 with 0 regions, Hanover 2,350 with 0 regions, historical T17-T37). If the full-Europe scale is meant to reward conquest with manpower, this ruling is the lever.
findings.repro: <scratchpad>/probe1.py for force limit and income at 28/45/60. <scratchpad>/econ_bav.py 40 Hanover (SOVEREIGN_SEED=jena) for the remnant pools.
findings.expected: Either the ruling stands and the docs say 'a larger empire is refilled by gold, not men', or a per-province term (capped) is added.
findings.actual: Flat 2,500.

mechanism.evidence: backend/models/world_state.py:343 `INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN = 2500`. get_manpower_regen_rates (world_state.py:8213-8250) sets `inf_regen = INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN` with the comment "no territory dependency". The only changes to it are the war-exhaustion scaling and a reform-law percentage applied last. world_state.py:407 `FORCE_LIMIT_PER_REGION = 2500` and :7973 show the force limit growing per controlled region. docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:3110 says "Infantry: 2,500/turn base (no territory dependency ... deliberately flat, an anti-snowball rubber band per the July-9 EC-2 gate)". I traced the code by hand and did not run the measured figures (force limit 130k to 210k, income, the Hanover and Bavaria pools).
mechanism.note: The mechanism is real, and it is a recorded user and gate decision (EC-2, July 9), not a defect. The infantry regen is flat per nation by design. Cavalry and artillery do scale with territory, with caps (ES-1b, ES-1a). Treat this as a design question. The ruling's open question is whether full-Europe scale should reward conquest with manpower, and that needs a user call. If the ruling stands, a doc line saying a larger empire is refilled by gold, not men would close it. I found no BUG_FIXES row for it.

reproduction.evidence: The code facts hold. world_state.py:343 has `INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN = 2500`. get_manpower_regen_rates sets `inf_regen = INFANTRY_BASE_REGEN` at line 8224, with no per-region term. The only modifier is the war-exhaustion penalty, which reduces it. world_state.py:407 has `FORCE_LIMIT_PER_REGION = 2500`, and the limit is floor + 2500 × controlled regions (lines 7964-7973). SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:3110 says the flat rate is "deliberately flat, an anti-snowball rubber band per the July-9 EC-2 gate". I did not re-run the scratchpad probe. It failed with ModuleNotFoundError because it was run without the repo on the path. I did not re-measure the 130k and 210k limits, the 2,590 and 7,840 income figures, or the Hanover and Bavaria remnant pools. The code reading shows the flat-regen mechanism and the force-limit scaling, which is the core of the finding.
reproduction.note: This is a recorded ruling (EC-2 gate), not a defect. It stands as a design observation: a larger empire is refilled by gold, not men, and the docs could say so plainly. If full-Europe conquest is meant to be rewarded with manpower, a capped per-province term is the lever. The P3 label overstates it, so I corrected it to design. The finding is not refuted because the mechanism is real and the finding itself says it is a design matter.

findings.title: P3.9 jealousy glory attack never reads the pair brake or the futility counter: one corps attacks the same marshal twice in a phase, every phase
findings.evidence: P3.9 returns the attack straight from find_autonomous_attack_target with only crossing/odds gates: `if glory_target is not None and self._admits({"action": "attack", "target": glory_target[0].name}): ... return ({"marshal": marshal.name, "action": "attack", "target": glory_enemy.name}, 4)`. Neither `_attacked_targets_this_turn` (the pair stamp P4 reads at 3745 and `_engageable_enemies` at 3381) nor `ai_attack_futility` (P4 3772, P0 3396) is consulted. Probe (in-process Mode A, scratchpad probe_dbl.py / probe_dbl2.py; not a driver digest): seed ulm turn 10 and 11, Spain: `attack Cuesta>Wellesley` twice each phase (3 of Spain's 3 actions), with attacked_set=[('Cuesta','Wellesley')] already stamped on the second evaluation and `P3.9 glory target -> Wellesley jealous_of='Castanos'` firing each time; futility for Cuesta:Wellesley went 0->2 (T10) ->3 (T11) and the rung kept firing. findings.title: P4/P0 price co-located allies at full strength (+8 percent each) but the executor only brings adjacent, eligible, non-literal, non-hostile, unfortified corps, by a probabilistic roll
findings.evidence: The AI sum filters only `not broken and not retreated_this_turn` (3515-3516); the +0.08 list (3612-3620) filters only strength>0, not broken and same nation/coalition. The executor additionally refuses Rule 7 fortified, Rule 8 on a post, Rule 10 drilling, Rule 12 moved_this_turn, Rule 13 Hostile relationship without SUPPORT, the Grouchy rule for `personality == "literal"` without a SUPPORT/PURSUE order (4367-4396), and rolls an arrival score (4399). The AI never issues SUPPORT (no strategic_order write in enemy_ai.py). Probe (scratchpad probe_conc.py, 4 seeds x 40 turns, passive France, wrapper on CombatExecutor._calculate_reinforcements for non-player attackers): reinforcement candidates 12/30/13/13 = 68, arrived 6/8/7/5 = 26 (38 percent); refusals: literal_personality 2/7/2/3 = 14, low_score 2/10/2/5 = 19, grievance_withheld 7, doctrine_delayed 3, fate_intervened 1. Austrian Mack (literal) is the standing example: Charles+Mack hit Deroy together on T2 and T3 on austerlitz and marengo.
findings.repro: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/1bd395101ae53e89/c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40/scratchpad/probe_conc.py austerlitz 40
findings.expected: The attack ratio counts a friend only if the executor would bring him (GR5: the AI prices what the resolver applies), as _muster_price already does for the defender's friends via combat._defender_muster.
findings.actual: A cautious corps beside a literal or fortified friend reads a 1.3 ratio it does not have; the battle is then fought with the lone corps. Caveat: my candidate pool is every adjacent friendly of the battle province, a superset of the AI's co-located sum, so 38 percent is an upper bound on the share of the AI's assumed help that arrives only if every candidate were co-located.

mechanism.evidence:
The mechanism holds when I trace the code by hand. enemy_ai.py:3508-3517 `_get_combined_strength_in_region` adds the full strength of every friendly marshal in the attacker's province, filtering only `broken` and `retreated_this_turn`. enemy_ai.py:3628-3636 builds `co_located_allies` with only strength>0, not broken, and same nation or coalition. The P4 loop adds `0.08` per ally at 3720-3729. In a P4 attack on an adjacent province, those co-located friends are the executor's adjacent reinforcement candidates. combat_executor.py `_is_reinforcement_eligible` (2055-2155) then refuses them on rule 7 (`fortified`), rule 8 (`holds_a_post`), rule 10 (`drilling`), rule 12 (`moved_this_turn`) and rule 13 (Hostile, with no SUPPORT order). `_calculate_reinforcements` (4343-4396) refuses `personality == "literal"` without a SUPPORT or PURSUE order, which the AI never issues. It then rolls an arrival score against a threshold, with a 5% fumble above 80. The AI's pricing of the attacker's own friends does not read any of these gates.

Two things limit the finding. I did not re-run the reviewer's probe. The 38% figure is the reviewer's own and is an upper bound, as the reviewer says. The defender side is already priced through `_muster_price`, so only the attacker side is optimistic. The docstring at 3501-3506 says the sum is for decision-making so the AI does not read itself as "too weak when it has allies ready to follow up", so the optimism is partly intended. I found no closed row or user ruling in BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT that covers or accepts this attacker-side gap. S14E-X216 and X217 fixed only the defender-side price and the player's defence desk.
mechanism.note: The mismatch is real, but it is an AI misjudgment of odds, not a mechanics break, so I rate it P3 (a design or AI-aliveness gap) and not P2. The executor stays deterministic and the LLM is not involved. The AI attacks somewhat more eagerly than its true force justifies. One possible fix is to price co-located friends through the executor's eligibility predicate and expected arrival (an expected-value sum like `_muster_price`), which would follow Golden Rule 5 and the GR5-style principle the reviewer cites.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the repro (PYTHONHASHSEED=0, probe_conc.py austerlitz 40). It reproduced the reviewer's austerlitz row (30 candidates, 8 arrived, refusals: 7 literal, 10 low_score). Those counts come from `_calculate_reinforcements`, which handles ADJACENT corps only. The AI's sum at enemy_ai.py:3500-3517 uses `get_friendly_marshals_in_region_indexed(marshal.location, ...)`, which is CO-LOCATED corps only. The coord_bonus list at 3628 is also co-located. A co-located corps is not a reinforcement. combat_executor.py:2182-2200 (`candidate.location == battle_region`) handles that case as "shares_the_field". Only a hostile (-2) relationship excludes such a corps, and the SRX-10 comment at ~740 says the co-located arm reads the same exclusions as `_get_casualty_participants`: broken, retreated this turn, or recovering. So the executor applies no fortified, drilling, moved_this_turn, literal-personality or arrival-roll gate to a co-located corps. The reviewer's own caveat concedes the pool was a superset. The probe's own output shows Charles+Mack (literal) striking Deroy together on T2 and T3, so the literal rule did not stop a co-located stack. The 38% arrival rate and the literal-refusal count therefore do not describe the AI's co-located sum, and the claimed mismatch does not follow. At most a small residual remains: the AI filter checks `broken` and `retreated_this_turn` but may not check retreat-recovery, which SRX-10 added for the muster. That is not what the finding claims, and I did not verify it.
reproduction.note: The probe measured adjacent reinforcement candidates, not the AI's co-located sum, which is a different path. A possible P3 sibling is whether enemy_ai.py:3515 omits a retreat-recovery exclusion that the executor applies (SRX-10). Worth a separate check, not filed here. The `_is_reinforcement_eligible` and Grouchy refusals apply to adjacent corps only.

findings.title: P4.6 coordinated-attack staging prices raw strength while P4 prices the effective ratio, so staged corps can assemble for an attack P4 still refuses
findings.evidence: P4.6: `solo_ratio = marshal.strength / enemy_strength` and `combined_ratio = combined / enemy_strength` against 1.5, with `enemy_strength = sum(e.strength for e in enemies_there)`. P4 divides by _defending_strength_in_region + _muster_price and then _evaluate_target_ratio (fortify, morale, drilling, overwatch, 3057-3120). No fortification, terrain or muster term reaches P4.6, and the relationship filter (>= -1) exists only in P4.6, not in P4's own co-located sum. Unmeasured: I did not run a seed that reproduces an assemble-then-refuse oscillation; the rung is bounded by the _marshal_visited_locations check.
findings.repro: Read 8100-8135 and 3612-3640; a fortified (defense_bonus 0.20) 40,000-man defender next door to 30,000 + 30,000 corps three provinces apart yields combined_ratio 1.5 at P4.6 and an effective ratio near 1.2 at P4 against a cautious 1.3 threshold.
findings.expected: One ratio function for the stage-and-strike pair.
findings.actual: Two ratio definitions.

mechanism.evidence: The two ratio definitions are real. P4.6 (`_find_coordinated_attack`, enemy_ai.py:8076-8205) computes `solo_ratio = marshal.strength / enemy_strength` and `combined_ratio = combined / enemy_strength` against a literal 1.5. `enemy_strength` is `sum(e.strength for e in enemies_there)`. No fortification, morale, drilling, overwatch or muster term enters it. P4 (about 3612-3720) computes `base_ratio = combined_strength / _defenders`. `_defenders` is the visible field plus `_muster_price`. It then applies `effective_ratio = self._evaluate_target_ratio(base_ratio, enemy, world)` plus a +0.08 coordination bonus for each co-located ally. So a fortified or reinforced defender can pass P4.6 and still fail P4's threshold. P4.6 also filters allies at relationship >= -1, which P4's co-located sum does not. I did not read `_evaluate_target_ratio` or the P4 thresholds, and I ran no seed, so the "about 1.2" figure in the repro is unverified. BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md have no row for coordinated-attack staging or AIMIL. The effect is bounded: the move toward allies uses the `_marshal_visited_locations` check, and P4.6 returns None when the marshal is fortified or drilling. The cost is a wasted staging march, not a crash or a rule violation. The finding itself says it is unmeasured.
mechanism.note: Confirmed as an inconsistency between two heuristics. It is not a defect that corrupts state, and no oscillation was demonstrated. P3-design: unify P4.6 on `_defending_strength_in_region`, `_muster_price` and `_evaluate_target_ratio` only if a measured seed shows repeated stage-then-refuse.

reproduction.evidence: I read enemy_ai.py lines 8076-8205 and 3600-3645 and did not run a playtest. At 8105 and 8166, P4.6 prices `solo_ratio = marshal.strength / enemy_strength` and `combined_ratio = combined / enemy_strength` against a flat 1.5. `enemy_strength` is the raw sum of `e.strength` over `enemies_there`. The P4.6 body has no fortification, terrain, morale or muster term. The relationship filter `marshal.get_relationship(m.name) >= -1` appears in P4.6 at 8125 and 8162. The co-located ally list in P4 (3612-3640) has no such filter. P4 builds its list from `world.get_marshals_in_region_indexed` with nation or coalition membership only. So the finding's code claim about two different ratio definitions is accurate. I did not re-read P4's `_evaluate_target_ratio` (3057-3120) or `_defending_strength_in_region` myself, and the finding's account of them is unconfirmed. I could not reproduce an assemble-then-refuse oscillation. The finding itself says it did not measure one either. The staging move is bounded by the `_marshal_visited_locations` check, so a loop is unlikely. P4.6 is a deliberately cheap staging heuristic. Staged corps that P4 then refuses to attack simply stay co-located and wait, which is a mild inefficiency and not a state corruption. I did not check BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for a ruling on this.
reproduction.note: The asymmetry is real: P4.6 uses a raw 1.5 ratio and P4 uses the effective ratio. The consequence is unmeasured and bounded. Treat it as a design observation, not a P3 defect. If it is pursued, the cheap fix is to have P4.6 call P4's `_evaluate_target_ratio` (3057-3120), not a new ratio function. Measure the assemble-then-refuse rate on seeded runs first.

findings.title: Eclipse coalition brews with one qualifier, cannot form, and is re-announced every 3 turns forever
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/coalition.py:3920 (gate), :3808-3819 (expiry), 7b eclipse pass; form_coalition needs 2 members (coalition.py:2483)
findings.evidence: coalition.py:3920 `if _eclipse_qualifying:` starts a brew on a non-empty list. form_coalition rejects it unless `len(all_members) >= 2` (A_LEAGUE_NEEDS_TWO_MEMBERS). At expiry (3818) the code only does `# Not enough nations — cancel` / `world.coalition_brewing = None` with no coalition_cooldown. Step 7b later in the same call re-brews the same set. Digest evidence: rev1106-aidip-friedland campaign_log 'Coalition brewing against Austria — Bavaria consulting (their alarm: 93)' on T18, T21, T24, T27, T30 (alarm 97 at the end) with no league ever formed and a dispatch 'Word from the chanceries' each time; rev1106-aidip-jena T28, T31, T34, T37 (Switzerland alone); rev1106-aidip-wagram T18, T21, T26 (Prussia alone).
findings.repro: ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --name x-friedland --fresh --seed friedland, then grep 'coalition_brewing_started' tools/playtest_runs/x-friedland/digest.jsonl. Expect one every 3 turns with a single consulting court.
findings.expected: A brew starts only when the qualifying set plus courts already at war with the target reaches 2, or a failed brew sets coalition_cooldown or a latch so it is not re-announced. A runaway hegemon at alarm 97 should either draw a league or say why not.
findings.actual: A structurally impossible coalition is announced and cancelled in a 3-turn loop. The CRITICAL-looking notice and the chancery dispatch line are spam, and a hegemon at alarm 93-97 never faces a league because one qualifier can never form it.

mechanism.evidence: The code path matches the claim. The eclipse pass (coalition.py ~3920) starts a brew on any non-empty `_eclipse_qualifying` list, with no check that the set plus courts already at war with the target reaches 2. At countdown expiry (~3808-3819) the code calls `form_coalition`, which returns failure when `len(all_members) < 2` (coalition.py ~2445 and A_LEAGUE_NEEDS_TWO_MEMBERS at ~2483). The only response is `world.coalition_brewing = None` plus dismissing the notification. It sets no cooldown, and the only `coalition_cooldown` writes (3034, 3730, 3847) are not on this path. Step 7b runs later in the same call with `coalition_brewing` None and `coalition_cooldown` 0, so it re-brews, re-logs `coalition_brewing_started`, adds a notification and queues the dispatch line. The digest agrees: rev1106-aidip-friedland/digest.jsonl has five `coalition_brewing_started` entries at log_turn 19, 22, 25, 28 and 31, each 3 turns after the last. The text is 'Bavaria consulting (their alarm: 93)' on the repeats (alarm 97 at turns 28 and 31), and the first entry names Prussia and Bavaria. The 3-turn spacing equals BREWING_COUNTDOWN. I did not rerun the playtest. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row that closes this. OCT27-5 and OCT27-D2 cover different symptoms. Two details are not established. The digest's first entry lists two qualifiers, so that cycle's failure may have come from failed declarations rather than a single qualifier. And since `already_at_war` counts toward the 2-member minimum, a single qualifier does not always fail. The loop itself is still real.
mechanism.note: The loop is real, but the damage is cosmetic and sits on a non-player target. The eclipse brew posts only a NORMAL-priority notice and a dispatch line, not the CRITICAL anti-France alarm. The 'hegemon never faces a league' claim is overstated, because the same pass runs whenever two or more courts qualify. The fix is small: set a short cooldown or a per-target latch when an eclipse brew's `form_coalition` fails, or require a viable member count before brewing. I rate it P3 rather than P2 because the effect is log and notice spam with no mechanical corruption.

reproduction.evidence:
I did not re-run the 40-turn playtest. I confirmed the code path by reading it and checked the existing digest.

Code (backend/game_logic/coalition.py):
- Line 3920 is `if _eclipse_qualifying:`. It starts a brew on any non-empty list, so one qualifier is enough.
- Line 2445 in form_coalition is `if not qualifying_nations or len(all_members) < 2: return {"success": False, ...}`. The player is stripped from `already_at_war` for a non-player target (about line 2436), so a single qualifier cannot form a league unless another AI court is already at war with the target.
- Expiry branch, lines 3818-3820: `# Not enough nations — cancel`, then `world.coalition_brewing = None` and `dismiss_by_type`. It sets no `coalition_cooldown` and no latch.
- Step 7b (lines 3908-3970) runs later in the same call. Its guard is `not world.coalition_brewing and world.coalition_cooldown <= 0`, both true after the failed expiry. It then recomputes the qualifiers and re-brews. That re-brew logs `coalition_brewing_started`, adds a notification and queues the `diplomatic_coalition_brewing_other` dispatch.

Digest (docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-aidip-friedland/digest.jsonl):
- `coalition_brewing_started` appears at lines 610, 697, 785, 873 and 949, with log_turn 19, 22, 25, 28 and 31.
- The text is "Coalition brewing against Austria — Bavaria consulting (their alarm: 93)" on turns 22 and 25, and the same with "alarm: 97" on turns 28 and 31.
- The first brew, on turn 19, had two qualifiers (Prussia and Bavaria). The later ones had Bavaria alone.
- The finding's turns of 18, 21 and so on are off by one (the log_turn values are 19, 22 and so on). That is immaterial.

I found no closed row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md that covers this. OCT27-5 and OCT27-D2 are different symptoms.
reproduction.note: The defect is real: a one-qualifier eclipse brew can never form, and it is re-announced every 3 turns with a rail notice and a dispatch line. I rate it P3 rather than P2 because nothing mechanical breaks. The cost is notice spam, and a hegemon at alarm 93-97 never draws a league. The fix is to start a brew only when the qualifying set plus the courts already at war with the target reaches 2, or to set a cooldown or latch when the expiry cancel fires. That cancel is in coalition.py, at the "Not enough nations — cancel" comment (around line 3818).

findings.title: The AI's settlement letter quotes an indemnity priced to the war that the payer cannot pay; the comment and docstring still say a bankrupt payer pays nothing
findings.evidence: Comment at 6024: 'A payer with an empty (or negative) chest cannot be squeezed, so the INDEMNITY is dropped'. The code is `if amount > 0 and not any(...gold_indemnity...)`, and since PC-R3 `amount` is war_priced_indemnity, which has no purse term. Probe with Austria at 3000, 50 and -200 gold, accepter France at score +80: all three return `{'type':'gold_indemnity','from':'Austria','to':'France','amount':4200}`. Ratification then clamps (settlement_ratify.py:537 `transfer = min(amount, max(0, available))`), so the letter promises 4,200 and delivers at most the chest. The AI-AI rows read the same way ('Hanover pays 2,538 gold', rev1106-aidip-historical T14). I did not confirm Hanover's chest on that turn.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO=none ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 -c "from pathlib import Path; from backend.models.world_state import WorldState; from backend.game_logic import ai_diplomacy as ad; w=WorldState.from_dict(WorldState.from_scenario('godot-client/project-sovereign/assets/maps/europe_1805.json').to_dict()); w.nation_gold['Austria']=-200; print(ad._settlement_offer_build_terms(accepter='France',proposer_nation='Austria',war_age_turns=10,accepter_war_score=80,world=w))"
findings.expected: Either the quoted amount is capped at what the payer can transfer (or carries a stream and surety, as the dictated letters do), or the stale comment and docstring ('a bankrupt payer -> white peace') are corrected to the PC-R3 ruling.
findings.actual: A quote and an acceptance that disagree (ACH-1's class). The player or table accepts a 4,200 indemnity from a court with nothing, the stale comment contradicts the code, and the winner's reward is silently small.
findings.prior_row: EC-W4 / PC-R3 ruling I item 3 (priced to the war, not the purse) - the ruling is kept, the letter's honesty is the finding

mechanism.evidence: I read the code and did not run the repro. (1) ai_diplomacy.py:5997 sets `amount = int(war_priced_indemnity(...)["lump"])`. war_priced_indemnity (ai_diplomacy.py:1227-1241) is built only from base + war age + |war_score| and has no treasury term; its docstring says "never to the payer's chest (no treasury term, no purse cap)". (2) ai_diplomacy.py:6031 `if amount > 0 and not any(...gold_indemnity...)` appends the clause with no check on the payer's gold, so a bankrupt or negative-gold payer still gets the full lump. This matches the reviewer's 4200 probe, which I did not re-run. (3) The comment at 6024 ("A payer with an empty (or negative) chest cannot be squeezed, so the INDEMNITY is dropped") and the docstring at 5979-5981 ("EC-W4: the AMOUNT prices to the payer's purse ... (a bankrupt payer -> white peace)") are stale; PC-R3 superseded them. The comment at 5995 even records "the ask on the rail fell 2,543 -> 363 as France fell". (4) settlement_ratify.py:537 `transfer = min(amount, max(0, available))` confirms the clamp at ratification, so the quoted figure can exceed what is actually moved. (5) BUG_FIXES.md:2129 (PC-R3, FIXED Oct 16) records "the ask does not fall with the purse" as the ruling. The war-priced amount is therefore deliberate. What remains is a stale comment and docstring, plus a quote that can exceed delivery. The dictated (player-pays) branch carries a stream and a surety, but this AI-to-AI and AI-to-player-winning branch does not.
mechanism.note: The mechanism is real, but the severity is overstated. The ruling to price to the war and not the purse is kept, and the ratify clamp is a deliberate safety. The definite defect is the stale comment at ai_diplomacy.py:6024-6030 and the docstring at 5979-5981, which a reader would take to mean that a bankrupt payer pays nothing. Whether to cap the quoted amount at the payer's gold, or add a stream and surety to this branch, is a design choice for the user. When the payer is the AI the quote is not harmful, since the player receives at most the chest. It becomes a defect only where the player is shown a figure it will not receive, which is the ACH-1 class.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the repro read-only. With Austria at 3000 gold and at -200 gold, `_settlement_offer_build_terms(accepter='France', proposer_nation='Austria', war_age_turns=10, accepter_war_score=80)` returned the same `{'type':'gold_indemnity','from':'Austria','to':'France','amount':4200}` clause. No purse term applies. The stale text is real: ai_diplomacy.py ~5981 says "(a bankrupt payer → white peace)" and the comment at 6024 says "A payer with an empty (or negative) chest cannot be squeezed, so the INDEMNITY is dropped". The code at 6033 is `if amount > 0 and not any(gold_indemnity)`, which does not drop it for a bankrupt payer. docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:10837 and docs/COALITION_SPEC.md:459 record the ruling: "priced to the war, never the purse... no treasury term, no purse cap", and the lump comes with a stream and surety_regions. settlement_ratify.py:537 does `transfer = min(amount, max(0, available))`, so the ratified lump delivers at most the chest. I did not check an AI-AI row's chest on a given turn.
reproduction.note: The behaviour is the intended PC-R3 ruling, so it is not a game defect. What stands is stale comment and docstring text that contradicts the code, plus a letter that quotes more than a bankrupt payer can transfer. It is a quote-versus-delivery honesty gap, not a mechanics bug. I did not check whether the player-facing quote is capped elsewhere. On the AI-to-player road the dictated clauses carry the lump with a stream and surety, so that road probably matches the ruling. P3 (comment fix, optionally a quote-side cap) is the right severity.

findings.title: AI-vs-AI refused design asks recur on a fixed 6-turn cadence with no escalation; the ordered-pair cooldown that refusals write has no reader on that path
findings.evidence: Trigger 0a is gated only by `recent` (the refusal-dedupe window, 6 turns) and design_ask_patience_holds (5471). rest_refused_pair stamps `{p}>{r}|nation` and `{p}>{r}|design_ask`, escalating x(1+prior) up to x3 via repeated_ask_factor. _is_on_cooldown is called with recipient= in only one place (ai_diplomacy.py:2986, the hegemon branch), so the AI-AI trigger path never reads those keys. Digest: rev1106-aidip-historical 'Ottoman rebuffs Austria (design ask)' T10, T16, T22, T28 (exactly 6 apart) and 'Sweden rebuffs Russia (design ask)' T11, T18, T23, T29; rev1106-aidip-marengo 'Bavaria rebuffs Austria' T9, 10, 16, 22, 34, 39, with 'Austria rebuffs Bavaria' on 5 turns.
findings.repro: Run the historical seed 40 turns and grep ai_ai_proposal_refused in digest.jsonl; the same (proposer, recipient, design ask) triple recurs every 6 turns for the whole game.
findings.expected: Per AI-2a seam 4 and OCT27-13 the refusal rests the ordered pair, with the escalating x1/x2/x3 type cooldown that repeated_ask_factor computes; a refused ask should get rarer.
findings.actual: The cooldown is written and not read on the court-to-court trigger. The only governor is the 6-turn dedupe window, so each refused pair logs about 5 identical rebuffs per run and the LOG and DIPLO rows fill with them. Each refusal also adds +6 weight, capped at 12, to the asker's intent. That hardening is intended, but the repetition adds nothing.
findings.prior_row: OCT27-13 (the writer was added, the reader was not)

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real. In backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py, trigger 0a (about line 5464 to 5473) is gated only by `recent`, the refused design_asks inside REFUSAL_DEDUPE_TURNS = 6 (line 602), and by design_ask_patience_holds. That patience gate only delays the first ask; it returns False once a design_ask is on the record (about line 722). rest_refused_pair (line 470) stamps the ordered-pair keys through apply_rejection_cooldowns(..., recipient=target), with the repeated_ask_factor escalation at line 442. My grep of `_is_on_cooldown` found no caller on the AI-AI trigger path that passes `recipient=`. The only reader of the `{p}>{r}|...` keys is the hegemon branch at lines 2986 to 2993. So the stamped cooldown is never consulted by trigger 0a, and a refused ask recurs about every 6 turns. I did not open the digests (the Ottoman, Sweden and Bavaria rows); the 6-turn cadence follows from the code.
mechanism.note: I downgrade this from a defect to design or P3 polish. The repeat is partly intentional. The 0a comment says the ask "exists to be REFUSED", and the refusal record is the ladder's substrate: war_council._ladder_climbed needs CRISIS_REFUSALS_REQUIRED refused asks before the court may demand (coerce). Repeated asks are therefore how the ladder escalates, and the dedupe window was the deliberate fix for shadowing the pair's other triggers. The finding is right that the x1/x2/x3 type cooldown that OCT27-13 writes is dead on this path. The prior row only claimed the writer for the hegemon reader. The effect is repetitive log lines, not wrong mechanics. A fix would be to make trigger 0a read the pair key, or to stop writing it for design asks. Either choice changes the ladder's pacing, so it needs a ruling and is not a free cleanup.

reproduction.evidence: I read the code and the digest and ran no playtest. The mechanics claim is true, but the cadence is documented as intended and the "no escalation" claim is wrong. (1) ai_diplomacy.py:5471-5483: trigger 0a returns a design_ask when `not recent and not design_ask_patience_holds(...)`. `recent` is get_refused_asks filtered by REFUSAL_DEDUPE_TURNS (602, = 6). It never calls _is_on_cooldown. (2) The _is_on_cooldown callers (1883-2986) pass recipient= only at 2988-2993 (the hegemon branch), so the `{p}>{r}|design_ask` stamp from rest_refused_pair (470) is not read on this path. That part of the finding is accurate. (3) The digest has the repetition: rev1106-aidip-historical/digest.jsonl holds 4 "Ottoman rebuffs Austria (design ask)" and 4 "Sweden rebuffs Russia (design ask)". (4) docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md:1825 (the scene-1 row, amended by S14k part 2) records this as intended: "one refused ask every six turns from each (the repeat-ask governor), never on the dispatch, each refusal a rung its design climbs". The 6-turn dedupe is a named design governor, and each refusal feeds the AI-3 ladder gate. The finding says the repetition adds nothing, but the refusal record is what the ladder reads. (5) No open BUG_FIXES row owns this symptom. OCT27-13 (BUG_FIXES.md:2846) fixed the missing writer, and the stamp is also read for the player-addressed and hegemon arms.
reproduction.note: The ordered-pair cooldown stamp going unread on the AI-AI design-ask trigger is a real observation, but at most a design or tuning question. The 6-turn re-ask is the documented repeat-ask governor and drives the ladder's refusal record. If the user wants refused asks to grow rarer, the fix is to read the x1/x2/x3 cooldown in trigger 0a. That would be a design decision and would change the ladder's refusal counts, so it should not be filed as a defect.

findings.title: sell_neutrality offers a token lump (all of a poor court's gold) because it lacks the minimum that friendly_gift has
findings.evidence: friendly_gift guards `if gift >= 25:` (1073). sell_neutrality computes `offer = max(SELL_NEUTRALITY_BASE, treasury*0.25*pay_mult)` then `offer = min(offer, treasury)` (1137) and appends it when `offer > 0`. Arm 2 only checks `terms.get('sweeteners')`, so any treasury >= 1 passes the 'a real offer, not a token' comment at :1920. Probe: Prussia at 7 gold at war with Hesse returns sweeteners [{'type':'gold_lump','value':7}] with the neutrality_compact clause. A treasury of -50 returns [] and is gated out, which is the intended behaviour.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO=none ".venv/Scripts/python.exe" -X utf8 -c "from backend.models.world_state import WorldState; from backend.game_logic import ai_diplomacy as ad; from backend.game_logic.settlement_helpers import ensure_war_instance_for_pair as e; w=WorldState.from_dict(WorldState.from_scenario('godot-client/project-sovereign/assets/maps/europe_1805.json').to_dict()); w.nation_gold['Prussia']=7; e(w,'Prussia','Hesse',entry_path='p'); print(ad._build_proposal_terms('Prussia','sell_neutrality',0,w)['sweeteners'])"
findings.expected: A neutrality purchase offers at least a floor, or is not offered. The gate comment says 'a real offer, not a token'.
findings.actual: A 7-gold payment buys a neutrality compact that binds France (renege = the strongest casus belli).

mechanism.evidence:
The probe at master reproduces it: `_build_proposal_terms('Prussia','sell_neutrality',0,w)['sweeteners']` printed `[{'type': 'gold_lump', 'value': 7}]` when Prussia held 7 gold at war with Hesse.

Code path in backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:
- Line 103 sets `SELL_NEUTRALITY_BASE = 250`.
- Lines 1134-1138 compute `offer = max(SELL_NEUTRALITY_BASE, ...)`, then `offer = min(offer, treasury)`, then append the lump if `offer > 0`. The 250 floor is therefore capped back down to the treasury, so any treasury of at least 1 passes.
- friendly_gift guards with `if gift >= 25:` at line 1073. sell_neutrality has no equivalent minimum.
- The arm-2 gate (lines ~1923-1927) checks only `terms.get("sweeteners")` and `slot_claim_allowed`. Its comment says "A real offer, not a token", but the check does not enforce that.

I found no closed row for this in docs/BUG_FIXES.md.

Mitigating context: the clause binds France in the same way whatever the sum, so a tiny lump does not change the mechanics. A court that is broke enough to offer 7 gold is an edge case, and the offer is a visible, player-declinable proposal.
mechanism.note: The mechanism holds. Fix: add a minimum to the sell_neutrality gate or the term builder, for example the same `>= 25` floor or a fraction of SELL_NEUTRALITY_BASE. Per Rule 10, sweep the sibling AI proposals that use `min(offer, treasury)` without a floor.

reproduction.evidence: Ran the given repro: it prints [{'type': 'gold_lump', 'value': 7}]. Code matches the finding. ai_diplomacy.py:1134-1139 computes offer = max(SELL_NEUTRALITY_BASE=250, ...), then min(offer, treasury), and appends it if offer > 0. friendly_gift at :1073 has a `gift >= 25` floor. The gate at :1923 only checks `terms.get("sweeteners")`, so the "real offer, not a token" comment at :1920 is not enforced. No BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md row covers this. S14E-28 only concerns the rendering of sell_neutrality terms.
reproduction.note: The defect is real but minor. The 250 floor is silently capped to the treasury, so a near-bankrupt court offers a token lump. The compact only binds France if the player accepts, so the player can decline. The effect is a low-value, odd-looking letter, not a mechanical break. A fix would be a minimum-offer check at the gate, similar to friendly_gift's `>= 25`.

findings.title: Code comment contradicts the spec for post-break states (comment says one level, map and spec drop two)
findings.evidence: Comment `# Post-break state: one level below broken treaty (E11)`; the map is ALLIANCE->NON_AGGRESSION, DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE->OPEN_BORDERS, NON_AGGRESSION->PEACE, each skipping a rung of _DOWNGRADE_ORDER (diplomacy.py:61). The spec at DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:1370 says 'drops two levels ... (2-level drop per design)' and :2773 says 'one level below'. validate_transition would reject all three as non-adjacent. The write bypasses it, so it is behaviourally fine.
findings.repro: grep -n 'post_break_map' -B3 backend/game_logic/diplomacy.py; compare _DOWNGRADE_ORDER at line 61.
findings.expected: One comment and one spec line agree with the map.
findings.actual: Two docs disagree with each other and with the code, so a future 'fix' to the validator or the map would be a regression.

mechanism.evidence: backend/game_logic/diplomacy.py:14386 comment: "# Post-break state: one level below broken treaty (E11)". Map at 14390-14392: ALLIANCE->NON_AGGRESSION, DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE->OPEN_BORDERS, NON_AGGRESSION->PEACE. _DOWNGRADE_ORDER (diplomacy.py ~60) = ALLIANCE, DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE, NON_AGGRESSION, OPEN_BORDERS, PEACE, so each of the three skips a rung (two-level drops). Validator at ~3627-3631 only accepts tgt_idx == curr_idx+1, so it would reject them. DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:1370 says "drops two levels ... (2-level drop per design)", which matches the map. DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:2773 says "one level below the broken treaty", which contradicts both. The code comment is wrong. One spec line (2773) is wrong and the other agrees with the code. The finding's claim that the write bypasses the validator was not traced; it only affects behaviour, not the doc mismatch.
mechanism.note: Doc-only defect. The map and spec line 1370 agree on a two-level drop by design. Only the code comment at diplomacy.py:14386 and spec line 2773 say "one level", so those two are the ones to fix.

reproduction.evidence: I ran grep and sed read-only against diplomacy.py and DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md. (1) diplomacy.py:14386 reads "# Post-break state: one level below broken treaty (E11)". The map at 14389-14396 sets ALLIANCE->NON_AGGRESSION, DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE->OPEN_BORDERS and NON_AGGRESSION->PEACE. (2) _DOWNGRADE_ORDER at diplomacy.py:61 is [ALLIANCE, DEFENSIVE_ALLIANCE, NON_AGGRESSION, OPEN_BORDERS, PEACE]. Each mapped drop skips one rung, so it is two levels. The comment's "one level" is wrong. (3) validate_transition at diplomacy.py:3627-3631 accepts only tgt_idx == curr_idx+1, so it would reject these drops. The map goes through set_diplomatic_state, which bypasses it (14412). (4) DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:1370 says "drops two levels ... (2-level drop per design)", which matches the code. DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:2773 says "returns to one level below the broken treaty (§7d)", which contradicts line 1370. The finding's description is accurate. Only a comment and a spec line are wrong, and behaviour is correct.
reproduction.note: This is a doc-only inconsistency with no behavioural impact. The fix is to edit the diplomacy.py:14386 comment and the DIPLOMACY_SPEC.md:2773 line to say "two levels", matching the spec line at :1370 and the code. I did not check BUG_FIXES.md for a closed row on E11/L-4, because the code and spec text confirm the finding directly.

findings.title: A 180-line try block (P-Bandwagon + vassal on-ramp) is closed by an except labelled 'import backend.game_logic.coalition'
findings.evidence: The try opens at 2871 and the except at 3051-3059 reports `report(exc, "ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase: import backend.game_logic.coalition")`, then `pass`es. The span covers the hegemon read, the share and tier gates, the intent bandwagon arm, check_vassalage_power_cap, _make_proposal and the vassalage on-ramp stamp. report() logs once per site per process (backend/errors.py), so a bug anywhere in those lines produces one mis-attributed WARNING and then silently no bandwagon proposals every turn. I found no triggering failure in 8 runs: server_console.log has no sovereign.errors lines.
findings.repro: grep -n 'import backend.game_logic.coalition' backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py; sed -n 2871,2873p and 3051,3060p.
findings.expected: The site string names the block (or the try is narrowed to the import).
findings.actual: A failure in the bandwagon and vassalage rungs would be reported under an import label, once.

mechanism.evidence: backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:2871 opens `try:` and its first statement is the coalition import. The matching handler at 3051-3052 reads `except Exception as exc:` then `report(exc, "ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase: import backend.game_logic.coalition")`. The try body between them includes the vassalage on-ramp tail at ~3040-3050 (`cooldowns[...offer_vassalage]`, `_set_cooldowns`, `assimilate_vassal_marshals`), well beyond the import. backend/errors.py's docstring says report logs "ONCE per site per process", so any failure in that span is logged once under the import label. The handler then runs debug_print and `pass`es. I traced this by hand and did not run a failure probe.
mechanism.note: The mislabel is real and the code does what the finding says. The finding slightly overstates "silently". The handler also calls debug_print with the nation, turn and exception text. That output is gated by the debug flag and is not a WARNING, so it is not reliably visible. The impact is limited to diagnosability. A bandwagon or vassalage bug would be attributed to an import and would warn once per process. No live failure was found. The fix is to rename the site string, or to narrow the try to the import.

reproduction.evidence: I ran `grep -n 'import backend.game_logic.coalition' backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py` plus `sed` on the two ranges. The label is at line 3052: `report(exc, "ai_diplomacy.process_diplomatic_phase: import backend.game_logic.coalition")`. The `try:` opens at line 2871 and its first statement is `from backend.game_logic.coalition import (_identify_max_bloc_share, _hegemony_signal_band,)`. The `except Exception as exc:` is at line 3051, so the try covers about 180 lines, all of it past the import. The handler then calls `debug_print("[HEGEMONY] bandwagon evaluation failed for {nation}...")` and `pass`es. In backend/errors.py, `report()` logs the full stack at WARNING only on the first call per `site` and only counts after that (lines 84-96, `_SPOKEN` dedupe). I did not trigger a failure, so the silent-after-first behaviour comes from reading the code. The label is wrong, and later failures at this site are counted but not logged.
reproduction.note: This is a real labelling and over-broad-try problem, but the harm is small. The first WARNING still carries the true exception type, message and stack, which point at the failing line despite the "import" label. The `debug_print` line says "bandwagon evaluation failed". The reviewer found no actual failure in 8 runs, and I did not trigger one. The fix is to narrow the try to the import, or rename the site string to something like "bandwagon + vassal on-ramp". The `pass` here is the recorded CODE-3 pattern of speaking once per site, not a silent swallow.

findings.title: The warmest passive-France arm is homogeneous across 8 seeds: same enemy set, same collapse, Prussia never joins, the ladder never reaches an ultimatum
findings.seam: war_council ladder (price coerce -> ultimatum -> war), coalition eclipse/formation gates; measured through the playtest driver
findings.evidence: 8 archived runs (rev1106-aidip-{historical,ulm,austerlitz,jena,marengo,eylau,wagram,friedland}), policy diplomacy=decline. wars records: Austria, Britain, Russia at T1 in 8/8. Switzerland (a French vassal that 'broke free') joins at T11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20. No other court is at war with France in any run. Zero incoming_ultimatum popups and zero AI war declarations against France, against about 25 'hardens ... prepared now to go as far as an ultimatum' COURTS lines. The Third Coalition dissolves on low_threat at T14-17 in 6 of 8 runs while 4 courts are still at war with France (coalition.py check_dissolution, DISSOLUTION_THREAT_THRESHOLD 20). Outcome: France at 0-16 provinces by T31-40 in 8/8, game over before T40 on four seeds (31, 35, 37, 38). Spread across seeds is only the date and the province count. The only AI-initiated war is Prussia on Hanover.
findings.repro: Run tools/playtest_driver.py --turns 40 --fresh --seed <s> --archive for the 8 seeds and read the `wars` records (first turn each enemy appears) and the final LEDGER row.
findings.expected: AI_INTENT_SPEC section 3.9 (assure the shapes, vary the casting) and the D1 band (1-4 AI-initiated wars per 40 turns): a Prussia bandwagoning on a collapsing France, a Fourth Coalition, a Sweden or Ottoman war, or a differing opening enemy set on some seeds.
findings.actual: One shape on all 8 seeds against a passive France. This arm cannot tell whether an ACTIVE France would see variety; the passive arm shows none, and Prussia's bandwagon rung ('joining the stronger side for pay') only courts France and never joins the war on the winning side. The user's 'multiple unpredictable outcomes' is therefore UNMEASURED for a thinking France and NOT demonstrated for a passive one.
findings.prior_row: AI_INTENT_SPEC section 3.8/3.9 and AI-V arm (a); no closed BUG_FIXES row names this arm

mechanism.note: The observations stand: zero incoming_ultimatum in all 8 digests, and the Third Coalition dissolves on low_threat while France is at war. I did not recount the per-seed wars records or the Switzerland join turns. The P2 defect framing does not hold. The finding says the arm "cannot tell" what an active France would see. The spec already treats a passive France as a degraded probe and does not assert variety from it. A passive France that collapses by T31-40 has already drawn the three opening enemies, so the ladder has little left to coerce. Whether an active France sees variety is a real open question, and it belongs to AI-V's scripted-France arm (b) and the N-seed sweep. I rate it design, not P2: not a defect, and no spec rule is broken by this run.
mechanism.evidence: Digests: docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-aidip-{historical,ulm,austerlitz,jena,marengo,eylau,wagram,friedland}/digest.md. `grep -ci incoming_ultimatum` returns 0 on all 8. Each opens with Austria capturing Franconia and Munich. backend/game_logic/coalition.py:2800 reads `if world.threat_by_target.get(france, 0) < DISSOLUTION_THREAT_THRESHOLD: return "low_threat"` (threshold 20 at line 58). The comment at lines ~2790-2793 (ulm t24) says the low-threat arm waits only while the target's own capital is held by a coalition member; otherwise it can dissolve a league whose members are still at war. IQ-2 (coalition.py ~2808) records this exact behaviour on a collapsed campaign as known, with only the display copy fixed. docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md:1431: 'Several §7a scenes and §4.6a beats are unreachable by a passive France *by construction*'. Line 1457: arm (a) uses a passive France as 'the ideal test case' only for the upward half. Line 1825, scene 1: 'with a passive France the hegemony share may never reach the P-Bandwagon gate', ruled UNREACHABLE BY DESIGN on Oct 3 (SR-8c). Line 1838 adds an arm map because a passive France cannot produce some scenes. The finding's own 'actual' text concedes the active-France case is unmeasured. The D1 '1-4 AI wars' band was replaced by the exposure calculus (AI_WAR_DECISION_SPEC v1.0), so the finding's 'expected' cites a deleted cap. No BUG_FIXES row covers this arm.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the playtests. I re-read the 8 archived digests (docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-aidip-*/digest.md and meta.json). All 8 use policy diplomacy=decline with mock llm. In every digest the coalition_dissolved log reads "Austria, Britain, Russia and Switzerland remain at war with us" (confirmed on 6 of 8; my grep showed only the first 4 matches on austerlitz and marengo). The sponsorship_granted lines show Britain binding Austria and Russia in all 8. The final LEDGER rows show France at 3, 16, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1 and 1 provinces on historical, ulm, austerlitz, jena, marengo, eylau, wagram and friedland, against 28 at the start. 'game over' or capture text appears in 32 to 38 of the lines in most digests, though not ulm, which has 14 matches and still ends with 16 provinces. Each digest has 6 to 12 "ultimatum" mentions, mostly COURTS lines like "The court of Prussia hardens over The Hanoverian Prize — prepared now to go as far as an ultimatum." I did not count incoming_ultimatum popups or AI war declarations against France myself. I did not check Switzerland's join turns (T11 to T20) or the Prussia-on-Hanover war. I also did not check the low_threat dissolution turns (T14 to T17) or the game-over turns (31, 35, 37, 38). The ledger rows I saw show the threat figure falling from the 60s to 0 to 14 by the end, which fits that account. The shape is homogeneous across seeds as claimed. docs/BUG_FIXES.md has no row for this arm. The spec itself concedes the limit. docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md line 1431 says the harness "had no player" and that passive France is by construction passive. Line 1457 says a passive France is the ideal test case for arm (a). Line 1825 says that with a passive France the hegemony share may never reach the bandwagon gate. Line 1838 adds an arm map because scenes a passive France cannot produce were demanded. The 1805 opening, with France at war with Austria, Britain and Russia, is Tier 1 fixed by spec 3.8.1. That makes the identical enemy set at T1 the specified behaviour, not a defect.
reproduction.note: The observations reproduce from the digests, but this is a measurement-coverage gap, not a game defect. A France that issues no orders and declines all diplomacy collapses under a 3-power coalition, and Prussia has no reason to bandwagon on a collapsing France. The spec already states that a passive France cannot show variety, and the finding says the same about the arm. It proves nothing about an active France. The useful follow-up is an active-France or scripted-France arm (spec arm map and the AI-V three-arm sweep) to test the 'multiple unpredictable outcomes' claim. The 8 seeds here cannot test it. The finding's own note that the 'warmest' arm is passive France is accurate.

findings.title: Great-power statecraft 'reaches_first: sponsor' and Prussia 'folds, then resents' are docstring claims with no ask-ordering effect
findings.evidence: `_ASK_FAMILY` has no 'sponsor' key (comment: 'a branch, not an ask - it never reorders candidates'), so Britain's and Russia's `reaches_first=('sponsor',)` is read only at ai_diplomacy.py:4555 and war_council.py:1030. Prussia's `"coercion": "folds"  # then resents (§3.3 owns the resentment)` produces only +10 acceptance (COERCION_FOLDS_DELTA); the resentment is not coded in statecraft.py (emergent_designs and instruments handle reneged-bargain grievances generally). The runs show Britain paying (sponsorship_granted 7 per run, all expired by T23 and not renewed while the war ran to T40; separate paymaster_subsidy rows continue) and landing expeditions, so 'pays and never marches' is not enforced, only asserted.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'reaches_first' backend --include=*.py; compare with the NATION_STATECRAFT comments.
findings.expected: Each character claim in the table maps to a named code path, or the comment says it is emergent.
findings.actual: Two of four majors' headline traits are descriptive only.

mechanism.evidence:
The finding is partly right and partly wrong.

1. Wrong: "sponsor" is not purely descriptive. backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:4555 reads it: `if "sponsor" not in (statecraft.get("reaches_first") or ()): continue`. That line gates which payers run the AI directed-sponsorship pass, so only Britain and Russia sponsor. backend/game_logic/war_council.py:1030-1032 reads it to pick a guarantor: `reaches = tuple(statecraft.get("reaches_first") or ())` then `if "sponsor" not in reaches and "align" not in reaches: continue`. statecraft.py:40-47 says "sponsor" is "a branch, not an ask — it never reorders candidates", and nation_config.py:185 says "the branch, not the rung". The code is honest about this. The finding's claim of "no ask-ordering effect" is true, but that is documented design, not a hidden gap.

2. Right: Prussia's `"coercion": "folds"  # then resents (§3.3 owns the resentment)` maps to two code paths. COERCION_FOLDS_DELTA=+10 (statecraft.py:31, applied at statecraft.py:83) and war_council.py:985, where a folds holder buys off the coveter. I found no grep hit in statecraft.py or nearby for a resentment that the fold itself produces. The comment defers it to §3.3, so it is emergent or owned elsewhere. This was a quick grep, not a full trace of §3.3.

3. Right: "pays and never marches" is flavour in the "style" strings. I found no code that stops Britain from marching.

4. Overall: this is a comment and documentation clarity issue with no game-behaviour defect, so P3 at most. The finding's own "expected" line asks only that comments say a trait is emergent, so the fix is wording. I did not open the digests, so the "7 per run, expired by T23" figures are unverified.
mechanism.note: Downgrade to a P3 documentation row. "Sponsor" has real code effects (the ai_diplomacy.py:4555 sponsorship gate and the war_council.py:1030 guarantor gate) and only skips ask reordering, which the code says explicitly. The one valid point is that Prussia's "then resents" comment names no code path and should be marked emergent or point at its owner.

reproduction.evidence: I ran grep -rn 'reaches_first|_ASK_FAMILY|resents' on backend/ and read the code at each hit; I did not run a playtest. (1) The finding's own premise is accurate. statecraft.py:40-46 has no 'sponsor' key, and the comment reads "'sponsor' is a branch, not an ask — it never reorders candidates." The finding then overreaches. ai_diplomacy.py:4555 is `if "sponsor" not in (statecraft.get("reaches_first") or ()): continue`. This is the AI sponsorship loop, so only nations with 'sponsor' pay sponsorships, and it is a real behavioural gate. war_council.py:1030-1034 uses "sponsor" or "align" to decide which nations offer a guarantee. nation_config.py:153-156 and :203 ("the branch, not the rung") document this as a branch from the start, so "sponsor" is wired. (2) 'pays and never marches' is not claimed in the code. The nation_config.py:196 comment reads "leads or funds coalitions", and nothing there promises Britain never lands troops. A run where Britain lands expeditions is therefore no contradiction. The finding's evidence that sponsorships expire by T23 concerns sponsorship cadence, not statecraft wiring. (3) Prussia 'folds' is wired: statecraft.py:83-84 returns COERCION_FOLDS_DELTA (+10), and diplomatic_executor.py:5910-5925 applies it at the ultimatum seam. The "then resents (§3.3 owns the resentment)" comment explicitly delegates the resentment to another spec section. The comments do not claim statecraft.py codes it, and the finding concedes that grievance handling exists generally elsewhere.
reproduction.note: 'Two of four majors' headline traits are descriptive only' is overstated. 'sponsor' gates AI sponsorships and guarantees at ai_diplomacy.py:4555 and war_council.py:1030. 'folds' is a coded acceptance delta. The one genuine nit is that the Prussia 'resents' comment could say 'emergent, via reneged-bargain grievances' for clarity, which is a doc-only P3-at-most tweak and not a game defect.

reproduction.evidence: I re-ran the DC-2 T8 probe itself. findings.seam: backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1234 (bar = need + 1000 + 5 x (bill + upkeep)) with ledger.state_charges_ceiling
findings.evidence: Computed from the real functions at the boot economy (net before Charges / fixed-point chest ceiling / Staff bar): Prussia k=0 laws 414 / 6,140 / 11,500; k=4 14 / 2,140 / 13,500. Austria k=0 405 / 5,375 / 11,500; k=4 -45 / 0 / 13,750. Russia k=0 1,450 / 14,083 / 11,500 (reachable), k=2 1,150 / 11,583 / 13,000 (unreachable). Britain always reachable (25,758 vs 11,500). Archived 97 runs: Prussia General Staff enacted in 10, Russia Divisional System in 29. rev1106-amb six seeds: Prussia 0/6, Russia 0/6. findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <scratch script>: WorldState.from_scenario(europe_1805.json); enact the first k non-Staff laws of Prussia; compare ledger.state_charges_ceiling(net_before_charges, rate) with 9000+1000+5*(bill+300).
findings.expected: A court that the doctrine design says 'cures its flaw by copying the corps system' (Prussia: Articles of War 'once the General Staff stands'; Russia: the Divisional System) can reach its Staff in a 40-turn campaign on some seed.
findings.actual: Prussia's Brittle and Russia's Slow-to-concentrate flaws are uncured on every ambient seed; Prussia pays 100 gold a turn for the Articles of War whose cure clause can never fire.

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism matches the cited code but I did not recompute the finding's numbers. reforms.py around line 1234 sets `bar = need + AI_PURSE_RESERVE + AI_PURSE_UPKEEP_TURNS * (law_upkeep_bill + upkeep)`. The rung also tests the Net before Charges against upkeep. `ledger.state_charges_ceiling` returns `CHARGES_HOARD_FLOOR + net*DIVISOR//rate`, and returns 0 when net <= 0. So a chest that settles below the bar can never reach it, and every cheaper law adds upkeep that raises the bar. The docs record this outcome as known: DOCTRINES_SPEC.md line 457 says "Prussia and Russia never afford their Staff in forty turns on any seed, held every turn by the chest half — RF-3's rung, recorded, not tuned (REFORMS_SPEC §7)". Line 424 and REFORMS_SPEC.md line 608 say the same. A save-for-the-Staff rule exists (`THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF`, from half the price) and it works for Austria and Britain, so the claim that the rung simply buys cheap laws first and raises the bar is partly outdated.
mechanism.note: This is a known, documented design limit, not a code defect. The save-for-the-Staff rule already landed and fixes Austria and Britain. The remaining gap is that Prussia's and Russia's chest ceilings sit below the bar. CLAUDE.md Rule 9 is only partly met: the item is recorded as "recorded, not tuned" and handed to REFORMS_SPEC §7, but I found no owner row, landing slice or behaviour test for a Prussia/Russia fix. That is a doc-contract gap, not a mechanics bug. The finding's P2 is too high. I rate it design, or P3 if the user wants the Rule 9 row filed.
