findings.title: The save-for-the-Staff rule has no reachability guard: it blocks every cheaper law while the Staff is unaffordable forever
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1308-1319 find_ai_enactment (saving = True ... if saving and not is_staff(row): continue)
findings.evidence: Repro: Russia at turn 20 with the Opolchenie and Extraordinary Levy in force, chest 6,000 / 9,000 / 12,000: find_ai_enactment(...) returns None with the rule on, and {'action': 'enact_law', 'target': 'arakcheev_artillery'} with THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF=False. The Staff refusal at those chests is 'the chest (12000) is under the bar (12750)'; Russia's fixed-point chest at that slate is 2000 + 1200 x 2500 / 300 = 12,000, below the bar. Consistent with rev1106-amb six seeds: Russia never enacts Arakcheev's Artillery or the War Ministry (1 gold law and 1 gold-drill law, 38 and 46 of 97 archived runs ever do).
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <scratch>: w=WorldState.from_scenario(europe_1805.json); w.current_turn=20; mark russia opolchenie+extraordinary_levy enacted_turn=2; for chest in (6000,9000,12000): print(reforms.find_ai_enactment(w,'Russia',chest,2)); repeat with reforms.THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF=False.
findings.expected: The rung saves only for a Staff its chest can reach (ceiling >= bar), else it buys what it can afford.
findings.actual: A court sitting in the band [half the Staff price, unreachable bar) enacts nothing for the rest of the game.
findings.prior_row: DOCTRINES_SPEC.md DC-2 (the rule's own landing record, line 457)

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism (backend/game_logic/reforms.py:1308-1319): `saving` goes True once treasury >= Staff price x 0.5, and `if saving and not is_staff(row): continue` skips every cheaper law, with no check that the chest can ever reach the Staff's purse bar. My probe (scratch script run from the repo root, since deleted) built Russia from europe_1805.json at turn 20, marked opolchenie and extraordinary_levy enacted at turn 2, and set `world.nation_gold['Russia']` to each chest. With the rule on, chests 6000, 9000 and 12000 return None. With `THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF=False`, the same chests return {'action':'enact_law','target':'arakcheev_artillery'}. At 13000 both settings enact divisional_system. `ai_purse_refusal` on the Staff at a 12,000 chest says "the chest (12000) is under the bar (12750)". The finding's mechanism and repro hold. One caveat: with law_refusal reading the real treasury, a bare chest argument gives None even with the rule off, so a repro must set nation_gold as I did. I did not verify the claimed fixed-point chest of 12,000. DOCTRINES_SPEC.md:~454 and REFORMS_SPEC.md:356 both record the consequence ("Prussia and Russia never afford their Staff in forty turns on any seed, held every turn by the chest half — RF-3's rung, recorded, not tuned"). The rule is intentional and the consequence is known, but no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row owns it and no reachability guard exists.
mechanism.note: The behaviour is real, but I rate it P3 rather than P2. The save-for-the-Staff rule is a deliberate DC-2 lever, and the spec names its side effect (Russia and Prussia never reach the Staff). The cost is that Russia never gets Arakcheev's Artillery or the War Ministry once the chest is at or above 4,500 gold, which is half the Staff's price. The simple fix is to save only when the chest's reachable ceiling is at least the bar, or to cap how long the court saves. CLAUDE.md rule 9 says no open-ended deferrals; this recorded-but-unowned limitation would need an owning row.

reproduction.evidence:
I ran an in-process probe, WorldState.from_scenario(europe_1805.json) with current_turn=20. I marked Russia's opolchenie and extraordinary_levy enacted_turn=2 and set the Russian treasury to each chest. With the rule on, reforms.find_ai_enactment(w,'Russia',chest,2) returned None at 6000, 9000 and 12000. With reforms.THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF=False it returned {'action':'enact_law','target':'arakcheev_artillery'} at all three chests. The Staff refusal at 12000 is 'the chest (12000) is under the bar (12750)'. Russia's Staff, divisional_system, costs 9000 with upkeep 300. The save trigger at reforms.py:1313 is treasury >= price * AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF_FROM (0.5), and reforms.py:1318-1319 reads `if saving and not is_staff(row): continue`. Nothing checks whether the chest can reach the bar. One caveat on the finding's repro: law_refusal reads the real treasury, not the passed chest argument, so the treasury must be set as well. I did not check the 12,000 fixed-point chest figure, nor the 38/46-of-97 archive counts.

This is a recorded design, not a new defect. docs/DOCTRINES_SPEC.md:457 (the DC-2 landing record) says: "Prussia and Russia never afford their Staff in forty turns on any seed, held every turn by the chest half — RF-3's rung, recorded, not tuned (REFORMS_SPEC §7)." Line 421 names the rule as the recommended fix. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row for it.
reproduction.note: The behaviour is real and reproduces, but the spec already records it as accepted. The Austria and Britain Staff-timing test (T8) passes because of this rule. A reachability guard, saving only when the chest ceiling reaches the bar, is a sensible improvement, since it would free Russia and Prussia to buy cheaper laws. It would also change BASELINE_SERIES and the doctrine cure timings, so it needs a user ruling first. Per CLAUDE.md rule 9 it needs a named owner row. The finding is right that the rule has no guard, but it is a known design tradeoff with its cost recorded, not a P2 defect.

findings.title: Courts' turn-1 Remounts decree (3 authority) plus the Orders in Council (15) strands Britain's Militia Transfer (the Irreplaceable cure) under the authority floor
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/standing.py:316-330 ai_refusal x affairs.py:2010 find_ai_edict authority fallback
findings.evidence: Computed: standing.ai_refusal('Britain', 15) at authority 45 returns ''; at 42 returns 'authority 42 -> 27 is under 30'. Britain boots at 60, enacts the Orders in Council T1 (60 -> 45) and the Remounts in authority T1 (rev1106-amb-* all six: '(1, Britain, the Remounts, 3 authority)'), leaving 42. A court's authority regrows only by a Bulletin or a Te Deum (+4, standing.py:536-540). Britain's Militia Transfer then arrives T32 / T36 / T40 on three seeds (ulm, marengo, austerlitz) and never on friedland, historical, jena. Not measured: Britain's authority trace (the digest does not print courts' authority), so the causal link is arithmetic plus the arrival pattern, not a traced fact.
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <scratch>: set world.nation_authority['Britain']=42; standing.ai_refusal(w,'Britain',15).
findings.expected: A court's cure law (15 authority) is not stranded by a 3-authority trade edict.
findings.actual: One 3-point decree is enough to close an authority-priced cure until a victory regrows the grip. AUTHORITY_CURRENCY_SPEC.md line 21 ('a court's standing only falls') documents the sink, not this consequence.
findings.prior_row: AU-20 / AU-14 (the courts' Decree in authority, ruled at the flip)

mechanism.evidence: The causal chain does not hold. (1) The premise that Britain enacts the Orders in Council on turn 1 is not shown in any digest. `grep -i "orders in council"` over docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-amb-*/digest.md returns nothing, and it also returns nothing for my own run (tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-verify-law4c, seed ulm, 40 turns). In that run Britain's only law enactment is the Commissariat, and its only turn-1 decree is the Remounts for 3 authority. (2) The authority gate was never reached. I wrapped `standing.ai_refusal` to log every Britain call and ran 40 turns on seed ulm. The wrapper wrote no Britain calls, so no authority-priced law ever got as far as the authority floor. (3) The rung's order explains the late arrival. In `reforms.find_ai_enactment` (reforms.py:1294-1330), `THE_AI_SAVES_FOR_THE_STAFF` makes the court skip every non-Staff row once its chest reaches a set share of the Staff price. Britain's Staff, `horse_guards_reforms` in europe_1805.json, costs 9000 gold. The Militia Transfer is the Irreplaceable cure only "while its Staff stands", so it follows the Staff and the purse bar (`ai_purse_refusal`: chest, upkeep and net). Authority is the last test in that function, behind the gold and net tests. The T32/T36/T40 arrivals fit gold and Staff timing. The finding's own evidence admits Britain's authority was never traced. (4) The arithmetic is correct but unreached. `ai_refusal` at standing.py:316-328 does refuse when authority minus 15 is under 30, and the Militia Transfer does cost 15 authority. In my run that branch never fired for Britain, so the finding shows only that the branch exists.
mechanism.note: At most this is a design observation: a court's authority only falls, and it regrows by Bulletin or Te Deum. That is already documented in the spec. I did not find a stranding of the Militia Transfer by authority on the ulm seed. I ran one seed only (ulm). The other seeds were not re-run, and the 15-authority Orders in Council may enact on a seed I did not trace. A reviewer who wants it to stand would need to log Britain's authority at the Militia's first refusal or at its arrival turn. My wrapper's logging only covered calls to `ai_refusal`, so it shows the gate was never reached, not what Britain's authority was.

reproduction.evidence: I read the code but could not run the repro. standing.py:316-326 `ai_refusal` returns a refusal whenever `authority - price < AI_AUTHORITY_FLOOR`, and reforms.py:1165 sets `AI_AUTHORITY_FLOOR = 30`. reforms.py:1249-1251 routes the courts' authority-priced laws through that gate. docs/REFORMS_SPEC.md:310 shows the Militia Transfer costs 15 authority plus 150 gold a turn. Britain therefore needs an authority of at least 45 to enact it. affairs.py:2010-2025 `find_ai_edict` falls back to authority only when gold refuses, which matches the reported Remounts decree. The 60 - 15 - 3 = 42 arithmetic is consistent with that code and with the cited digests, but I did not verify the Orders in Council price, the Remounts price or Britain's boot value of 60. My probe failed (`WorldFactory.create` is not the factory API), so I did not call `ai_refusal` at 42 and 45 myself. I found no closed row or ruling covering this in BUG_FIXES, DESIGN_REFINEMENT or STATUS. REFORMS_SPEC.md:316 says the Militia Transfer's cure also needs the Horse Guards Reforms and the General Staff, and the rung saves for the Staff once the chest passes half its price. Staff timing and gold can therefore also explain the T32-40 arrivals, so the finding's causal link remains unmeasured.
reproduction.note: The floor arithmetic is real, but the harm is unproven and arrival is only delayed (three seeds arrive T32-40, three never). Gold constraints and Staff timing are competing explanations. Recommend a design-level note unless someone traces Britain's authority per turn with `standing.standing_of` in a Mode A run. Kind is the game's design rather than a harness defect.

findings.title: Stale comment says the AI never repeals; SFR-B14 made it repeal before a lapse
findings.evidence: enemy_ai.py:7048: '# as the ledger's forecast. The AI never repeals - the lapse rule is' versus enemy_ai.py:6931-6936 which calls ai_repeal_before_lapse and returns the repeal order.
findings.repro: grep -n 'The AI never repeals' backend/ai/enemy_ai.py
findings.expected: The Priority 1.78 comment matches the Priority 0.5 repeal rung.
findings.actual: The comment contradicts the code three screens above it.

mechanism.evidence: backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:7048 reads "# as the ledger's forecast. The AI never repeals — the lapse rule is" (the Priority 1.78 enact-law comment, lines 7043-7049). Priority 0.5 at enemy_ai.py:6928-6936 reads "repeal = ai_repeal_before_lapse(world, nation, admin_ap)" under "if 'repeal_law' not in skip_actions" and returns it. It is labelled "SAVE THE SLATE (SFR-B14, GR5)" and says it repeals before a lapse. The comment therefore contradicts the code in the same function. I did not check BUG_FIXES.md for a closed row. This is a stale comment and has no runtime effect.
mechanism.note: Doc-only defect. A fix would reword the comment to say the AI repeals only to avoid a lapse (Priority 0.5) and never otherwise. The finding says "three screens above"; the actual gap is about 110 lines.

reproduction.evidence: I ran `grep -n 'The AI never repeals' backend/ai/enemy_ai.py`. It returned line 7048: "# as the ledger's forecast. The AI never repeals — the lapse rule is". The comment sits under "Priority 1.78: ENACT A LAW" (lines 7043-7050). I then read lines 6925-6940. They hold "Priority 0.5: SAVE THE SLATE (SFR-B14, GR5)". That block calls `ai_repeal_before_lapse(world, nation, admin_ap)` and returns the repeal order when the AI holds the purse and a law would lapse. So the AI does repeal, which contradicts the Priority 1.78 comment. The claim is accurate. One nuance: the comment can be read as describing only the enactment rung, since 1.78 itself never repeals and the lapse rule is its discipline. Even so, the SFR-B14 repeal rung makes the blanket statement stale.
reproduction.note: This is a comment-only inaccuracy at backend/ai/enemy_ai.py:7048, with no behavioural impact. A fix would reword the comment to say the enactment rung never repeals, and that the Priority 0.5 SFR-B14 rung repeals only to save a law that would lapse at turn's end. I did not check docs/BUG_FIXES.md for a closed row on this.

findings.title: naval.py recomputes the blockade cut percent inline instead of calling blockade_cut_percent (a second source of the same figure)
findings.evidence: naval.py:1216 min(100, int(round((1.0 - BLOCKADE_TRADE_FACTOR) * _f * 100))) duplicates blockade_cut_percent(factor) whose docstring says 'ONE source for the phrase below and the LAWS tab's effect line'. Today the arithmetic agrees (both give 62 for x1.25), so no live disagreement.
findings.repro: sed -n 1205,1218p backend/game_logic/naval.py; sed -n 1454,1458p backend/game_logic/naval.py
findings.expected: Every surface quoting the cut reads blockade_cut_percent.
findings.actual: Two copies; the next change to one will split the Admiralty's board line from the LAWS tab.

mechanism.evidence: The duplication is real. In backend/game_logic/naval.py, blockade_forecast_sentence (around lines 1213-1216) computes the cut inline: `_cut = (f"cut by {min(100, int(round((1.0 - BLOCKADE_TRADE_FACTOR) * _f * 100)))}%")`. Lines 1454-1458 define blockade_cut_percent(factor), whose docstring says "ONE source for the phrase below and the LAWS tab's effect line (RF-4a)". Its body is `min(int(round((1.0 - BLOCKADE_TRADE_FACTOR) * float(factor) * 100)), 100)`. The inline expression is the same formula (the two clamps differ only in order), so the arithmetic matches today. Other callers do use the helper: naval.py:1468 (blockade_trade_words), naval.py:3059 and reforms.py:788-790. blockade_forecast_sentence is the one site that bypasses it. I found no RF-4a entry in docs/BUG_FIXES.md that covers this site, so it is not a closed row. It is cosmetic maintainability debt with no live behavioural divergence.
mechanism.note: Confirmed as a minor DRY and sibling-sweep miss. The fix is to replace the inline expression with `blockade_cut_percent(_f)`. blockade_cut_percent is defined later in the module than its inline use, but that is fine because the call happens at runtime. No player-visible bug today.

reproduction.evidence: I read backend/game_logic/naval.py. The inline copy is at line 1216: `_cut = (f"cut by {min(100, int(round((1.0 - BLOCKADE_TRADE_FACTOR) * _f * 100)))}%")`. The helper is at line 1454: `def blockade_cut_percent(factor: float) -> int:`. Its docstring says "ONE source for the phrase below and the LAWS tab's effect line (RF-4a)", and its body is `min(int(round((1.0 - BLOCKADE_TRADE_FACTOR) * float(factor) * 100)), 100)`. The arithmetic is identical, so nothing disagrees today. The other callers (naval.py:1468, naval.py:3059, reforms.py:790) use the helper. Only line 1216 recomputes the figure. I did not run the code, because the finding is a static duplication and the sed output was enough.
reproduction.note: This is a real but cosmetic maintainability issue. There is a second copy of the formula, and no behavior is wrong at present. The fix is to replace the inline expression at line 1216 with `blockade_cut_percent(_f)`. The helper is defined later in the module, but Python resolves it at call time, so the call is safe.

findings.title: recruit_morale laws are void in any province with a training ground (and so is Russia's -10 trade-off)
findings.seam: backend/commands/economy_executor.py:1898-1909 (law term added to RECRUIT_MORALE, then replaced by RECRUIT_MORALE_TRAINED)
findings.evidence: economy_executor.py:1909 'RECRUIT_MORALE = self.RECRUIT_MORALE_TRAINED' (70) overwrites the law-adjusted base (40 + law). The Jager Battalions (2,500 gold + 100/turn), the Articles of War, the New Order carry +10/+5 that does nothing there, and the Extraordinary Levy's -10 never bites there. The code comment documents it ('void where they apply'). Infantry batch is 10,000 men, so on a 30,000-man corps the +10 is about +2.5 morale at base.
findings.repro: read economy_executor.py:1898-1912
findings.expected: A law's morale term is either additive to the trained rung or its void case is said on the law's own tab line.
findings.actual: The LAWS tab states the effect unconditionally; the void case is only a code comment.

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real, but it is documented, specified behaviour. economy_executor.py:1896-1909 adds the law term to RECRUIT_MORALE, stores it as law_morale, then `if region.has_building("training_ground"): RECRUIT_MORALE = self.RECRUIT_MORALE_TRAINED`. That replaces the law-adjusted value with the flat 70. Moore's floor of 60 then applies only if the value is below 60. The code comment says "Training Ground's rung and Moore's floor, which replace it (so it is void where they apply)". REFORMS_SPEC.md:571 says the same: "BEFORE the training ground's flat rung and Moore's floor, which replace it (so the law is void there)". So this was a designed, spec-recorded rule, not a bug. The unconditional LAWS tab wording is not checked: I did not open the tab text, so the "void case is only a code comment" claim is unverified. The spec text is a second place that states the void case, though not on the tab line.
mechanism.note: Not a defect. The void-where-trained behaviour is stated in REFORMS_SPEC.md:571 and in the code comment. At most this is a presentation or design polish item, such as saying "void where a training ground stands" on the law's tab line. Russia's -10 never biting in trained provinces may be intended: the training ground sets a flat 70 rung. I did not check whether the law result text (T8 note) names the law only when its term is what the recruits carry; the code comment at about line 1925 suggests it does.

reproduction.evidence: I read backend/commands/economy_executor.py:1896-1912, and the code matches the finding. The law's term is added at 1902-1904 (`RECRUIT_MORALE = max(0, min(100, RECRUIT_MORALE + sum(...)))`). `law_morale` is saved at 1905. If the region has a training ground, line 1909 then runs `RECRUIT_MORALE = self.RECRUIT_MORALE_TRAINED`, which discards the law term. The recruit result names the law only when `RECRUIT_MORALE == law_morale` (line 1927). The law's description string (reforms.py:769-773) reads "{who} muster at {n:+d} morale" with no condition. I did not run the game, so the unqualified-description point rests on reading that string, not on a rendered LAWS tab. I did not check the cost figures or the Russia trade-off beyond the code path.
reproduction.note: This was a deliberate choice, not a bug. The comment at economy_executor.py:1896-1898 says the term is "void where they apply". docs/REFORMS_SPEC.md:571 documents it too: "BEFORE the training ground's flat rung and Moore's floor, which replace it (so the law is void there)". The only gap is that the LAWS tab line carries no caveat. Rate it P3 or design, as the reviewer filed it. It is not a defect to fix, but a one-clause qualifier on the tab line would close it.

findings.title: An enemy court's AI crash row (V2-19) is suppressed by the fog filter, so the player is never told a court skipped its turn
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/enemy_phase_fog.py:filter_enemy_phase_by_visibility (the 'Missing region or below FULL -> suppress' tail, ~line 214) against turn_manager.py:1312 _error_row
findings.evidence: turn_manager.py:1312-1318: `def _error_row(): # V2-19: Surface error to player instead of swallowing silently / return {"action": "error", "message": f"{nation} encountered an error during their turn", "battle_message": ""}`. The row has no ai_action, events or region, so it matches no involves_player arm. The filter's docstring says 'Missing/unrecognized fields -> suppress', and the grep for "error" in enemy_phase_fog.py finds nothing. Probe (scratchpad crash.py, in-process 1805, Austria's process_nation_turn forced to raise on the first end turn): the response has 'enemy_phase', the string 'encountered an error' appears nowhere in it, and the only trace is errors.tally(): [{'site': 'turn_manager.TurnManager._run_ai_phases: the military phase', 'count': 1}] plus server stderr. Sibling: _process_enemy_turns' execute_commission_only crash (turn_manager.py:1432-1435) reports to the tally but adds no row at all. Grep of BUG_FIXES.md, DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md and the archives for 'encountered an error' / 'V2-19' found no closed row.
findings.repro: Run the script /c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/1bd395101ae53e89/c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40/scratchpad/crash.py with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (monkeypatches EnemyAI.process_nation_turn to raise for Austria, then POST /command 'end turn'). Or call filter_enemy_phase_by_visibility on {'nations': {'Austria': {'actions': [{'action': 'error', 'message': 'Austria encountered an error during their turn', 'battle_message': ''}]}}}.
findings.expected: A crashed court is reported on a visible row (the notice rail, the campaign log, or an error row that bypasses the fog gate). V2-19's stated intent is 'surface error to player instead of swallowing silently', and DD-C's rule is 'nothing fails silently'.
findings.actual: The error row is built, then dropped by the fog filter for every enemy court. The player sees an enemy phase with that court missing. Only the server console and the `/debug errors` tally record the crash.

mechanism.evidence: I traced this by hand and did not run it. The row built at turn_manager.py:1312-1318 is `{"action": "error", "message": ..., "battle_message": ""}`. It has no `naval_diorama`, `events`, `ai_action` or region. In enemy_phase_fog.py `filter_enemy_phase_by_visibility`, every `involves_player` arm needs one of those fields, so none matches. `action_region` stays None, so the `if action_region:` block is skipped and the code reaches the comment "# Missing region or below FULL -> suppress (safe default)" with no append. A nation whose only action is the error row is then left out of `filtered_phase["nations"]`. Neither enemy_phase_fog.py nor main.py has an arm for `action == "error"`. A grep of backend/ and godot-client/ for "encountered an error" finds only turn_manager.py:1208 (an unrelated marshal command) and the `_error_row` itself, so nothing else surfaces the text. The V2-19 comment says "Surface error to player instead of swallowing silently", but the fog gate defeats that for enemy courts. All three `_error_row()` call sites go through the same filter: the single-guard path, the military-phase crash, and the admin-phase crash. The crash is still recorded by `_errors.report` and the debug print. My own probe script failed on an import path (no `backend` module outside the repo cwd), so I did not reproduce it at runtime.
mechanism.note: The mechanism holds: an enemy court's crash row is dropped by the fog filter. I rate it P3 rather than P2 because it is a diagnostic-visibility gap, not a wrong game state. The tally and the log still record the crash, and the partial marches survive under `separate_ai_phases`. A crash in AI code is a rare engine fault. The fix is small: give `action == "error"` an exemption in the filter, or send it to the notice rail. I did not check the claimed sibling (the `execute_commission_only` crash at turn_manager.py:1432-1435) and make no claim about it.

reproduction.evidence: Reproduced two ways. (1) Direct call: filter_enemy_phase_by_visibility({'nations':{'Austria':{'actions':[{'action':'error','message':'Austria encountered an error during their turn','battle_message':''}]}}}, stub world with player_nation='France') returned {'nations': {}, 'total_actions': 0, 'summary': []}. The row is dropped. (2) The finding's scratchpad crash.py, with PYTHONHASHSEED=0, forces Austria's process_nation_turn to raise (RuntimeError) and then does a POST /command 'end turn'. It printed 'keys has enemy_phase: True', 'error text visible anywhere in response: False', and the tally [{'site': 'turn_manager.TurnManager._run_ai_phases: the military phase', 'count': 1, ...}]. The crash is also written to stderr. turn_manager.py:1316 builds the row ('encountered an error during their turn'). The only other hit for that string in backend/ or godot-client/ is turn_manager.py:1208, a different crash message. enemy_phase_fog.py has no 'error' arm; its tail comment is '# Missing region or below FULL -> suppress (safe default)'. Grep of docs/*.md for 'V2-19' found no hit in the active docs. I did not search the archives.
reproduction.note: The defect is real, but I rate it P3, not P2. It only occurs after an enemy AI exception, which is already logged to stderr and the errors tally. The player's loss is a missing 'a court skipped its turn' notice. Separately, filtering out error rows is arguably consistent with fog rules, since a crash is an engine fault and not a world event. The finding says V2-19 intended to show the error to the player, and that intent is defeated. I did not check whether the client ever rendered that row before the fog filter was lifted out. The fix would be a one-line bypass for action=='error', or routing the crash to the notice rail. The sibling case, execute_commission_only crashing at turn_manager.py:1432-1435 with no row at all, was not run.

findings.title: One exception inside advance_turn leaves the campaign permanently stuck: every later End Turn re-runs the whole enemy phase and reports success without advancing
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:12555 _advance_turn_internal R20 guard together with backend/commands/meta_executor.py:436-439 and turn_manager.end_turn
findings.evidence: world_state.py:12555 `if self._last_advanced_turn >= self.current_turn: debug_print("[WARNING] advance_turn already ran for turn ...skipping"); return`, stamped at the START of the advance (`self._last_advanced_turn = self.current_turn`, ~12580) before current_turn is incremented. Probe (scratchpad stuck.py, in-process 1805, process_construction_timers raises on its first call): `end turn #1: success=False turn_after=1 msg='Error: synthetic advance crash'`. Then `#2: success=True turn_after=1 msg='Turn 1 is already underway!' moves=2`, `#3: ... moves=4`, `#4: ... moves=4`. The count is the enemy marshals standing off their spawn square; the enemy phase therefore runs again on each retry, so it still plays. meta_executor.py:436-439 turns turn_ended==next_turn into `"success": True, "message": f"Turn {world.current_turn} is already underway!"`. A save written in that state carries last_advanced_turn == current_turn and reloads stuck. No test pins this: grep of tests for 'already underway' and 'advance crash' finds nothing relevant.
findings.repro: Run /c/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/1bd395101ae53e89/c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40/scratchpad/stuck.py with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (it patches WorldState.process_construction_timers to raise once, then POSTs 'end turn' four times).
findings.expected: After a crash mid-advance, a retry either completes the advance idempotently (resume from the stage that failed) or fails loudly and offers recovery (reload the autosave). It must not report success while the turn can never advance, and it must not replay the enemy phase on every click.
findings.actual: The first click shows 'Error: <exception text>'. Every later click returns success=True with 'Turn N is already underway!', the turn counter never moves, and the enemy AI takes another set of actions each time. The only exit is loading an older save. The 'R20 idempotency' guard turns a transient fault into a soft-lock.

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real and I reproduced it. world_state.py:12555 reads `if self._last_advanced_turn >= self.current_turn:` and returns early. The stamp `self._last_advanced_turn = self.current_turn` is set at line 12567, near the start and before the increment and before the stages that can raise. After one exception, a retry sees N >= N and skips the advance. turn_manager.end_turn then reports turn_ended == next_turn, and meta_executor.py:436-439 turns that into success=True with "Turn N is already underway!". I ran the reviewer's stuck.py with PYTHONHASHSEED=0. Output: #1 success=False turn_after=1 'Error: synthetic advance crash' last_adv=1; #2, #3 and #4 success=True turn_after=1 'Turn 1 is already underway!', with the count of moved enemy marshals rising 1 → 2 → 4 → 5. The turn never advances and the enemy phase re-runs. last_advanced_turn is serialized at line 10052 and restored at line 11075, so a save taken in that state reloads stuck. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row covering this, and no ruling.
mechanism.note: The soft-lock is real, but the probe injects the exception. Nothing found shows an organic exception inside advance_turn, so this is a robustness gap in the recovery path rather than a live player-facing bug. P2 overstates it. A fix would stamp `_last_advanced_turn` at the end of the advance, or reset it on exception. Failing loudly instead of reporting success would also help.

reproduction.evidence:
Ran the reviewer's stuck.py with PYTHONHASHSEED=0. Output: "end turn #1: success=False turn_after=1 msg='Error: synthetic advance crash' last_adv=1 ... moves=1", then #2, #3 and #4 each "success=True turn_after=1 msg='Turn 1 is already underway!' last_adv=1", with moves 2, 4 and 4. The turn never advanced, and the enemy moves count kept growing, so the enemy phase re-ran on each retry.

Code checked: world_state.py:12555 `if self._last_advanced_turn >= self.current_turn: ... return`. The stamp `self._last_advanced_turn = self.current_turn` is at line 12567, at the start of the advance and before the fallible stages. The crash was in process_construction_timers at world_state.py:12837. meta_executor.py:436-439 turns turn_ended==next_turn into success=True "Turn N is already underway!". last_advanced_turn is serialized (world_state.py:10052 and 11075), so a save made in that state reloads stuck.

Grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for "already underway", "advance crash" and "_last_advanced_turn" found no closed row or user ruling covering this.
reproduction.note: The probe injects a synthetic exception, so this is a fault-tolerance gap rather than a bug seen in normal play. It only bites if an unexpected exception fires inside advance_turn. When it does, the campaign soft-locks and the failure reports as success. I rate it P2, as filed. The only observed effect is the wrong success report and the replayed enemy phase. If an advance crash is judged unlikely enough, it could drop to P3.

findings.title: The --reload-every contract ('byte-identical modulo load lines and re-raised answers') is false: Berthier's after-battle wording changes after a reload
findings.seam: tools/playtest_driver.py:1692 reload_round_trip docstring and docs/PLAYTESTING.md:364-367 against backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:748 reset_observation_rotation (called from WorldState.__init__)
findings.evidence: diff of tools/playtest_runs/rev1106-turn-reload/digest.md against rev1106-turn-noreload/digest.md (20 turns, reload at t5/10/15/20): beyond the RELOAD note lines, two lines differ. Turn 10 enemy phase, reload: 'Massena's army has been badly mauled. Archduke Charles proved the stronger force today.' against noreload: 'The toll on Massena's forces is heavy, Sire. This defeat will be felt.' Turn 15: 'Ney stood alone, Sire. Bernadotte never came.' against 'Not one corps reached Ney. Bernadotte was expected; Ney fought the battle single-handed.' Casualties (196/2613, 2509/1292) are identical. Cause: battle_report.py:748-749 `def reset_observation_rotation(): _OBSERVATION_COUNTS.clear()` runs on every WorldState construction, including a load. The ruling is recorded (IQ6-X1 / IQ-8 item 8 in docs/archive/BUG_FIXES_2026_Q3.md:800: 'a loaded campaign does NOT continue its own rotation'), so the behaviour is a decision. Only the harness contract text is wrong.
findings.repro: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/playtest_driver.py --script tools/playtest_scripts/commanded_full40.json --turns 20 --diplomacy accept --reload-every 5 --name X --fresh`, then the same without --reload-every, then diff the digests. Archived: docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-turn-reload and rev1106-turn-noreload.
findings.expected: The documented contract matches what is measured: 'identical modulo load lines, re-raised answers and Berthier's display-only observation line, whose per-pair rotation restarts on load (IQ-8 item 8)'. Or the rotation is carried through the save.
findings.actual: A reader who treats 'byte-identical' as an oracle for save fidelity gets false diffs, and a real diff could hide among these.
findings.prior_row: IQ6-X1 / IQ-8 item 8 (a stated ruling; this is the harness contract text)

mechanism.evidence:
The mechanism holds. backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:745-749: `def reset_observation_rotation(): ... _OBSERVATION_COUNTS.clear()`. Its docstring says it is called from WorldState.__init__ for "every campaign creation, new or loaded". backend/models/world_state.py:1806-1807 calls it. A load therefore restarts the per-pair rotation of Berthier's after-battle lines.

The contract text is overstated. docs/PLAYTESTING.md:364-367 says: "byte-identical to the no-reload run MODULO the load lines and any re-raised answer". tools/playtest_driver.py:1688 repeats it.

I ran diff on docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-turn-reload/digest.md against rev1106-turn-noreload/digest.md. Apart from the RELOAD/re-raised lines and the title, two lines differ:
- Line 251, turn 10: "Massena's army has been badly mauled. Archduke Charles proved the stronger force today." against "The toll on Massena's forces is heavy, Sire. This defeat will be felt."
- Line 331, turn 15: "Ney stood alone, Sire. Bernadotte never came." against "Not one corps reached Ney. Bernadotte was expected; ..."

The casualty figures are identical, so only the wording differs. The reload-every contract as written is false.
mechanism.note: Real, but it is a harness contract-text defect (kind harness/doc), not a game defect. The game behaviour is a recorded ruling (IQ6-X1 / IQ-8 item 8: a loaded campaign does not continue its own rotation). The fix is to amend docs/PLAYTESTING.md:364-367 and the docstring at tools/playtest_driver.py:~1688 to add "and Berthier's display-only observation wording, whose rotation restarts on load". I did not open docs/archive/BUG_FIXES_2026_Q3.md:800 to check the ruling quote. I took its existence from the finding and from the reset function's docstring.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the playtests. I diffed the archived digests docs/audits/playtest_digests/rev1106-turn-reload/digest.md and rev1106-turn-noreload/digest.md. Apart from the title line and the RELOAD note lines (t5, t10, t15, t20), exactly two lines differ. Line 251 (reload) reads "Massena's army has been badly mauled. Archduke Charles proved the stronger force today." Line 249 (noreload) reads "The toll on Massena's forces is heavy, Sire. This defeat will be felt." Line 331 (reload) reads "Ney stood alone, Sire. Bernadotte never came." Line 327 (noreload) reads "Not one corps reached Ney. Bernadotte was expected; Ney fought the battle single-handed." The casualty figures are identical in both. The cause is in the code. backend/game_logic/battle_report.py:745-749 defines reset_observation_rotation(), which runs _OBSERVATION_COUNTS.clear(). Its docstring says it is called from WorldState.__init__ for every campaign creation, "new or loaded". backend/models/world_state.py:1806-1807 makes that call. The false contract text is at tools/playtest_driver.py (reload_round_trip docstring): "byte-identical to the no-reload run MODULO the load lines AND any answer the load re-raises". It is also at docs/PLAYTESTING.md:364-367: "byte-identical to the no-reload run MODULO the load lines and any re-raised answer". Neither text mentions Berthier's observation wording, so the contract is wrong as written.
reproduction.note: The finding is real but small. The kind is harness/doc, not the game. The game behaviour was ruled earlier (IQ6-X1 / IQ-8 item 8, as the finding cites; I did not re-open that archive). Combat results are unchanged and only the display-only Berthier line differs. The fix is to add "and Berthier's display-only observation line, whose per-pair rotation restarts on load" to the docstring and to PLAYTESTING.md. The alternative is to carry the rotation counter through the save.

findings.title: The 14 console-only 'except Exception' handlers (4 in main.py, 3 in the desks, 3 in llm_client, others) count as spoken but never reach errors.report or the /debug errors tally
findings.seam: backend/main.py:3991 (the /command premise stage), 6325, 6719, 6778; backend/models/world_state.py:13166; backend/ai/question_desk.py:528 and 3241; backend/ai/state_desk.py:4165; backend/ai/llm_client.py:2447
findings.evidence: main.py:3991-3992: `except Exception as _exc: print(f"[PREMISE] {_exc}")` inside _command_parse. If split_premise or premise_refusal raises, the issuance-time premise check is skipped and the order proceeds unchecked, with no player-visible or tallied trace. world_state.py:13166-13169 logs `logging.getLogger(__name__).warning("IQ-4: the mission rail restate failed", exc_info=True)` instead of errors.report. main.py:6325-6332 `_get_fortify_state_safe` prints, then returns {"direction": "error", ..., "error": str(e)}. The census (tools/_code_health_census.py) reports `except Exception: total=549 {'reports': 526, 'silent': 6, 'logs': 14, 'reraise': 3}`, where 'logs' are exempt from tests/test_code_health_ratchet.py's SILENT_HANDLERS_CAP = 6. errors.py's docstring says 'Every broad except speaks'.
findings.repro: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/_code_health_census.py`, then list the 'logs' handlers with a script that finds `except Exception` blocks lacking report( in the next 7 lines. The output matches the 14 sites above.
findings.expected: Per CODE-3 / DD-C every broad except goes through errors.report (once per site, in the /debug errors tally), at least on the /command chain (main.py:3991).
findings.actual: The tally and any score instrument reading it do not see these 14 sites. A recurring failure at main.py:3991 would be invisible apart from a stdout line.

mechanism.evidence: The sites are real and as quoted. backend/main.py:3991-3992 reads `except Exception as _exc:` then `print(f"[PREMISE] {_exc}")`. If split_premise or premise_refusal raises, the premise check is skipped and execution falls through to `ctx.parser.parse` unchecked. world_state.py:13166-13169 uses `logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(..., exc_info=True)`. main.py:6322-6332 prints `[FORTIFY_STATE_ERROR]` and returns a dict with direction "error". None of these call errors.report, so the /debug errors tally never counts them. tools/_code_health_census.py:171-176 classifies a handler as `reports` only if it calls report with a site string. Otherwise, if the body matches the regex `\b(log|logger|logging|print|warn)\w*`, it counts as `logs`. Only the remaining handlers count as `silent`, and only `silent` is capped. So `logs` is a deliberate exempt bucket. docs/CODE_HEALTH_PLAN.md around lines 1330-1361 records "logs 28 → 14" as a known residue, and no ruling says these must be converted. The finding is partly mis-framed: the census never counts these 14 as "spoken", it counts them as `logs`. They do emit a console or log line, so they are not silent. The gap is only that they are invisible to the tally and to the score instrument. I did not run the census or look for a closed BUG_FIXES row.
mechanism.note: A true but minor consistency gap against the errors.py docstring "Every broad except speaks". The fix is cheap: convert main.py:3991 to report(exc, "main._command_parse: premise") at least, and ideally all 14 handlers in the census `logs` bucket. Impact is limited to the /debug errors tally and the score instrument. Nothing is mis-simulated, and a premise failure still leaves a stdout line. Treat it as a P3 observability row, not a gameplay defect.

reproduction.evidence: I ran `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 tools/_code_health_census.py`. It printed `except Exception: total=549 {'reports': 526, 'silent': 6, 'logs': 14, 'reraise': 3}`. The census builds that 'logs' class at tools/_code_health_census.py:174. Handlers in it are not counted as silent, so the ratchet's SILENT_HANDLERS_CAP = 6 (tests/test_code_health_ratchet.py:33, :57-59) never sees them. I did not list the 14 sites individually, so only the main.py:3991 and world_state.py:13166 sites were checked in the source. main.py:3991-3992 reads `except Exception as _exc:` then `print(f"[PREMISE] {_exc}")`. If split_premise or premise_refusal raises there, the issuance-time premise check is skipped and execution continues to `parser.parse` unchecked. world_state.py:13166-13169 uses `logging.getLogger(__name__).warning("IQ-4: the mission rail restate failed", exc_info=True)`. Neither goes through `errors.report`, so neither reaches the `/debug errors` tally. backend/errors.py's docstring says "Every broad except speaks" and describes the tally. No BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row covers this (grep for TURN-4, 'console-only' and a logs exemption found nothing).
reproduction.note: The finding is real but small. Each handler does emit a stdout or logger line, so none is truly silent. The gap is that those lines miss the process tally and any instrument reading it, and the CODE-3 ratchet exempts them. The premise check (main.py:3991) failing open is deliberate graceful degradation, not a game-state corruption path. The fix is mechanical: swap in `report(exc, "<site>")` at the 14 sites, and either move them into the ratchet's count or document the exemption. I confirmed the census reading and the two sites quoted above, not each of the remaining 12.

findings.title: docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md 'Turn Resolution Order' is an 8-step Phase 6.2 summary of a roughly 60-stage advance_turn
findings.evidence: The doc lists: 1 clear flags, 2 tactical states, 3 turn increment, 4 stability, 5 war damage, 6 bankruptcy desertion, 7 income, 8 resets/cavalry/trust/reckless. The code between world_state.py:12542 and :13400 also runs, in this order: settlement-draft discard and petition lapse, relation snapshot, strategic-objection lapse, vindication decay, construction timers, increment, stability and recovery, supply attrition, literal-fidelity events, capital garrison regen, bankruptcy desertion, process_diplomacy_turn, proposal in transit, cooldown tick, vassal processing, clear_turn_battles, coalition, AI-AI diplomacy, war council, third-party settlements, clear_stale (12998), admiralty tick, income, trade, Continental System penalties, action reset, treaty clauses, vassal tribute, recurring settlement gold, sponsorship, dotation, reform lapse, the Return, bankruptcy, manpower, the mission-notice restate, then cavalry, trust, reckless, jealousy, evacuation corridors, agendas, formations, moments, fog and the Moniteur. The order is load-bearing (comments say 'must run BEFORE income', 'after vassal processing but BEFORE income'). CLAUDE.md tells readers to compare with this section.
findings.repro: Read docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:2662-2672 against `grep -n '^        # [A-Z]' backend/models/world_state.py` between lines 12542 and 13400.
findings.expected: The documented order matches the code, or the section points to the in-code section banners as the authority.
findings.actual: The doc omits about 50 stages. Several stages are pinned in the code by comments but not in any reference. A reviewer trusting the 8-step list would miss real ordering constraints.

mechanism.evidence: docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:2662-2672 "### Turn Resolution Order" lists exactly 8 steps, each tagged "Phase 6.2.x". `_advance_turn_internal` is at backend/models/world_state.py:12542, and 144 comment banners (`^        # [A-Z]`) fall between 12542 and 13400. The doc's list is therefore a stale Phase 6.2 summary, not the live order. No other "Turn Resolution" section exists in the doc. One part of the finding is wrong: CLAUDE.md never tells readers to compare against this section. Its "Turn processing" row (line 164) points to world_state.py advance_turn and meta_executor, and nothing else.
mechanism.note: This is a real documentation gap with no runtime effect. The section is scoped to the economy chapter as a 6.2 summary, but it is titled as the whole turn order. Fix by adding a pointer to the in-code section banners as the authority, or by marking the list "economy steps only". Drop the claim that CLAUDE.md points readers at this section.

reproduction.evidence: docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:2662 "### Turn Resolution Order" is an 8-line block (steps 1-8, tagged Phase 6.2.A/B/C) and is the only heading with that name in the docs. backend/models/world_state.py:12542 is `def _advance_turn_internal`. Between lines 12542 and 13400, `awk` found 144 banner-style comment lines (`^        # [A-Z]`), so the code has far more stages than the doc lists. Other sections of SYSTEMS_REFERENCE (lines 8607, 11939, 13108) describe individual stages by position, for example "after process_intent_movements and before the fog and Le Moniteur", but no section gives the full order.
reproduction.note: The doc is stale as a full-order reference. It is a summary, not a defect in the game. The finding's claim that "CLAUDE.md tells readers to compare with this section" did not hold up: the grep found no mention of the section in CLAUDE.md, whose "Turn processing" row points to world_state.py advance_turn and meta_executor.py. Kept at P3 documentation drift. The fix is to retitle the section as a Phase 6.2 summary and point it at the in-code banners.

findings.title: Drill payoff (shock_bonus +20% attack) is never consumed by a garrison assault, so a drilled corps assaults capitals at +20% for as long as it keeps assaulting
findings.evidence: Code: combat_executor.py:5926 `attacker_modifier = marshal.get_attack_modifier()` reads shock_bonus (marshal.py:1339-1342 `modifier *= (1.0 + shock * 0.10)`) and clears nothing. The only clears of shock_bonus are combat.py:166 (_cancel_drill, defender side), combat.py:564-568 (resolve_battle, with the comment 'a pragmatic exception to Golden Rule #1'), and movement_executor.py:2171. grep 'shock_bonus' in combat_executor.py returns 0 lines. Probe (Europe boot, Austria's Mack 60k assaults Paris garrison 25k, is_ai_command): with shock_bonus=2 the result was shock_bonus 2 after the assault, drill_complete_turn 1 not reset, attacker losses 5,208. With shock_bonus=0 attacker losses were 6,250. The bonus applied and was not spent. Not found in BUG_FIXES, DESIGN_REFINEMENT or the 2026 archives.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 scratchpad/p2.py (Europe boot via WorldState.from_scenario; Mack beside Paris; paris.garrison_strength=25000; mack.shock_bonus=2; execute {'action':'attack','target':'Paris'}; print mack.shock_bonus afterwards -> 2). Output: (2, 1, 54792, ...) vs (0, -1, 53750, ...).
findings.expected: Rule 4: read the drill, use it, then clear it (shock_bonus, drilling, drilling_locked and drill_complete_turn reset), as resolve_battle does at combat.py:564-568. A garrison assault is an attack, as the MC-1c comment at combat_executor.py:5908 says for Iron Resolve.
findings.actual: The +20% (and the +5% personality drill synergy) stays on the marshal after every garrison assault. A player or enemy AI corps that drills once then assaults capitals repeatedly keeps the bonus until a marshal-vs-marshal battle spends it. enemy_ai.py:3925-3928 and 5227 value shock_bonus when choosing, so the AI exploits it too.

mechanism.evidence:
By hand trace, the garrison assault never spends the drill bonus.
- backend/commands/combat_executor.py:5926 reads `attacker_modifier = marshal.get_attack_modifier()`. marshal.py:1339-1342 applies `modifier *= (1.0 + shock * 0.10)` and clears nothing.
- grep of `shock_bonus` in combat_executor.py returns 0 lines. The sibling garrison code at 5908-5912 does handle Iron Resolve consumption (MC-1c), but nothing handles the drill.
- The only code that zeroes shock_bonus is combat.py:164-166 (defender side), combat.py:563-567 (resolve_battle: shock_bonus, drilling, drilling_locked and drill_complete_turn reset), movement_executor.py:2171 (retreat) and marshal.py:884 (clear_combat_transient_state). None is called from _resolve_garrison_combat.
- Rule 4 in CLAUDE.md (read, use, then clear) and the combat.py comment at 557-562 show the bonus is meant to be one-time use. A garrison assault skips the clear.
- I did not re-run the probe. The code path is unambiguous, and the reporter's numbers (attacker losses 5,208 vs 6,250) match a +20% modifier that stays on the marshal.
- No closed row in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md covers drill/shock_bonus on garrison assaults.
mechanism.note: The defect is real, but P1 is too high. It is a bounded leak: +20% attack (plus the personality drill synergy) persists across repeated garrison assaults until a marshal-vs-marshal battle, retreat or army break clears it. It needs a prior completed drill. It does not crash or corrupt state, and the AI shares the same executor, so both sides benefit equally. The fix is small: capture the drill bonus before get_attack_modifier in _resolve_garrison_combat and reset the four drill fields afterward, as combat.py:563-567 does. Per Rule 10, the sweep should also check other callers of get_attack_modifier outside resolve_battle, such as bombardment, charge and auto-charge, for the same missing clear.

reproduction.evidence: The finding reproduces. I booted Europe with WorldState.from_scenario(europe_1805.json, seed historical) and put Austria's Mack (60k) in Paris against a 25k garrison. I then called CommandExecutor()._resolve_garrison_combat(m, paris, w, {"world": w}) with Mack's shock_bonus set to 2 and then 0. The probe is saved at C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\1bd395101ae53e89\c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40\scratchpad\v1.py. Output was (shock_bonus after, drill_complete_turn after, attacker losses): shock=2 gave (2, 1, 5208) and shock=0 gave (0, -1, 6250). So the +20% applied, losses fell by about 17%, and the bonus and drill_complete_turn were not cleared. Code: combat_executor.py:5926 reads `attacker_modifier = marshal.get_attack_modifier()`, and marshal.py:1339-1342 applies shock_bonus. combat.py:563-568 (resolve_battle) is where the clear lives. The MC-1c comment at combat_executor.py:5908 treats a garrison assault as an attack for Iron Resolve, which the same function does consume. grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md, DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md and the other docs found no row or ruling that exempts garrison assaults from spending the drill.
reproduction.note: I rate it P2, not P1. The effect is a one-time +20% attack that persists across garrison assaults only, until a marshal-vs-marshal battle spends it. Garrison combat has no other consequence, and there is no crash or save corruption. I did not test the repeated-assault loop or the enemy AI valuing shock_bonus (enemy_ai.py:3925-3928, 5227). The AI claim is plausible but unverified. The fix is small: read the drill in _resolve_garrison_combat, then reset shock_bonus, drilling, drilling_locked and drill_complete_turn as combat.py:563-568 does. The sibling sweep (rule 10) should also check the cavalry charge path and any other combat path that calls get_attack_modifier without a clear.

findings.title: Strategic-order defiance by an aggressive marshal ordered to HOLD becomes a sulk because the fallback table is keyed lowercase and the strategic path passes uppercase
findings.evidence: defiance.py: `if original_action in ("defend", "fortify", "hold", "wait", "retreat", "SUPPORT", "MOVE_TO"):` mixes lowercase tactical names and uppercase strategic names. strategic_executor.py:3963: `original_action = strategic_type  # e.g., "HOLD", "SUPPORT", "PURSUE"`, so HOLD arrives uppercase and misses the lowercase 'hold'. Direct call: aggressive {'HOLD': None, 'hold': 'attack', 'SUPPORT': 'attack', 'MOVE_TO': 'attack'}. End to end (calculate_defiance_chance forced to 1.0, STRONG concern, handle_objection_response('insist')): Ney SUPPORT -> defiance_action 'attack'; Ney HOLD -> defiance_action 'wait', outcome 'inconclusive'. tests/test_v2b_session1.py:192 pins only the lowercase 'hold'. V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC.md table row 93-95: 'Defying Defend/Fortify/Hold/Wait -> Aggressive: Attack nearest enemy'.
findings.repro: Scratch pytest importing tests.test_strategic_objections fixtures: monkeypatch defiance.calculate_defiance_chance -> 1.0 and strategic_executor.apply_mood_variance -> STRONG; Ney (Belgium, Wellington adjacent) 'hold' strategic order; executor.handle_objection_response('insist', gs). Prints (True, 'wait', 'inconclusive'). Direct: get_defiant_action(aggressive_marshal, 'HOLD') is None.
findings.expected: HOLD (uppercase, the strategic type) defers to attack nearest enemy for an aggressive marshal, as the spec table says and as the SUPPORT and MOVE_TO cells do.
findings.actual: The aggressive marshal sulks (inconclusive, no vindication, 3-turn cooldown). The HOLD row of the spec table is unreachable from the strategic path.

mechanism.evidence: defiance.py:134-135 reads `if original_action in ("defend", "fortify", "hold", "wait", "retreat", "SUPPORT", "MOVE_TO"):`. strategic_executor.py:3964-3968 reads `original_action = strategic_type  # e.g., "HOLD"...`, then `defiant_action = get_defiant_action(...)`, then `if defiant_action is None: defiant_action = "wait"`. The strategic type for a hold order is the uppercase "HOLD" (strategic_executor.py:958 `if strategic_type == "HOLD"`). So "HOLD" misses the lowercase "hold" entry, the function returns None, and the caller turns that into "wait". The tactical path, which passes lowercase, is unaffected. I did not run the repro; this is a hand trace. No BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md row covers it (grep for get_defiant_action found nothing relevant).
mechanism.note: The mechanism is real and the case-mix is a plain bug. Severity should be P3 rather than P2. It only affects an aggressive marshal who objects to a strategic HOLD and then defies, and defiance is capped at 40% chance. The result is a passive sulk (wait) instead of an attack, a mild fidelity gap against the V2B spec table, with no crash or state corruption. Sibling sweep: the cautious branch (defiance.py:144) lists only attack/SUPPORT/MOVE_TO and is not affected by the HOLD miss. PURSUE returning None for an aggressive marshal is intended (an aggressive marshal wouldn't object to attack). A fix would normalise the case, for example `original_action.lower()` with lowercase names in both tuples, or add "HOLD" to the tuple.

reproduction.evidence: backend/commands/defiance.py:134-135 has `if original_action in ("defend", "fortify", "hold", "wait", "retreat", "SUPPORT", "MOVE_TO"):`. backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:3964-3968 has `original_action = strategic_type  # e.g., "HOLD"...`, then `defiant_action = get_defiant_action(marshal, original_action)`, then `if defiant_action is None: defiant_action = "wait"`. Probe I ran in-process with an aggressive, non-artillery stub marshal: get_defiant_action for ('HOLD','hold','SUPPORT','PURSUE') returned [None, 'attack', 'attack', None]. So uppercase HOLD returns None and the strategic path then falls back to 'wait'. I did not re-run the end-to-end insist flow. I confirmed the direct call and both code sites by reading them.
reproduction.note: The case mismatch is real. The effect is narrow: a strategic-order defiance by an aggressive marshal ordered to HOLD becomes a sulk (inconclusive) instead of an attack, which contradicts the spec table row. Nothing crashes and no state is corrupted, so I rate it P3 rather than P2. PURSUE returning None is plausibly intended, since an aggressive marshal would not defy it. The fix is to normalize case, e.g. `original_action.lower()` against lowercase names, or to add "HOLD" to the tuple.

findings.title: A cautious marshal who insists-then-defies a PURSUE order sulks; PURSUE is in neither personality's fallback table
findings.evidence: Cautious Davout objects to PURSUE (probe: 'The odds are not in our favor'), yet get_defiant_action(cautious, 'PURSUE') and ('pursue') both return None. End to end with defiance forced to 1.0: Davout pursue Wellington -> (True, 'wait', 'inconclusive'), whereas Davout support/move_to -> 'fortify' (inconclusive, a deferred defensive vindication). The V2B spec table has columns for SUPPORT and MOVE_TO and none for PURSUE.
findings.repro: Same scratch pytest as COMBAT-2 with ('Davout','pursue','Wellington') and the fallback forced; or get_defiant_action(cautious_marshal, 'PURSUE') -> None.
findings.expected: Either PURSUE joins the table (cautious: fortify, the same counsel V1 offers on a PURSUE; aggressive: n/a), or the spec says a PURSUE defiance is deliberately a sulk. The spec is silent, so a ruling is needed.
findings.actual: The one strategic order a cautious marshal most often objects to has a defiance outcome that is always a wasted 1 AP, a 3-turn cooldown and no stakes.

mechanism.evidence:
The mechanism is real. backend/commands/defiance.py:142-146 reads `if personality == 'cautious': if original_action in ("attack", "SUPPORT", "MOVE_TO"): return "fortify"; return None`. PURSUE is not in that tuple. The aggressive branch (lines 134-135) also omits it, but an aggressive marshal does not object to PURSUE (spec line 638: aggressive no-intel PURSUE is only MILD).

The caller at backend/commands/strategic_executor.py:3964-3968 sets `original_action = strategic_type` ("HOLD", "SUPPORT", "PURSUE"). It then runs `defiant_action = get_defiant_action(...)` and `if defiant_action is None: defiant_action = "wait"`. A cautious PURSUE defiance therefore always becomes a sulk. It charges 1 AP through `world.spend_actions` and ends 'inconclusive' per `defiance_succeeded`'s `if defiance_action == "wait": return None`.

docs/V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC.md:89-101 gives the fallback table. Its columns are Defend/Fortify/Hold/Wait, Attack, Retreat, SUPPORT and MOVE_TO. There is no PURSUE column. Spec line 638 does say cautious PURSUE with no intel objects at STRONG, so the objection path exists but its defiance outcome is unspecified. Spec lines 696-697 repeat the table with no PURSUE.

A grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for pursue-and-defiance found no closed row or ruling covering this. The only hits were the unrelated ACH-1, ACH-F3 and S14E-D1 rows.

I did not run the end-to-end probe. I traced the code by hand instead, and it can produce the claimed behaviour.

This is a spec gap with a safe default, not a bug. Nothing crashes, and the sulk is a coded fallback for an unmapped order. The impact is a gameplay-quality gap: the PURSUE defiance is always a wasted action with no stakes, and the spec is silent. It needs a user ruling, as the finding says.
mechanism.note: Severity moves from P3 to design. The fallback table in V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC.md never listed PURSUE, and the code's None-then-wait path is an explicit, safe default. The ruling to ask for is whether cautious PURSUE defiance should map to fortify, as V1's counsel already does, or whether a sulk is deliberate. Any fix needs a spec table edit plus a defiance.py tuple change, so it falls under Golden Rule 9, and the siblings should be swept (the aggressive branch, and the HOLD and PURSUE columns).

reproduction.evidence: I ran an in-process probe against defiance.get_defiant_action with mock cautious and aggressive marshals. Output: cautious PURSUE -> None, pursue -> None, SUPPORT -> fortify, MOVE_TO -> fortify, attack -> fortify. Aggressive PURSUE -> None, SUPPORT -> attack, MOVE_TO -> attack. Source: backend/commands/defiance.py:144 reads `if original_action in ("attack", "SUPPORT", "MOVE_TO"): return "fortify"`, so PURSUE is missing from the cautious branch. The aggressive tuple at lines 134-135 also omits PURSUE. docs/V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC.md mentions PURSUE only for the fog-trigger objection (lines 321, 638, 790) and has no PURSUE fallback column. A grep of BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md found no row or ruling on a PURSUE defiance fallback. I did not run the end-to-end defiance-forced path (Davout -> wait / inconclusive), so I take that part on the reviewer's word. The missing table entry is enough to confirm the mechanism.
reproduction.note: The table gap is real, but it looks like an unspecified case with no recorded ruling, not a code defect. The code follows the V2B table as written. Nothing crashes: the outcome is an inconclusive sulk (wait), which defiance_succeeded already handles. P3 overstates it, so I rate it design. A user ruling is needed on whether PURSUE gets a cautious 'fortify' fallback or stays a deliberate sulk. Any fix should also decide whether the aggressive branch should cover PURSUE, which is moot because the aggressive marshal rarely objects to it.

findings.title: S15H-3's sibling: literal, loyalist and dove marshals' strategic-objection popups (V2 raised, V1 silent) are always built bare, with no Trust arm; loyalist, dove and sovereign can never defy
findings.evidence: strategic_executor.py:1993-1995: `preferred = (_get_aggressive_preferred(...) if ctx.marshal.personality == 'aggressive' else _get_cautious_preferred(...) if ctx.marshal.personality == 'cautious' and fallback_offers_his_counsel() else None)`. Probe (V1 forced silent, MODERATE concern, Davout re-labelled, PURSUE): aggressive ['proceed','preferred','compromise']; cautious [same]; literal, loyalist, dove ['proceed','compromise']. The scenario roster has 11 literal, 3 loyalist and 1 dove marshals, 15 in all. S15H-3's own commit text calls this 'a reading for the user, not taken'. get_defiant_action returns None for loyalist, dove, sovereign ('Unknown personality - no defiance').
findings.repro: Scratch pytest: monkeypatch strategic_executor.apply_mood_variance -> MODERATE and disobedience.check_strategic_objection -> None; set Davout.personality to 'literal'/'loyalist'/'dove'; execute strategic PURSUE Wellington; print the option types of result['objection']['options'].
findings.expected: A user ruling: either every personality that can raise a strategic popup gets a Trust arm, or the spec records that literal, loyalist and dove popups have no Trust arm by design.
findings.actual: Unruled. For these 15 marshals every strategic objection is Insist or Compromise only, with trust decided by no counsel. Their defiance is also structurally impossible, apart from literal's documented never-defies.

mechanism.evidence: I traced the code by hand and did not run the probe. strategic_executor.py:1992-1995 is the fallback site when V2 raises MODERATE or higher and V1 returns no options. It sets `preferred` to the aggressive chain for 'aggressive', to _get_cautious_preferred for 'cautious' (behind fallback_offers_his_counsel()), and to None for every other personality. _build_strategic_options then builds only the Proceed and Compromise options when `preferred` is None, so literal, loyalist and dove marshals get no Trust arm in this fallback. defiance.py:126-148 get_defiant_action returns None for 'literal', and for every personality that is not 'aggressive' or 'cautious' it falls through to the comment "Unknown personality — no defiance". So loyalist, dove and sovereign can never defy. The docs grep found no spec or ruling that sets this by design. CLAUDE.md has no such rule, and the only loyalist hit is a Voice Bible character description. The S15H-3 commit text itself calls this a reading for the user that was not taken. The behaviour exists, but it is not a regression or a crash.
mechanism.note: This is an unruled design question, not a defect. A personality with no preferred-alternative counsel gets no Trust arm in the V2-raised, V1-silent fallback, and non-aggressive/non-cautious personalities have no defiance mapping. Literal's never-defies is documented. Recommendation: have the user record a ruling in OBJECTION_V2 or V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC (a Trust arm for every personality, or none by design for these three). P3 at most if the user wants parity; not a bug on the pre-deploy gate.

reproduction.evidence: I ran a scratch pytest. It reused TestTheFallbackKeepsHisCounsel._force_the_fallback (apply_mood_variance forced to MODERATE, check_strategic_objection forced to None) and sent Davout "pursue Wellington" with his personality set in turn. I deleted the file afterwards, and git status shows no test changes. Option types in the objection popup: aggressive ['proceed','preferred','compromise']; cautious ['proceed','preferred','compromise']; literal ['proceed','compromise']; loyalist ['proceed','compromise']; dove ['proceed','compromise']. The code is strategic_executor.py:1993-1995 as quoted: only 'aggressive' and 'cautious' get a preferred option, and every other personality gets None. Literal never defying is documented in V2B_DEFIANCE_SPEC.md:97 and SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:760. My grep found no doc line saying loyalist, dove or sovereign popups have no Trust arm by design, or that they cannot defy. I did not check get_defiant_action itself.
reproduction.note: The behaviour reproduces. It only happens on the V1-silent fallback path, which is rare (about 1 in 12 PARTIAL-sight rolls). Nothing crashes, and the player still gets Proceed and Compromise. It is a missing ruling on whether these personalities should have a Trust arm, not a defect. The S15H-3 commit text already calls it 'a reading for the user, not taken'. P3 is generous, so I rate it design: either record 'no Trust arm for literal, loyalist and dove' in the spec, or have the user rule on adding one.

findings.title: Precision Execution's '+1 to all skills, capped at 8' lowers a skill of 9 or 10 to 8 (Soult's tactical 9 becomes 8 while he is 'buffed')
findings.evidence: Code: `if self.precision_execution_active: base = min(8, base + 1)`. Probe: Marshal literal with tactical 9, shock 6: get_effective_skill('tactical') = 9 off, 8 with precision_execution_active=True; shock 6 -> 7. The Europe boot has one literal marshal above 7: Soult, tactical 9. The next line's docstring for the crown says it 'never reduces a skill', so Precision's clamp is inconsistent with it. meta_executor.py:803 sets the flag for ambiguity <= 20 and strategic_score > 60 (crisp orders), which is exactly when the player is rewarded.
findings.repro: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 scratchpad/p6.py -> prints 9 then '8 7'.
findings.expected: max(base, min(8, base+1)), so the buff never reduces a skill.
findings.actual: The reward for crisp orders is a -1 tactical (dice bonus and roll) for the roster's best literal tactician.

mechanism.evidence: backend/models/marshal.py:1670-1671: `if self.precision_execution_active: base = min(8, base + 1)`. A skill of 9 or 10 therefore becomes 8. The docstring at 1663-1666 says only the crown "never reduces a skill", and the crown's own line is `min(10, base + 1)`. Soult is a literal marshal with tactical 9 (godot-client/project-sovereign/assets/maps/europe_1805.json:175-176). The buff is applied only to literal marshals (executor.py:3087, `personality == 'literal'`) and is set by meta_executor.py:803 when ambiguity <= 20 and strategic_score > 60. combat.py:269 reads `marshal.get_effective_skill('tactical')`, so the lowered value reaches combat. Reading the code by hand, Soult's tactical drops 9 -> 8 while the buff is active. I did not run the probe. No BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row covers this. MC-V-1 only accepts that the buff is player-only. JEALOUSY_SPEC rejects a penalty design, which fits the claim that a stat cut is unintended.
mechanism.note: The bug is real but narrow. The only live case is Soult's tactical 9, plus any other literal marshal with a skill of 9 or higher. Fix: `base = max(base, min(8, base + 1))`. The "capped at 8" wording looks like a deliberate ceiling on the buff, and the unintended part is that it also lowers skills already above 8. The finding is a sibling of the class the crown line already guards against.

reproduction.evidence: backend/models/marshal.py:1670-1671 reads `if self.precision_execution_active: base = min(8, base + 1)`. I ran an in-process probe, Marshal("Soult", ..., skills={"tactical":9,"shock":6}). It printed 9 with the flag off, then "8 7" with precision_execution_active=True. The flag is set at meta_executor.py:803 (`if ambiguity <= 20 and strategic_score > 60`). combat.py:269 reads get_effective_skill('tactical'), so the lowered value reaches combat. grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for precision_execution found no closed row and no ruling. The docstring's claim that the crown 'never reduces a skill' is not true of the Precision clamp before it.
reproduction.note: Real but minor. Skills of 9 or 10 lose 1 point for the 3 turns after a crisp order. Soult's tactical 9 is the only affected Europe-boot marshal, as far as I checked. I did not confirm Soult's personality, so I did not check that the +1 applies to him in play. The fix is the one-liner `base = max(base, min(8, base + 1))`.

findings.title: The Grouchy ambiguity buff (strategic_combat_bonus and strategic_defense_bonus, +5 to +15%) has no expiry and survives a rout, so crisp 'fortify' or 'defend' orders bank an attack bonus for a later battle
findings.evidence: meta_executor.py:796-799: `if bonus > 0 and action in COMBAT_ACTIONS: marshal.strategic_combat_bonus = bonus; marshal.strategic_defense_bonus = bonus`, where COMBAT_ACTIONS = attack, charge, defend, fortify. Both fields are consumed only by get_attack_modifier and get_defense_modifier (marshal.py:1345-1349 and 1487-1491). grep across backend/ found no per-turn decay, and clear_combat_transient_state (marshal.py:~884-900) does not include them. The docs call them 'one-shot' bonuses consumed in combat (SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:366, 1552-1553). MC-V-1 accepted the buff as a parser economy, but not its persistence.
findings.repro: Static: grep -rn 'strategic_combat_bonus' backend (no decay or clear outside the two consume sites). Dynamic probe not run.
findings.expected: Either a turn expiry (as Iron Resolve's anti-banking rule at marshal.py:1366-1369 intends: 'no banking'), or a recorded ruling that the buff waits for the next battle.
findings.actual: A literal marshal ordered 'fortify' crisply keeps +15% attack until his next attack, however many turns later, and keeps it through a rout.

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism traced by hand. meta_executor.py:796-799 sets `marshal.strategic_combat_bonus = bonus` and `marshal.strategic_defense_bonus = bonus` for any action in ["attack","charge","defend","fortify"]. A grep of backend/ for both field names finds these writers and readers only. The writers are meta_executor.py:798-799 and feedback.py:159 (the same bonus for inspiring commands). The readers are marshal.py:1345-1349 (`if consume: self.strategic_combat_bonus = 0`) and marshal.py:1487-1491 (the defense twin), plus the battle_report snapshots and serialization. No per-turn decay exists. `clear_combat_transient_state` (marshal.py:874-899) lists drilling, shock_bonus, fortified, defense_bonus, stance and the like, but not these two fields. So a crisp "fortify" or "defend" order banks the attack bonus, which is consumed only on the marshal's next attack call. Being attacked consumes only the defense twin. Because the clear function omits the fields, a rout leaves them standing. The docs call the bonus one-shot, consumed in combat (SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:366, 1552). MC-V-1 (MARSHAL_CONTENT_PASS_SPEC.md:185) accepts the buff only as a player-phrasing economy and says nothing about expiry. I found no recorded ruling that it should persist.
mechanism.note: The behaviour is real, but the stakes are low. The bonus is small (5-15%), it applies only to literal marshals on crisp orders, and it is consumed by the next battle. It is a design and consistency gap, not a crash or state corruption. The persistence-through-rout claim holds because the fields are missing from clear_combat_transient_state. A fix would be a turn expiry or adding both fields to the clear function. That is a user decision, since MC-V-1 left the question open. The finding did not run a dynamic probe, and neither did I; this verdict rests on the code trace.

reproduction.evidence:
I ran the finding's own static repro: a grep for strategic_combat_bonus and strategic_defense_bonus across backend/. I did not run a dynamic probe, and a grep can only show that no clearing code exists, not that none runs. Writers: meta_executor.py:798-799 sets both fields (`marshal.strategic_combat_bonus = bonus` / `marshal.strategic_defense_bonus = bonus`) when `bonus > 0 and action in COMBAT_ACTIONS`. COMBAT_ACTIONS is ["attack","charge","defend","fortify"] at line 785. ai/feedback.py:159 also writes strategic_combat_bonus. Consumers: marshal.py:1345-1349 and 1487-1491, each guarded by `if consume:`. Other references are battle_report.py snapshots, serialization (marshal.py:1935-1936 and 2156-2157) and docs. The grep shows no per-turn decay or clearing of either field, so a buff set by a crisp "fortify" or "defend" order stays until a later attack or defense consumes it. The attack bonus is consumed by the next attack. The defense bonus is consumed when the marshal is next attacked. A rout does not clear either field.

Prior rows: MC-V-1 (BUG_FIXES_2026_Q3.md:10821, MARSHAL_CONTENT_PASS_SPEC.md:185) accepted the buff as a player-only parser economy. It does not rule on persistence. The docs describe the bonus as "one-shot ... consumed in combat" (SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:366, 1552). The code does that. It never says the bonus expires, so the "consumed on use, no expiry" reading is consistent with the docs. This is a design question, not a bug.
reproduction.note: The mechanical claim is true: the buff has no expiry and no rout clear. It also has no player-facing harm. The buff is bounded at +5 to +15%, and a new crisp order overwrites it rather than stacking. It is a banked buff that fits the "consumed on use" wording in the docs. If the user wants "no banking", the fix is a one-turn expiry like the Iron Resolve rule at marshal.py:1366-1369. No ruling on this exists, so it should be filed as a design question, not a P3 defect.

findings.title: Rule 1 residue: combat.py re-derives the recklessness share to rescale it by terrain, and the coordination magnitudes are authored in combat_executor.py
findings.evidence: combat.py:~583-591: `recklessness_bonus = attacker._get_recklessness_attack_bonus() ... original_contribution = 1.0 + recklessness_bonus; scaled_contribution = 1.0 + (recklessness_bonus * terrain_cav_mult); shock_multiplier *= scaled/original`. This re-derives a marshal.py term inside the resolver, and the battle report must then match it. combat_executor.py:1928 `adjacent_atk = adj_count * 0.02`; 2005-2010 `dedicated_atk = 0.05`, `capped_atk = min(raw_atk, 0.25)`, `capped_def = min(raw_def, 0.20)`: the magnitudes that marshal.py:1417 multiplies in are authored in the executor and only stamped on the marshal. The x1.30, x0.60, x1.50 and x2 terms are covered by TACTICAL_TRIANGLE_SPEC as target-type interactions. Nothing is wrong numerically today. This is the next place a change would have to be made in two files.
findings.repro: Read combat.py:575-625 and combat_executor.py:1928-2010.
findings.expected: Terrain-scaled recklessness lives in marshal.py (get_attack_modifier(terrain=...)), and the coordination constants sit beside the other tunables on Marshal.
findings.actual: Two files hold the arithmetic that CLAUDE.md Golden Rule 1 assigns to one.

mechanism.evidence: The cited code is as described. backend/game_logic/combat.py:583-591 reads `attacker._get_recklessness_attack_bonus()` (defined at marshal.py:1110). It computes `scaled_contribution / original_contribution` and multiplies the result into `shock_multiplier`. marshal.py:1361-1363 already applies `modifier *= (1.0 + recklessness_bonus)` inside get_attack_modifier, so combat.py divides that term back out and re-applies a terrain-scaled version. This is a re-derivation outside marshal.py. battle_report.py:139 repeats the terrain scaling, so the report has to stay in step with it. SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md:2414 documents this as intended ("combat.py ... TERRAIN_CAVALRY_EFFECTIVENESS to scale recklessness attack bonus"). I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row that rules on it, and I did not search them beyond the grep. The coordination constants at combat_executor.py:1928 and 2005-2010 were not opened beyond the lines the finding quotes. Grep for the terrain-scaling symbols found no row closing this symptom. The finding says nothing is numerically wrong today, and I did not test that.
mechanism.note: The result is correct and the split is documented, so this is a Rule 1 maintainability residue rather than a defect. It is a design-level cleanup candidate: pass terrain into get_attack_modifier, and move the coordination constants onto Marshal. Calling it P3 would also be defensible. Only the terrain-scaled recklessness part is a literal recalculation in combat.py. The combat_executor.py constants only stamp values onto the marshal, which is a weaker complaint.

reproduction.evidence: I read the code and ran nothing else. combat.py:580-591 has `recklessness_bonus = attacker._get_recklessness_attack_bonus()`, then `original_contribution = 1.0 + recklessness_bonus`, `scaled_contribution = 1.0 + recklessness_bonus*terrain_cav_mult`, then `shock_multiplier *= scaled/original`. That re-derives a term that marshal.py already builds at marshal.py:1361 inside get_attack_modifier. combat_executor.py:1928 has `adjacent_atk = adj_count * 0.02`. Lines 1985, 1993 and 1994 have `dedicated_atk = 0.05`, `capped_atk = min(raw_atk, 0.25)` and `capped_def = min(raw_def, 0.20)`. Lines 1996-1997 stamp those onto `m.total_coordination_attack_bonus` and `m.total_coordination_defense_bonus`, and marshal.py:1415 multiplies the attack stamp in. The magnitudes are therefore authored in the executor and the application is in marshal.py. Neither BUG_FIXES.md nor DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md has a row or ruling for this (grep for COMBAT-7 and terrain_cavalry_adjustment returned nothing). The finding itself says nothing is numerically wrong today.
reproduction.note: The facts are accurate, but this is a maintainability and Golden Rule 1 purity item. It produces no wrong output.
