The terrain-scaled recklessness piece is a real, if mild, second site for arithmetic that belongs to marshal.py. The coordination constants are plausibly intentional, since the executor computes the coordination context and only stamps it on the marshal. Treat the whole finding as a P3-or-lower design cleanup. If it is kept, CLAUDE.md Rule 9 requires a named owner row and test.

findings.title: AI chest forecast runs the whole ledger economy builder (two full-map region scans plus display rows) per nation, several times a turn
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/ledger.py:1084 chest_forecast -> ledger.py:1104 _build_economy (scans at ledger.py:1351 and 1364); callers reforms.py:955 lapse_forecast / reforms.py:1282 ai_holds_the_purse, affairs.py:2010 find_ai_edict, war_council._restraint_block_reason
findings.evidence: cProfile of turns 1-24, seed historical, LLM_MODE=mock: _build_economy 339 calls (14 a turn), cumulative 1.126 s of 6.16 s total (18%). Turns 30-35: chest_forecast 80 calls, 0.292 s of 1.46 s (20%); _build_economy 95 calls, 0.347 s. Code: ledger.py:1351 'for region in world.regions.values():' builds construction_queue and ledger.py:1364 'for region in world.regions.values():' builds income_breakdown, both only to emit display rows. chest_forecast reads just the 'net' key (ledger.py:1096: net = int(_build_economy(world, nation).get('net', 0) or 0)). Each call also builds _levy_block (get_levy_status 95 calls, 0.101 s). Both loops filter on controller == player, so get_nation_regions would serve them.
findings.repro: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <scratch>: build the world as in tools/ai_v_sweep.py run_one, cProfile 24 end_turns, print entries for ledger.py:1104 _build_economy. Scratch: C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/1bd395101ae53e89/c93e5074-9889-43d4-af44-edb3471fff40/scratchpad/prof25.py
findings.expected: A per-nation-per-turn AI read of the chest after income should be one cached scalar, or a net-only path. Rule 8 says use get_nation_regions and cache per turn.
findings.actual: Each forecast rebuilds the full economy tab payload, with two O(all regions) scans per call and about 14 calls a turn. This is the single largest identifiable AI-phase cost, and it grows with the 1805 region count and nation count.

mechanism.evidence: The seam matches the finding. ledger.py:1084 chest_forecast reads only the net: `net = int(_build_economy(world, nation).get("net", 0) or 0)`. That call builds the whole economy tab payload. _build_economy contains two `for region in world.regions.values():` loops at ~1351 (construction_queue) and ~1364 (income_breakdown). Both filter on `region.controller != player` and exist only to emit display rows. The payload also calls `_levy_block(world, player)` at ~1471. WorldState.get_nation_regions (world_state.py:4637) is a per-turn cached lookup that would serve both loops. The call sites are real and AI-side: affairs.py:672 and :1590, reforms.py:970, war_council.py:639 and :742. main.py:687 is the player's own call. Neither docs/BUG_FIXES.md nor docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md has a row for this. The closed rows SFR-D23 and DDB-13 are about the forecast's correctness and mention no cost. I did not rerun the profile, so the 14 calls a turn and the 18% share are the reviewer's numbers. I did not check whether _build_economy has other costly scans besides the two cited.
mechanism.note: The Golden Rule 8 violation is real. A scalar-only call pays for display rows and runs two full-region scans. The measured cost is about 47 ms a turn on the current map (1.1 s over 24 turns) and has not caused a failure. That makes it a scale-readiness cleanup, so P3 rather than P2. The fix is small: add a net-only path, or build the display rows lazily, and read the nation's regions through get_nation_regions.

reproduction.evidence: I ran the reviewer's scratch profile, prof25.py, unchanged: 24 end_turns, seed historical, LLM_MODE=mock, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. The ledger.py:1104 `_build_economy` line printed 339 calls with 1.364 s cumulative, against 7.67 s total tottime. That is about 14 calls a turn and roughly 18%, which matches the finding. Code read at ledger.py:1084-1100: `chest_forecast` calls `_build_economy(world, nation)` and keeps only `.get("net")`. At ledger.py:1351 and 1364, `for region in world.regions.values(): if region.controller != player: continue` builds the construction_queue and income_breakdown display rows. Rule 8 in CLAUDE.md prefers `get_nation_regions` for this. I grepped BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for chest_forecast and SCALE-1. The hits are SFR-D23, DDB-13 and S14E-X189, all correctness fixes that made `chest_forecast` the single source. None is a performance row, and no ruling excuses the cost. I did not re-measure the per-callee breakdown (the reviewer's 0.292 s of 1.46 s figure for turns 30-35).
reproduction.note: The cost is real and reproducible, and it is a Rule 8 breach in spirit. It is a performance issue that costs about 0.3 s of a roughly 7 s, 24-turn run, with no wrong output, so I rate it P3. The reviewer's P2 holds only if a scale target is known to be missed. The fix is small. Give `chest_forecast` a net-only path, or per-turn caching, so the two display-row scans and `_levy_block` are skipped. I did not measure how much of the 1.36 s is the two region scans versus the rest of the builder, so the reviewer's 'two full-map scans' framing is plausible but not isolated.

findings.title: Law and edict effect reads rebuild the affairs deck on every call, including once per region in the supply cap
findings.seam: backend/game_logic/reforms.py:136 effect_terms -> affairs.py:1861 edicts_in_force (loops deck(world)) -> moments.py:252 affairs_deck (list comprehension calling affairs.py:177 entry_armed per entry); consumer world_state.py:8901 _supply_multiplier -> reforms.py:261 supply_capacity_factor
findings.evidence: 24-turn profile: affairs_deck 12,226 calls (0.293 s cum), edicts_in_force 10,016 calls (0.404 s cum, 6.6% of total), entry_armed 35,340 calls per 6 turns. In turns 30-35, get_effective_supply_cap ran 668 times (0.133 s) because the multiplier calls supply_capacity_terms, effect_terms and edicts_in_force once per region. moments.py:252-254: 'return [e for e in (affairs_block(world).get("deck") or []) if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("id") and entry_armed(e)]'. The store block is static after boot and only the armed set changes.
findings.repro: Same profile as SCALE-1; print entries matching affairs_deck / edicts_in_force. Count of get_effective_supply_cap callers: _supply_pressure_move 487 calls per 6 turns.
findings.expected: A per-region or per-marshal read should hit a per-turn-cached terms table for the nation (the get_active_nations pattern).
findings.actual: O(deck) work is repeated per region per call, about 500 deck builds a turn. The cost multiplies with region count and nation count at full 1805 scale.

mechanism.evidence: I traced the path by hand and did not run the profile, so the call counts and timings are the reviewer's, not mine. The code path matches the claim. world_state.py:8925-8932 `_supply_multiplier` calls `reforms.supply_capacity_factor` whenever `self.reforms` is set. That calls `supply_capacity_terms`, then `_terms` (reforms.py:203), then `effect_terms` (reforms.py:136). `effect_terms` calls `affairs.edicts_in_force` (reforms.py:152). `edicts_in_force` (affairs.py:1861-1874) returns early only when the edicts store is empty or there is no lord. Otherwise it loops `deck(world)`, and `deck` (affairs.py:233) is `MO.affairs_deck`. That function (moments.py:252-260) rebuilds the list on every call, running `entry_armed(e)` (affairs.py:177) once per entry. `entry_armed` goes through `row_armed`, which is a chain of string compares plus a call to a `standing.*_armed()` function. No cache exists anywhere on the chain. Because `get_effective_supply_cap` calls `_supply_multiplier` per region, the full deck rebuild repeats per region and per marshal read, as the finding says. The cost is real but small (the reviewer measured 6.6% of a 24-turn profile).
mechanism.note: I found no SCALE-1 or SCALE-2 row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md, and no ruling that accepts this cost. The finding is a performance defect, not a correctness one: results are identical, only repeated work. The reviewer's own profile puts it at 6.6% of total time, so P3 is right. It does fall under CLAUDE.md Golden Rule 8 (no repeated per-region work in hot paths). Likely fixes: memoize `affairs_deck` per world, since the block is static after boot and the armed set only changes with the standing seams. Or cache the nation's `effect_terms` per turn, as `get_active_nations` does.

reproduction.evidence: I ran a read-only in-process probe. It booted WorldState.from_scenario(europe_1805.json), which gave 126 regions with world.reforms truthy. It wrapped affairs.edicts_in_force and moments.affairs_deck with counters, then called get_effective_supply_cap(player, region) once for each of the 126 regions. Output: "regions 126 time 0.0069 {'deck': 0, 'edicts': 126}". So the per-region path does call edicts_in_force once per region, through the chain world_state.py:8931 supply_capacity_factor -> reforms.py supply_capacity_terms -> effect_terms -> affairs.edicts_in_force. Nothing is cached per turn. The code matches the finding: affairs.py:1870 `for e in deck(world)` runs after the early return at line 1865 (`if not store or not lord: return []`), and moments.py:252-254 rebuilds the list with entry_armed per entry. In my fresh boot the edicts store is empty, so affairs_deck was never reached (0 calls) and the whole sweep cost only 7 ms. The deck rebuild only happens in a mid-campaign world where edicts have been decreed. I did not reproduce the reviewer's 12,226 affairs_deck calls or the 0.404 s figure. The per-region call pattern is confirmed. The size of the cost in a live game rests on the reviewer's profile. I found no closed row for this in BUG_FIXES.md (grep for SCALE-2 and affairs_deck returned nothing).
reproduction.note: Real but minor performance debt. The edict read does O(deck) work per region once any edict exists, but the deck is small. Measured cost is under 7% of a turn in the reviewer's profile, and about 0.05 ms per region on a fresh board with no edicts. It matters only for scale (CLAUDE.md Golden Rule 8) and is a cheap fix: cache the per-nation terms per turn, or hoist supply_capacity_factor out of the per-region loop. Kind is defect (scale hygiene), not a correctness bug.

findings.title: Every /command and GET /status response re-sends the full 126-province map_data (about 165 KB of a 175-190 KB body)
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:11678 get_game_state_summary (map_data built at 11995 for all self.regions) via main.py build_base_response / GET /status
findings.evidence: /command 'status' at T1: 192,295 bytes, of which game_state 181,045 and game_state.map_data 165,607 (naval_overlay 12,976, active_wars 8,811). GET /status 202,127 bytes. Warm status command 48 ms of which get_game_state_summary alone is 18.9 ms plus json.dumps 1.3 ms. Bodies measured at T40: /status 173 KB, 'economy' cmd 178 KB, 'Ney, attack Mack' 177 KB. The payload is about 1.3 KB per province per response, so it scales linearly with the map, and every typed command, even a refusal, pays it.
findings.repro: curl-equivalent in-process: TestClient(backend.main.app).post('/command', json={'command':'status'}); print len(content) and sorted key sizes of ['game_state'] (scratch keys.py in the scratchpad dir).
findings.expected: Rule 8 and the scale plan: the whole-map block ships when it changed (turn start, a capture, a move) or on request; a no-op command returns a delta or a version stamp.
findings.actual: The full block is rebuilt and shipped on every response. At 126 provinces about 175 KB each, which is tolerable on localhost, but a full-1805 map would multiply it several times.

mechanism.evidence: Mechanism is real by code reading. backend/models/world_state.py:11995 puts `"map_data": map_data` into get_game_state_summary, and the dict is built by a loop over all regions (line 11885, `map_data[region_name] = {`). get_filtered_game_state_summary (around line 12165) calls get_game_state_summary() again and then loops `summary["map_data"].items()` at line 12186. The Godot client consumes the block: main.gd, region_panel.gd and map_renderer_base.gd all reference map_data. I did not reproduce the byte counts or timings. I found no BUG_FIXES or DESIGN_REFINEMENT row and no spec ruling that covers this payload. The only "map_data" hit in docs is the DESIGN_REFINEMENT S14E-D10 row, which is about map tinting. I found no mechanism for sending a delta or a version stamp.
mechanism.note: The finding is the Rule 8 class (a per-region scan on every response), but it is a design and scale concern, not a correctness defect. Cost is linear in provinces. The filtering pass costs about 19 ms per response at 126 provinces, and 175 KB on localhost is harmless. Nothing is broken today, so P2 overstates it and I rate it design. Fixing it means changing the client contract (delta or versioned map_data), which needs a named owner row under Golden Rule 9, not a patch. I could not trace Godot's handling in detail, so I do not know whether it can tolerate an absent map_data.

reproduction.evidence: I ran a TestClient probe in-process (scratchpad keys.py, with PYTHONPATH=.). POST /command 'status' returned 177,654 bytes. game_state was 181,045 bytes when re-serialised, the same figure the finding gives. game_state.map_data was 165,607 bytes, which matches the finding exactly, and naval_overlay was 12,976, also exact. GET /status returned 186,648 bytes against the finding's 202,127, which is within run-to-run variation. A grep of docs/BUG_FIXES.md and docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md for SCALE-3 or a map_data delta/version-stamp ruling found only the S14E-D10 camp-tint row. That row adds to map_data and does not slim it, so no closed row or ruling covers this.
reproduction.note: The numbers reproduce. The payload is a whole-map block rebuilt on every response, which is a scale and efficiency concern and not a correctness bug. I did not time the 18.9 ms summary build or test a delta mechanism. P3 or design is the honest rating on localhost at 126 provinces. It matters only if the map grows to the full 1805 Europe.

findings.title: war_instances[*].offer_history is an unbounded append, one entry a turn per live dictated-peace war
findings.evidence: 120-turn in-process run (historical): world.to_dict()['war_instances'] = 2,957 B (n=1) at T1, 7,103 B (n=2) at T40, 12,359 at T60, 17,659 at T80, 22,960 at T100, 28,280 at T120 with the war count flat at 2. war_1.offer_history has 89 entries, 23,456 B, about 263 B each (Britain to France, 'Chatillon', outcome 'sent', once per turn). No trim: ai_diplomacy.py:1510 appends, and the readers at 1262-1267, 1521 and 1542 only need the recent dictated letters and the refused count. The source of the growth is real; the run needed a reset of the terminal ending (see notes).
findings.repro: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -X utf8 <scratch growth.py> (120 end_turns, snapshot world.to_dict() sizes at 1/20/40/60/80/100/120). Scratch growth.py in the scratchpad dir.
findings.expected: Per-war history is capped like event_log (500) and command_history (50).
findings.actual: Linear growth, about 265 B per turn per war. It is harmless in a 40-turn campaign but unbounded in a long one, and it is rewritten into every autosave.

mechanism.evidence:
I confirmed the mechanism by reading the code. I did not re-run the 120-turn growth script.

- `backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:1510` reads `instance.setdefault("offer_history", []).append(entry)`. This is the only append site.
- It is called from `record_dictated_offer` at lines 3097 (bilateral `harsh_peace`) and 6508 (settlement offer where the player's war score is at or below -decisive). Neither site trims or caps the list.
- `note_dictated_refusal` (1521) only mutates an entry's outcome, and the readers at 1267, 1542 and 1521 only scan the list.
- `dictated_ratchet` (1276) counts only refused or lapsed entries and caps the result at `DICTATED_RATCHET_CAP = 2` (line 1212). Trimming to recent entries would therefore not change behaviour.
- `settlement_helpers.py:1812-1817` merges instances by concatenating `offer_history`, so merges also do not shrink it.
- A grep of BUG_FIXES.md and DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md found no closed row or ruling about trimming this list. The only related row is OCT27-29, which fixed the merge dropping the list.

The growth is real: one entry per dictated letter per live war, linear in turns. The reviewer's figure of about 263 B per entry is plausible for the entry's fields. The list lives on the war instance dict, which is serialized (docs and line 1198 say so), so it is rewritten into every autosave.
mechanism.note: Real but low impact. The growth is bounded by war length and only occurs while a dictated-peace letter is re-sent each turn. A 40-turn campaign adds about 10 KB. The fix is to keep only the last N entries, say 10-20, after the append at line 1510. This is safe because the ratchet cap is 2 and refused_peace_standing only looks at a short memory window. Merge and serialization pins would need a quick check.

reproduction.evidence: I did not re-run the 120-turn growth script. I confirmed the mechanism by reading the source. backend/game_logic/ai_diplomacy.py:1510 is `instance.setdefault("offer_history", []).append(entry)` in record_dictated_offer, and the entry is a ~260 B dict. It has no cap or trim. grep over backend/ finds no other writer that trims it. The only other writers are settlement_helpers.py:1812-1817, which concatenates histories when two war instances merge, and settlement_helpers.py:1853, which is a comment. The readers at ai_diplomacy.py:1267, 1276, 1521 and 1542 only walk the list. The history is stored on the war instance dict, so it is serialized with it (comment at ai_diplomacy.py:1198). docs/BUG_FIXES.md has one offer_history row, OCT27-29, which fixed the merge to concatenate. It does not cover growth, so the unbounded append is not a closed or ruled item. The finding's measured figures (about 263 B per entry, 89 entries, about 23 KB) are consistent with the entry shape in the code. The growth only occurs while a war stays live and dictated letters keep going out.
reproduction.note: The append is real and unbounded, but the impact is small: about 10 KB per war over a 40-turn campaign, growing only while a war stays open. If a cap is added, the "refused count" reader at ai_diplomacy.py:1276 would need either a stored running counter or a window large enough to hold the refusals it counts. The finding's cap suggestion does not mention this. This is a latent scale and save-size issue, not a correctness bug.

findings.title: The API summary scans every marshal once per province and every refresh rebuilds the whole marshal index
findings.seam: backend/models/world_state.py:11696-11697 (get_game_state_summary: for region_name in self.regions -> self.get_marshals_in_region(region_name), linear, documented at world_state.py:4902-4912) and world_state.py:4818 _build_marshal_index via refresh_marshal_indexes (enemy_ai.py:517,536,558,938,957,1447)
findings.evidence: get_marshals_in_region docstring: 'Uses linear scan for correctness... Internal hot paths use _get_marshals_in_region_indexed() instead.' get_game_state_summary calls it 126 times a response, about 126 x 35 comparisons. Profile 24 turns: _build_marshal_index 5,078 calls, 0.119 s cum (212 rebuilds a turn, each O(marshals) plus resets the live-visibility cache world_state.py:4831). The player-marshal relationships block at world_state.py:11853-11860 loops all marshals per player marshal.
findings.repro: Same 24-turn profile; print _build_marshal_index and get_marshals_in_region callers (get_marshals_in_region 2,288 calls).
findings.expected: Per-response and per-action paths use the indexed lookup or a one-pass bucket, as Rule 8 describes.
findings.actual: O(regions x marshals) per API response and O(actions x marshals) per AI turn. It is small at 126 x 35 (about 0.4 ms and 5 ms a turn), but it is quadratic in the 1805 roster, and each rebuild also drops the live-visibility cache that exists to avoid scans.

mechanism.evidence:
The code matches the finding. I read these in backend/models/world_state.py without running the profile.
- get_marshals_in_region (line 4902) is a linear scan: `for marshal in self.marshals.values() if marshal.location == region_name`. Its docstring says it is kept linear on purpose so tests that edit marshals without rebuilding the index stay correct.
- get_game_state_summary calls it once per region at line 11698: `marshals_here = self.get_marshals_in_region(region_name)`. That is about 126 x 35 = 4.4k comparisons per response, as claimed.
- _build_marshal_index (line 4818) is O(marshals). It also resets `_live_visible_regions_cache` (lines 4830-4831). The cache is already keyed by turn, so the reset costs a recompute of at most one set per nation.
- I did not re-run the 24-turn profile, so the call counts (5,078 rebuilds, 2,288 scans) are the reviewer's. They are consistent with the code.
- I did not find a SCALE-5 row or a matching closed row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md.
mechanism.note: The mechanism is real but the severity is overstated. The summary loop is per-region by nature, and the scan inside it is O(marshals). The reviewer's own figures are about 0.4 ms per response and 5 ms per turn. The roster is not growing the way regions are: the 1805 roster is already loaded, and the 126 regions are already at full scale. The "quadratic in the 1805 roster" claim is therefore speculative. Rule 8 targets per-region scans over `world.regions.values()` in hot paths called many times per turn. The summary is called once per response, so it is not clearly a Rule 8 violation. The cache reset is cheap because the cache is already turn-keyed. If anyone cleans this up, the fix is a one-pass bucket by location at the top of the summary. It is not a defect.

reproduction.evidence: Code is as described. world_state.py:11696-11698 loops `for region_name, region in self.regions.items()` and calls `self.get_marshals_in_region(region_name)`. world_state.py:4902-4908 documents it as a linear scan. `_build_marshal_index` (4818-4832) rebuilds the whole index and also resets `_live_visible_regions_cache` (4831-4832). I loaded the 1805 scenario with `WorldState.from_scenario` and profiled one `get_game_state_summary()` call: 126 regions, 281 `get_marshals_in_region` calls at 0.001 s cumulative. The summary as a whole took about 27 ms per call (0.070 s under cProfile). Most of that is `_region_recruit_block`, `recruit_quote` and `doctrines.supply_ground` at about 0.02 s, so the marshal scan is a minor share. One `refresh_marshal_indexes()` call took 0.0028 ms. I did not re-run the 24-turn profile. No SCALE-5 row exists in docs/BUG_FIXES.md.
reproduction.note: The pattern is real, but the measured cost is negligible: about 1 ms of a roughly 27 ms summary, and a rebuild costs microseconds. It is a scale-readiness nit against Rule 8, not a current defect. It is only worth fixing if the roster grows a lot, for example with a single-pass bucket in `get_game_state_summary`. The finding's cache-reset point is a design observation I did not measure.

findings.title: Combat pricing and income code rescan all marshals per call (O(M) inside per-candidate and per-region loops)
findings.seam: backend/commands/combat_executor.py:2512 _priced_coordination (touched = [m for m in world.marshals.values() if m.nation in nations], line about 2556) and world_state.py:7466 get_disrupted_regions (one pass over world.marshals, uncached by design)
findings.evidence: 24-turn profile: _priced_coordination 4,332 calls, tottime 0.167 s, cum 0.664 s (11%), called per AI candidate target inside _evaluate_marshal (1,564 calls, cum 1.947 s, 32% of all time). get_disrupted_regions 4,157 calls (173 a turn), 0.161 s cum, called from calculate_turn_income/upkeep and the dotation, vassal and dispatch readers. The docstring says 'recomputed per call so mid-turn movement is reflected'.
findings.repro: Same profile; rows for combat_executor.py:2512 and world_state.py:7466.
findings.expected: A per-turn memo keyed on a marshal-movement stamp, or a nation-indexed marshal list (get_marshals_by_nation).
findings.actual: Per-candidate times per-marshal times O(M) work. Today it totals about 50 ms of a 90 ms turn; the cost grows roughly with the square of the roster at 1805 scale.

mechanism.evidence: The mechanism is real. combat_executor.py `_priced_coordination` (~line 2556) runs `touched = [m for m in world.marshals.values() if m.nation in nations]` on every entry. It then snapshots the transient fields of each touched marshal. That is a full O(M) pass per call, and the docstring shows the context manager is entered per priced candidate. world_state.py:7466 `get_disrupted_regions` makes one uncached pass over `self.marshals.values()`. Its docstring says "recomputed per call so mid-turn movement is reflected in reports", so the lack of a cache is deliberate. It is not a region scan, so CLAUDE.md Golden Rule 8 (no per-region scans in hot paths) is not violated. I did not re-run the profile, so the call counts and timings (4,332 calls, 173 per turn, about 50 ms of a 90 ms turn) are the reviewer's and unverified. Nothing in BUG_FIXES.md or DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md records or rules on this cost, so there is no closed row and no ruling to refute it. The "grows with the square of the roster" claim holds only if candidate count scales with M. The 1805 roster is fixed, so growth is probably gentler than quadratic.
mechanism.note: This is a performance and scalability observation, with no correctness defect. The cost is about 55% of a 90 ms turn on the current board, which is acceptable today. A per-nation marshal index or a per-turn memo keyed on a movement stamp would help. Any such memo must keep the mid-turn-movement freshness the `get_disrupted_regions` docstring requires. File it as a design or P3 note, not a defect.

reproduction.evidence: The code matches the finding. combat_executor.py `_priced_coordination` (def at 2512) builds `touched = [m for m in world.marshals.values() if m.nation in nations]` on every call. world_state.py:7466 `get_disrupted_regions` makes one uncached pass over `world.marshals`, and its docstring says "recomputed per call so mid-turn movement is reflected". I did not re-run the 24-turn profile, so the 4,332-call and 4,157-call counts and the 11% share are unconfirmed. My own probe loaded the europe_1805 scenario with `WorldState.from_scenario`: 24 marshals, 126 regions. `get_disrupted_regions()` cost 10.6 µs per call over 1000 calls. At the reported 173 calls a turn that is about 1.8 ms a turn, far below the finding's "about 50 ms of a 90 ms turn" (that figure is mostly `_priced_coordination` inside candidate evaluation). I found no SCALE-6 or `_priced_coordination` scale row in docs/BUG_FIXES.md or docs/DESIGN_REFINEMENT.md (the grep hits only mention it for the SF-CL-1 forecast), so no closed row refutes it.
reproduction.note: The linear rescans exist and are cheap on the 24-marshal roster. The finding's quadratic-at-1805-scale growth is an extrapolation I did not measure. `get_disrupted_regions` is negligible; `_priced_coordination` is the only part worth a memo, and a nation-indexed marshal list would be enough. P3 design or backlog, not a defect. If it is kept, golden rule 9 needs an owner row and a landing slice.
